units.la: Coniunge l. eum qui. de iurisdict. l. si locus. de iud. l. si index. de re iud.
units.tr: Conjoin l. eum qui. de iurisdict. l. si locus. de iud. l. si index. de re iud.

units.la: Nemo ]cui condemnandi potestas non competit, is absoluere non potest l. 6. in sin. principii. ff. de off. proconf. & è contra l. 3. de re iudic.
units.tr: "No one" [Nemo]: one who lacks the power of condemning cannot acquit: l. 6. in sin. principii. ff. de off. proconf. and conversely l. 3. de re iudic.

units.la: Condemnare ] condemnare non potest vulgata. Potest] excipe l.3.§.2.C.vbi senatores. Haec lex repetitur in l.3.de re iud. pertinet ad veterem formulam iudicum datorum, quae erat Condemna eum index, si pareat, &c. Quaeritur, an is possit absoluere? Ita, quia & condemnare & absoluere potuit. Cuiac.in Recitat.
units.tr: "Condemn" [Condemnare]: the Vulgate reads "cannot condemn." "Can" [Potest]: except l.3.§.2.C.vbi senatores. This law is repeated in l.3.de re iud. It pertains to the old formula of appointed judges, which was "Judge, condemn him if it is proved," and so on. It is asked whether such a judge can acquit. Yes, because he could both condemn and acquit. Cujas, in Recitat.

units.la: Lex 38. De herede.
units.tr: Law 38. On the heir.

units.la: SIcut poena ex delicto defuncti, heres tenerí non debet; ita nec lucrum facere, si quid ex ea ad eum peruenisset.
units.tr: Just as an heir ought not to be bound by the penalty arising from the dead man's offence, so neither should he make a gain, if anything from it has come to him.

units.la: Coniunge l.12.de oblig. & actionib.
units.tr: Conjoin l.12.de oblig. & actionib.

units.la: Poena] 2. Ecl.3.cap.37.v.l.33.de obligat.
units.tr: Penalty: 2. Ecl.3.cap.37.v.l.33.de obligat.

units.la: Ex] Recte ait lex, Ex delicto. Nam ex contractu haeres tenetur in solidum l.ex deposi ti 12. de oblig. & act. Ex delictis defuncti, haeredes tenentur de eo, quod ad ipsos peruenit. l.3. de vi, & viarm. Ex contractibus in solidum. l.hoc iure 152. & vlt.h.t. quae lex tota pertinet ad titul. unde vi. In omnibus contractibus, inquit, in quibus inest doli praestatio vel bona fides, agitur de dolo in solidum aduersus heredem: quod repetitur l.ad ea.157.§.vlt.hoc tit. Denique ex contractibus actiones de dolo in heredes dantur in solidum: actio illa extraordinaria in solidum non datur de dolo. Ab hac sententia quae dicitur dari actionem ex contractu in solidum, excipitur actio depositi, incendii, naufragii, tumultus causa; qui ex his causis negat depositum, tenetur in duplum, haeres autem in simplum plum tantum, siue peruenerit, siue non. Nam videtur esse ex delicto. Denique ex contractu est actio poenalis plerumque in defunctum. Excipitur ab hac regula actio de precario, quae est ex quasi contractu & tamen in haeredes ea nō datur ob dolum malum, nisi quatenus peruenerit. l. quaesitum 8. §. vlt. de precar. quia precarium haeredem non sequitur; alii contractus sequuntur haeredes, qua de causa in solidum tenentur. Dices: soluitur morte societas: sociis tamen in solidum datur. Resp. Etsi societas non sequatur haeredem, sequitur tamen lucrum l. nemo 35. l. verum 63. §. in haredem. 8. pro socio. Ex precario nullum potest praestari emolumentum haeredi: ut, si quis usus sit veste aliena precario, nullum transit commodum in haeredem. Itaque a definitione excipe actionem depositi, quam nominatim excipit Bulg. in l. in depositi 9. depos. Et ad eas actiones referendus est §. Alioquin. Instit. de perpet. & tempor. act. Cuiac.
units.tr: "From": the law rightly says "from an offence." For from a contract the heir is bound for the whole: l. ex deposito 12. de oblig. & act. From the offences of the deceased, heirs are bound only for what has come to them: l.3. de vi, & viarm. From contracts, for the whole: l. hoc iure 152. & vlt. h.t. That law as a whole pertains to the title unde vi. "In all contracts," it says, "in which there is an obligation to perform in good faith or with good faith, an action for fraud lies against the heir for the whole": this is repeated in l. ad ea. 157. §. vlt. hoc tit. Finally, actions for fraud are given against heirs from contracts for the whole; that extraordinary action for fraud is not given for the whole. From this statement, that an action from a contract is given for the whole, the action of deposit is excepted, as are actions for fire, shipwreck, and tumult; whoever denies a deposit on these grounds is bound for double, but the heir only for single, whether or not it has come to him. For it seems to arise from an offence. Finally, a penal action arising from contract usually lies against the deceased. The action on precarium is excepted from this rule, which arises from a quasi-contract, and yet is not given against heirs for wicked fraud except so far as something has come to them: l. quaesitum 8. §. vlt. de precar. because precarium does not pass to the heir, whereas other contracts pass to heirs, for which reason they are bound for the whole. You will object: partnership is dissolved by death, yet an action is given to partners for the whole. Reply: although partnership does not pass to the heir, the gain does pass: l. nemo 35. l. verum 63. §. in heredem. 8. pro socio. From precarium no advantage can be furnished to the heir: as, if someone has used another's clothing by precarium, no benefit passes to the heir. Therefore, from the definition, except the action of deposit, which Bulgarus expressly excepts, in l. in depositi 9. depos. And to these actions must be referred the paragraph Alioquin, Instit. de perpet. & tempor. act. Cujas.

units.la: Delicto Delicti nomen latissime accipe pro omni maleficio. Nam hoc nomine non tantum priuata delicta veniunt, ut furtum, iniuria, rapina, damnum iniuria datum, sed & dolus, & metus, & iniqua distributio, ob quam comparatur actio tributoria, ex qua non tenetur haeres, nisi ex eo, quod peruenit dolo defuncti, hoc est, quod ait l. toties 44. h.t. quae lex pertinet ad actionem illam tributoriam. Eadem est conditio omnium actionum in factum, quæ dolum coercent, vt in actione, quod falso tutore aut ore gestum esse dicetur, & in edicto, si mensor, & in edicto, de eo per quem factum erit: Illis edictis punitur dolus, nec dabuntur iis edictis actio in heredem, nisi peruenerit aliquid ad eum.
units.tr: "Offence" [Delicto]: take the term offence very broadly, for any wrongdoing. For under this name come not only private offences, such as theft, injury, robbery, damage wrongfully done, but also fraud, fear, and unfair distribution, on account of which the action for distribution is brought, against which the heir is not bound except for what has come to him through the deceased's fraud. This is what l. toties 44. h.t. says, and that law pertains to that action for distribution. The condition is the same for all actions on the case that punish fraud: as in the action which is said to have been done by a false tutor or by a false mouth, and in the edict "if the surveyor," and in the edict "concerning the one by whom it shall have been done." These edicts punish fraud, and no action under them is given against the heir unless something has come to him.

units.la: Delictum intelligitur etiam de quasi delicto, qua actione nihil heres præstat, nisi inceperit à testatore l. vlt. §. vlt. naut. caup. stabularii, &c. l. 5. §. hæc autem de iis qui effud. vel deiec. Cuiac. in Recit. posth.
units.tr: An offence is also understood to include a quasi-offence, against which the heir offers nothing unless the matter began with the testator: l. vlt. §. vlt. naut. caup. stabularii, &c. l. 5. §. haec autem de iis qui effud. vel deiec. Cujas, in Recit. posth.

units.la: Ad eum idem est in pupillo leg. 3. §. 1. de tributoria. v. l. 1. l. 5. de autoritat. tut. in Ecclesia, & bonæ fidei possessore. Decius hic. Gothof.
units.tr: "To him": the same holds for a ward, l. 3. §. 1. de tributoria. v. l. 1. l. 5. de auctorit. tut., in the case of the Church, and of a possessor in good faith. Decius here. Gothofredus.

units.la: Hæres ex delicto defuncti, poenali actione non tenetur; neque poenam fert, neque lucrum, nisi de eo, quod ad eum peruenit. h. & l. pupillum 111. §. in hæredem infr. h. t. Pœna est accipienda latissime. Nam non solæ pœnales actiones, sed & mixtæ veniunt; quæ habent hoc commune, vt morte rei percant: vt, furti actio non datur in hæredem, etiamsi quid ad eum peruenerit, quia mere pœnalis est. Serui corrupti actio, & arborum furtim caesarum, & damni, & metus causa in heredes dantur de eo, quod ad eos peruenit, ne lucrum ferant ex delicto defuncti, quod turpe est. Excipitur tantum actio vi bonorum raptorum, quae mixta est, & non datur in heredem. l. 2. §. vlt. vi bon. rapt. & tamen caeterae omnes mixtae actiones in heredem dantur de eo, quod ad eum peruenerit, quia vt ea lex ostendit, eo nomine est propria plerumque actio in heredem. Mixtis actionibus insunt actiones ex delicto, quae rei persecutionem habent, quibus nihil persequitur actor: nisi quod ad rem attinet. Hae actiones non dantur in heredem, nisi de eo, quod peruenit; cuiusmodi est actio de dolo, & condictio rerum amotarum. Excipitur sola condictio furtiua, quae datur in heredem in solidum leg. in condictione 9. de condict. furt. Leuius est submouere quam surripere. Ex iis constituimus omnes actiones ex delicto morte interire, excepta condictione furtiua. Quod quamuis dissuadere videatur l. 9. §. vlt. & l. 10. de rut. & rat. distrahend. quae leges videntur condictionem furtiuam numerare inter eas actiones, quae morte intereunt. Omnino tamen eam distinguere oportet a caeteris actionibus; & quidem furti & damni iniuria dati actio interit morte: condictio vero furtiua non ꝑ non interit. Itaque separari debet à cæteris actionibus. Rursus ita constituimus ex superioribus, omnes actiones, quæ rem, aut utrumque persequuntur, dari in heredem de eo, quod ad eum peruenit, excepta actione vi bonorum raptorum. Quæ vero meram pœnam persequuntur, nullo modo in hæredem dantur. Eadem est conditio actionis iniuriarum. Cuiac. in Recitat. posth.
units.tr: An heir is not bound by a penal action arising from the deceased's offence; he neither bears the penalty nor takes the gain, except for what has come to him: here, and l. pupillum 111. §. in heredem infr. h. t. Penalty must be taken very broadly. For not only penal actions come under it, but also mixed actions, which have this in common, that they die with the death of the party: for example, an action for theft is not given against the heir even if something has come to him, because it is purely penal. The action for corrupting a slave, and that for trees cut secretly, and for damage, and for fear, are given against heirs for what has come to them, so that they do not profit from the deceased's offence, which is disgraceful. Only the action for goods seized by violence is excepted, which is mixed, and is not given against the heir: l. 2. §. vlt. vi bon. rapt. Yet all the other mixed actions are given against the heir for what has come to him, because, as that law shows, for that reason there is usually a proper action against the heir. Within mixed actions there are actions arising from offence which have the character of pursuing a thing, in which the plaintiff claims nothing except as far as it concerns the thing. These actions are not given against the heir except for what has come to him; of this kind is the action de dolo, and the condictio rerum amotarum. Only the condictio furtiva is excepted, which is given against the heir for the whole: leg. in condictione 9. de condict. furt. It is less serious to remove than to steal. From these points we establish that all actions arising from offence die with the death, except the condictio furtiva. Although l. 9. §. vlt. & l. 10. de rut. & rat. distrahend. seems to dissuade this, since those laws seem to count the condictio furtiva among the actions which die with the person, nevertheless it must be distinguished from the other actions. The action for theft and for damage wrongfully done dies with the person; but the condictio furtiva does not die. Therefore it ought to be separated from the other actions. Again, from what has been said above, we establish that all actions which pursue a thing, or both the thing and the penalty, are given against the heir for what has come to him, except the action for goods seized by violence. But those which pursue a mere penalty are in no way given against the heir. The same holds for the action for injuries. Cujas, in Recitat. posth.

units.la: Lex 39. De eo quod per alium fit quo minus fiat.
units.tr: Law 39. On that which is done by another so that it may not be done.

units.la: IN omnibus casibus pro facto accipitur id, in quo per alium mora fit quo minus fiat.
units.tr: In all cases, that is taken as done in which delay is caused by another so that it is not done.

units.la: Certum est, conditionem haberi pro completa, si per debitorem fiat, quo minus impleatur conditio. l. in executione 85. §. vlt. de verb. obligat. Quidam promisit sub conditione, & curauit ne conditio existeret: lex ait, Eum tenéti, perri, perinde ac si impleta esset. Idem est in l. 24 §. Iulianus de condit. & demonstrat. Quid dicemus, si non per contrahentes fiat, quo minus conditio impleatur? Puto etiam hoc casu conditionem haberi pro completa, si per alium, in cuius persona erat implenda, fiat, quo minus impleatur. Finge ab haerede mihi legatum relictum, si Gaio decem darem, Gaius non vult accipere? non ideo minus petam legatum. Per alium non videtur mora fieri, nisi factum in eius personam sit collatum. Aliud est moram facere, aliud obstare conditioni, ut si ita sit conditio, si decem dederis Gaio: si te volentem dare, vel accipientem quis prohibeat, dicitur obstare: si Gaius nollet accipere, dicitur per illum mora fieri. Quid vero si per extraneum impediatur conditio? videtur hoc casu non haberi pro impleta, imo defecisse l. inde Neratius 23. §. idem 2. ad L. Aquil. Species est: heres esto, si seruum Stichum manumiserit. Stichus occiditur ante aditam hereditatem. Mors Stichi obstat conditioni: nec poteris adire hereditatem, sed habebis aestimationem serui occisi ex lege Aquilia, quo seruo manumisso tibi adquisisses hereditatem. Itaque si extraneus sit impedimento conditioni, non habetur pro impleta. Obstat l. quae sub conditione 8. §. mortuo autem 7. de condit. institution. & l. impia 45. de legat. 1. In quibus haeres ita institutus, si seruum manumanumiserit, seruo occiso adit hereditatem. Respondeo in l. inde Neratius 23. considerandum est, seruum fuisse occilum post mortem testatoris, quo tempore iam debuerat manumitti seruus. At in l. quæ sub condit. 8. seruus est mortuus viuo testatore, nec poterat manumitti conditionis implendæ caula. Cuiac. in Recit. posth.
units.tr: It is certain that a condition is regarded as fulfilled if the debtor brings it about that the condition is not met. l. in executione 85. §. vlt. de verb. obligat. Someone promised under a condition and took care that the condition should not come about: the law says he is to be held liable just as if it had been fulfilled. The same holds in l. 24 §. Iulianus de condit. & demonstrat. What shall we say if the condition is not prevented by the contracting parties? I think that in this case too the condition is regarded as fulfilled if it is prevented by another, in whose person it was to be fulfilled. Suppose an heir has left me a legacy on condition that I give ten to Gaius, and Gaius refuses to accept it: I shall not on that account claim the legacy any the less. Delay does not seem to be caused by another unless the act was directed at that person's own person. It is one thing to cause delay, and another to stand in the way of a condition. For example, if the condition is that you give ten to Gaius: if someone prevents you, though you are willing to give, or prevents Gaius, though he is willing to accept, he is said to stand in the way; but if Gaius were unwilling to accept, delay is said to be caused by him. But what if the condition is hindered by a stranger? In this case the condition seems not to be regarded as fulfilled, but rather to have failed. l. inde Neratius 23. §. idem 2. ad L. Aquil. The case is this: "Be heir if you manumit my slave Stichus." Stichus is killed before the inheritance is entered upon. Stichus's death stands in the way of the condition, and you cannot enter upon the inheritance, but you will have the value of the slain slave under the Lex Aquilia, since by manumitting the slave you would have acquired the inheritance. Therefore, if a stranger is an obstacle to the condition, it is not regarded as fulfilled. The objection is l. quae sub conditione 8. §. mortuo autem 7. de condit. institution. and l. impia 45. de legat. 1. In these, an heir was so instituted, "if he manumit the slave," and the slave was killed, and he entered upon the inheritance. I reply: in l. inde Neratius 23 it must be considered that the slave was killed after the testator's death, when the slave ought already to have been manumitted. But in l. quae sub condit. 8 the slave died while the testator was alive, and could not be manumitted for the purpose of fulfilling the condition. Cuiac. in Recit. posth.

units.la: Lex 40. De furioso & prodigo.
units.tr: Law 40. On the insane and the prodigal.

units.la: Furiosi, vel eius cui bonis interdictum sit, nulla voluntas est.
units.tr: The insane, or one whose goods have been interdicted, has no will.

units.la: Vide l. 5. ff. h. t. vbi hæc lex exposita est.
units.tr: See l. 5. ff. h. t., where this law is explained.

units.la: Furiosi ] ac dementis leg. 17. ff. Qui Testam. Quod ad furiosos attinet, distinguendum est; alii sunt in continuo furore, alii interuallatum habent furorem. Priores ne quidem adquirere possunt: alii possunt in iudicio, Testamento, tutela & similibus. vide Hotom. 3 obs. 29. Adde notata sup. ad l. 5. h. t.
units.tr: Insane] and demented, law 17, ff. Qui Testam. As regards the insane, a distinction must be made: some are in continuous madness, others have intermittent madness. The former cannot acquire anything at all; the latter can in judicial proceedings, in a will, in guardianship and in similar matters. See Hotomanus, 3 obs. 29. Add the notes above on law 5, h. t.

units.la: Eius ] masculi vel mulieris. l. 15. ff. de curat. surios.
units.tr: Of him] whether man or woman. law 15, ff. de curat. furiosi.

units.la: Cui bonis ] id est prodigi leg. 1. ff. de curat. surios.
units.tr: Whose goods] that is, of a prodigal, law 1, ff. de curat. furiosi.

units.la: Interdictum ] à iudice scilicet, idque non perfunctorie, sed vel ex officio, de industria: aut prodigi agnatus, aut amicis petentibus. Decius hic. Nulla] in amittendo & alienando l. 26. ff. de contra. empt. l. 18. ff. quitestam. l. 12. ff. de vsurpat. non in adquirendo. l. 5. in f. ff. de acquir. haered. l. 6. ff. de verb. obligat. l. 3. ff. de nouationibus. l. 18. §. 2. ff. de castrensi peculio.
units.tr: Interdicted] by a judge, namely, and not perfunctorily, but either ex officio, deliberately; either at the petition of the prodigal's agnate or of friends. Decius here. No (no will) in losing and alienating: law 26, ff. de contrahenda emptione; law 18, ff. qui testamenta; law 12, ff. de usurpationibus; not in acquiring: law 5, in fine ff. de acquirenda haereditate; law 6, ff. de verborum obligationibus; law 3, ff. de novationibus; law 18, §2, ff. de castrensi peculio.

units.la: Nulla est] Hinc colligit Clatus, Prodigalitate poenam eleuari. f. sentent. §. vlt. quaest. 60. n. 6.
units.tr: Has no will] From this Clarus infers that punishment is lessened by prodigality. f. sentent. §. vlt. quaest. 60. n. 6.

units.la: Lex 41. De Actore & reo. Dere obscura.
units.tr: On matters that are obscure. Law 41, on plaintiff and defendant.

units.la: NOn debet actori licere, quod reo non permittitur.
units.tr: The plaintiff ought not to be allowed what is not permitted to the defendant.

units.la: Actori] & accusatori.
units.tr: Plaintiff] and the accuser.

units.la: Reo] v. l. 125. h. t. cap. non licet 32. de regul. in sext. vbi vide Dynum: ad el. 17. l. 25. ff. de procuratoribus. Nota de argumento à reo ad actorem l. 9. §. 6. ff. de iureiurand.
units.tr: Defendant] see law 125 of this title, chapter "non licet" 32 de regul. in sext., where see Dynus on el. 17, law 25 ff. de procuratoribus. Note the argument from defendant to plaintiff, law 9 §6 ff. de iureiurando.

units.la: Duae hic sunt regulae. Prima exemplum est: Reo non licet mutare procuratorem post litem contestatam. idem ergo est in actore. leg. quae omnia 25. de procurat. Vulgo dicitur: Quod licet actori, licet & reo: qua de causa Ioannes scribit, reo licere in se onus probandi transferre, cum id actori liceat. Secundum Ioannem igitur multo magis reo constat morem esse gerendum probare volenti.
units.tr: There are two rules here. The first is an example: the defendant may not change his procurator after the joinder of issue. The same therefore holds for the plaintiff, law "quae omnia" 25 de procuratoribus. It is commonly said: what is allowed the plaintiff is allowed the defendant too. For this reason John writes that the defendant may transfer the burden of proof onto himself, since this is allowed the plaintiff. According to John, then, it is much more agreed that the defendant who wishes to prove should be accommodated.

units.la: Secunda regula. Notissimum est ei, qui sol-uit uit sciens, non competere condictionem indebiti. Is ergo qui ignorans soluit, habet condictionem indebiti; & sic repetitionem quæ fit per condictionem indebiti. tot. tit. de condict. indeb. Si dubitetur; an quis ignorans vel sciens soluerit, præsumitur ignorans. l. si non sortem. 26. §. si quis falso. 2. de condict. indeb. Sic in obscuro potius fauere debemus condicenti indebitum, quam reo contendenti sibi donatum esse. Potest obiici l. idem est. 17. de reb. dub. cuius hæc est sententia: Vir & vxor simul decesserunt: repetentne dotem hæredes vxoris, quasi præmortuo viro; an vero mariti hæredes quasi præmortua vxore retinebunt? Fauebitur hoc casu potius hæredibus mariti, quam iis, qui repetunt quasi præmortuo marito? Species hæc non conuenit huic regulæ, quia dos quam retinet hæres mariti, non est lucrum aduentitium, sed rei iam quæsitæ retentio. Itaque ea nihil obstat. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: The second rule. It is well known that one who pays knowingly has no condictio indebiti. One who pays in ignorance therefore has the condictio indebiti, and so the recovery which is made by the condictio indebiti. See the whole title de condictione indebiti. If it is doubtful whether someone paid knowingly or in ignorance, he is presumed to have paid in ignorance, law "si non sortem" 26, §"si quis falso" 2 de condictione indebiti. So in an obscure matter we ought rather to favour the one who claims what was not owed than the defendant who contends that it was given to him. An objection may be raised from law "idem est" 17 de rebus dubiis, whose sense is this: husband and wife died together. Do the wife's heirs recover the dowry as though the husband died first, or will the husband's heirs keep it as though the wife died first? Should the husband's heirs be favoured in this case rather than those who recover as though the husband died first? This case does not fit this rule, because the dowry which the husband's heir keeps is not an accidental gain but the retention of a thing already acquired. So it does not stand in the way. Cuiacius in Recitationes.
On §1.

units.la: Repetitioni ] magis ei fauetur qui repetit, quam qui de lucro captando certat. Imo magis fauendum minori qui alienum accepit & dilapidauit, quam minori suum repetenti l. ii. §. 6. ff. de minorib. Ea res Gothofr. mouet, vt hic putet, non inconcinne legi, retentioni in l. 91. §. 3. in sin. ff. de verb. obligat.
units.tr: Repetitioni] more favour is shown to the one who recovers than to one who contends for gain. Indeed a minor who received what belonged to another and squandered it should be favoured more than a minor who recovers his own, law ii §6 ff. de minoribus. Gothofredus is moved by this, so that he thinks it not unfittingly read "retentioni" in law 91 §3 in sin. ff. de verb. obligat.

units.la: 2. Eclog. 3. cap. 40. l. 33. ff. eod. l. 14. §. 1. ff. de religiosis.
units.tr: 2. Eclog. 3, cap. 40; law 33 ff. eod.; law 14 §1 ff. de religiosis.

units.la: In re obscura melius est fauere Gaio sortem reperienti, quam Titio vsuras petenti: & fauetur actori potius, quam reo, quia actor de damno, reus de lucro certat. l. ult. §. si omnes. de iure deliberand. Cum vterque certat de damno, vel lucro, fateor faueri reo, hoc est, in pari causa. Dispar autem est causa, si actor de lucro, de damno reus disceptet. In dispari causa ei, qui de damno est sollicitus, potius fauemus. Præsumitur igitur potius ignorans soluisse quam sciens.
units.tr: In an obscure matter it is better to favour Gaius, who recovers his share, than Titius, who seeks interest. The plaintiff is favoured rather than the defendant, because the plaintiff contends about loss, the defendant about gain, law ult. §"si omnes", de iure deliberandi. Since each contends about loss or gain, I grant that the defendant is favoured, that is, when the cause is equal. But the cause is unequal if the plaintiff contends about gain and the defendant about loss. In an unequal cause we favour rather the one who is anxious about loss. Therefore it is more likely that one who paid was presumed to have paid in ignorance than knowingly.

units.la: Ad Leg. 42. De Ignorantia.
units.tr: On Law 42, on ignorance.

units.la: QVi in alterius causam succedunt, iustam habent causam ignorantiæ, an id quod peteretur, deberetur. Fideiussores quoque non minus quam hæredes iustam ignorantiam possunt allegare. Hæc ita de hærede dicta sunt, si cum eo agetur, non etiam si agar. Nam plane si agar, certus esse debet, cum sit in potestate eius, quando velit, experiri, & ante debet rem diligenter explorare, & tunc ad agendum procedere.
units.tr: Those who succeed to another's cause have a just reason for ignorance whether what is sought was owed. Sureties too may plead just ignorance no less than heirs. These things are said of the heir if he is sued, not if he sues. For if he sues, he must be certain, since it is in his power to bring suit whenever he wishes; he ought first to investigate the matter carefully, and only then proceed to act.

units.la: Alterius alieni facti ignorantia excusat. l. ii. ff. ad Velleianum. l. 21. §. 1. ff. de act. empt. l. ult. in f. ff. pro suo. non proprii, ac muneris. hinc illud, Non potest esse pastoris excusatio, si lupus oues comedit. medit, & pastor nescit.cap quamuis.20. extr.de reg.iuris.
units.tr: Ignorance of another's act excuses: law ii ff. ad Velleianum; law 21 §1 ff. de act. empt.; law ult. in fin. ff. pro suo, not one's own but of one's office. Hence the saying: "It is no excuse for a shepherd that the wolf ate the sheep and the shepherd did not know it," cap. quamvis 20 extr. de reg. iuris.

units.la: An venia dignam & immunem à poena? vtique. Imo, non vtique l.9 ff.de nautico fœnore.l.77.ff.de verb.obligat.solue. Non vtiq;, strictò iure: aliud ex æquo dicimus. adde dict. cap.14.
units.tr: Is he worthy of pardon and immune from penalty? Certainly. Indeed, not certainly: law 9 ff. de nautico faenore; law 77 ff. de verb. obligat., solve. Not certainly, strictly by law; we say otherwise in equity. Add the said chapter 14.

units.la: l.19.ff.eod. adde l.49.§.2.ff.de verb. obligat.cap.cum quis 14.de regul.in sexto.
units.tr: l.19 ff. eod. Add l.49 §2 ff. de verb. oblig.; cap. cum quis 14 de reg. in sexto.

units.la: ea cessat in iis quæ in Testamento continentur.l.12.ff.de transactionib.
units.tr: This ceases in those things which are contained in a testament: law 12 ff. de transactionibus.

units.la: aliud erit, si ipsi petant. infr.h.t.& l.49.§.2.ff.de verb.oblig.
units.tr: It will be otherwise if they themselves sue: infra h.t. and law 49 §2 ff. de verb. oblig.

units.la: l.59.ff.de condict.indeb.v.l.8.§.8.l.29.in princ.& §.2.ff.mandati.
units.tr: Law 59 ff. de condict. indeb.; v. l. 8 §8, law 29 in princ. and §2 ff. mandati.

units.la: d.§.2.& l.37.ff.de arbitris : nisi iusta causa aliud suadeat.
units.tr: D. §2 and law 37 ff. de arbitris: unless a just cause suggests otherwise.

units.la: l.5. in f.ff.de except.doli l.6.Cod.de temp.in integ.
units.tr: Law 5 in fin. ff. de except. doli; law 6 Cod. de temp. in integ.

units.la: aliud in reo l.2.C.de dilationibus.
units.tr: Otherwise in the defendant: law 2 C. de dilationibus.

units.la: Hæres iuste ignorare potest negotia defuncti: quamobrem si heres soluerit, potest ei dari condictio indebiti, quæ non datur ob supinam ignorantiam. Eadem ratione hæredi eius, cum quo contrahitur, non potest iusiurandum deferri: quia contractum defuncti potest ignorare. Itaque recusabit iusiurandum. Paul. lib.2. Sentent. tit.2. Fideiussori quoque iusta est ignorantia: si fideiussor conuentus ex causa fideiussionis,
units.tr: An heir may justly be ignorant of the affairs of the deceased. Therefore if the heir pays, a condictio indebiti can be given to him, which is not given on account of gross ignorance. For the same reason the oath cannot be deferred to the heir of the one with whom the contract was made, because he may be ignorant of the deceased's contract; so he will refuse the oath. Paul, lib. 2 Sent. tit. 2. For a surety too there is just ignorance: if a surety, sued on the ground of the suretyship,

units.la: Pagina 99 (marginal Latin notes as above). sionis, omiserit exceptionem pacti, vel non numeratæ pecuniæ, & cum eam ignoraret, soluit, nihil ei imputatur, & repeteret solutum actione mandati a reo principali. Idem est, si, cum debitor soluisset, fideiussor ignarus soluerit; nam repetet fideiussor solutum. l. si fideiussor. 29. mandati. Quod dixinus hæredis esse iustam ignorantiam, hoc procedit ita, si heres conuenia-tur ex contractu defuncti: Non si agat. Nam si agit, paratus debet venire ad agendum, hoc est, diligenter explorato iure defuncti. Itaque non est iusta ignorantia hæredis agentis: sed eius cum quo agitur, qui plerumque incogitanter accedit ad causam. l. pure. 5. §. penult. de dol. except. l. 2. C. de dilation. Præterea, hæc ratio efficit, vt reus qualiter qualiter instructus veniat ad iudicium. l. 1. de edendo, vt constet de re vel qualitate, quæ petitur. Nam edita actio debet comprehendere non tantum genus actionis, sed & rei qualitatem, idque propter periculum plus petitionis, vt scribitur constitut. Hermog. Cæterum hæres si petit, iustam ignorantiam non allegat: imo si plus petat, causa cadit iure antiquo, vel iure nouo in poenam incidet ex causa iusta. Nam debuit rem diligentius explorare, quando vellet agere. Cuiac. in Recitat. posth.
units.tr: Page 99 (marginal Latin notes as above). ...sionis: if he omits the exception of pact or of money not counted, and not knowing this, pays, nothing is charged against him, and he may recover what he paid by the action of mandate against the principal debtor. The same holds if, when the debtor has already paid, the surety pays in ignorance; for the surety will recover what he paid, law "si fideiussor" 29 mandati. What we have said of the heir's just ignorance holds only if the heir is sued on the contract of the deceased, not if he sues. For if he sues, he ought to be ready to come to the action, that is, having carefully explored the law of the deceased. Hence it is not just ignorance in the heir who sues, but in the one against whom suit is brought, who usually comes to the cause without thought. Law "pure" 5 §penult. de dol. except.; law 2 C. de dilation. Moreover, this reason makes the defendant come to court somehow prepared, law 1 de edendo, so that the matter or quality which is sought is made clear. For the action set out must comprehend not only the kind of action but also the quality of the thing, and that on account of the danger of seeking too much, as is written in the constitution of Hermogenianus. Otherwise, if the heir sues, he does not plead just ignorance; indeed, if he seeks more, the case fails under the old law, or under the new law he falls into penalty without just cause. For he ought to have investigated the matter more carefully when he wished to sue. Cuiacius in Recitationes posthumae.

units.la: Ad L. 43. De concurrentibus de- fensionibus.
units.tr: On Law 43, On Concurrent Defences.

units.la: Nemo ex his qui negant se debere, prohibetur etiam alia defensione vti, nisi lex impedit.
units.tr: No one who denies that he owes is barred from also using another defence, unless the law prevents it.

units.la: Prohibetur ] nisi mentitus sit. l. 1. §. 15. ff. si quadrupes l. 21. §. 2. l. 22. in sin ff. de noxalib.
units.tr: Is barred ] unless he has lied. l. 1. §. 15. ff. si quadrupes l. 21. §. 2. l. 22. in sin ff. de noxalib.

units.la: Euiidem ] 2. Eclog. 3. cap. 43. nam variarum rerum nomine, varias simul actiones edi posse constat. l. 11. ff. de iurisdict. l. 35. §. 1 ff. locati.
units.tr: Of the same ] for it is agreed that, on account of different matters, different actions may be brought at the same time. l. 11. ff. de iurisdict. l. 35. §. 1 ff. locati.

units.la: Vna ] vna tantum Pac. In realibus actionibus Hotomannus 27. illustr. id admittit arg. l. 3. l. 5. l. 6. l. 7. ff. de excep. rei iudicat. in personalibus negat. l. 130. b. t. l. 14. §. 2. ff. de excep. rei iudic. l. 60. de obligat. vide Hotom. ibid.
units.tr: One ] one only, Pacius. In real actions Hotomannus, 27 illustr. admits this, arg. l. 3, l. 5, l. 6, l. 7, ff. de excep. rei iudicat.; in personal actions he denies it. l. 130, b. t., l. 14. §. 2. ff. de excep. rei iudic., l. 60, de obligat.; see Hotom. ibid.

units.la: Debet ] & potest, non modo post vnius actionis damnationem l. 93. §. 1. ff. de legat. 3. l. 28. §. ultimo ff. de liberat. verum etiam post vnius victoriam l. 10. ff. de act. empt. l. 18. ff. de obligat. interdum eandem instaurare ac referre certis de causis, veluti ob iustum errorem l. 13. ff. de instit. l. 1. §. ultimo ff. quando de pecul. l. 4. §. ultim. ff. quod cum eo. vide Hotomannum ibidem.
units.tr: May ] and may, not only after condemnation in one action l. 93. §. 1. ff. de legat. 3, l. 28. §. ultimo ff. de liberat. but also after winning one l. 10. ff. de act. empt., l. 18. ff. de obligat., and sometimes renew and bring back the same action for certain reasons, such as a just error l. 13. ff. de instit., l. 1. §. ultimo ff. quando de pecul., l. 4. §. ultim. ff. quod cum eo.; see Hotomannus there.

units.la: Duæ hîc proponuntur regulæ, vna de reo, altera de actore. Vtraque coniunctâ efficies, plus reo permitti quam actori. Reo permittitur pluribus exceptionibus vti, etiam diuersis l. is qui dicit. 5. l. nemo. 8. de exceptio. & negare potest se accepisse pecuniam, & praeterea opponere pacti exceptionem. Actori autem non permittitur pluribus actionibus vti eadem de re simul ad eundem finem l. plura 53. de obligat. & act. vt legatorum nomine non potest legatarius vti variis actionibus, l. cum filius. 76. §. penult. de legat. 2. Et si commodatarius rem deteriorem fecerit, ei qui commodauit competunt duae actiones, commodati & legis Aquiliae: sed vna tantum debet esse contentus. De re etiam furto sublata est actio in rem, & actio furti; vna tantum debet esse contentus. Sed addit in hac lege, nisi lex impediat. Hanc interpretationem recipit ex Novell. 18. de trient. & semiss. §. studium. ex qua forsitan haec verba adiecta sunt, vt similia verba l. 1. Cod. de reb. cred. propter l. vlt. eod. Ea Nouella continetur, vt reus conuentus rei vindicatione, qui negauit rem esse actoris, postea conuictus, non possit allegare contra, sed transferre debet rem in actorem. Caeterum cum initio negauit rem esse actoris, non debet transfugere ad hypothecam de actione conuentionali. Cautetur autem ea Nouella vt is, qui negauit se debere, non possit postea dicere, se soluisse. Nam iterum soluit, qui negauit se debere. Haec est poena inficiationis: nis: & ita lex impedit, ne reus vtatur pluribus exceptionibus. Cuiac.in Recitat.posth.
units.tr: Two rules are proposed here, one concerning the defendant and the other the plaintiff. Taken together they show that more is permitted to the defendant than to the plaintiff. The defendant is permitted to use several exceptions, even different ones l. is qui dicit, 5, l. nemo, 8, de exceptio.: he may deny that he received the money and, besides, plead the exception of agreement. The plaintiff, however, is not permitted to use several actions concerning the same matter at once for the same end l. plura 53, de obligat. & act.; for example, on account of a legacy the legatee may not use various actions l. cum filius 76. §. penult. de legat. 2. And if a borrower has damaged the thing, two actions lie for the lender, the action on loan and the action under the Lex Aquilia; but he must be content with only one. Likewise, for a thing taken by theft, there is an action in rem and an action for theft; he must be content with only one. But in this law he adds "unless the law prevents it." This interpretation is taken from Novell. 18, de trient. & semiss. §. studium, and perhaps from it these words were added, as similar words appear in l. 1. Cod. de reb. cred.; on account of l. vlt. eod. That Novella holds that a defendant sued by a vindication of the thing, who denied that the thing belonged to the plaintiff and was afterwards convicted, may not plead in opposition, but must hand the thing over to the plaintiff. Moreover, since he at first denied that the thing belonged to the plaintiff, he must not turn to the hypothec of the personal action. That Novella also provides that one who denied that he owed cannot afterwards say that he has paid, for one who denied the debt pays again. This is the penalty for denial, and so the law prevents the defendant from using several exceptions. Cuiac. in Recitat. posth.

units.la: Ad Leg. 44. De herede.
units.tr: On Law 44, On the Heir.

units.la: TOties in heredem damus actionem de eo, quod ad eum peruenit, quoties ex dolo defuncti conuenitur, non quoties ex suo.
units.tr: As often as we grant an action against an heir concerning what came to him, so often is he sued on account of the deceased's fraud, and not whenever it is on his own.

units.la: Ad Leg. 45. De conuentionibus.
units.tr: On Law 45, On Agreements.

units.la: NEque pignus, neque depositum, neque precarium, neque emptio, neque locatio rei suæ consistere potest. Rei proprietatem proprietarius emere non potest, sed possessionem, & econtra leg. 28. de acquir. possess.
units.tr: Neither a pledge, nor a deposit, nor a precarium, nor a purchase, nor a lease of one's own thing can stand. Of the thing: the owner cannot buy the ownership, but can buy possession, and conversely. leg. 28. de acquir. possess.

units.la: Huius regulæ multi sunt effectus, ad id vt interpelletur vsucapio; si rem, quam cœpi vsucapere, domino locauerim. Idem est, si eam rem domino vendidero, vel pignori obligauero. l. ei, à quo 21. l. non solum 33. §. si rem suam 5. de vsurpat. & vsucap. Et si dominus ignorans rem suam emerit, pretio soluto indebiti condictionem habet, quia emptio rei meæ non consistit, leg. sua rei 18. de contrah. empt. Qui rem suam conducit, non tenetur locati; qui rem suam apud se deponi patitur, non tenetur depositi. l. qui rem suam 15. depos. Postremus effectus huius regulæ est, vt pignus tollatur adquisitione dominii, licet non semper actio hypothecaria tollatur. l. pen. §. ult. de except. rei iudic. in cuius specie sublata hypotheca comparatione dominii, non tollitur hypothecaria actio l. 25. de noxal. act. Male Accursius ad d. l. penult. coniungit l. debitor 59. ad Senatusconsultum Trebellianum. Quæstio legis penultimæ est, an sublata hypotheca, tollatur actio hypothecæ? Recte ait Iurisconsultus, REI SVÆ, hoc est proprietatis: nam possessionis & precarium & venditio potest consistere. l. si aliquam rem 28. de adquirend. possess. l. si in emptione 34. §. rei sue, de contrah. empt. Si rem mean meam mihi reddi stipuler, valet stipulatio: si dari, non valet leg. 4. §. Labeo, de doli except. Rursus hæc non valent, si fiant pure, si sub conditione, valent. Item, rem meam recte emo sub conditione. l. existimo 98. de verborum obligat. Præterea quædam ex iis negotiis inter ignorantes non recte contrahuntur, inter scientes recte. Sciens dominus à sciente domino recte conducit: ut si fundum meum possideas, ego recte à te conducam, cum rem possidere videar iure conductionis. l. quædam 77. de rei vindicat. Re, quam volumus alienare, conducta, vel in ea relicto vsufructu, videtur vsusfructus ab eo constitui. Cuiac. in Recit. posth.
units.tr: This rule has many effects. Usucapion is interrupted if I let to its owner a thing I have begun to usucapt. The same holds if I sell that thing to its owner or pledge it to him. l. ei, à quo 21, l. non solum 33, §. si rem suam 5, de vsurpat. & vsucap. And if an owner, unaware, buys his own thing, he has an action for recovery of what was paid as not owed, because a purchase of my own thing does not stand. leg. sua rei 18, de contrah. empt. One who hires his own thing is not bound by the contract of lease; one who allows his own thing to be deposited with himself is not bound by the contract of deposit. l. qui rem suam 15, depos. The last effect of this rule is that a pledge is removed by acquisition of ownership, although the hypothecary action is not always removed. l. pen. §. ult. de except. rei iudic., where, in that case, when the hypothec is removed by the acquisition of ownership, the hypothecary action is not removed. l. 25. de noxal. act. Accursius wrongly joins l. debitor 59, ad Senatusconsultum Trebellianum, to the said penultimate law. The question of the penultimate law is whether, when the hypothec is removed, the hypothecary action is also removed. The Jurist rightly says OWN THING, that is, of ownership, for of possession both a precarium and a sale can stand. l. si aliquam rem 28, de adquirend. possess.; l. si in emptione 34, §. rei sue, de contrah. empt. If I stipulate that my own thing be returned to me, the stipulation is valid; if that it be given, it is not valid. leg. 4. §. Labeo, de doli except. Again, these are not valid if made purely, but they are valid if made under a condition. Likewise, I may validly buy my own thing under a condition. l. existimo 98, de verborum obligat. Moreover, some of these transactions are not validly contracted between parties who are unaware, but are validly contracted between parties who know. An owner who knows conducts from an owner who knows validly: for example, if you possess my farm, I may validly hire it from you, since I seem to possess the thing by right of the lease. l. quædam 77, de rei vindicat. A thing we wish to alienate, once leased, or with a usufruct left in it, is seen to create a usufruct by that person. Cuiac. in Recit. posth.

units.la: De posteriore sententia huius legis dictum est in l. 27. h. tit.
units.tr: Concerning the latter opinion of this law, it has been said in l. 27, h. tit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 46. De pæna.
units.tr: On Law 46. On penalty.

units.la: QVod à quoquam pœnæ nomine exactum est, id eidem restituere nemo cogitur.
units.tr: No one is compelled to restore to the same person what has been exacted from anyone under the name of a penalty.

units.la: Repetere ] pœnæ depensæ, repeti non solent. l. 19. l. 42. ff. de condict. indeb. leg. 22. ff. de pignorat. adde leg. 52. in sin. Pro socio. leg. 74. de solut. In l. pœna 42. de condict. indeb. ICTus ait: Non solent repeti pœnæ quæ depensæ sunt. Verbo SOLENT significatur esse regulam. ut in l. pupillum h. t. & comprobatur l. 1. ad L. Iul. de ambitu. Si damnatus de ambitu in integrum restituatur, restituitur famæ suæ, sed non peter pœnam 100. aureorum, licet res redierit ad causam indebiti. Idem probatur in leg. 3. §. & si sub conditione 14. de tab. exhibend. Quidam legatarius est sub conditione, ea pendente sibi vult exhiberi tabulas: feret pœnam contumaciæ heres, nisi exhibuerit: ablata pœna contumaciæ, deficit conditio. An cogitur pœnam restituere? minime. Pœnæ enim non solent repeti quæ depensæ sunt. Lex ait, eidem, hoc est, à quo pœna exacta est. Comprobatur hæc regula in l. si debitor. 79. de furt. & l. id quod 74. de solution. Interdum fit furtum rei suæ. Quod si creditor furti actionem aduersus debitorem habuerit, an in sortem computabitur pœna? Minime, sed cedet lucro creditoris. In conductore & commodatario id fit, ut, qui rem conduxit, si rem surripuit, locatori teneatur locato. l. 6. locati. leg. ult. §. sin autem C. de furt. Namque magna est differentia inter creditorem, conductorem, locatorem, commodatarium. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: To be reclaimed] Penalties that have been paid are not usually reclaimed. l. 19, l. 42, ff. de condict. indeb.; leg. 22, ff. de pignorat.; add leg. 52, in fin., Pro socio; leg. 74, de solut. In l. pœna 42, de condict. indeb. the jurist says: Penalties that have been paid are not usually reclaimed. The word USUALLY signifies that this is a rule, as in l. pupillum, h. t., and it is confirmed by l. 1, ad L. Iul. de ambitu. If a man condemned for bribery is restored to his former position, he is restored to his reputation, but he does not demand the penalty of 100 gold pieces, although the matter has returned to the basis of the undue payment. The same is shown in leg. 3, §. and if under a condition, 14, de tab. exhibend. A legatee is under a condition, and while it is pending he wishes the tablets to be shown to him; the heir will bear the penalty for contumacy unless he has shown them. When the penalty for contumacy has been removed, the condition fails. Is he compelled to restore the penalty? By no means: for penalties that have been paid are not usually reclaimed. The law says "to the same person", that is, to the one from whom the penalty was exacted. This rule is confirmed in l. si debitor, 79, de furt., and l. id quod, 74, de solution. Sometimes a theft of one's own property occurs. But if the creditor has an action for theft against the debtor, is the penalty to be counted in the principal? Not at all; it will go to the creditor's profit. This happens in the case of the hirer and the borrower: one who has hired a thing, if he has stolen it, is liable to the lessor for the hired thing. l. 6, locati; leg. ult., §. sin autem, C. de furt. For there is a great difference between creditor, hirer, lessor and lender. Cuiac. in Recitat.

units.la: Ad Leg. 47. De consilio, & sociis.
units.tr: On Law 47. On counsel, and partners.

units.la: Consilii non fraudulenti nulla obligatio est: caeterum si dolus & calliditas intercessit, de dolo actio competit.
units.tr: There is no obligation arising from counsel that is not fraudulent; but if deceit and cunning intervened, an action for deceit lies.

units.la: Ex tit. mand. v. l. 2.
units.tr: From the title on mandate, see l. 2.

units.la: Consilii ] 2. Eclog. 3. cap. 46. c. nullus 62. de reg. in sexto l. 2. in f. ff. mandati.
units.tr: Counsel] 2. Eclog. 3, cap. 46; c. nullus 62, de reg. in sexto; l. 2, in fin., ff. mandati.

units.la: Nam fraudulentum obligat. v. l. 8. ff. de dolo. l. 1. §. 3. ff. de serv. corrupt. l. 43. §. 3. ff. de furtis l. 20. C. eod. l. 16. ff. de poenis: & si alter sine consilio nostro id non erat facturus. leg. 6. §. 5. ff. mandati.
units.tr: For fraudulent counsel does bind: see l. 8, ff. de dolo; l. 1, §. 3, ff. de serv. corrupt.; l. 43, §. 3, ff. de furtis; l. 20, C. eod.; l. 16, ff. de poenis; and also if the other would not have acted without our counsel: leg. 6, §. 5, ff. mandati.

units.la: 2. Eclog. 3. c. 47 l. 19. l. 20. ff. pro socio. dicidem in liberto liberti l. 105. ff. de verb. signif. & vasallo mei vasalli, & colono mei coloni ( ratione tamen alterius, non eiusdem praedii, quod à me vasallus habet. ) Non idem in amico inimici mei. leg. 1. §. 10. ff. de off. pref. urb. l. 3. ff. de testib. l. 4. §. 3. ff. de legationibus: v. l. 28. C. de inoff. & in fideiussore fideiussoris mei l. 27. §. 2. §. 3. §. 4. ff. de fideiussoribus.
units.tr: 2. Eclog. 3, c. 47; l. 19, l. 20, ff. pro socio. The same is said of the freedman of a freedman, l. 105, ff. de verb. signif.; and of the vassal of my vassal, and the tenant of my tenant (though by reason of the other holding, not the same estate, which the vassal holds from me). It is not the same with the friend of my enemy. leg. 1, §. 10, ff. de off. pref. urb.; l. 3, ff. de testib.; l. 4, §. 3, ff. de legationibus; see l. 28, C. de inoff. And with the surety of my surety, l. 27, §§. 2, 3, 4, ff. de fideiussoribus.

units.la: Duae sunt sententiae huius legis. Prima pertinet ad negotium mandati, ut docetur l. 2. §. ult. mandati. Mandatum non contrahitur tua tantum gratia, ut si ego mandem tibi, ut pecunia tua fundum potius emas, quam foenus contrahas, hoc non est mandatum, sed consilium, quod nempe suadet, ut potius in eam rem convertas pecuniam, quam in aliam: tu debes explorare, an consilium tibi expediat. Itaque ex consilio nemo obligatur. Aliud est mandatum, aliud consilium. Ex mandato est obligatio, ex consilio bona fide dato, non item; ex consilio mala fide dato, est actio de dolo. Mandaui procuratori meo, vt vteretur consilio Sempronii, qui adhibitus, suasit, vt pecuniam meam fœnori collocaret: quo consilio vsus est Procurator, & res male cecidit, nam eam male collocauit: Sempronius non tenebitur, nisi dolo suasit: tunc enim tenebitur de dolo malo, non mandato. l. idem quaero §. si quis ea. 7. mandati. Nunquam ex consilio est actio mandati, sed de dolo. Malum consilium coercetur in maleficiis, propriis actionibus, vt actio ex ope consilioque datur in duplum. l. vlt. C. de noxal. actionibus. Est etiam actio serui corrupti l. 1. l. persuaderi. de seruo corrupt. Ait Praetor, teneri hac actione dupli eum, qui persuasit seruo alieno. Persuadere, est cogere sibi parere, illud certe plus est quam compellere, hoc est valde compellere. Sed inquit dict. l. 1. Persuadere est verbum commune. Nam suadet is & qui bonum consilium & qui malum dat. Ideoque Praetor adiicit, MALO CONSILIO. Posterior sententia legis iumpta est ex l. nam socii 20. pro soc. Species sumitur ex l. qui admittitur 19. eodem. Finge. Ego & tu sumus socii, ego admisi in societatem Titium; qui mihi tantum erit socius, non tibi, cum societas tantum contrahatur consensu, & cum, quem admisi ego, tu non admiseris; & dices: Socii mei socius, non est meus socius. Si ergo
units.tr: There are two opinions on this law. The first concerns the transaction of mandate, as is taught in l. 2, §. ult., mandati. A mandate is not contracted solely for your benefit. For example, if I order you to buy land with your money rather than lend it at interest, this is not a mandate but counsel, which indeed urges you to put the money to that use rather than another; you must judge whether the counsel is advantageous to you. Therefore no one is bound by counsel. Mandate is one thing, counsel another. From mandate there is an obligation; from counsel given in good faith there is none; from counsel given in bad faith there is an action for deceit. I commissioned my agent to follow the advice of Sempronius, who, being consulted, advised him to lend my money at interest. The agent followed this advice, and the matter turned out badly, for he invested it badly. Sempronius will not be liable unless he gave the advice by deceit; for then he will be liable for malicious deceit, not under the mandate. l. idem quaero, §. si quis ea, 7, mandati. There is never an action of mandate arising from counsel, but only for deceit. Malicious counsel is punished in crimes by specific actions, such that an action arising from aid and counsel is given for double the amount. l. ult., C. de noxal. actionibus. There is also the action on the corrupted slave: l. 1; l. persuaderi, de seruo corrupt. The Praetor says that he who has persuaded another's slave is liable to this action for double. To persuade is to compel another to obey oneself; this is certainly more than to compel, which is itself a great deal. But, says dict. l. 1., to persuade is a common word. For he persuades who gives good counsel as well as he who gives bad. Therefore the Praetor adds MALICIOUS COUNSEL. The latter opinion of this law is taken from l. nam socii, 20, pro soc. The case is taken from l. qui admittitur, 19, eodem. Suppose: I and you are partners; I have admitted Titius into partnership; he will be my partner but not yours, since partnership is contracted only by consent, and you did not admit the one whom I admitted. And you will say: My partner's partner is not my partner. If therefore

units.la: {y} ... habeam duos socios, cum mihi sint ambo socii, an ideo inter se censebuntur socii? Minime: fieri enim potest, vt ego cum iis contraxerim, ii tamen inter se non contraxerint. Cuiac.
units.tr: {y} ... I have two partners: since both are partners to me, are they therefore reckoned partners among themselves? No: for it can happen that I contracted with them, yet they did not contract among themselves. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 48. De calore iracundia, & de Diuortio.
units.tr: On Ad Leg. 48: On the heat of anger, and on divorce.

units.la: QVicquid calore iracundiæ vel fit vel dicitur, non prius ratum est, quam si perseuerantis apparet iudicium animi fuisse: ideoque breui reuersa vxor, nec diuortisse videtur.
units.tr: Whatever is done or said in the heat of anger is not valid until it is shown that the judgement of the mind was lasting; and so a wife who returns shortly afterwards is not thought to have divorced.

units.la: Extit. de dittort.
units.tr: Extat, de divortiis.

units.la: Diciuur in contractib. l. 9. ff. de publicanis: in voto, Dec. hic num. 3. in iuramento. l. 2. C. ad L. Iul. Maiestat. confessione, Decius hic, numero 4. at non in delictis. qua de re v. l. 5. C. de iniuriis.
units.tr: It is said of contracts, l. 9 ff. de publicanis: of a vow, Dec. hic num. 3. of an oath, l. 2 C. ad L. Iul. Maiestat. of a confession, Decius hic, number 4. but not of crimes. On this matter see l. 5 C. de iniuriis.

units.la: Perseuerantia perseuerantis Pac. animi perpetuitate l. 3. ff. de diuortiis: & merito. Nam ex perseuerantia animi deliberatio praesumitur l. 38. §. 6. ibi, & ideo abstinenti ff. de adulter.
units.tr: Perseverantia (of perseverans, Pac.) is by constancy of mind, l. 3 ff. de divortiis: and rightly so. For a deliberate intention is presumed from persistence of mind, l. 38 §6, where it reads "and therefore abstaining", ff. de adulter.

units.la: Breui v. l. 33. ff. de ritu.
units.tr: Breui, see l. 33 ff. de ritu.

units.la: Vxor id ampliatur ad fugitiuum & bannitum Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Uxor: this is extended to a fugitive and an outlawed person, Gothofr. hic.

units.la: Diuortium est, quod animi perpetuam dissensionem habet: quod fit calore iracundiæ, non est diuortium. Ex qua sententia multa sequuntur, vt l. quod si 31. de Iur. dot. hoc casu dotem non nouam censeri, sed eiusdem matrimonii monii manere: vel etiam vt donatio facta interim non valeat, sed vt confirmetur morte, vt omnes donationes inter virum & vxorem. Et vocatur iurgium, non diuortium. Hæc sententia pertinet etiam ad eum, qui inconsulto accusauit, vel peierauit per Principem. l. 2. ad L. Iul. maiest.
units.tr: Divorce is that which involves a lasting dissension of mind; what is done in the heat of anger is not divorce. From this opinion many consequences follow: as in l. quod si 31 de iure dotium, that in this case the dowry is not regarded as new but remains that of the same marriage; or also that a gift made in the meantime is not valid but is confirmed by death, as are all gifts between husband and wife. And it is called a quarrel, not a divorce. This opinion also applies to one who accused without consultation, or gave false testimony under oath before the Prince, l. 2 ad L. Iul. maiest.

units.la: Ad Leg. 49. De circumuentione.
units.tr: On Ad Leg. 49: On circumvention.

units.la: ALterius circumuentio, alteri non præbet actionem.
units.tr: Another's circumvention does not give an action to the other.

units.la: Ex tractatu de Tutelis.
units.tr: From the treatise on Guardianships.

units.la: Alterius ] puta serui l. 24. ff. de acquir. possess. procuratoris. l. 6. §. 2. ff. de condict. indeb.
units.tr: Of another: for example, of a slave, l. 24 ff. de acquir. possess.; of a procurator, l. 6. §. 2. ff. de condict. indeb.

units.la: Actionem ] & lucrum v. l. 206. h. t. leg. 3. §. 12. de peculio l. 14. ff. de condict. indeb. vel damnum v. l. 155. h. t.
units.tr: Actionem ] and gain, cf. law 206 of this title, law 3 §12 de peculio, law 14 de condictione indebiti; or loss, cf. law 155 of this title.

units.la: Ambigua est oratio. Nam verbum circumuentio hic ambiguum est: & ex inscriptione, certa interpretatio duci non potest. Bulg. & Accurs. ita deducunt. Tutor circumuenit eum, cum quo contrahebat nomine pupilli: hæc tutoris circumuentio non efficit, vt pupillus habeat actionem l. 4. §. illa etiam quaestio. 23. de dolo except. l. sed & 15. de dolo. Idem Bulgarus statuit in curatore & procuratore. Et quidem præbet Procurator domino non raro actionem, sed non ex dolo factam. Bona fides nobis sæpe parat actionem, dolus non parat. Si ministerium alterius bona fide intervenerit, saepe praebet actionem, dolus nunquam. Verum ex suo etiam dolo nemo sibi parat utilem actionem. Cur ergo ita de alterius dolo constituimus, cum de suo quisque dolo ita debeat constituere? Dolus meus non praebet mihi actionem. Nam si dolus intervenerit, non habeo actionem. l. & eleganter. 7. de dolo. ut ex alieno dolo, sic nec ex suo quis lucrari solet, l. ult. §. 3. de eo, per quem factum erit, &c. Aut, si praebet, inutilem praebet propter exceptionem doli mali? Qua de causa Ioanni potius assentior, qui circumventionem passive accipit. Dominus servum emit per procuratorem; deceptus est procurator, quia nesciebat esse morbosum? Dominus non est deceptus, sed deceptus est procurator. Quoties autem Procuratori competit actio redhibitoria: sane ex sua persona non competit, si sciens emit: nec ex domini persona, quia altero circumuento alter qui circumuentus non est, non habet actionem. Circumuento tamen domino habet actionem Procurator. l. cum mancipium §1. de aedilitio edicto. Recte ait, alii, vel alteri. Nam ei, qui circumuentus est, circumuentio praebet actionem: atque ita in hac significatione recte regula constituitur de alterius tantum dolo. Recte etiam Ioannes ad d. l. & eleganter. 4. de dolo, negat dolum mediatoris seu proxenetae, qui induxit contrahentes ad contrahendum, dantem causam contractui, vitiare contractum. Dolus contrahentium vitiat contractum; ut in specie d.l.& eleganter. Dolus serui, quo inductus dominus est, vt venderet eum bonae fidei emptori, non vitiat contractum: si dolo emptoris sit circumscriptus, vt venderet, non valet venditio. Proxeneta qui aliquid dolo facit, tenetur de dolo.l.2.de proxenet. Proxeneta igitur dolo non vitiatur contractus: nam cessaret actio de dolo, quae tum cessat, cum aliud est remedium seruandi sui. Cum ergo sit actio de dolo in proxeneta, apparet vtiliter contractum esse, nec obstat regula: Alterius circumuentio alteri non praebet actionem. Nam circumuentio hic actiue non capitur, sed passiue. In actiua significatione regula accipitur de eo, qui contrahit dolo malo, vt posuimus exemplum de curatore, procuratore, tutore. Proxeneta non contrahit, nec eius interuentu praebetur actio: quia non ipse negotiuni gerit. Itaque falsum est, quod vulgo existimant, contractum vitiari dolo proxenetae: sed est in eum actio de dolo, dict.l.2.
units.tr: The wording is ambiguous. For the word circumvention is ambiguous here, and a certain interpretation cannot be drawn from the title. Bulgarus and Accursius deduce it thus: a guardian circumvented the person with whom he was contracting in the name of the ward; this circumvention by the guardian does not give the ward an action (l. 4 §illa etiam quaestio, de dolo except.; l. sed & 15 de dolo). Bulgarus holds the same for a curator and a procurator. And indeed a procurator often gives an action to his principal, but not one arising from fraud. Good faith often secures an action for us; fraud does not. If another's service has intervened in good faith, it often gives an action; fraud never does. Yet no one gives himself a useful action by his own fraud. Why then do we lay down the rule as we do for another's fraud, when each ought to lay it down in the same way for his own fraud? My fraud gives me no action: for if fraud has intervened I have no action (l. & eleganter 7 de dolo). As one does not usually profit from another's fraud, so neither does one profit from one's own (l. ult. §3 de eo per quem factum erit, etc.). Or, if it does give an action, does it give a useless one on account of the exception of bad faith? For this reason I rather agree with John, who takes circumvention in the passive sense. A master buys a slave through a procurator; the procurator is deceived because he did not know the slave was diseased? The master is not deceived, but the procurator is. Whenever the procurator has the redhibitory action, certainly it does not belong to him in his own person if he buys knowingly; nor does it belong in the master's person, because when one party has been circumvented, the other, who was not circumvented, has no action. Yet when the master has been circumvented, the procurator has an action (l. cum mancipium §1 de aedilitio edicto). Others rightly say "of another or of the other". For circumvention gives an action to the one who has been circumvented; and so in this sense the rule is rightly laid down concerning another's fraud only. John also rightly denies, in ad d.l. & eleganter 4 de dolo, that the fraud of a broker or go-between, who induced the contracting parties to contract and so gave cause for the contract, vitiates the contract. The fraud of the contracting parties vitiates the contract, as in the case of the said l. & eleganter. The fraud of a slave, by which the master was induced to sell him to a buyer in good faith, does not vitiate the contract; if the master was circumvented by the buyer's fraud into selling, the sale is not valid. A broker who does something by fraud is bound by the action for fraud (l. 2 de proxenetis). Therefore the contract is not vitiated by the broker's fraud; for the action for fraud would cease, and it ceases when another remedy exists for protecting one's own interest. Since, then, there is an action for fraud against the broker, it appears that the contract is validly made, and the rule does not stand in the way: another's circumvention does not give an action to the other. For here circumvention is not taken actively but passively. In the active sense the rule concerns one who contracts with malicious fraud, as we have given the example of a curator, procurator, or tutor. The broker does not contract, nor is an action given through his intervention, because he does not himself conduct the business. Thus it is false what people commonly think, that the contract is vitiated by the broker's fraud; rather there is an action for fraud against him (dict. l. 2).

units.la: Ad Leg.50.Carere culpa.
units.tr: On Law 50. Being free from fault.

units.la: Culpa carer qui scit, sed prohibere non potest.
units.tr: He who knows, but cannot prevent, is free from fault.

units.la: Exstit. de Noxalib.
units.tr: From the title On Noxal Actions.

units.la: Qui scit] l. 109. h. t. l. 33. in sin. ff. locati. l. 1. §. 18. l. 3. ff. de Silaniano.
units.tr: He who knows] l. 109 h. t.; l. 33 in fin. ff. locati; l. 1 §. 18, l. 3 ff. de Silaniano.

units.la: Prohibere ] Proditionis species est, delictum futurum non detegere. Ideoque subditus qui consilia aduersus Principem inita non detexit, punitur l. 5. C. ad L. Iul. maiest.
units.tr: To prevent] Failing to disclose a future crime is a kind of treason. Therefore a subject who did not disclose plans formed against the Prince is punished, l. 5 C. ad L. Iul. maiest.

units.la: Non potest ]alias colonus l. 13. §. 7. ff. locati. seruus l. 1. §. 18. ff. de Silaniano: dominus l. 2. §. 1. ff. de noxalib. l. 6. ff. de iure patronatus: qui non prohibet cum prohibere posset, tenetur. Est enim specialis ac mutua inter huiusmodi personas connexio. An idem in aliis personis? quidam aiunt voluntatis ac officii magis esse quam necessitatis, alteri benefacere l. 17. §. 3. ff. commodati. Sic sentit Gothofr. hic. Hominis interesse hominem beneficio affici l. 7. in fi. ff. de seruis exportandis: ideoque cum iuste puniri, qui cum lacertis aut telo armatus, aggressorem facile poterat propulsare; & passus est inermem interfici. Seneca in Troade act. 2. Non patiar; in me culpa cunctorum redit. Qui non vetat peccare, cum possit, iubet.
units.tr: He cannot] In other cases the tenant (l. 13 §. 7 ff. locati), the slave (l. 1 §. 18 ff. de Silaniano), the master (l. 2 §. 1 ff. de noxalib.; l. 6 ff. de iure patronatus): one who does not prevent when he could prevent is liable. For there is a special and mutual connection between persons of this kind. Is the same true of other persons? Some say that doing good to another is a matter of will and duty rather than of necessity, l. 17 §. 3 ff. commodati. Gothofredus here agrees. It is in a man's interest that a man be helped by a benefit, l. 7 in fin. ff. de seruis exportandis; and so it is rightly punished when one who was armed with a club or a weapon could easily have warded off the attacker, and yet allowed an unarmed man to be killed. Seneca in Troades, act 2: "I will not allow it; the guilt of all returns upon me. He who does not forbid a sin when he can, commands it."

units.la: Si domino sciente seruus noxam committat; dominus tenetur in solidum suo nomine. Excusatur tamen, si dominus sciuerit; & non potuerit prohibere; quod demonstrat l. in omnibus 3. & l. in delictis 4. de noxal. actio. Interdum enim dominus non potest prohibere: vt, si seruus proclamat ad libertatem, vel domino trans flumen existente seruus aliquid faciat, quod prohibere non possit dominus cis flumen existens. Ad hanc speciem pertinet haec regula de noxalibus actionibus l. 9. Sed extendi potest ad alia multa, secundum l. saepe 63. de re indic. Quaeritur: an res inter alios iudicata aliis noceat? Nocet, si potuerit prohibere agentem; non nocet, si non potuerit prohibere. v. l. flaminum 24. §. quanquam. 6. de damn. infect. Species eius est. Quidam promisit damni infecti; opus factum est ab alio eo nesciente, non tenetur: at eo sciente tenetur, nisi non prohibere potuerit: nec cogitur promissor probare factum, quod prohibere non potuerit. Ex regulis ius non est constituendum. Pater, qui filium patitur bina sponsalia contrahere, vel ducere uxorem, quae nondum expleuit tempus luctus, notatur infamia: hoc ita, si patitur pater, hoc est, si non prohibuerit, cum prohibere potuit. Et generaliter, nullum patitur crimen, hoc est nullum crimen fert patienter, & tolerat is, qui non prohibet, cum prohibere non potest. Huc pertinet l. si quis seruo 20. C. de furt. Cuius species haec est. Seruus domino sciente nec contradicente, cum prohibere posset, suasu alterius fecit furtum? Dominus habebit furti & serui corrupti actionem aduersus eum, qui suasit. Et nullum crimen patitur, qui prohibuit, cum prohibere posset. Lege Cornelia de falsis & ille qui num mos adulterinos fecit, punitur, imo & qui non prohibuit confiari, cum prohibere posset. l.9.§.1. de leg. Cornel. de fals. Es Agellius l.7. inquit: Solent puniri, qui morituris auxilium non ferunt. Cuiac.
units.tr: If a slave commits a wrong with his master's knowledge, the master is liable in full on his own account. Yet he is excused if he knew but could not prevent it, as the law in omnibus 3 and the law in delictis 4 de noxal. actio show. For sometimes a master cannot prevent: for example, if a slave cries out for liberty, or if, while the master is across the river, the slave does something that the master, standing on this side of the river, cannot prevent. To this kind belongs the rule about noxal actions, l. 9. But it can be extended to many other cases, according to l. saepe 63 de re indic. The question is: does a thing judged between others harm those who were not parties? It harms if he could have prevented the plaintiff; it does not harm if he could not have prevented him. See l. flaminum 24 §. quanquam 6 de damn. infect. This is a species of it. Someone promised security against threatened damage; the work was done by another without his knowledge, and he is not bound; but if he knew of it he is bound, unless he could not prevent it. Nor is the promisor compelled to prove a deed that he could not prevent. Law should not be established from rules. A father who allows his son to contract two betrothals, or to take a wife who has not yet completed her mourning period, is marked with infamy; this holds if the father allows it, that is, if he does not prevent it when he could. And generally, one who allows a crime does not suffer it; that is, he who does not prevent what he cannot prevent bears and tolerates the crime. To this belongs l. si quis seruo 20 C. de furt. Its case is this: a slave, with his master's knowledge and without objection, when he could have prevented it, committed a theft at another's urging. The master will have an action for theft and for corrupting a slave against the one who urged it. And one who prevented a crime, when he could prevent it, does not suffer it. Under the Cornelian law on forgeries, one who made counterfeit seals is punished, indeed also one who did not prevent a forgery when he could. l. 9 §. 1 de leg. Cornel. de fals. Agellius, l. 7, says: those who do not bring help to the dying are usually punished. Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad Leg.51. Non capere.
units.tr: On Law 51. Not to acquire.

units.la: NOn videtur quisquam id capere, quod ei necesse est alii restituere.
units.tr: A person does not seem to acquire that which he is necessarily bound to restore to another.

units.la: Ex tit. de bon. possess. supr. in l.13. est explicata.
units.tr: Explained above in the title On Possession of Goods, in l. 13.

units.la: Restituere] v.2. Eclog.3. cap.52. l.49. ff. de donationib. int. vir. l.42. ff. de legat.2. l.16. §.15. ff. ad Trebellianum. l.3. §.4. ff. de legat. praestand. l.71. ff. de verb. signif. multo minus is cepisse videbitur, qui à re petenda exactione removetur l.13. ff. eod. Idem in eo qui tantum erogat, quantum accipit l.122. in f. ff. de legat.1. aut qui alii administrat l.10. in sin. ff. de inoff. aliud erit si ex longo interuallo quis cogatur restituere, & medio tempore vtilitatem perceperit. l.49. ff. de donat. int. vir. l.45. l.73. §.4. ff. ad L. Falcid. l.22. §.2. ff. ad Trebell. Gothof. hic.
units.tr: Restore] see Eclog. 3 cap. 52; l. 49 ff. de donationib. inter uirum et uxorem; l. 42 ff. de legatis 2; l. 16 §. 15 ff. ad Trebellianum; l. 3 §. 4 ff. de legatis praestandis; l. 71 ff. de verborum significatione. Much less does he seem to have acquired who is removed from the pursuit of the thing to be claimed, l. 13 ff. eod. The same holds for one who pays out just as much as he receives, l. 122 in fin. ff. de legatis 1; or for one who administers for another, l. 10 in sin. ff. de inoff. It will be otherwise if someone is compelled to restore after a long interval and in the meantime has enjoyed the profit: l. 49 ff. de donat. int. vir.; l. 45; l. 73 §. 4 ff. ad L. Falcid.; l. 22 §. 2 ff. ad Trebell. Gothofredus here.

units.la: Ad Leg.52. Non defendere.
units.tr: On Law 52. Not defending.

units.la: NOn defendere videtur, non tantum qui latitat, sed & is qui praesens negat se defendere, aut non vult suscipere actionem.
units.tr: A man is held to not defend himself not only if he lies hidden, but also if, present in court, he declares that he will not defend, or does not wish to take up the action.

units.la: latitare, negare defensionem, nolle suscipere actionem, paria sunt. Gothof. hic.
units.tr: To lie hidden, to deny a defence, and to be unwilling to take up an action are equivalent. Gothofredus, here.

units.la: defendere quid, v. l. 35. §. 3. ff. de procuratoribus. l. 21. in fi. ff. Ex quib. caus. maior.
units.tr: to defend something; see l. 35 §. 3 ff. de procuratoribus; l. 21 in fine ff. Ex quibus causis maior.

units.la: non tantum qui praesens negat s.d.a.n.u.s. actionem, sed & is qui latitat. Faber 1. semest. 23. & recte. Est enim a verioribus & confessis ad difficiliora progrediendum.
units.tr: Not only he who, present, denies that he will defend, or does not wish to undertake the action, but also he who lies hidden. Faber, 1. semest. 23. And rightly so. For one must proceed from what is more evident and admitted to what is more difficult.

units.la: Non recte defendit, qui latitat. v. l. 5. §. 3. ff. Quibus ex caus. in possess. Quid sit latitare v. l. 3. ff. de iudiciis. l. 1. l. 28. ff. de fideicom. libertat. l. 7. §. 4. ff. quibus ex caus. in poss.
units.tr: He does not rightly defend who lies hidden (latitat); see l. 5 §. 3 ff. Quibus ex causis in possessionem. On what it is to lie hidden (latitare), see l. 3 ff. de iudiciis; l. 1, l. 28 ff. de fideicommissariis libertatibus; l. 7 §. 4 ff. quibus ex causis in possessionem.

units.la: l. 11. §. 4. ff. de interrogat.
units.tr: l. 11. §. 4. ff. de interrogat.

units.la: Haec regula pertinet proprie ad actionem Fauianam; de qua in tit. si quid in fraud. patroni. Actione Fauiana revocatur, quod libertus alienavit in fraudem patroni. Paulianae locus est, si quis conventus rem suam non defendat. l. 3. Quae in fraud. creditor. Ex eadem causa Fauianae locus est, si libertus se non defendat. l. 1. §. quid si in lite 7. si quid in fraud. patr. Nunc dicamus, quando videatur rem non defendere. Primo non defendit, si latitat, hoc est, turpiter se occultat l. Fulcinius. quib. ex caus. in possess. eatur. Si quis igitur latitat, ille non defendit rem suam. Deinde non defendere etiam dicitur, qui praesens est in iudicio, & patitur se vinci, aut qui ultro se patitur damnari ex contumacia. Igitur libertus; qui rem suam non defendit, his modis, si data opera aliquid admisit, actione Fauiana restituitur patrono. Cuiac. in Recitat. posth.
units.tr: This rule belongs properly to the Fabian action, which is treated under the title si quid in fraud. patroni. By the Fabian action is recovered what a freedman has alienated to defraud his patron. The Pauline action applies if someone who is sued does not defend his own property; see l. 3. Quae in fraud. creditor. By the same reasoning the Fabian action applies if a freedman does not defend himself; see l. 1. §. quid si in lite 7. si quid in fraud. patr. Now let us say when a man seems not to defend his property. First, he does not defend if he lies hidden, that is, if he shamefully conceals himself; see l. Fulcinius, quib. ex caus. in possess. So whoever lies hidden does not defend his property. Next, a man is also said not to defend if, present in court, he allows himself to be defeated, or if out of obstinacy he allows himself to be condemned. Therefore a freedman who does not defend his property in these ways, if he has deliberately permitted something, is restored to the patron by the Fabian action. Cuiacius, in Recitationes posthumae.

units.la: Ad Leg. 53. De solutione indebiti.
units.tr: On Law 53. On the payment of what is not owed.

units.la: CVius per errorem dati repetitio est, eius consulto dati donatio est.
units.tr: That which is given through error is recoverable; that which is given deliberately is a gift.

units.la: Ex tit. si quid. in fraud. pat.
units.tr: From the title si quid in fraud. pat.

units.la: Consulto ] qui dat indebitum per errorem, repetit: qui consulto, donare intelligitur: ideoque non repetit l. 1. in f. ff. de condict. indeb. v. l. 9. C. de condict. indeb.
units.tr: Deliberately: one who gives what is not owed through error may recover it; one who gives deliberately is understood to make a gift, and therefore cannot recover it. See l. 1. in fin. ff. de condict. indeb.; see l. 9. C. de condict. indeb.

units.la: Donatio est] dummodo alieno nomine non detur. l. 19. §. 1. ff de condict. indeb.
units.tr: Is a gift: provided it is not given in another's name. l. 19. §. 1. ff. de condict. indeb.

units.la: Hæc quoque lex pertiner ad Fauianam actionem: idque constat ex l. tenetur, 5. si quid in fraud. patron. quæ est ex lib. 42. ad edict. quo tractauit Paulus de Fauiana actione hoc modo. Si libertus sciens indebitum soluerit, vt minueret bona patroni, actione Fauiana revocatur, & donasse videtur in l. qui fundum 9. §. seruus meus 2. pro emptore. Et ita in l. 6. si quid in fraud. patron. si libertus, cum frandare patronum vellet, filiofamilias contra Senatusconsultum pecuniam crediderit, non erit inhibenda actio Fauiana: quia libertus donasse magis in hunc casum intelligendus est in fraudem patroni: quam contra Senatusconsultum credidisse. Id verum est, si sciens hoc fecerit: si vel ro per errorem soluerit, tunc cessat Fauiana, & competit condictio indebiti. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: This law also pertains to the Fabian action, and this is established by l. tenetur, 5. si quid in fraud. patron., which is from book 42 on the edict, where Paulus treated the Fabian action in this way: if a freedman, knowing that something was not owed, paid it in order to diminish his patron's goods, he is recalled by the Fabian action and is considered to have given a gift; see l. qui fundum 9. §. seruus meus 2. pro emptore. And so in l. 6. si quid in fraud. patron.: if a freedman, wishing to defraud his patron, lent money to a son under power, contrary to the Senatusconsult, the Fabian action will not be refused, because in this case the freedman must be understood to have given in fraud of the patron rather than to have lent contrary to the Senatusconsult. This holds if he did so knowingly; if he paid through error, then the Fabian action ceases and the condiction of what is not owed applies. Cuiacius, in Recitationes.

units.la: Ad Leg. 54. De Iuris translatione.
units.tr: On Law 54. On the transfer of right.

units.la: NEmo plus iuris in alium transferre potest, quam ipse habet.
units.tr: No one can transfer to another more right than he himself has.

units.la: Ex tit. unde legit. Paci.
units.tr: From the title unde legit. Paci.

units.la: Nemo ]l. 120. h.t. 2. Eclog. 3. cap. 35. c. nemo. 79. de regul. in 6. v.l. 20. ff. de adquir. rer. dom. excipe procuratorem §. 42. 43. Inst. de rer. divis. tutorem, curatorem l. 22. C. de administr. tut. executorem iudicii §. vlt. Instit. de off. iud. malae fidei venditorem & creditorem (cui licet rem debitoris interdum alienare l. 46. ff. de adquir. rerum.) censitorem, flumen, imperatorem. vide Dynam ad d. cap. 49. adde tit. quibus alienare non licet. Instit.
units.tr: No one: l. 120. h.t.; Eclog. 3. cap. 35.; c. nemo, 79. de regul. in 6.; v. l. 20. ff. de adquir. rer. dom. Except a procurator (§§ 42, 43, Inst. de rer. divis.), a tutor or curator (l. 22. C. de administr. tut.), an executor of a judgment (§ ult. Instit. de off. iud.), a seller or creditor in bad faith (who may sometimes alienate a debtor's property; l. 46. ff. de adquir. rerum), a censor, a river, an emperor. See Dynamus on the said chapter 49; add the title quibus alienare non licet, Instit.

units.la: Plus iuris ] sed idem, puta idem dominium l. 11. §. 2. ff. de act. empt. eandem seruitutes, causas, iura: eadem onera & vitia l. 1. C. sine censu. Lex autem inquit plus iuris; l. nemo. 120. h.t. plus commodi. Nemo plus dat iuris, quam habet. l. 59. h.t. heres actionem habet, quam habuit defunctus, & pleniorem nonnunquam l. reperitur 84. ad L. Falcid. leg. si per imprudentiam 51. §. non mirum 3. de euictionibus. Eandem habet haeres. Sed aliquando plus venier, quam veniret viuo testatore; ob accidentia.
