Contumax est, qui prætori non respondet, & superbus est, qui alii non respondet. Eadem ratione in cessione in iure tacens negանti comparatur. Gaius 2. Instit. Est & alia differentia inter titulum de confessis, & titulum de interrog. in iure faciend. Nam ille pertinet ad eos, qui veluti conuenti incerti conditione fatentur se debere; qui conuenti actione Leg. Aquil. fatentur, se occidisse, vel vulnerasse; Qui conuenti rei vindicatione fatentur, rem suam non esse: Hic vero pertinet ad eos, qui fatentur; vt qui fatetur, se hæredem esse ex semisse; qua ex re actor cognoscit, se tantum agere pro semisse, & vero necesse est, vt actor de eo certioretur ne incidat in periculum plus petitionis, qua de causa interrogationes & responsiones in iis causis sunt necessariæ; Tacens est contumax, & habetur pro negante, & tenetur in solidum. Itaque hæc regula non pertinet ad tit. de interrogat. in iure faciend. sed ad tit de confessis. ex quo confessus habetur pro iudicato, sed si propalam sit confessus, non si tacuerit; Nam etsi habeatur pro confesso, qui mortem sibi conscivit, aut actori pretium dedit; tamen non habetur pro damnato. l. eius 29. de iure fisci. l. qui rei postulat. 3. de bon. eorum, qui ante sententiam. Alia quæstio est, an, qui tacet, consentire videatur? Idem non est tacere & consentire; In superiore quæstione taciturnitas, modo negationem, modo confessionem imitatur, & in tit. de interrogat. modo nullum consensum, modo neutrum. l. item quæritur. 13. §. vlt. locati. In hac autem quæstione consensum imitatur taciturnitas, in iis scil. causis, in quibus voluntas exquisita non requiritur. l. 3. & 4. sup. h. tit. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: This rule seems to belong to the Aquilian law. For although we sometimes say "to cause damage" in the sense of "to suffer" it, here it is understood as "to inflict." l. 30. ad leg. Aquiliam. Now he seems to cause damage, that is, to inflict it, who does what he has no right to do: for example, if a magistrate has used more force than necessary against a man defending himself more fiercely, or if a man has killed a wife who was caught in adultery, he is not liable under the Aquilian law. And this is most evident in the Aquilian law, since the words "against right" are added. And although the action under the Aquilian law is for injury by damage done, the rule properly belongs, like the previous one, to the interdict ne quid in loco publico. Cuia. in Recit. hic. Interrogations are put to those who, when questioned by the praetor or by an opponent, under pressure from the praetor, are compelled to answer. These, by their own admission or by a lie, are liable to the interrogatory action. If they confess, it is clear they are liable; if they deny falsely, they bear this penalty of lying, so that they are liable for the whole amount. l. de aetate 11. §. si cum esset 2. l. si seruus 16. de interrogat. in iur. faciend. What shall we say if, when questioned by the praetor, he keeps silent? Here too he is liable for the whole amount, as one in contempt; for whoever does not answer is in contempt, that is, he scorns the authority of the praetor, and so he bears the penalty of contumacy, just as if he had denied it. d. l. de aetate. §. qui tacuit 4. & §. nihil interest 6. d. tit. l. non solum 39. de procurator. He who does not answer the praetor is contumacious, and he who does not answer another is proud. For the same reason, in surrender in court, silence is equated with denial. Gaius, 2. Instit. There is also another difference between the title de confessis and the title de interrog. in iure faciend. For the former concerns those who, as if sued on an uncertain condition, admit that they owe; those who, when sued under the Aquilian law, admit that they killed or wounded; those who, when sued by a claim of ownership, admit that the thing is not theirs. The latter, however, concerns those who admit a fact, as one who admits that he is heir to a half share; from this admission the plaintiff learns that he is suing only for the half, and it is necessary that the plaintiff be informed of this, lest he fall into the danger of claiming too much. For this reason, questions and answers are necessary in such cases. The silent person is contumacious and is held to be denying, and is liable for the whole amount. Therefore this rule does not belong to the title de interrog. in iure faciend. but to the title de confessis, by which one who has confessed is held as already judged; but this holds if he has confessed openly, not if he has kept silent. For although one who has taken his own life, or paid money to the plaintiff, is held to have confessed, he is not held to be condemned. l. eius 29. de iure fisci. l. qui rei postulat. 3. de bon. eorum, qui ante sententiam. Another question is whether one who keeps silent seems to consent. To be silent and to consent are not the same thing. In the previous question, silence imitates now denial, now confession, and in the title de interrogat. now no consent, now neither. l. item quæritur. 13. §. vlt. locati. But in this question silence imitates consent, namely in those cases in which an express will is not required. l. 3. & 4. sup. h. tit. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 143. De contrahentibus & eo- rum successoribus.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 143. On Contracting Parties and Their Successors.

units.la: QVod ipsis, qui contraxerunt, obstat, & successoribus eorum obstabit.
units.tr: What stands in the way of those who themselves contracted will also stand in the way of their successors.

units.la: Successoribus] l. 52. §. 1. sup. de pact. l. 37. sup. de acquir. hared. hinc illa regula, Resoluto iure dantis, resoluitur ius accipientis & habentis ab eo causam. v. l. 2. C. pignus pignori. adde l. 160. in sin. inf. eod. Gothof. Explicationem huius legis vide sup. in l. 54. vbi dixi. Cuiac.
units.tr: Successors] l. 52. §. 1. sup. de pact. l. 37. sup. de acquir. hared. Hence that rule: when the right of the giver is dissolved, the right of the receiver and of one who holds through him is dissolved. See l. 2. C. pignus pignori. Add l. 160. in sin. inf. eod. Gothofredus. For an explanation of this law, see above at l. 54., where I spoke of it. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 144. De licito & honesto: De tempore in stipulationibus spectando.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 144. Concerning the lawful and the honourable: concerning the time to be regarded in stipulations.

units.la: Non omne, quod licet, honestum est.
units.tr: Not everything that is permitted is honourable.

units.la: §. In stipulationibus id tempus spectatur, quo contrahimus.
units.tr: In stipulations the time is regarded at which we contract.

units.la: Non] Coniunge L. si filiusfam. 68. de verb. obligat. Pac.
units.tr: Not: compare law 68, "si filiusfamilias", de verborum obligationibus. Pac.

units.la: Omne] l. 197. 2. Eccl. 3. c. 140. Exemplum vide in l. 14. §. 2. sup. de ritu. Goth.
units.tr: Everything: law 197; 2 Eccl. 3, c. 140. See an example in law 14, §2, above, de ritu nuptiarum. Gothofredus.

units.la: Licet] i. impunitum legibus: Cum Iulia Nouerca Bassiani ei sinum nudasset, vellem, inquit, si liceret, at illa, si libet licet, an nescis Imperatorem leges dare, non accipere.
units.tr: Permitted: that is, not forbidden by the laws. When Julia Noverca had exposed her breast to Bassianus, he said, "I would, if it were permitted." But she replied: "If you wish, it is permitted. Or do you not know that the Emperor makes laws, not that he accepts them?"

units.la: Honestum] Exemp. vide in l. 27. in sin. sup. de hæred. petit. l. 1. in sin. sup. de periculo. tanta est honesti ratio; hinc turpis persona, vide l. 27. sup. de inofficioso. Conditio. l. 112. §. 3. sup. de legat. 1. l. 63. §. 7. sup. ad Trebell. Vita. l. 43. §. 5. sup. de ritu. arbiter. l. 9. §. 3. sup. de arbitr. turpiter datum, sup. de condict. ob turp. Gothof.
units.tr: Honourable: examples see law 27, at the end, above, de hereditatis petitione; law 1, at the end, above, de periculo. So great is the reason of honour. Hence a person of disgraceful character: see law 27, above, de inofficioso testamento; law 112, §3, above, de legatis 1; law 63, §7, above, ad Trebellianum; the life of ... ; law 43, §5, above, de receptis arbitris; law 9, §3, above, de arbitris; what is given dishonourably, above, de condictione ob turpem causam. Gothofredus.

units.la: Est] Vel vtile πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ' οὐ πάντα συμφέρει· πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ' οὐ πάντα οἰκοδομεῖ. I. Corint. 10. 10. vers.23. & cap.6. vers.12. & Siracus cap.37: vers.31. οὐ γὰρ πὰντα πᾶσι συμφέρει, ἡ οὐ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐν παντὶ δοκιμεῖ. Goth.
units.tr: Is: or "useful". "All things are lawful for me, but not all things are expedient; all things are lawful for me, but not all things edify" [πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ' οὐ πάντα συμφέρει· πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ' οὐ πάντα οἰκοδομεῖ] (1 Cor. 10.23; and ch. 6, v. 12). And Sirach ch. 37, v. 31: "For not everything suits everyone, nor is every soul approved in everything" [οὐ γὰρ πάντα πᾶσι συμφέρει, ἢ οὐ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐν παντὶ δοκιμεῖ]. Gothofredus.

units.la: Stipulationibus ] l.18.sup.eod.vide l.78.in sin. sup.de verb.ob. Licet habere concubinam, sed non honestum est, L probrum 41. de ritu nupt. licet dare meretrici, sed non honestum est. l.4. §.1.de condict. ob turp.caus. hæc non prohibentur ob solam causam honestatis. Quædam tamen sunt, quæ prohibentur ob solam honestatis rationem; eo referenda est regula; Non omne, quod licet, honestum est: hoc est, non non omne, quod licet, est permittendum. Nam in nuptiis naturale ius & pudor spectatur, non ciuile ius leg. adoptiuus 14. §. 2. de ritu nupt. Boni mores, non leges: quod honestum est, non quod licet. l.197. inf. hoc tit. semper in coniunctionibus, hoc est in nuptiis. Post diuortium ab vxore ex alio suscepta filiam mihi ducere licet, sed non est honestum. Ergo ab eiusmodi nuptiis abstinendum est. §. si vxor. Instit. de nuptiis. Male Bulgarus: licere contrahentibus se inuicem decipere, non tamen decere. Nam honestum est cum dicatur, licere naturaliter. Litem si pretio 22. §. vlt. & l. seq. locati. Vendere licet pluris, si possum, Bulgarus tamen non debuit dicere, decipere; nam significat dolum, sed circumuenire, circumscribere, quo significatur fraus, quæ est in re ipsa;
units.tr: It is permitted to keep a concubine, but it is not honourable: law "probrum" 41, de ritu nuptiarum. It is permitted to give to a prostitute, but it is not honourable: law 4, §1, de condictione ob turpem causam. These things are not prohibited on the ground of honesty alone. Some things, however, are prohibited on the ground of honesty alone, and to these belongs the rule: Not everything that is permitted is honourable; that is, not everything that is permitted is to be allowed. For in marriages natural law and modesty are considered, not civil law: law "adoptivus" 14, §2, de ritu nuptiarum. Good morals, not laws: what is honourable, not what is permitted. Law 197, below in this title: always in connections, that is, in marriages. After divorce from a wife, I may marry the daughter I had by another wife, but it is not honourable. Therefore one must abstain from such marriages: §"si uxor", Institutes, de nuptiis. Bulgarus is wrong: it is lawful for contracting parties to deceive one another, but not seemly. For "honestum" is said of what is lawful by nature. Law "Litem si pretio" 22, §last, and the following law, locati. It is lawful to sell for more, if I can; but Bulgarus ought not to have said "decipere", for that signifies deceit, whereas "circumvenire" and "circumscribere" signify fraud, which lies in the thing itself;

units.la: Ad tit. Digest. de diuers. Reg. Iur.
units.tr: On the title of the Digest, "On Various Rules of Law"

units.la: Dolus debet abesse in contractu: non licet mihi dolo te inducere, vt mihi vendas minoris, sed detracto dolo, possunt se circumscribere contrahentes. Redeamus ad nuptias: licet ducere consobrinam, vel defunctæ vxoris sororem, honestum tamen non est. Ergo inhibendum, sic pleraque, quæ iure ciuili licent, iure Prætorio emendantur, quasi minus honesta, vt licet rem meam vendere, etiamsi fraudentur creditores: & tamen rescinditur venditio iure Prætorio. Licet vsucapere rem absentis metus causa, & vero res mea fit vsucapione: rescinditur tamen vsucapio ex iure Prætorio, ex tit. quib. ex caus. maior.
units.tr: Fraud must be absent from a contract: I may not induce you by fraud to sell to me at a lower price, but once the fraud is removed, contracting parties may overreach one another. To return to marriage: it is permitted to marry a first cousin, or the sister of a deceased wife, yet it is not honourable. Therefore it must be restrained. In this way many things that are permitted by civil law are corrected by praetorian law, as being less honourable. For example, I may sell my own property even if my creditors are defrauded, and yet the sale is rescinded by praetorian law. I may acquire by usucapion the property of an absent man out of fear, and the thing truly becomes mine by usucapion; yet the usucapion is rescinded by praetorian law, from the title "quibus ex causis maior".

units.la: Ad §. In stipulationibus, &c.
units.tr: On the paragraph "In stipulations", etc.

units.la: Quæ ad hunc §. spectant tradita sunt sup. in l. 13. & l. 115. Cui. in Recit.
units.tr: What pertains to this paragraph has been handed down above, in law 13 and law 115. Cuiacius, in Recitations.

units.la: Ad Leg. 145. An quis fraudari dicatur.
units.tr: On Law 145: whether someone is said to be defrauded.

units.la: Nemo videtur fraudare eos, qui sciunt & consentiunt.
units.tr: No one is thought to defraud those who know and consent.

units.la: Nemo ]Ex tit. qua in fraud. Creditorum.
units.tr: No one] From the title qua in fraud. creditorum.

units.la: Sciunt ]c. scienti & consentienti 27. de reg. in 6. 2. ecl. 3. c. 41. l. 1. in sin. sup. de act. empt. l. 24. §. 9. sup. de ædilitio. l. 1. §. 3. sup. depositi l. 1. in sin. supr. quod falso tutore: & hæc quidem locum habere existiexistimo, in sciente simul, & consentiente. Gothofr.
units.tr: Knowing] c. scienti & consentienti 27. de reg. in 6. 2. ecl. 3. c. 41. l. 1. in sin. sup. de act. empt. l. 24. §. 9. sup. de aedilitio. l. 1. §. 3. sup. depositi l. 1. in sin. supr. quod falso tutore: and I think this rule holds good where a person both knows and consents at the same time. Gothofredus.

units.la: Consentiunt] l. ii. sup. si quid in fraud. patroni. & volunt l. ii. in sin. sup. de in ius vocando l. i. § 5. sup. de iniuriis. l. 8. § 5. sup. de aqua pluu. l. 3. § 5. sup. de homine libero, voluisse intelligitur, qui aduersus se aliquid scripsit. leg. 8. § 6. supr. eod. Gothofr.
units.tr: Consent] l. 2 sup. si quid in fraud. patroni. & volunt l. 2 in sin. sup. de in ius vocando l. 1 § 5 sup. de iniuriis. l. 8 § 5 sup. de aqua pluv. l. 3 § 5 sup. de homine libero: he is understood to have willed a thing who has written something against himself. Law 8, § 6, supra, same title. Gothofredus.

units.la: Pertinet ad actionem Paulianam, & est repetita ex leg. 6. § praterea, quae in fraud. cred. & locum habetur in actionibus, Pauliana, Fabiana, & Calusiana. Si quid libertus gesserit consentiente patrono, non est satis, scire, sed consentire est necesse. leg. non videtur si quid in fraud. patroni. leg. 9. de aq. pluu. arc. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: It pertains to the Pauline action, and is repeated from law 6, § praeterea, quae in fraud. cred., and it holds in the Pauline, Fabian and Calusian actions. If a freedman has done something with the consent of his patron, it is not enough that the patron knew; consent is necessary. Law "non videtur si quid in fraud. patroni", law 9 de aqua pluv. arc. Cuiacius, in Recitations.

units.la: Ad Leg. 146. De eo quod quis egit ante libertatem.
units.tr: On Law 146: concerning what someone did before his liberty.

units.la: QVod quis, dum seruus est, egit, proficere libero facto non potest.
units.tr: What a man did while he was a slave cannot benefit him once he has become free.

units.la: Proficere] l. 98. § vlt. de solut. Et nocere vide leg. 1. & passim tit. Codicis an seruus ex suo facto. Gothofr.
units.tr: To benefit] law 98, last §, de solutionibus. And for "to harm", see law 1, and passim, title of the Code, whether a slave is bound by his own act. Gothofredus.

units.la: Ait proficere; addatur, vel nocere, quod seruus egit in seruitute, id post libertatem neque prodest ei, neque nocet, ut si seruus ante conditionem libertatis existens, pactus sit cum creditoribus hæreditariis, pactum non prodest; ideo non datur exceptio pacti, sed doli, l. Iurisgent. 7. §. penult. de pact. Eadem regula constituitur in filiofamilias. Nam quod ante manumissionem egit, nihil prodest, vel nocet. Verbum egit refertur ad contractum & pactum. Nam ex delicto in seruitute commisso seruus tenetur. Sed de hac regula & eius vitiis est tit. Cod. an seruus post manumiss. pro suo facto teneatur. Cuia. in Recit.
units.tr: He says "to benefit"; let "or to harm" be added. What a slave did while in slavery neither benefits nor harms him after liberty. For example, if a slave, while still before the condition of liberty, made a pact with the creditors of an inheritance, the pact does not benefit him; therefore no exception of pact is given to him, but only an exception of fraud, law "Jus gentium" 7, penultimate §, de pactis. The same rule is laid down for a son under paternal power. For what he did before manumission neither benefits nor harms him. The word "did" refers to contract and pact, for a slave is bound for a delict committed in slavery. But on this rule and its defects there is a title Code, whether a slave after manumission is bound for his own act. Cuiacius, in Recitations.

units.la: Ad Leg. 147. De generalibus & specialibus.
units.tr: On Law 147: on general and special things.

units.la: SEmper specialia generalibus insunt. Specialia] v. l. 80. l. 113. sup. eod. 2. ecl. 3. cap. 141. species inest suo generi, inest, id est, comprehenditur c. generi per speciem derogatur 34. de reg. in 6. Goth.
units.tr: Special things are always contained in general ones. Special things] see law 80, law 113, above, same title; Eclogues 2, 3, ch. 141. A species is contained in its genus; it is included, that is, comprehended. Ch. "the general is derogated by the special", 34, de reg. in 6. Gothofredus.

units.la: Vide sup. in l. 110. vbi tractatum est quod huc pertinet. Cuiac.
units.tr: See above, on law 110, where what pertains here is treated. Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad Leg. 148. De eo, cuius effectus omnibus prodest.
units.tr: On Law 148: concerning that whose effect benefits all.

units.la: CVius effectus omnibus prodest, eius & partes ad vniuersos pertinent.
units.tr: Whose effect benefits all, its parts also pertain to all.

units.la: Cuius ] ex tit. de reb. auth. iud. possid.
units.tr: Whose] from the title de reb. auth. iud. possid.

units.la: Eius ] Qui omnibus prospicit, nullos excipit, hinc, qui totum restituere tenetur vindicanti, nullam partem retinere debet. adde l.67. sup. de rei vind. Qui totum alienat, nullam partem retinet. l.25. sup. de usur. Qui omnes servos legat, nullum excipit. 152. sup. de leg. Goth.
units.tr: Its] He who provides for all excepts none; hence, one who is bound to restore the whole to the claimant ought to retain no part. Add law 67, above, de rei vindicatione. He who alienates the whole retains no part. Law 25, above, de usuris. He who bequeaths all his slaves excepts none. 152, above, de legatis. Gothofredus.

units.la: Pertinent ] Hinc colligunt, idem ius esse in parte quod in toto arg. l.82. supr. de acq. hared. cuius reg. 4. except. vid. hic apud Dec. Nihil eorum quæ tradunt Interpretes, conuenit huic regulæ : Nos vtamur hoc exemplo, vno creditore misso in possessionem rei seruandæ causa, vel possidere iussu, eius rei effectus omnibus prodest. Nam missio possessionis fit in rem, non in personam, & possidere iussus, possidet omnibus. l.is qui §. si plures. vt in possess. leg. caus. leg. cum vnus 12. de rebus aut. ind. possid. Creditor fructus restituere debet l. Prator 9. §. his verbis 3. l. creditor 14. d. tit. Cum igitur effectus rei eius prosit omnibus, impensæ etiam pertinent ad omnes: hoc est, si vnus missus sit, & impenderit necessaria, vt si fulcierit ædificia, ad omnes pertinet, quia commune negocium gessit. d.l. Prator 9. §. generaliter, 4. d. tit. cuius rei pars est, vt communiter omnia onera sustineant. Cui. in Recit.
units.tr: Pertain] Hence they infer that the same law holds for a part as for the whole: arg. law 82, above, de acquirenda hereditate; rule 4, exception; see here Dec. None of what the interpreters hand down agrees with this rule. We use this example: when one creditor is sent into possession to preserve a thing, or is ordered to possess it, the effect of that thing benefits all. For the sending into possession is made in rem, not in personam, and one who is ordered to possess, possesses for all. Law "is qui" § "si plures", ut in possessionem; law "causa"; law "cum unus" 12, de rebus auctoritate iudicis possidendis. A creditor must restore the fruits: law "Praetor" 9, § "his verbis" 3; law "creditor" 14, same title. Therefore, since the effect of the thing benefits all, expenses too pertain to all: that is, if one creditor who was sent into possession spent what was necessary, such as shoring up the buildings, it pertains to all, because he managed a common business. Law "Praetor" 9, § "generaliter" 4, same title, of which it is a part that all together bear all the burdens. Cuiacius, in Recitations.

units.la: Ad Leg.149. De lucro ex persona alterius.
units.tr: On Law 149. On gain from another's person.

units.la: EX qua persona quis lucrum capit, eius factum præstare debet.
units.tr: He from whose person someone takes gain ought to make good that person's act.

units.la: Lucrum ]
units.tr: Gain ]

units.la: Debet ] Excipe donatarios,
units.tr: Ought ] Make an exception for donees.

units.la: Eadem est sententia huius legis, quae superioris. Factum scilicet defuncti Vt si defunctus rem haeredis pignori obligauerit, id pignus tanquam alienum non valet, sed cum dominus rei haeres extiterit, ratum habere debet. Aliud exemplum peti potest ex lege si non solum 10. si quis omiss. caus. est. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: The meaning of this law is the same as that of the preceding one: the act of the deceased. For example, if the deceased had pledged an heir's property as security, that pledge is not valid as the property of another, but once the owner of the thing has become heir, he ought to ratify it. Another example can be sought from the law beginning "If not only," 10, "si quis omiss. caus." Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 150. De eo qui possidet, vel habet, aut dolo desiit possidere, vel habere.
units.tr: On Law 150. On one who possesses or holds, or by fraud has ceased to possess or hold.

units.la: PArem esse conditionem oportet eius, qui quid possideat, vel habeat: atque eius, cuius dolo malo factum sit, quo minus possideret vel haberet.
units.tr: The condition of the one who possesses or holds something ought to be equal to that of the one by whose wicked fraud it came about that he did not possess or hold.

units.la: Parem ] Ex tractatu interdictorum.
units.tr: Equal ] From the treatise on interdicts.

units.la: Cuius dolo malo ] vid. l. 131. sup. eod. l. 2. §. 42. sup. ne quid in loco publico.
units.tr: By whose wicked fraud ] See law 131 above, under the same title; law 2 §. 42 above, on "ne quid in loco publico."

units.la: Hæc lex iam explicata est supra l. 131 Cuiac. Ad Leg. 151. De damno.
units.tr: This law has already been explained above, on law 131. Cuiac. On Law 151. On damage.

units.la: NEmo damnum facit, nisi qui id fecit, quod facere ius non habet.
units.tr: No one causes damage except one who does what he has no right to do.

units.la: Ex rit. ne quid in loco publico, vbi mentio fit damni.
units.tr: From the title "ne quid in loco publico," where mention is made of damage.

units.la: Quod facere ius non habet ] Damnum dare est iniuriam facere. l. 1. §. 10. 11. sup. ne quid in loco publico. vi facit, qui facit iniuriam. l. 73. §. 2. sup. eod. vim non facit, qui suo iure vtitur. l. 155. inf. eod. qui iniuria quid facit, punitur: è contra, factum legitime, poenam non meretur. l. 6. C. de adulteriis. vid. Goth.
units.tr: What he has no right to do ] To cause damage is to do an injury: law 1 §§. 10, 11 above, ne quid in loco publico. He uses force who does an injury (law 73 §2 above, same title). He does not use force who uses his own right (law 155 below, same title). Whoever does something wrongly is punished; on the contrary, what is done lawfully does not deserve punishment (law 6 C. de adulteriis). See Gothofred.

units.la: Pertinere videtur haec regula ad legem Aquiliam. Nam etsi damnum facere dicamus aliquando pro pati, tamen hoc loco dare intelligitur. l. 30. ad leg. Aquiliam. Is porro videtur damnum facere, hoc est dare, qui id facit, quod facere ius non habet: vt si quid violentius secerit magistratus aduersus se defendentem acrius: vel qui suam attrectantem vxorem occiderit, non tenetur l. Aquilia: Et hoc in l. Aquilia est euidentissimum: cum sit additum, contra ius. Et cum actio legis Aquiliae sit iniuria damni dati, proprie tamen, sicut superior regula, pertinet ad interdictum, ne quid in loco publico.
units.tr: This rule seems to pertain to the Lex Aquilia. For although we sometimes say "to cause damage" for "to suffer damage," here it is understood as "to inflict" (law 30, ad leg. Aquiliam). Moreover, he seems to cause damage, that is, to inflict it, who does what he has no right to do: for example, if a magistrate has used more violence against a man defending himself more fiercely; or one who kills his wife while she is in an illicit embrace is not liable under the Lex Aquilia. And this is most evident in the Lex Aquilia, since the words "against right" were added. And although the action under the Lex Aquilia is for injury from damage done, the rule, like the preceding one, properly pertains to the interdict "ne quid in loco publico."

units.la: Cuia. in Recit. hic.
units.tr: Cuiac. in Recit. here.

units.la: Ad Leg. 152. De mandato. De ratihabitione. De hærede.
units.tr: On Law 152. On mandate. On ratification. On the heir.

units.la: HOciure vtimur, vt quidquid omnino per vim fiat, aut in vis publicæ, aut priuatæ crimen incidat. §. 1. Deiicit & qui mandat §. 2. In mal eficio ratihabitio mandato comparatur; - §. 3. In contractibus, quibus doli præstatio vel bona fides inest, hæres in solidum tenetur.
units.tr: We use this rule: whatever is done at all by force falls under the crime either of public or of private violence (§1). He who orders an ejection is also liable (§2). In wrongdoing, ratification is compared to mandate (§2). In contracts that carry good faith or liability for fraud, the heir is bound for the whole (§3).

units.la: Tora hæc lex pertinet ad interdictum, unde vi. Ne quid vi fiat, non tantum prospicitur interdicto, quo coercetur vis publica & priuata, vis armata & non armata: sed etiam corrigitur & prospicitur legibus Iuliis de vi publica & priuata l. 1. §. ne quid. de vi & vi arm. & ex legibus Iuliis priuatorum & publicorum iudiciorum l. si preces. 32. de pœnis.
units.tr: This law pertains to the interdict "unde vi" (on forcible ejection). It is provided not only by the interdict by which public and private force is restrained, armed and unarmed, but is also corrected and provided for by the Julian laws on public and private violence (law 1 §. "ne quid de vi" and "de vi armata"), and by the Julian laws on private and public judgments (law "si preces" 32, de poenis).

units.la: Ad §. 1. Deiicit.
units.tr: On §1. He who ejects.

units.la: Ille §. pertinet ad interdictum unde vi. de quo sup. in l. 60. Hic vero explicatus est in l. 34. & in l. 38. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: That §. pertains to the interdict "unde vi," on which see above in law 60. Here, however, it has been explained in law 34 and law 38. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 153. De obligatione & liberatione. De adquisitione & amissione. De possessione.
units.tr: On Law 153. On obligation and liberation. On acquisition and loss. On possession.

units.la: Fere quibuscunque modis obligamur, iisdem in contrarium actis liberamur, cum quibus modis acquirimus, iisdem in contrarium actis, amittimus. Ut igitur nulla possessio adquiri, nisi animo & corpore poterit: ita nulla amittitur, nisi in qua utrumque sit in contrarium actum.
units.tr: We are bound by almost whatever modes, and freed by the same modes acted to the contrary; as we acquire by certain modes, so by the same modes acted to the contrary we lose. Therefore, just as no possession can be acquired except with mind and body, so none is lost unless both are acted against.

units.la: Fere] Cur haec particula fere, seu quidem addita est? ut intelligas possessionem non iisdem semper modis amitti, quibus adquiritur: facilius enim amittitur, quam adquiritur. Corpus requiritur in adquirenda; at solus animus sufficit in amittenda. l. 3. §. 6. supr. de adquir. possess. vid. Scholion apud Harm. 2. tit. 1. Gothofred. hic.
units.tr: Almost ] Why was the particle "almost," or "indeed," added? So that you understand possession is not always lost by the same modes by which it is acquired: for it is lost more easily than it is acquired. Body is required in acquiring, but mind alone suffices in losing. Law 3 §6 above, de adquirenda possessione; see the scholion in Harm. 2 tit. 1; Gothofred here.

units.la: Quibuscunque modis] l. 35. l. 100. sup. eod. l. 8. sup. de adquir. possess. l. 80. sup. de solutio.
units.tr: By whatever modes ] Law 35, law 100 above, same title; law 8 above, de adquirenda possessione; law 80 above, de solutionibus.

units.la: Utrumque in contrarium] Imo solo animo possessio amitti potest. l. 3. §. 6. sup. de adquir. possess. vtique si animo eam amittere incipimus; secus si corpore. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Acted to the contrary, both ] Indeed, possession can be lost by mind alone (law 3 §6 above, de adquirenda possessione), certainly if we begin to lose it by the mind; otherwise by the body. Gothofred here.

units.la: Vide quæ dicta sunt in l. 35. quæ huic plane consonat. Cuiac.
units.tr: See what has been said on law 35, which plainly agrees with this. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 154. De petitore & possessore.
units.tr: On Law 154: On the plaintiff and the possessor.

units.la: De dolo & pæna.
units.tr: On fraud and penalty.

units.la: CVm par delictum est duorum, semper oneratur petitor, & melior habetur possessoris causa: sicut fit, cum de dolo excipitur petitoris, neque enim datur talis replicatio petitori, Aut si (NON) rei quoque in ea re dolo actum sit. §. 1. Illi debet permitti pœnam petere, qui in ipsam non incidit.
units.tr: When the wrong is equal on both sides, the plaintiff is always burdened and the possessor's cause is held to be the better one. This happens, for example, when the plaintiff is met with a plea of fraud, since no such replication is granted to the plaintiff: Or if (not) an action for fraud was also brought against the defendant in that matter. §1. The one who did not fall into the penalty ought to be allowed to demand it.

units.la: Replicatio] l. 4. §. 13. sup. de dolo mali, &c.
units.tr: Replication: law 4, §13, above, on the wrong of fraud, etc.

units.la: Aut si] si non rei.
units.tr: Or if: if not of the defendant.

units.la: Rei] hinc constat, non audiri replicationem actoris dolosi, aduersus reum dolosum excipientem.
units.tr: Of the defendant: hence it is clear that the replication of a fraudulent plaintiff is not heard against a fraudulent defendant who pleads an exception.

units.la: Qui
units.tr: Who

units.la: Non incidit] Cur ita? nemini datur actio, nisi ex honesta causa l.76. in sin. sup. de furt. Goth.
units.tr: Did not fall: Why so? No action is given except from an honourable cause, law 76, at the end, above, on theft. Gothofredus.

units.la: Initio ostenditur in pari delicto meliorem esse causam possessoris; qua de re tractatur in l.33. sup. sicut in pari causa lucri, melior est causa possessoris: sic in pari causa damni adversus doli exceptionem non datur alia replicatio. l. apud Celsum 4. §. Marcellus. 13. de doli except. Dolus vero debet actori nocere, non reo. Communis dolus nocet magis actori, quam reo. l. si seruum 91. §. sequitur. 3. de verb. oblig. Qua de causa & dolo non agit, qui & ipse in eadem re dolum facit; sed dolus cum dolo compensatur. l. si duo. 36. de dolo. Et similiter de poena non agit, qui & ipse in poenam incidit, hoc est, quod dicitur in hac lege: Illi debet permitti, poenam petere, qui in ipsam non incidit: Recte. Ut si actor & reus mutuo stipulati sunt poenam iudicii sistendi causa, si neuter sistat, neuter aget ex stipulatu de poena: nam vtrque incidit in poenam. Similiter dicimus in l. si uxor. 13. §. index 5. ad l. Iul. de adult. virum ab uxore iure pudicitiam non exigere, nisi & ipse exhibeat.
units.tr: At the outset it is shown that, where the wrong is equal, the possessor's cause is the better one. This is treated in law 33, above, where, as in an equal cause of gain the possessor's cause is better, so in an equal cause of loss no other replication is granted against the plea of fraud. Law "apud Celsum" 4, §Marcellus, 13, on the exception of fraud. Fraud ought to harm the plaintiff, not the defendant. Mutual fraud harms the plaintiff more than the defendant: law "si servum" 91, §sequitur, 3, on verbal obligations. For this reason, one who is himself guilty of fraud in the same matter does not sue for fraud either; the fraud is set off against fraud: law "si duo" 36, on fraud. Likewise, one who has himself incurred the penalty does not sue for the penalty. This is what is said in this law: the one who did not fall into the penalty ought to be allowed to demand it. Rightly so. For example, if plaintiff and defendant have mutually stipulated a penalty to secure appearance in court, and neither appears, neither will sue on the stipulation for the penalty, since both have incurred the penalty. We say similarly, in law "si uxor" 13, §index 5, on the Julian law on adultery, that a husband cannot demand chastity from his wife by right unless he himself also submits to it.

units.la: Cuiac. in Recitat. posthum.
units.tr: Cuiacius, in the posthumous Recitations.

units.la: hic.
units.tr: here.

units.la: Ad Leg. 155. Cui factum noceat. De eo qui iure suo vitur. De causis poe- nalibus.
units.tr: On Law 155. To whom an act may do harm. Concerning one who uses his own right. Concerning penal causes.

units.la: FActum cuique suum,non aduersario nocere debet. §. 1. Non videtur vim facere, qui iure suo vtitur, & ordinaria actione experitur. §.
units.tr: A person's act ought to harm himself, not his adversary. §1. One does not seem to use force when he uses his own right and proceeds by an ordinary action. §2.

units.la: 2. In poenalibus causis benignius interpretandum est.
units.tr: In penal causes the interpretation should be more lenient.

units.la: Factum] ex tract. interdictorum.
units.tr: Factum: from the title on interdicts.

units.la: Cuique suum] leg. 39. l. 49. l. 134. sup. eod. l. 9. sup. qua in fraudem credit.
units.tr: Cuique suum: law 39, law 49, law 134 above in the same title, law 9 above on what was done to defraud creditors.

units.la: Iure suo] v. l. 151. sup. eod. l. 12. in sin. sup. de vi.
units.tr: Iure suo: see law 151 above in the same title, and law 12 near the end above on violence.

units.la: Benignius] c. in poenis. 49. de reg. in 6. l. 192. in sin. infr. eod. l. 2. supra de liberis & posthum. mitior lex sequenda. l. 32. in sin. supr. de poenis. poenae molliendae. l. 42. sup. de poenis. humaniorem sententiam sequi oportet. l. 10. §. 1. sup. de reb. dubiis. si modo negocium id pati potest, si non praesumitur delictum. vid. Alciat. 3. praesumpt 1. puta furtum. l. 51. sup. pro socio. inusta infamia. l. 4. §. 2. supr. de suspectis. adde l. 23. in sin. supr. de adulteriis. siquidem, odia & poenas quantum fieri potest, restringi oportet. c. odia 15. de reg. in 6. Goth. hic.
units.tr: Benignius: c. in poenis 49, de regulis iuris in 6; law 192 near the end below in the same title; law 2 above on children and posthumous heirs: the milder law is to be followed; law 32 near the end above on penalties: penalties are to be softened; law 42 above on penalties: one ought to follow the more humane opinion; law 10 §1 above on doubtful matters: if the business can bear it, if a wrong is not presumed. See Alciat, 3 praesumpt. 1, for example theft; law 51 above on partnership: infamy inflicted; law 4 §2 above on suspects; add law 23 near the end above on adultery: since hatreds and penalties ought to be restricted as far as possible; c. odia 15, de regulis iuris in 6. Gothofredus, here.

units.la: Pertinet ad interdictum, unde vi, hoc modo. Finge: Proprietarius deiecit fructuarium, ita ut non possit frui fundo: unde accidit, ut usufructus non utendo interierit. Factum igitur proprietarii nocet fructuario ipso iure, quia finitur usufructus ipso iure. Sed quia iniquum est, ideo praetor iubet usumfructum restaurari: & hoc a proprietario, quia suum cuique factum nocet. l. si plures. 9. §. sin. de vi & vi armat. Sumi etiam potest exemplum (latissime enim patet haec regula) ex l. 1. §. si reus. 3. de eo, per quem fact. erit quo minus quis in indic. sist. Repromisit poenam iudicio sistendi causa, dolo actoris non stetit: hoc est, per actorem factum est, ne sisteret se iudicio, an incidit in poenam? Respondeo: quod non. Nam si petatur poena ex stipulatu, quia non stetit, repellitur actor doli exceptione.
units.tr: It pertains to the interdict Unde vi, in this way. Suppose the owner ejected the usufructuary, so that he could not enjoy the land; as a result the usufruct was lost through non-use. The owner's act therefore harms the usufructuary by law itself, because a usufruct ends by law itself. But since this is unjust, the praetor orders the usufruct to be restored, and he orders this against the owner, because each person's own act harms him. law si plures 9 §sin, de vi et vi armata. An example may also be taken (for this rule extends very widely) from law 1 §si reus 3, de eo per quem factum erit quo minus quis in iudicio sistatur. He promised a penalty as surety for appearing in court; he did not appear because of the plaintiff's fraud, that is, because of the plaintiff's act he was prevented from appearing in court. Does he fall into the penalty? I answer: no. For if the penalty is demanded under the stipulation, the plaintiff is repelled by the exception of fraud, because he did not appear.

units.la: Ad §. Non videtur. & §. In poenalib.
units.tr: On §. Non videtur, and §. In poenalib.

units.la: De eo quod sequitur in hac lege, satis dictum in l. semper 56. sup. quod scil. pertineat ad interdictum Unde vi. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: What follows in this law has been sufficiently discussed in law semper 56 above, namely that it pertains to the interdict Unde vi. Cuiacius, in Recitationes.

units.la: Lex 156. Inuitum non defendere. De actione & exceptione. De eo qui in alterius locum successit. De auctore & emtore.
units.tr: Law 156. No one is to defend against his will. On action and exception. On one who has succeeded into another's place. On seller and buyer.

units.la: De inuito. Ex tractatu interdictorum.
units.tr: On the unwilling party. From the treatise on interdicts.

units.la: INuitus nemo (rem) cogitur defendere. §.
units.tr: No one is compelled to defend a thing against his will. §.

units.la: 1. Cui damus actiones, eidem & exceptionem comcompetere multo magis quis dixerit. §. 2. Cum quis in alterius locum successerit, non est æquum, ei nocere hoc, quod aduersus eum nocuit, in cuius locum successit. §. 3. Plerumque emtoris eadem causa esse debet, circa perendum ac defendendum, quæ fuit auctoris. §. 4. Quod cuique (pro eo) præstatur, non inuito tribuitur.
units.tr: 1. Whoever is given actions, one will much more readily say that the exception is available to the same person. §. 2. When someone has succeeded into another's place, it is not fair that what was damaging against the predecessor, into whose place he succeeded, should harm him. §. 3. The cause of the buyer ought generally to be the same, in pursuing and in defending, as that of the seller. §. 4. What is granted to each person (on his behalf) is not assigned to him against his will.

units.la: Inuitus ] adde quæ dixi ad leg. 59. §. eod. Goth.
units.tr: Unwilling: add what I said on law 59, §. of the same title. Gothofred.

units.la: Cogitur defendere ] l. 17. C. de procur. puta noxali iudicio. l. 29. l. 33. sup. de noxali. sed & executor esse. Decius hic num. 1. procuratoris munus sustinere, l. 8. §. 1. sup. de procurator: datus tamen ad agendum, cogitur defensionem suscipere. l. 33. §. 4. sup. de procur. l 4. sup. de tutelis. & munus persequi, satisdare. l. 35. §. 2. sup. de procurator. non tamen vltra prouocationem. l. 17. C. de procur. nec extra suam prouinciam l. 35. §. 2. sup. de procur. non abstimiliter cogitur nemo inuitus agere & accusare l. 1. C. ut nemo inuitus. vectigal conducere. l. 29. §. 1. sup. de publicanis. aut in conductione vectigalis perseuerare, lustro peracto l. 3. §. 6. sup. de iur. fisci. seu frumentum vilius, quam annona exigit, vendere. l. vlt. sup. de annona. potest tamen quis iusta de causa cogi inuitus negotiationem aliquam exercere. l. 9. §. 9. sup. de pœnis. & seruos suos distrahere l. 2. sup. de his qui sunt sui iuris. potest etiam cogi aduocatus ad postulandum. vid. l. 7. C. de postul. doctor ad consilium dandum.vid. l. 6. C. de advocatis diversorum iudiciorum, eaque quis procuratione defungi, quam nostro tempore procuratores exercere solent. Decius hic argum. l. 1. §. 11. sup. de variis & extraordin. Ita notarius instrumentum conficere cogi potest, ut & caupo, hospes, nauta, tabernarius, commeantes, & vectores, excipere l. 1. sup. nauta, caupones, quod Decius turpissime, & contra omnem iuris & aequi artem extendit ad meretrices in lupanari stantes. Goth. hic.
units.tr: Compelled to defend: law 17, C. de procuratoribus, namely in a noxal judgment; laws 29 and 33, D. de noxalibus; but he may also be made to serve as executor. Decius here, no. 1, says that he may be made to undertake the office of procurator; law 8, §. 1, D. de procuratoribus. Yet one who has been appointed to bring an action is compelled to take up the defence, law 33, §. 4, D. de procuratoribus; law 4, D. de tutelis; and to pursue the business and to give security, law 35, §. 2, D. de procuratoribus; but not beyond an appeal, law 17, C. de procuratoribus, nor outside his own province, law 35, §. 2, D. de procuratoribus. Not in the same way, no one is compelled against his will to bring or to prosecute an action, law 1, C. ut nemo invitus; to farm a tax, law 29, §. 1, D. de publicanis; or to persist in the farming of a tax after the lustrum is completed, law 3, §. 6, D. de iure fisci; or to sell grain for less than the annona demands, law last, D. de annona. Yet for a just cause a man may be compelled against his will to carry on some business, law 9, §. 9, D. de poenis; and to sell off his slaves, law 2, D. de his qui sunt sui iuris. An advocate may also be compelled to plead, see law 7, C. de postulando; a teacher to give counsel, see law 6, C. de advocatis diversorum iudiciorum; and a person may be required to discharge the function which procurators in our time usually exercise. Decius here argues from law 1, §. 11, D. de variis et extraordinariis. So a notary may be compelled to draw up a document, as may an innkeeper, a host, a sailor, a shopkeeper, travellers and passengers to receive guests, law 1, D. nautae caupones. Decius shamefully and against all the art of law and fairness extends this even to prostitutes standing in the brothel. Gothofred here.

units.la: Actiones ] actionem vulgat. Hal.
units.tr: Actions: the Vulgate reads actionem. Halander.

units.la: Multo magis ] nota argumentum ab eo quod minus, ad id quod magis aequum est. add. cap. qui ad agendum admittitur 71. de regul. in 6. l. 1. §. 4. sup. de superficiebus.
units.tr: Much more: note the argument from the lesser to what is more equitable. Add chapter qui ad agendum admittitur 71, de regulis, in VI; law 1, §. 4, D. de superficiebus.

units.la: Quis dixerit ] fauetur enim reis l. 125. supr. eod. & retentioni. l. 4. C. de usuris. & liberationi l. 5. sup. de poenis. Id tamen fallit in iudiciis recuperandae possessionis, in quibus reo, qui spoliavit, non datur exceptio dominii, nisi prius restituerit possessionem. Datur ei actio, negatur exceptio l. 25. C. de locato. l. 1. C. si per vim. l. 7. C. de vi publica. l. 14. C. de agricolis. adde Nouel. 88. & merito, cum actio & exceptio referantur ad res diversas: haec ad possessionem, illa ad proprietatem. Goth. hic.
units.tr: One will say: for the defendant is favoured, law 125, D. of the same title, and in retention, law 4, C. de usuris, and in discharge, law 5, D. de poenis. This does not hold, however, in suits for recovering possession, in which the defendant who dispossessed another is not granted the exception of ownership unless he first restores possession. He is granted an action but denied an exception: law 25, C. de locato; law 1, C. si per vim; law 7, C. de vi publica; law 14, C. de agricolis. Add Novel 88. And rightly so, since action and exception relate to different things: the one to possession, the other to ownership. Gothofred here.

units.la: In alt. locum ] vulg. Hal. alicuius, & ira Cui.
units.tr: In another's place: the Vulgate, Halander, read alicuius (someone's), and so Cuiacius.

units.la: Aequum ei nocere hoc ] successori non nocet. cer, quod eius auctori nocere non potuit. l. 3. §. 2. in sin. sup. de itinere actuque. adde l. 76. in sin. sup. de contrahenda empt. l. 37. sup. de acquir. hereditate. & contra quod auctori nocere potuit, successori nocere potest. leg. 143. supr. eodem. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: It is not fair that this should harm him: a successor is not harmed by what could not harm his predecessor, law 3, §. 2, at the end, D. de itinere actuque; add law 76, at the end, D. de contrahenda emptione; law 37, D. de acquirenda hereditate. And conversely, what could harm the predecessor can harm the successor, law 143, D. of the same title. Gothofred here.

units.la: Plerunque ] nam quod auctoribus bonae fidei prodesse potuit, successori malae fidei nocere incipit. l. 2. §. 17. sup. pro emptore.
units.tr: Generally: for what could benefit a predecessor in good faith begins to harm a successor in bad faith, law 2, §. 17, D. pro emptore.

units.la: Eadem causa esse debet ] 2. Eclog. 2. c. 152. §. 3. l. 2. sup. de hereditat. vendit. l. 20. sup. de adquir. rer. domin. l. 2. in sin. sup. pro emptore. l. 5. C. de hereditate vendita. l. 26. C. de evict. Goth. hic.
units.tr: The cause ought to be the same: Eclogues 2, c. 152, §. 3; law 2, D. de hereditate vendita; law 20, D. de acquirendo rerum dominio; law 2, at the end, D. pro emptore; law 5, C. de hereditate vendita; law 26, C. de evictionibus. Gothofred here.

units.la: Inuito ] l. 69. sup. eod. l. 19. §. 2. sup. de donat.
units.tr: Against his will: law 69, D. of the same title; law 19, §. 2, D. de donationibus.

units.la: Non tribuitur ] Quidam ita legunt, non eripitur ex cap. indultum 7. de regul. in 6.
units.tr: Is not assigned: some read non eripitur (is not taken away), from the chapter indultum 7, de regulis, in VI.

units.la: Rem alienam scilicet nemo inuitus defendit. Nam tutor & curator quidem datur inuitus, & defendit pupillum inuitus: quia haec sunt munera publica, sed ad agendum, vel defendendum procurator non datur inuitus, l. si filiusfamilias 8. §. inuitus 1. de procur. Defensor enim nullus est, hoc est, nullus accedit ad defensionem nisi voluntarie. Veruntamen procurator, postquam datus est ad agendum, & suscepit mandatum; cogitur omnino defendere actorem, si sint mutuae petitiones, & eo nomine debet cavere, Iudicatum solui. Omnino cogitur, alioqui non agit. Quod agit, debet cavere uere rem ratam haberi, vt demonstratur l.33.§. vlt. & l.35.§.defendere 3.l. 43.§.pœna 4.de procurator. Procurator autem datus ad defendendum, àquo dominus cauit, iudicatum solui; vel etiam si ipse cauit; omnino cogitur iudicium accipere. An etiam si iustam causam habeat excusationis ? non vtique omnino, fecundum Labeonem.d.l. 43. §.vltim. Aliud iudicium fuit Sabino, qui putauit,eiusmodi caufam habentem, nullo modo cogendum iudicium accipere, etiamsi fatis dederit Iudicatum solui : sed dicebat committere stipulationem iudicatum solui ob rem non defensam.Sic non cogetur rem omnino defendere, fi iustam habeat causam : sed tenebitur ob rem non defenfam, in qua etiam causa habebitur ratio excusationis iustæ: fecundum præscriptum l. 45. de procurator.
units.tr: Clearly no one defends another's property against his will. For a tutor and a curator are indeed appointed against their will, and defend the ward against their will, because these are public offices; but a procurator is not appointed against his will to sue or defend. Law si filiusfamilias 8, §. inuitus 1, de procuratoribus. For there is no compulsory defender: that is, no one comes to the defence except voluntarily. Nevertheless, once a procurator has been appointed to sue and has accepted the commission, he is altogether compelled to defend the plaintiff if there are mutual claims, and on that account he must give security for the payment of the judgment. He is altogether compelled, otherwise he does not sue. Whatever he does, he must give security that the principal will hold it as ratified, as is shown in law 33, §. last, and law 35, §. defendere 3, and law 43, §. poena 4, de procuratoribus. But a procurator appointed to defend, to whom the owner has given security for the payment of the judgment, or even if he himself has given it, is altogether compelled to accept the trial. Even if he has a just cause of excuse? Not in every case, according to Labeo, d. law 43, §. last. Sabinus held a different view: he thought that a person with such a cause should in no way be compelled to accept the trial, even if he has given security for the payment of the judgment; but he said that the stipulation for payment of the judgment is incurred for a thing not defended. So he will not be compelled to defend the matter at all if he has a just cause; but he will be liable for the thing not defended, in which case account will also be taken of the just excuse, according to the rule of law 45, de procuratoribus.

units.la: Ad §. Cui damus.
units.tr: On §. Cui damus.

units.la: Sumitur ex l.vnic. §. is autem verfic.plane de superfici. Superficiario datur vindicatio vtilis aduersus dominum foli. Superficies quidem cedit solo: cuius est solum, eius est fnperficies: sed superficiarium Prætor habet pro domino, eique dat vtilem actionem: multo magis dabit exceptionem doli. Eodem modo ex edicto, Ex quibus causis maiores; datur actio: multo magis igitur exceptio l.nec non 28. §. exemplo 5. exquibus causis maior. Ergo cui damus actionem, eidem & damus exceptionem. Contra vero, cui damus exceptionem, non semper damus actionem. Nam sunt multæ causæ, ex quibus retentionem habemus ope exceptionis, non tamen petitionem habemus. l. Paulus 14. de dolli except. vt si quis in alieno solo ædificauerit, non potest sumptus petere à domino: sed si possideat ædificium, eos seruabit per retentionem & exceptionem doli l. 2. §. 1. de rei vindic. C. Gregor.
units.tr: This is taken from l. unica §. is autem, verse "plane," de superficiebus. A superficiary is given a utile vindication against the owner of the soil. The building (superficies) indeed belongs to the soil: whose the soil is, his the building is. But the praetor treats the superficiary as owner and gives him a utile action; much more will he give him an exception of fraud. In the same way, by the edict Ex quibus causis maiores, an action is given; much more, therefore, an exception: l. nec non 28, §. exemplo 5, ex quibus causis maior. Therefore, to whom we give an action, to him we also give an exception. On the other hand, to whom we give an exception, we do not always give an action. For there are many causes from which we have retention by means of an exception, yet we do not have a claim to recover. l. Paulus 14, de dolli except. For example, if someone has built on another's soil, he cannot demand his expenses from the owner; but if he possesses the building, he will keep them by retention and by exception of fraud. l. 2. §. 1. de rei vindic. C. Gregor.

units.la: Ad §.3. Plerumque emptoris.
units.tr: On §.3. Plerumque emptoris.

units.la: Quod ad sequentes duas sententias attinet, sciendum, interdictum de itinere actuque priuato, & aqua quotidiana, & æstiua non dari tantum actori. l. 2. in sin. si seruit, vindic. l. penult. de itin. actuque priuato. l. 1. §. ait Prætor 37. de aqu. quotid. & æstiua. Et eo referendæ sunt hæ duæ sententiæ; quarum vna est de hærede, altera de emptore, quam exposui in l. 54. sup.
units.tr: As for the following two opinions, it should be noted that the interdict concerning a way and private passage, and concerning daily and summer water, is not given only to the plaintiff. l. 2. in sin. si seruit, vindic. l. penult. de itin. actuque priuato. l. 1. §. ait Prætor 37. de aqu. quotid. & æstiua. And to this these two opinions are to be referred: one of which concerns the heir, the other the buyer, which I set out in l. 54. sup.

units.la: Ad §.4. Quod cui q.
units.tr: On §.4. Quod cui q.

units.la: Vt inuitus nemo defendit, ita inuitus nemo defenditur, l. 27. §. 1. de procurator. Et generaliter, vnusquisque renunciare potest iis, quæ pro se introducta sunt l. penult. C. de pactis. Et sic priuilegio fori renunciare possumus. Hæres remitremittere potest l. Falcidiam. Cuiac. in Recit: posthum. hic.
units.tr: Just as no one defends an unwilling person, so no one is defended against his will: l. 27. §. 1. de procurator. And generally, each person can renounce those things which were introduced in his favour: l. penult. C. de pactis. And so we can renounce the privilege of the forum. An heir can remit (the Falcidian portion). Cuiacius on the Recitations of the Posthumous, here.

units.la: Lex 157. De seruis. De eo, qui dolo fecit, quo minus haberet. De successoribus.
units.tr: Law 157. On slaves. On one who by fraud brought it about that he did not have. On successors.

units.la: A Dea, quæ non habent atrocitatem facinoris, vel sceleris, ignoscitur seruis, si vel dominis, vel his, qui vice dominorum sunt, veluti tutoribus, & curatoribus obtemperauerint. §.1. Semper qui dolo fecit, quo minus haberet, pro eo habendus est ac si haberet. §.2. In contractibus successores ex dolo eorum, quibus successerunt, non tantum in id, quod peruenit, verum etiam in solidum tenentur: Hoc est, vnusquisque pro ea parte, qua hæres est.
units.tr: Pardon is granted to slaves for deeds that lack the atrocity of a crime or wickedness, if they obeyed either their masters or those who stand in the place of masters, such as guardians and curators. §.1. He who by fraud brought it about that he did not have is to be regarded as if he had. §.2. In contracts, successors are held liable for the fraud of those to whom they succeeded, not only to the extent of what came to them, but even for the whole; that is, each one for that part of which he is heir.

units.la: Ad ] Ex tractatu interdictorum. l. is qui in puteum. §. si tut. quod vi aut clam.
units.tr: On "Ad": from the treatise on interdicts. l. is qui in puteum. §. si tut. quod vi aut clam.

units.la: Qui vice dominorum ] tutores sunt vice dominorum pupillarium rerum, vt hic: domini loco. l. 27. sup de administr. tutor. adde l. 56. §. 4. sup. de furt. Goth.
units.tr: Qui vice dominorum ] Guardians stand in the place of masters of the ward's property, as here, in the place of the master. l. 27. sup. de administr. tutor. Add l. 56. §. 4. sup. de furt. Goth.

units.la: Obtemperauerint ] l. 167. in sin. inf. eod.
units.tr: Obtemperauerint ] l. 167. in sin. inf. eod.

units.la: Quo minus haberet ] vid. l. 78. 150. sup. eod.
units.tr: Quo minus haberet ] See l. 78, 150. sup. eod.

units.la: X
units.tr: X

units.la: Ex dolo] vid. l. 152. in sin. sup. eod.
units.tr: Ex dolo: see l. 152, in sin., sup. eod.

units.la: In solidum tenentur] imo tunc non tenetur, §. 1. verf. aliquando Inst. de perpet. & temp. act.
units.tr: "They are held for the whole": nay, rather, in that case he is not held; §. 1, the passage beginning "sometimes", Inst. de perpet. & temp. act.

units.la: Hoc est] Puto legendum tenentur, vel vnusquisque, &c. vt sit sensus; socium haeredem in solidum, teneri etiam in solidum: pro parte, ex rata partis. l. 9. sup. de condict. furtiua. & ita intellige leg. 12. leg. 49. supr. de obligat. Gothofredus hic. Sumpta est ex l. 11. §. si tutoris ff. quod vi aut clam. Eo interdicto non coercetur vis atrox, sicut interdicto, unde vi: quo coercetur is, qui deiecit aliquem armis, vel sine armis. Sed interdicto, quod vi aut clam, tenetur, qui contra, quam prohibeatur, facit, quia putat se hoc iure facere, & tenetur, siue ius habuerit faciendi, siue non: nam non debebat contemnere prohibitionem. Finge. Seruus Pupilli iussu tutoris facit opus vi aut clam, an erit in noxa seruus, hoc est, an pupillus tenetur noxali actione? an seruus ipse tenetur post manumissionem: quia noxa caput sequitur? Er verius est, seruum non esse in noxa. Vis non est ita atrox, vt imputari debeat ei, qui paruit domino; imo & ei ignoscitur qui paruit tutori: nam tutor est vice domini, hoc est, pupilli. Quod ita verum est, vt seruus non possit torqueri in tutorem. l. 2. C. de quaest. Sic etiam si iussu vxoris, seruus eius res amouerit marito diuortii gau-
units.tr: Hoc est: I think we should read "tenentur," or "unusquisque, etc.," so that the sense is: the heir as partner is held for the whole, and likewise is held for the whole, but only for the part, in proportion to his share. See l. 9 sup. de condict. furtiua; and understand l. 12 and l. 49 sup. de obligat. in this way; Gothofredus here. It is taken from l. 11 §. si tutoris ff. quod vi aut clam. By that interdict violence of an atrocious kind is not restrained, as it is by the interdict unde vi, which restrains one who dispossesses someone, with or without arms. But one is held by the interdict quod vi aut clam who acts contrary to what is prohibited, because he thinks he is acting by right; and he is held whether or not he had the right to act, for he ought not to disregard the prohibition. Suppose a slave of a ward does a work by force or stealth on the guardian's order. Will the slave be in noxa, that is, is the ward liable by a noxal action? Or is the slave himself liable after manumission, since noxa follows the head? The truer view is that the slave is not in noxa. The violence is not so atrocious that it should be imputed to him who obeyed his master; indeed, pardon is granted also to one who obeyed a guardian, for the guardian stands in place of the master, that is, of the ward. This is so true that the slave cannot be tortured against the guardian: l. 2. C. de quaest. So too, if at the wife's order her slave removed goods from her husband during a divorce, the slave is pardoned.

units.la: Nothing further. causa, ignoscitur seruo. Ideo non est in noxa. Nam & hoc non habetur pro facinore, hoc est, pro furto. Furtum est scelus. Sed aliud est surari: aliud amouere. Fere hoc etiam est furari: sed rem ipsam lenitate verbi mitigant. Itaque hoc non habetur pro furto. Si vero ipse seruus sine iussu dominæ surripuerit, erit noxalis actio & liber factus tenebitur: si iussu dominæ, excusabitur. l. si cum mulier §. penult. rerum amot. sic si seruus iussu domini libertatem sibi adscripserit, cum scriberet testamentum, non tenetur. Sciendum est, scriptorem testamenti, qui sibi aliquid adscribit, teneri falsi, nisi sua manu id postea approbarit testator in calce testamenti. Nunc si seruus iussu domini sibi adscripsit libertatem, non tenetur, nec amittit libertatem leg. diuus 15. §. & quatenus 3. de leg. Corn. de falsi. similiter is, qui damnum iniuria dedit iussu domini, non tenetur: secus est, si sciente tantum domino, & patiente, damnum dedit. Nam tunc dominus tenetur non tantum suo nomine in solidum, quod passus est damnum dare: sed & noxaliter, quod noxa caput sequitur. Nam differentia est inter scienter, & libenter. Et ita accipe l. 2. §. 1. de noxal. act. ita etiam accipienda est l. 169. infr. quæ tota est de noxal. act. Is damnum dedit, qui iubet dare: eius vero serui nulla est culpa, qui fecit iussu domini. Seruus talis non est in noxa.
units.tr: Nothing further. A cause: the slave is pardoned. Therefore he is not in noxa. For this too is not regarded as a crime, that is, as theft. Theft is a crime, but to carry off is one thing and to steal another; yet carrying off is almost the same as stealing, and they soften the matter by the gentleness of the word. Therefore this is not regarded as theft. If, however, the slave himself has stolen without his mistress's order, there will be a noxal action, and once freed he will be liable; if at the mistress's order, he will be excused. l. si cum mulier §. penult. rerum amot. So too, if a slave wrote himself down as free at his master's order when the master was writing his will, he is not liable. It must be noted that the writer of a will who inserts something in his own favour is liable for forgery, unless the testator afterwards approves it in his own hand at the foot of the will. Now, if a slave, at his master's order, wrote himself down as free, he is not liable, nor does he lose his freedom. leg. diuus 15. §. & quatenus 3. de leg. Corn. de falsi. Similarly, one who wrongfully causes damage at his master's order is not liable; it is otherwise if he caused the damage with the master merely knowing and permitting it, for then the master is liable not only in his own name for the whole damage he allowed, but also noxally, since noxa follows the head. For there is a difference between knowingly and willingly. Understand it thus from l. 2. §. 1. de noxal. act.; and it is to be understood in the same way from l. 169. infr., which is entirely about noxal actions. He causes the damage who orders it done; but the slave who acted at his master's order bears no fault. Such a slave is not in noxa.

units.la: Ad §. Semper.
units.tr: On the paragraph "Semper."

units.la: Hic §. expositus est in l. 131. & 151.
units.tr: This paragraph is explained in laws 131 and 151.

units.la: Ad §. In contractibus.
units.tr: On the paragraph "In contractibus."

units.la: De hoc vltimo §. huius legis vide, quæ dicta sunt sup. in l. 38. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: On this last paragraph of this law, see what was said above on law 38. Cujas, in Recitationes.

units.la: Ad Leg. 158. De Pignore.
units.tr: On law 158. Concerning a pledge.

units.la: CReditor, qui permittit, rem venire, pignus demittit.
units.tr: A creditor who permits the thing to be sold releases the pledge.

units.la: Demittit] dimittit Hal. i. remittit ius pignorum; l. 4. §. 1. sup. quibus modis pig. l. vlt. Cod. de remiss. pign. non tamen ipsum delictum. l. 3. §. de pactis, causa dubitandi in hac lege sumi potest ex l. 160. inf. eod. Goth.
units.tr: "Releases": dimittit, that is, remittit the right of pledges; law 4 §. 1 above, on the ways pledges are extinguished; last law of the Code, on the remission of pledges. Yet not the debt itself: law 3 §. on pacts. The doubt in this law can be drawn from law 160 below, under the same title. Gothofredus.

units.la: Rem scilicet pignori obligatam, pignus soluitur, si debitor id vendat voluntate creditoris: nisi consenserit salua pignoris causa: l. sicut 8. §. si volunt. 6. quib. modis pignus solu. in qua lege plenissime hac de re disseritur. Cuiac. in Recit. posthum.
units.tr: Clearly, when a thing mortgaged to a creditor is sold by the debtor with the creditor's consent, the pledge is extinguished, unless he has consented while preserving the security of the pledge: law "sicut" 8 §. "si voluntate", in the title on the ways pledges are extinguished, where this matter is discussed most fully. Cujas, in Recitationes posthumae.

units.la: Ad Leg. 159. Differentia obligationis & dominii.
units.tr: On law 159. The difference between obligation and ownership.

units.la: NOn vt ex pluribus causis debeeri nobis idem potest, ita ex pluribus causis idem possit & nostrum esse.
units.tr: Just as one thing can be owed to us on several grounds, so the same thing cannot be ours on several grounds.

units.la: Non ] Ex pluribus causis rem eandem possidere possumus : l.3. §.4. sup. acquirenda possess. semel res mea esse potest, saepius deberi potest, l.14. §. 2. supr. de excep. rei iudicata. Quod iam nostrum est, aut proprium, magis aut amplius nostrum fieri non potest §.10. Instit. de legatis §. 4. Instit. de act. Goth.
units.tr: "Not": we can possess the same thing on several grounds (law 3 §. 4 above, on acquiring possession). A thing can be mine only once, but it can be owed to me many times (law 14 §. 2 above, on the exception of a thing adjudged). What is already ours, or our own, cannot become more or further ours (Institutes 2.1 §. 10; on legacies §. 4; on actions §. 4). Gothofredus.

units.la: Coniunge l. & an eadem §. 1. de except. rei iudicatae, ait: non ex pluribus causis. Id declaratur in d.l. & an eadem: Res amplius, quam semel nostra esse non potest: nam quod factum est meum ex una causa, non potest adhuc meum fieri ex alia, §. sicut Instit. de actionibus. Itaque si egero vindicatione, & litem amisero, non possum eandem rem postea vindicare, quasi ex alia causa; cum iam non potuerit esse mea ex pluribus causis, sed res eadem nobis debetur ex pluribus causis saepius, ut ex mutuo, ex stipulatu, ex testamento. Item nobis potest quis debere ex pluribus causis, ideoque si egero in personam ex una causa; nec obtinuero, non postea prohibeor agere ex altera. Et hac in re differunt, actio in rem, & in personam; actio in rem non iteratur: actio in personam iteratur, mutata causa. Ergo aliud est, nobis deberi, aliud nostrum esse. Pecunia, quae in arca est, nostra est; quae in nominib. est, nō est nostra. l. singulari 15. de reb. cred. Eadem est differentia inter dominium & possessionem; Res mea tantum mea esse potest ex vna causa; possidere eam possum ex pluribus causis; vt emptor, qui vsucepit, possidet pro emptore, & pro suo; dominus est per vsucapionem tantum. l. 3. §. ex plu-rimis 4. de acquir. possess. Sicut aliud est, nobis quid deberi, aliud nostrum esse; ita & aliud, possideri a nobis, & aliud, aliquid nostrum esse. Nam quaecunque possidentur a nobis, non sunt nostra. Itaque haec non sunt permiscenda. l. naturaliter 12 §. nihil de acquirend. possess. l. pen. §. 1. eod. l. 1. §. huius. vti possidetis. Sen. 4. nat. quaest.
units.tr: Compare the law "et an eadem" §. 1 on the exception of a thing adjudged, which says: not on several grounds. This is made clear in the said law "et an eadem": a thing cannot be ours more than once; for what has become mine by one cause cannot become mine again by another (Institutes on actions, the §. "sicut"). So if I have brought an action of vindication and lost the suit, I cannot afterwards vindicate the same thing on the ground of some other cause, since it could not be mine on several grounds; but the same thing can be owed to us repeatedly on several grounds, as by loan, by stipulation, or by will. Likewise someone can owe us on several grounds, so that if I have sued personally on one ground and not succeeded, I am not afterwards barred from suing on another. In this respect an action in rem and an action in personam differ: an action in rem is not repeated; an action in personam is repeated, the cause having changed. Therefore it is one thing to be owed to us, another to be ours. The money that is in the chest is ours; what is in debts is not ours (law "singulari" 15, on loans). The same difference holds between ownership and possession: my thing can be mine on one ground only, but I can possess it on several grounds; as a buyer who has acquired by usucapion possesses both as buyer and as owner, while he is owner only through usucapion (law 3 §. "ex pluribus" 4, on acquiring possession). Just as it is one thing for something to be owed to us and another for it to be ours, so it is also one thing for something to be possessed by us and another for it to be ours. For whatever is possessed by us is not necessarily ours. Therefore these must not be confused (law "naturaliter" 12 §. "nihil", on acquiring possession; last law §. 1 of the same title; law 1 §. "huius", on "as you possess"; Seneca, Natural Questions 4).

units.la: Ad Leg. 160. Differentia inter vendere, & vendenti consentire. De eo, quod fit per maiorem partem. De iure Legatarii, &c.
units.tr: On law 160. The difference between selling and consenting to a seller. On what is done by the greater part. On the right of a legatee, etc.

units.la: ALiud est vendere, aliud est vendenti consentire. §. 1. Refertur ad vniuersos quod publice fit per maiorem partem. §. 2. Absurdum est plus iuris habere (eum) cui legatus sit fundus, quam haeredem, aut ipsum testatorem, si viueret.
units.tr: To sell is one thing; to consent to the seller is another (§. 1). What is done publicly by the greater part is referred to all (§. 2). It is absurd for the one to whom a farm has been bequeathed to have more right than the heir, or the testator himself, were he alive.

units.la: Ex tit. de litigiosis.
units.tr: From the title on litigious things.

units.la: Aliud] Imo non aliud l. 158. sup. eod.
units.tr: "Another": nay, not another; law 158 above, under the same title.

units.la: Est] Nisi sit vtrobique eadem ratio, hinc minor necalienare, nec alienationi consentire potest l. 2. si aduersus donationem. cui vnum eorum rum permittitur, alterum quoque conceditur, l.162. l.165. inf. eod. Goth.
units.tr: "Is": unless the reason is the same on both sides; hence a minor can neither alienate nor consent to an alienation (law 2, "si adversus donationem"). When the one of these two things is permitted, the other is also granted (laws 162 and 165 below, under the same title). Gothofredus.

units.la: Aliud ] si aliud est, igitur cui unum eorum non licebit, aliud ei permitti intelligetur. l.2. C. de manumiss. vindicta.
units.tr: "Another": if it is another, then what is not permitted to one is understood to be permitted to another (law 2 Code, on manumission by vindication).

units.la: Consentire ] Hinc, aliud est contrahere, aliud contrahenti consentire.
units.tr: "To consent": hence, it is one thing to contract, another to consent to one who contracts.

units.la: Maiorem ] v. l.3. l.4. supra quod cuiusque. l.19. supra ad municipalem: facit l.10. supra de pactis. l.7. in fine Cod. de omni agro deserto. l.148. sup. eod. & ita intellige l.10. sup. de aqua pluvia, vel per eos, à quibus res municipii geri solent. l.97. sup. de condit. & demonstr. l.uni. §.1. sup. de liber. universf. l.1. §.2. sup. de acquir. possess. Sic maioris partis bonorum litis ratio habetur in excusando tutore. l.21. sup. de excusat. tut. & maioris partis anni, ut res aliqua fundi esse dicatur vel negetur l.18. §.12. sup. de instruct. quod omnes tangit, & ab omnibus deber approbari. c. quod omnes 29. de reg. in 6. Goth.
units.tr: "Greater part": see law 3, law 4 above, on what belongs to each; law 19 above, on municipalities; law 10 above, on pacts; law 7 at the end of the Code, on all deserted land; law 148 above under the same title; and understand law 10 above, on rainwater, or through those by whom the affairs of a municipality are usually managed (law 97 above, on conditions and demonstrations; law "uni" §. 1 above, on the freedom of universal succession; law 1 §. 2 above, on acquiring possession). So too the greater part of the goods is taken into account in excusing a guardian (law 21 above, on excuses from guardianship); and the greater part of a year is considered, so that a thing is said to be or not to be part of an estate (law 18 §. 12 above, on instructing). What touches all must be approved by all (chapter "quod omnes" 29, On rules, in the Sixth Book). Gothofredus.

units.la: Legatus ] Legatarius non est potioris iuris, quam heres, aut defunctus, l.120. l.143. sup. eod. l.176. in sin. inf. eod. Gothof.
units.tr: "Legatee": a legatee has no greater right than the heir or the deceased (law 120, law 143 above under the same title; law 176 at the end below, under the same title). Gothofredus.

units.la: Initium huius legis expositum est in l. 21. sup. Cuia.
units.tr: The beginning of this law is explained in law 21 above. Cujas.

units.la: Ad §. Refertur.
units.tr: On the paragraph "Refertur."

units.la: Sensus est; quod facit maior pars creditorum, omnes fecisse videntur. leg. iurisgent. 7. §. vlt. & l. seq. de pact. l. vlt. C. qui bon. ced. poss. l. quod si nemo de excus. tutor. Et quod maior pars curiae facit. l. quod maior ad municip. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: The sense is this: what the greater part of the creditors does is taken to be done by all. See leg. iurisgent. 7, §. vlt., and the following law, de pact.; l. vlt. C. qui bon. ced. poss.; l. quod si nemo de excus. tutor. And what the greater part of a city council does is taken as done. l. quod maior ad municip. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad §. Absurdum.
units.tr: On the paragraph "Absurdum."

units.la: Hic §. expositus est in l. 54. supra.
units.tr: This §. was explained in l. 54 above.

units.la: Ad Leg. 161. De eo per quem factum est, quo minus conditio im- pleatur.
units.tr: On Law 161. Concerning the person through whom the condition was prevented from being fulfilled.

units.la: IN iure ciuili receptum est, quoties per eum, cuius interest, conditionem non impleri, fiat, quo minus impleatur, perinde haberi; ac si impleta conditio fuisset: quod ad libertatem, & legata, & ad haeredum institutiones perducitur; quibus exemplis stipulationes quoque committuntur; cum per promissorem factum esset, quo minus stipulator conditioni pareret.
units.tr: It is established in the civil law that whenever a condition is prevented from being fulfilled by the person whose interest it is, the matter is treated just as if the condition had been fulfilled. This extends to freedom, to legacies and to the institution of heirs; and by these examples stipulations too are brought into effect, when the promisor has brought it about that the stipulator could not comply with the condition.

units.la: In] Ex tractatu Praetoriar. stipulat.
units.tr: "In": from the treatise of the Praetorian stipulations.

units.la: Interest] cap. imputatur 41. c. cum non stat 66. de regulis in sext. 2. Ecloga 25. cap. 156. v. l. 24. sup. de condit. & demonst.
units.tr: It matters: cap. imputatur 41; c. cum non stat 66; de regulis in Sext. 2; Ecloga 25; cap. 156; see law 24, above, on conditions and demonstrations.

units.la: Conditionem] πληρωθῆναι τὸν ὁρισμὸν impleti conditionem Ecl. ibidem ... 6. Harmenop. 2. Plane ordo est inuersus, sic restituo; Quoties per eum, cuius interest, conditionem impleri, non fiat, quo minus impleatur, &c. quod optime conuenit legi 3. 9. 10. in fine, l. 28. sup. de statulib. cap. imputari 41. & cap. cum non stat per eum 66. de reg. in sext. Ut interrim dicam in dicto cap. 66. quo minus sumi pro quin, vel quod magis. Gothof.
units.tr: "Conditionem": [πληρωθῆναι τὸν ὁρισμὸν] the fulfilment of the condition, Ecl. ibidem; 6, Harmenop. 2. The order of the words is plainly reversed; I restore it thus: "Whenever, through the person whose interest it is, the condition is not fulfilled, so that it is not carried out, etc.", which agrees very well with l. 3, 9, 10 at the end, l. 28 above de statulib., cap. imputari 41, and cap. cum non stat per eum 66, de reg. in sext. Meanwhile I note that in the said cap. 66 "quo minus" is to be taken as "quin" or "quod magis". Gothof.

units.la: Libertatem] Ecl. ibidem l. 20. §. 3. l. 28. sup. de statulib.
units.tr: "Libertatem": Ecl. ibidem; l. 20, §. 3; l. 28 above, de statulib.

units.la: Legata] Eclog. ibid. & l. 24. l. 5. §. 5 sup. quando dies legati.
units.tr: Legacies] Eclog. ibid. & l. 24. l. 5. §. 5 sup. quando dies legati.

units.la: Institutiones] Ecl. ibid. & dict. l. 24. l. 3. sup. de condit. instit.
units.tr: Institutions] Ecl. ibid. & dict. l. 24. l. 3. sup. de condit. instit.

units.la: Stipulationes] Ecl. ibid. & dicta l. 24.
units.tr: "Stipulationes": Ecl. ibid.; and the said l. 24.

units.la: Cum pareret] Leg. 85. sup. de verbor. oblig.
units.tr: "Cum pareret": Leg. 85 above, de verbor. oblig.

units.la: Huius legis explicatio iam praemissa est in leg. 39. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: The explanation of this law has already been given in leg. 39 above. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 162. De receptis propter necessitatem.
units.tr: On Law 162. Concerning things admitted because of necessity.

units.la: QVae propter necessitatem recepta sunt, non debent in argumentum trahi.
units.tr: What has been admitted because of necessity ought not to be drawn into precedent.

units.la: Necessitatem] με δι αιάγκην 2. eclog. 3. cap. 162. με ὠδῆς κανόνας νόμως λεχθέντας 6. Harmenop. 2. contra rationem iuris. l. 14. l. 15 sup. de leg. contra tenorem rationis. l. 16. sup. de legib. ut ea quae a iure communi exorbitant, cap. quae a iure 28. de reg. in sext. quae ob gratiam alicui conceduntur, cap. quod ob gratiam 61. de regul. in sext. sic necessitas probabilem facit manumissionem. l. 27. sup. de manumiss. testam. Clarus etiam id innui putat, furem excusari à pœna furti commissi, propter extremam necessitatem 5. sentent. §. furtum vers. quandoque: Necessitas etiam excusat venditionem filii. l.2. Cod. de pat. qui filios. Quod non est licitum in lege, necessitas facit licitum cap. quod non est extra de regulis; hinc illud, necessitas non habet legem: Non ignoscitur tamen ei, quæ obtentu paupertatis turpissimam vitam agit. l. 45. §. 5. sup. de ritu Gothof.
units.tr: "Necessitatem": [διὰ ἀνάγκην] through necessity; 2, Ecloga 3, cap. 162; [μὴ ὡς ... κανόνας νόμως λεχθέντας] rules spoken as law, 6, Harmenop. 2. Against the reason of the law: l. 14, l. 15 above, de leg.; against the tenor of reason: l. 16 above, de legib.; so that those things which depart from the common law, cap. quae a iure 28, de reg. in sext.; which are granted to someone as a favour, cap. quod ob gratiam 61, de regul. in sext. Thus necessity makes a manumission probable: l. 27 above, de manumiss. testam. Clarus thinks this also implied, that a thief is excused from the penalty of theft committed through extreme necessity: 5 sentent. §. furtum vers. quandoque: Necessity also excuses the sale of a son: l.2 Cod. de pat. qui filios. What is not lawful by law, necessity makes lawful: cap. quod non est extra de regulis; hence the saying, necessity has no law. Yet he is not pardoned who, under the pretext of poverty, leads a most shameful life. l. 45, §. 5 above, de ritu Gothof.

units.la: Argumentum] Consequentias. l.14. sup. de oblig. ad regulas iuris. l.15. §. de legib. Ecl. ibidem. Harmenop. ibid. id est exemplum; hinc sine exemplo subuenire §.9. in fine Instit. de iure naturali. sanstirer eri consequenz. Gothof.
units.tr: "Argumentum": consequences. l.14 above, de oblig., to the rules of law; l.15, §. de legib. Ecl. ibidem. Harmenop. ibid. That is, an example; hence to help without an example, §. 9, in fine Instit. de iure naturali. A consequence of this kind. Gothof.

units.la: Vide l.141. paulo ante explicatam, & l.110. §.1. & 2. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: See l. 141, explained a little earlier, and l. 110, §. 1 and 2. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 163. De donatione; vend- itione, concessione.
units.tr: On Law 163. Concerning gift, sale and grant.
