units.la: CVi ius est donandi, eidem & vendendi, & concedendi ius est.
units.tr: To whom the right of giving belongs, to him belongs also the right of selling and granting.

units.la: Cui ius] Ex tit. de liber. causa.
units.tr: "Cui ius": from the title de liber. causa.

units.la: Donandi] Argumentum à maiori ad minus, qui potest donare, potest vendere, multo magis concedere, 2. ecl. 3. c. 158. adde l. 21. sup. cod.
units.tr: "Donandi": an argument from the greater to the lesser: whoever can give can sell, and much more can grant; 2, Ecl. 3, c. 158. Add l. 21 above, same title.

units.la: Sic, cui testamenti factio est, donare potest mortis causa, & non causa l.7.in sin.sup.de donat. sic, qui potest alienare, potest alienationi consentire l.165.sup.eod.Goth.
units.tr: So too, one who has the capacity to make a will can give in view of death, though not otherwise: l. 7 in fine above, de donat. So too, one who can alienate can consent to an alienation: l. 165 above, same title. Goth.

units.la: Eidem & ] Et econtra prohibitus vendere, donare non potest; imo potest l.4.C.de fideiussorib. solue. Voluntati defuncti non repugnat, qui donat sorori, quod extra familiam vendere aut pignori dare non potest. Goth.
units.tr: "Eidem": And conversely, one forbidden to sell cannot give; indeed he can pay the surety: l. 4 C. de fideiussorib. He does not go against the will of the deceased who gives to a sister what he could not sell outside the family or pledge. Goth.

units.la: Concedendi ] καὶ ἐγχωρεῖν αὐτῷ δύνανται, Ecl.ibidem, id est, etiam credere potest: Concedendi vocabulo quidam intelligunt colonarium contractum. Goth.
units.tr: "Concedendi": [καὶ ἐγχωρεῖν αὐτῷ δύνανται] and they can grant it to him, Ecl. ibidem; that is, he can also lend on credit. Some understand the word "concedendi" to mean the tenant-farming contract. Goth.

units.la: Ius est ] imo non est. Decurio donare potest, vendere non potest l. ult. C. de prædiis Decurionum. id merito sublatum Novella 38. Gothofr.
units.tr: "Ius est": indeed it is not. A decurion can give but cannot sell: l. ult. C. de praediis Decurionum; this was rightly abolished, Novella 38. Gothofr.

units.la: Huius regulæ exempla & ratio explicata sunt in l.21.sup.Cuiac.
units.tr: The examples and the reason for this rule have been explained in l.21 above, Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg.164. De Hæredibus & iudi- ciis pænalibus.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 164. On heirs and penal judgments.

units.la: POenalia iudicia semel accepta in hæredes transmitti possunt.
units.tr: Penal judgments, once begun, can be transmitted to heirs.

units.la: Pænalia ] Ex tit. de liberali causa l.utique.
units.tr: Penal] From title On a liberal cause, law utique.

units.la: Semel ] 2.Eclog.3.cap.159. alias non contestata minime transmittuntur l.11.in sin.supr.eod.l. 26.l.58.sup.de obligat. §. 1. in fine Instit. de perpetuis l.unica C.ex delicto defuncti. Quin, non omnia mnia contestata in hæredes transeunt, hæredes rei ob delictum (paucis exceptis) non tenentur, nisi lata sententia. l. 20. sup. de accusat. Gothofred.
units.tr: Once begun] Eclogues 2, book 3, chapter 159. Otherwise matters not yet contested are not transmitted: law 11, at the end, above, same title; law 26; law 58, above, On obligations; §1, at the end of Institutes, On perpetual obligations; the sole law of the Code, On a debt arising from a delict of the deceased. Indeed, not all contested matters pass to heirs; the heirs of a defendant in a delict are not liable (with few exceptions) unless sentence has been pronounced. Law 20, above, On accusations. Gothofredus.

units.la: De hac lege vide explicationem l. nemo. 87. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: For this law see the explanation of law Nemo, 87, above, Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad Leg. 165. De eo qui alienat vel alie- nanti consentit.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 165. On one who alienates, or consents to the alienation of another's property.

units.la: CVm quis possit alienare, poterit consentire alienationi; cui autem donare non conceditur, probandum erit, necsi donationis causa consenserit, ratam eius voluntatem habendam.
units.tr: Since a person who may alienate may also consent to an alienation; but where donation is not permitted, it must be proved that, if he consented for the sake of a donation, his consent is to be held valid.

units.la: Alienare ] Cui maius licet, eidem minus est permissum v.l. 21. l. 66. sup. eod. Goth.
units.tr: Alienate] One to whom the greater is permitted is also permitted the lesser. Law 21; law 66, above, same title. Gothofredus.

units.la: Et hæc lex intelligitur ex explicatione legis 21. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: This law is also understood from the explanation of law 21, above, Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad Leg. 166. De defensore rei aliena.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 166. On the defender of another's property.

units.la: QVi rem alienam defendit nunquam lo- cuples habetur.
units.tr: One who defends another's property is never considered wealthy.

units.la: Qui ] Ex tit. de damno infecto.
units.tr: One who] From the title On damage not yet done.

units.la: Habetur ] Nota argumentandi speciem à contrario sensu, id est, nunquam ita quisquam locuples habendus est, vt immunis à satisdan- do sit eius nomine, quem defendit l. 35. §. 3. l. 51. in sin. l. 52. l. 53. sup. de procurat. nisi defendat necessariam personam l. 3. sup. in ius vocati. l. 2. §. 2. sup. qui satisdare, adde l. 95. sup. eod. l. 134. §. 1. sup. de verb. significat. l. 63 in sin. princ. sup. ad legem Falcid. Goth. Vide sup. in l. 35. Cuia.
units.tr: Is considered] Note this form of argument from the contrary sense: that is, no one is ever to be regarded as so wealthy as to be exempt from giving security on account of the person whom he defends. Law 35, §3; law 51, at the end; law 52; law 53, above, On agents, unless he defends a necessary person. Law 3, above, On those summoned to court; law 2, §2, above, Who must give security. Add law 95, above, same title; law 134, §1, above, On the meaning of words; law 63, at the end of the beginning, above, on the Falcidian law. Gothofredus. See above on law 35, Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad Leg. 167. De his, quae accipientis non fiunt. De iussu Iudicis.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 167. On things that do not become the recipient's. On the order of a judge.

units.la: Non videntur data, quae eo tempore, quo dantur accipientis non fiunt. §. 1. Qui iussu iudicis aliquid facit, non videtur dolo malo facere, qui parere necesse habet.
units.tr: Things are not considered given if, at the time they are given, they do not become the property of the recipient. §1. One who does something by order of a judge is not seen to act with malicious intent, since he is bound to obey.

units.la: Non ] ex tit. de aqu. plu. arc.
units.tr: Not] From the title On water and rain-water channels.

units.la: Videntur ] Proprie, secus improprie, ratione personae l. 55. sup. de cond. & demonstr. vel contractus l. 4. sup. de usur.
units.tr: Considered] Strictly, otherwise improperly, by reason of the person or of the contract. Law 55, above, On conditions and demonstrations; law 4, above, On usury.

units.la: Data ] v. l. ult. sup. de condict. causa data leg. 75. in sin. de verborum obligat. §. 14 Instit. de actionibus.
units.tr: Given] See the last law, above, On condictio for a cause given; law 75, at the end, On verbal obligations; §14 of the Institutes, On actions.

units.la: Iudicis ] l. 269. inf. eod. adde l. 137. sup. eodem. vel superioris l. 157. sup. eod.
units.tr: Of a judge] Law 269, below, same title; add law 137, above, same title, or of a superior, law 157, above, same title.

units.la: Non ] iussus iudicis excusat a dolo & delicto. l. 6. §. 4. sup. de iurisd. l. 7. §. 2. in sin. sup. de minorib. l. 8. sup. de leg. Commissor. l. 4. sup. de aqua pluvia l. 13. §. 2. sup. de iniur. non conferr tamen ad lucrum, idque sentit Oldendorp. classe 1. act. 3. in fine. Gothofr.
units.tr: Not] An order of a judge excuses from fraud and delict. Law 6, §4, above, On jurisdiction; law 7, §2, at the end, above, On minors; law 8, above, On the law of forfeiture; law 4, above, On rain-water; law 13, §2, above, On injuries. It does not, however, contribute to gain; Oldendorp thinks so, class 1, act 3, at the end. Gothofredus.

units.la: Dare, est rem perfecte accipientis faceret; proprie ita accipitur in stipulatione, Rem dari, l. ubi autem 75. §. vlt. de verbo obligat. l. 1. C. de contrahend. stipul. & in formula actionis in personam, quod te dare & facere oportet. §. sic itaque Instit. de act. & in vulgari formula testamentorum Dari, aut donari, Data aut donata, & frequentissime ab authoribus nostris l. 4. Cod. de præpos. sac. arar.
units.tr: To give is to make a thing wholly the property of the recipient. It is so understood properly in a stipulation: that a thing be given; law Ubi autem, 75, §last, On verbal obligations; law 1, Code, On entering into stipulations; and in the formula of an action in personam, what you ought to give or do; §Sic itaque, Institutes, On actions; and in the common formula of wills, to be given, or donated, given or donated; and very frequently by our authors: law 4, Code, On the praepositi of the sacred treasury.

units.la: Ad §. Qui iussu, &c.
units.tr: On §. Qui iussu, etc.

units.la: Sepulcri violati actione tenetur is, cuius dolo malo sepulcrum violatum est, vt prima edicti verba demonstrant l. 1. de sepul. violat. Itaque non tenetur hac actione, qui iussu iudicis sepulcrum demolitus est, puta ex ea causa, vt si ex eo aqua pluuia noceat vicino, & ita huic regulæ coniungenda est l. 4. de aq. & aq. plu. arc. air, quia parere necesse habet. Et eadem ratione parcitur seruo, quod diximus in l. 157. sup. proinde sicut in atrocioribus, si paruerit domino seruus, nō excusatur: ita nec excusatur is, qui aliquid atrocius iussu iudicis admisit. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: One who is liable to the action for violated tombs is the one by whose malicious intent the tomb was violated, as the first words of the edict show. Law 1, On violated tombs. Accordingly, one who demolished a tomb by order of a judge is not liable to this action, for instance on the ground that water from rain would harm a neighbour as a result. So this rule must be joined to law 4, On water and rain-water channels, because he is bound to obey. And for the same reason a slave is pardoned, which we said above in law 157. Therefore, just as a slave who obeyed his master is not excused in more atrocious cases, so one who committed something more atrocious by order of a judge is not excused. Cuiacius, in the Recitationes.

units.la: Ad Leg. 168. De obscuris.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 168. On unclear matters.

units.la: CApienda occasio est, quæ præbet benignius responsum. §. 1. Quod factum est cum in obscuro sit, ex affectione cuiusque capit interpretationem.
units.tr: One must seize the opportunity that yields the more favourable answer. §1. Since what was done is unclear, it takes its interpretation from the disposition of each person.

units.la: Occasio ] id est, interpretatio.
units.tr: Opportunity] That is, interpretation.

units.la: Benignius ] v. l. 56. sup. eod. τὸ φιλάγαθον 2. Ecl. 3. cap. 164. ut & cap. 57. φιλάνθρωπον.
units.tr: More favourable] See law 56, above, same title. τὸ φιλάγαθον [to philagathon], Eclogues 2, book 3, chapter 164, as also chapter 57, φιλάνθρωπον [philanthropon].

units.la: Obscuro ] De obscuro ait de l. 9. sup. eod.
units.tr: Unclear] He speaks of the unclear in law 9, above, same title.

units.la: Cuiusque ] puta testatoris, l. 12 sup. eod.
units.tr: Of each] That is, of the testator; law 12, above, same title.

units.la: Principium huius legis enarratum est supr. in l. 65.
units.tr: The beginning of this law was explained above, in law 65.

units.la: Ad §. Quod factum, &c.
units.tr: On the paragraph beginning "What is done", etc.

units.la: Varii sunt modi obscuritatis explicandæ, de quibus superius; Eos in summam digeram hoc loco, qui videlicet hoc titulo continentur. Non volo omnes, cum iurisperiti ea de re dicendo suppeditent innumeros: explicatur obscuritas eo assumto, quod verisimilius, est siue quod actum cogitatumque verisimilius videtur, quod plerunque fit, quod est minimum, quod est benignius, quod significatur, quod stat à re fauorabili, veluti libertate, dote, vel à persona fauorabili, vel rei gerendæ aptius, quod sententiæ proferentis proximius, & vt hic traditur, quod affectioni, charitati, necessitudini respondet. Affectio indicium voluntaris. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: There are various ways of clearing up obscurity, which were discussed above. Here I will set out in summary those that this title contains. I will not give all of them, since jurists in discussing this matter supply countless others. Obscurity is resolved by assuming what is more probable: whether what was done or intended is more likely, which usually happens; what is smallest; what is most favourable; what is signified; what leans toward a favourable thing, such as liberty or dowry, or a favourable person, or what is more suitable for the business to be carried out; what is closer to the judgement of the one pronouncing it; and, as is taught here, what corresponds to affection, charity or close kinship. Affection is a sign of the will. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 169. De eo quod pendet.
units.tr: On the law 169, concerning what is pending.

units.la: IS damnum dat, qui iubet dare: eius vero nulla culpa est, cui parere necesse est. §. Quod pendet, non est pro reo, quasi sit. Principium huius legis explicatum exemplis & ratione in leg. 157.
units.tr: He who orders damage to be done is the one who causes it; but no fault attaches to the one who must obey. §. What is pending is not against the defendant, as if it were. The beginning of this law has been explained by examples and reasoning in law 157.

units.la: Ad §. Quod pendet.
units.tr: On the paragraph "What is pending".

units.la: Hoc pertinet ad noxalem actionem. Statuliber tas, hoc est, libertas, quae pendet ex conditione & die, pro eo non est, quasi sit: quia statuliber detentus est noxae l. 19. de noxal. act. Cuia. in Recit.
units.tr: This pertains to the noxal action. A statuliber, that is, one whose liberty depends on a condition or a day, is not treated as if he were free, because a statuliber is held liable to noxal surrender (law 19, de noxalibus actionibus). Cuia. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 170. De facto à Iudice.
units.tr: On law 170, concerning a deed done by a judge.

units.la: Factum à Iudice, quod ad officium eius non pertinet, ratum non est.
units.tr: A deed done by a judge that does not pertain to his office is not valid.

units.la: Quod ad officium eius non pertinet, Græci interpretantur iurisdictionem; officium tamen latius patet: Nam & ea complectitur, quæ non sunt imperii, neque iurisdictionis. l. 1. de iurisdict. omn. iud. Sed forte iurisdictionem accipiunt pro notione, quod probo: Factum à iudice quod ad notionem eius non pertinet, ratum non est, ut si Iudex communi dividundo fundum hæreditarium non hereditario servire disponat. leg. ut fund. 18. comm. dividund. l. 10. usufruct. quemadmod. caveat. vel si Iudex familiæ erciscundæ fundum duobus hæredibus prælegatum dividat. l. item Labeo 22. §. 1. familiæ erciscund. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: The Greeks interpret "what does not pertain to his office" as jurisdiction; but office extends more widely, for it also embraces things that are neither of command nor of jurisdiction (law 1, de iurisdictione omnium iudicum). Perhaps, however, they take it to mean cognizance, which I prove thus: a deed done by a judge that does not pertain to his cognizance is not valid, as when a judge in the common action for dividing an inheritance orders a farm not to serve the inheritance (law "ut fundus", 18, communi dividundo; law 10, de usufructu quemadmodum cavetur), or when a judge in the action for dividing an estate divides a farm that has been given as a prelegacy to two heirs (law "item Labeo", 22, §1, familiae erciscundae). Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 171. De obligatione.
units.tr: On law 171, concerning obligation.

units.la: Nemo ideo obligatur, quia receptutus [?] est ab alio, quod praestiterit.
units.tr: No one is bound merely because another has been or will be recompensed for what he has performed.

units.la: Obligatur] Puta ad opus, sua impensa Titio restituendum.
units.tr: Is bound] For example, to restore the work to Titius at his own expense.

units.la: Quia] id est, Quamuis, vt sit sensus, non si socius impensas socii nomine factas ab eodem potest repetere, tenetur eas actori praestare, est enim iniquum, innocentem nocentis facto obligari l. 11. §. 2. sup. de aq. plu. Gothof.
units.tr: Because] that is, although; so that the sense is: if a partner cannot recover from the same partner the expenses incurred in the partner's name, he is nonetheless bound to make them good to the claimant, for it is unjust that an innocent person be bound by the deed of a wrongdoer. l. 11. §. 2. sup. de aq. plu. Gothof.

units.la: Recepturus est] iudicio communi diiudun-do scilicet.
units.tr: Will receive] namely, in the common action for dividing.

units.la: Ab alio] Puta a Maeuio, socio, qui opus Titio damnosum fecit.
units.tr: From another] For example, from Maevius, the partner, who did the damaging work to Titius.

units.la: Sumatur exemplum ex l. sup. 11. §. apud 2. de aq. & aq. plu. arc. Fundus communis est duo-rum, si in eo vnus opus facit, ex quo aqua plu-uia vicino nocet, alter non facit; hic qui non facit, non tenetur aquae pluuiae arcendae, vt o-pus restituat, quod actione communi diiudun-do recepturus sit a socio, quia nemo ideo ob-ligatur; & is, qui obligatus non est, non ideo obligatur, quod actionem habiturus sit de eo, quod praestiterit; alioquin obligaretur quili-ber hac ratione ad soluendum pro alio, quia recepturus est actione ne-gotii gesti. Cuiac. in
units.tr: Take as an example the law above, 11, §. "apud" 2, de aqua et aquae pluviae arcendae. A common field belongs to two persons. If one of them does work on it from which rainwater harms a neighbour, and the other does not, the one who does not is not bound to remove the rainwater by restoring the work, because he will recover it from his partner in the common action for dividing; no one is bound merely because he will have an action for what he has performed. Otherwise anyone would be bound on this ground to pay for another, because he will recover by the action of negotiorum gestio. Cuiac. in

units.la: Recit.
units.tr: Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 172. De ambiguis.
units.tr: On Leg. 172. Concerning ambiguities.

units.la: IN contrahenda venditione ambiguum pactum contra venditorem interpretandum est. Ambigua autem intentio, ita accipienda est, ut res salua actori sit.
units.tr: In making a sale, an ambiguous agreement is to be interpreted against the seller. An ambiguous claim, however, is to be understood so that the thing remains safe for the plaintiff.

units.la: Contra] Pactio obscura vel ambigua venditori nocet. L.39. sup. de pact. l.33. in sin. s de contrahend. emptione, & stipulatori. l.38. §.15. sup. de verb. obligat. quia potuit re integra apertius dicere l.21 sup. de contrah. empt. imo venditori est utilis L.34. sup. de contrahenda empt. solue ut ibidem. Gothof.
units.tr: Against] An obscure or ambiguous agreement harms the seller: L.39, above, de pact.; l.33 at the end, de contrahenda emptione; and the stipulator: l.38 §.15, above, de verb. oblig.; because he could have spoken more clearly while the matter was still whole: l.21, above, de contrah. empt. Indeed it is useful to the seller: L.34, above, de contrahenda empt.; solve as there. Gothofredus.

units.la: Interpretandum est] Aliud in oratione aperta, & magis verisimili. l.34. sup. eod. beneficiis principum. l.43. sup. de vulgar. iudiciis §.1. inf. eod. & confessione Decius hic. Gothof.
units.tr: Is to be interpreted] It is otherwise in an open and more plausible statement: l.34, above, eod.; (on) the benefices of princes; l.43, above, de vulgaribus iudiciis; §.1, below, eod.; and by confession, Decius here. Gothofredus.

units.la: Intentio] χάραγμα 2. ecl.3. cap.167. Intentio iudicialis ambigua secundum praesentem intelligitur l.66. sup. de iudiciis. l.20. in sin. sup. de exceptionem rei iud. c. l.83. §.1. sup. de verborum obligat. Gothof.
units.tr: Claim] [χάραγμα] a mark, 2 ecl. 3, cap. 167. A judicial claim that is ambiguous is understood according to the present (situation): l.66, above, de iudiciis; l.20 at the end, above, de exceptione rei iudicatae; l.83 §.1, above, de verborum obligationibus. Gothofredus.

units.la: Vtres] ne alioquin actus ipse pereat l.12. sup. de reb. dubiis.
units.tr: So that] lest otherwise the act itself perish: l.12, above, de rebus dubiis.

units.la: Sit] si id interpretatio ferre potest, quid enim si impugner testatoris voluntatem? l.7. sup. de vulg. quid si necessariis destituatur. l.2. §.7. sup. de dolo excep. Vide quae huc spectant sup. in l.69. Cuiac.
units.tr: Remain] if interpretation can bear it. For what if I were to attack the will of the testator? l.7, above, de vulgaribus; what if he is deprived of necessaries? l.2 §.7, above, de dolo et exceptione. See what pertains here above, in l.69. Cujacius.

units.la: Ad Leg. 173. Condemnati in id, quod facere possunt: De restitutione: De mora: de eo qui petit, quod redditururus est.
units.tr: On Leg. 173. Those condemned to what they are able to do; on restitution; on delay; on one who sues for what he is about to repay.

units.la: IN condemnatione personarum, quae in id, quod facere possunt, damnantur, non totum, quod habent, extorquendum est, sed & ipsarum ratio habenda est, ne egeant. Cum verbum, Restituas, in lege inuenitur, etsi non specialiter de fructibus additum est, tamen etiam fructus sunt restituendi. Vnicuique sua mora nocet, quod & in duobus reis obseruatur. Dolo facit qui petit, quod redditururus est.
units.tr: In the condemnation of persons who are condemned only to what they are able to do, not everything they have is to be extracted from them, but account is also to be taken of their circumstances, so that they do not lack necessities. When the word "restore" is found in a law, even if fruits are not specifically added, the fruits too are to be restored. Each person's delay harms himself alone, which is also observed in the case of two defendants. He acts with malice who sues for what he is about to repay.

units.la: Quae] l. 20. sup. eod. l. 12. sup. soluto. L6. sup. de reiud. 2. ecloga 3. cap. 169.
units.tr: Which] l.20, above, eod.; l.12, above, soluto; L.6, above, de re iudicata; 2 ecloga 3, cap. 169.

units.la: Egeant] l. 30. sup. de re indic.
units.tr: Lack] l.30, above, de re iudicata.

units.la: Restituas] v. l. 38. §. 4. sup. de vsur. l. 75. sup. de verborum significat. 2. ecl. 3. cap. 169.
units.tr: Restore] see l.38 §.4, above, de usuris; l.75, above, de verborum significatione; 2 ecl. 3, cap. 169.

units.la: Sua] vide l. 134. in sin. sup. eod. c. mora sua cuiuis est nocina 25. de regul. in 6. l. 5. sup. de reb. cred. l. 12. in sin. sup. deposit. l. 3. in sin. sup. de actionibus emt. l. 32. §. 3. sup. de vsur. L14. sup. de iure dot. l. 39. §. 1. vers. ipsum l. 47. in sin. sup. de leg. 1. l. 78. in princ. & §. 2. l. 48. sup. de legatis. 2. l. 18. sup. ad Trebellian. l. 12. sup. de aqua pluu. Goth.
units.tr: Own] see l.134 at the end, above, eod.; the saying: a person's own delay harms no one but himself, rule 25 de regulis in 6; l.5, above, de rebus creditis; l.12 at the end, above, depositi; l.3 at the end, above, de actionibus empti; l.32 §.3, above, de usuris; L.14, above, de iure dotium; l.39 §.1, the phrase "ipsum"; l.47 at the end, above, de legatis 1; l.78 at the beginning and §.2; l.48, above, de legatis 2; l.18, above, ad Trebellianum; l.12, above, de aqua pluvia. Gothofredus.

units.la: Nocet] nocet tamen mora rei fideiussori. l. 88. sup. de verb. oblig.
units.tr: Harms] yet the delay of a principal debtor does harm a surety: l.88, above, de verborum obligationibus.

units.la: Reis]
units.tr: Co-debtors]

units.la: Principium huius legis explicauimus sup. in l.28.
units.tr: I have explained the beginning of this law above, in l.28.

units.la: Ad §.1. Cum verbum, &c.
units.tr: On §.1. Since the word, etc.

units.la: Verbum; RESTITVAS, in legibus & edictis plenam significationem habet, vt etiam fructus restituantur, l. videamus 38. §. in Fabiana 4. de usur. quae est ex eodem lib. Cuiac.
units.tr: The word RESTORE, in laws and edicts, has its full meaning, so that the fruits too are restored: l. videamus 38 §. in Fabiana 4, de usuris, which is from the same book. Cujacius.

units.la: Ad §.2. Vnicuiq;, &c.
units.tr: On §.2. Each person's, etc.

units.la: non aduersario non correo, quod additur in hac regula dict. l. mora §. penult. at mora rei fideiussori nocet, quia scilicet fideiussiones accessiones sunt, quod in eod. lib. Paulus annotauerat, vt apparet ex l.88. de verb. oblig. Eadem regula de dolo traditur: vnicuique dolum suum nocere non alteri, l. si ex duob. de tut. & rationib. distrah. l. 9. quae in fraud. cred. l. si procurat. de doli except. sed quod regula ait de correis, ci ob. ei obstare videtur l. vlt. de duob. reis stipul. Verum ea de interruptione loquitur, non de mora. Interruptio generale quiddam est, mora fit in persona. Item obstare videtur l. penult. eod. tit. sed illa de facto loquitur (vt si vnus rem puta hominem promissum, occiderit) non de mora. Is qui moram non fecit, liberatur, te naturaliter peremta, etiamsi correus moram fecerit: nam mora fit in persona, is qui non occidit, si correus occiderit, non liberatur. Hoc factum, hæc culpa communis est, & in rem. Vulgo male eam appellant moram in faciendo, vt docui in l. 23. de verb. oblig.
units.tr: Not to the adversary, not to a co-obligor; what is added in this rule is the saying of the law on delay, §. penultimate. But delay of a principal debtor does harm a surety, because surety obligations are accessory, as Paulus had noted in the same book, as appears from l.88, de verborum obligationibus. The same rule is handed down concerning fraud: each person's fraud harms himself and not another, l. si ex duobus, de tutelis et rationibus distrahendis; l.9, quae in fraudem creditorum; l. si procurator, de doli exceptione. But what the rule says about co-obligors seems to be opposed by l. last, de duobus reis stipulandi. Yet that law speaks of interruption, not of delay. Interruption is something general; delay occurs in the person. Likewise l. penultimate under the same title seems to oppose, but that speaks of an act (as when one of them has killed the man promised), not of delay. He who did not cause the delay is freed, the thing having perished naturally, even if the co-obligor caused the delay; for delay occurs in the person: he who did not kill is not freed if the co-obligor killed. This act and this fault is common and affects the thing. Commonly, people wrongly call it delay in doing, as I showed in l.23, de verborum obligationibus.

units.la: Ad §. 3. Dolo facit, &c.
units.tr: On §. 3. "Dolo facit," etc.

units.la: Repetitus est hic §. ex l. 8. de dolo excep. quod redditurus est scilicet ei, à quo petit, non si alii l. si socer §. penult. solut. matrim. Iis obstare videtur l. 1. §. 1. quorum legat. verum, vt eleganter Iohannes ait, aliud est petere possessionem, aliud reddere, siue dare debere, sicut & effectu differunt. Nam aliud est proprietatem, aliud possessionem esse consecutum. Cuia. in Recit.
units.tr: This §. is repeated here from law 8, On the exception of fraud (de dolo excep.), namely that he is bound to return it to the one from whom he sues, not if it is to another (si alii), as in law "si socer" §. penult., On the solution of marriage (solut. matrim.). Law 1 §. 1, On those whose legacy (quorum legat.), seems to stand in the way. But, as John elegantly says, it is one thing to seek possession and another to return or give it, just as they differ in effect. For it is one thing to have obtained ownership, another to have obtained possession. Cuiacius, in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 174. Posse de repudiatione.
units.tr: On Law 174. Being able, concerning repudiation.

units.la: Qui potest facere, vt possit conditioni parere, iam posse videtur. §. Quod quis, si velit, habere non potest, id repudiare non potest.
units.tr: One who can bring it about that he is able to obey a condition is already seen to be able. §. What someone cannot have, if he wishes, he cannot repudiate.

units.la: Qui
units.tr: Who

units.la: ] Coniunge l.3.de bon.possess.
units.tr: ] Join with l.3.de bon.possess.

units.la: Non potest ] Quod non potest haberi, repudiari non potest. l.18. sup. de acquir. hæreditate.
units.tr: Cannot ] What cannot be had cannot be repudiated. l.18. sup. de acquir. hæreditate.

units.la: Non ] Repudiatio est quædam priuatio quæ subiectum aliquod præsupponit. l. 8. §. 2. sup. de optione l. 59. §. 6. in sin. sup. de hæredi. instit. v. l.3. sup. eod. Institutus sub conditione casuali non potest repudiare, antequam conditio extiterit. Idem est in substituto sub conditione potestativa. l.13. §. 1. de acquir. hæredit. Nam conditioni parendo non ideo videtur statim pro hærede gerere. l.5. de condit. & demonstr. Ergo potest repudiare. Contra conditioni non parendo, non statim videtur repudiare hæreditatem, l. 1. de curat. bon. dand. Ergo adire potest; conditione posteaimpleta: sed a Prætore præstituetur tempus, intra quod conditioni pareat. Hanc repudiare videtur, dummodo tamen id dicat, cum potest conditioni parere l. 1. §. qui sub condit. si quis omissa causa. testam. Idemque est, si tum id dicat, cum poterit facere, ut conditioni pareat, ut cum potest expedire negotia, quibus distringitur, ac tum instituere iter Alexandriam, cum forte hæc conditio adscripta fuisset, ut Alexandriam vel, &c. Cuiac.
units.tr: Not ] Repudiation is a kind of privation, which presupposes some subject. l. 8. §. 2. sup. de optione; l. 59. §. 6. in sin. sup. de hæredi. instit.; or l.3. sup. eod. One instituted under a casual condition cannot repudiate before the condition has been fulfilled. The same holds for a substitute under a potestative condition: l.13. §. 1. de acquir. hæredit. For by obeying the condition one is not thereby seen to act at once as heir: l.5. de condit. & demonstr. Therefore he can repudiate. On the other hand, by not obeying the condition, he is not at once seen to repudiate the inheritance: l. 1. de curat. bon. dand. Therefore he can take it up, once the condition is afterwards fulfilled; but the Praetor will fix a time within which he must obey the condition. He is seen to repudiate it, provided however that he says so at a time when he is able to obey the condition: l. 1. §. qui sub condit.; si quis omissa causa, testam. And it is the same if he says so at the time when he will be able to bring it about that he obeys the condition, as when he is able to settle the affairs by which he is hindered, and at that time to undertake a journey to Alexandria, when perhaps this condition had been attached, that he go to Alexandria or, etc. Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad §. Quod quis, &c.
units.tr: On §. "What someone," etc.

units.la: Hic §. iam explicatus est sup. in l. 3. Cuia.
units.tr: This §. has already been explained above, in law 3. Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad Leg. 175. Serui. Qui in alterius ius succedit.
units.tr: On Law 175. Slaves. One who succeeds into another's right.

units.la: IN his quæ officium per liberas fieri personas leges desiderant, seruus interuenire non potest. §. 1. Non debeo melioris conditionis esse, quam auctor meus, à quo ius in me transiit.
units.tr: In those matters which the laws require to be performed by free persons, a slave cannot intervene. §. 1. I ought not to be of a better condition than my author, from whom the right passed to me.

units.la: Quæ dicta sunt de fœminis in l. 2. sup. dicuntur etiam de seruis, nam ciuilia munera soli mares & liberi exercent. Ex hac ratione serui reipublicæ causa abesse non possunt l. vlt. inf. alia sunt officia seruilia, vel actuum gestus l. 1. §. 1. Cone quis liber. erat olim seruire tabellarii ossicium l. 3. de tab. exhib. alia sunt officia liberorum hominum. In principio legis malo legere, in his officiis, quæ. Cuiac.
units.tr: What has been said of women in law 2 above is also said of slaves, for civil offices are exercised only by free men. For this reason slaves cannot be absent for the sake of the commonwealth: last law below. Other duties are servile, or concern the performance of acts: law 1 §. 1, Whether anyone free... It was once servile to serve as a courier (tabellarii officium): law 3, On the production of tablets (de tab. exhib.). Other duties belong to free men. I would prefer to read at the beginning of the law: "in these duties which..." Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad §. Non debeo,
units.tr: On §. "I ought not,"

units.la: Hic §. expositus est in leg. Nemo plus iuris 54. sup. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: This §. has been set out in the law "Nemo plus iuris," 54 above. Cuiacius, in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 176. Ne singulis concedatur, quod per magistratum publice fieri potest. De libertate & necessitu- dine.
units.tr: On Law 176. That what can be done publicly through the magistrate should not be granted to individuals. On liberty and necessity.

units.la: Non est singulis concedendum, quod per magistratum publice possit fieri, ne occasio sit maioris tumultus faciendi. §. Infinita æstimatio est libertatis, & necessitudinis.
units.tr: What can be done publicly through the magistrate is not to be conceded to individuals, lest there be occasion of greater tumult. §. The estimate of liberty and of necessity is infinite.

units.la: Quæ iure potestatis fiunt & necessitudinis, ad iniuriarum actionem non pertinent. l. 13. §. quæ iure. de iniur. quod potest quis per magistratum, non potest per se. Cuiac.
units.tr: Things done by right of power and necessity do not belong to the action for injuries. Law 13, §. "quae iure," On injuries (de iniur.): what a person can do through the magistrate he cannot do on his own. Cuiacius.

units.la: Ad §. Infinita, &c.
units.tr: On §. "Infinite," etc.

units.la: Dixi de huius §. sensu sup. in l. libertas 106.
units.tr: I have spoken of the sense of this §. above, in the law "Libertas" 106.

units.la: Ad Leg. 177. Qui in ius alterius succe- dit. De ignorantia.
units.tr: On Law 177. One who succeeds into another's right. On ignorance.

units.la: Qui in ius dominiumve alterius succedit, iure eius uti debet. §. Nemo videtur dolo exseexsequi, qui ignorat causam, cur non debeat petere.
units.tr: One who succeeds into another's right or ownership ought to use his right. §. No one is seen to act with fraud who, being ignorant of the cause why he ought not to sue, sues.

units.la: Principium huius legis explicatum in l. nemo 54; hoc tit.
units.tr: The beginning of this law has been explained in law "Nemo" 54; this title.

units.la: Ad §. Nemo videtur, &c.
units.tr: On §. "No one is seen," etc.

units.la: Exsequi est petere; exlecutio est petitio; l. in exsecut. §. de verb. obligat. Qui petit, non repellitur exceptione doli, si ignorat causam, cur non debeat petere. l. 2. §. sed & generaliter. de dolo except. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: To pursue (exsequi) is to seek; execution (exlecutio) is a petition: law "in exsecut." §. On the meaning of obligation (de verb. obligat.). One who sues is not repelled by the exception of fraud if he is ignorant of the cause why he ought not to sue: law 2 §. "sed & generaliter," On the exception of fraud (de dolo except.). Cuiacius, in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 178. De principali & accessorio.
units.tr: On the Law 178. On the principal and the accessory.

units.la: Cum principalis causa non consistit, plerunque ne ea quidem, quæ sequuntur, locum habent.
units.tr: When the principal cause does not stand, as a rule the things that follow from it do not take effect either.

units.la: Hanc sententiam etiam Paulus lib. 21. ad edictum expresserat. Unde est l. 129. sup. ubi explicata est.
units.tr: Paul also expressed this opinion in book 21 on the Edict. Hence law 129 above, where it is explained.

units.la: Ad Leg. 179. De obscura voluntate manumittentis.
units.tr: On the Law 179. On the unclear will of a manumitter.

units.la: I N obscura voluntate manumittentis, fauendum est libertati.
units.tr: In an unclear will of a manumitter, liberty is to be favoured.

units.la: fn. Coniunge l. si pecul. de statulib.
units.tr: Note: join the law si pecul. de statulib.

units.la: Libertati v. l. 20. sup. eod. 2. ecl. 3. c. 175.
units.tr: On liberty, see law 20 above, same title, 2nd edition, 3rd book, 175.

units.la: Eandem sententiam aliis verbis expressit Pompon. in l. quoties 20. sup. vbi exemplum tale ponitur: Seruus liber esse iussus, simulque ei legatum traditum est, si filius ad 14. annum peruenerit; Filius non peruenit ad 14. annum; Legatum perimitur, libertas competit. Nec propterea competit ex testamento; nam sic etiam competeret legatum, sed competit iure singulari; quia interpretamur pro libertate, licet legatum non competat. Quid si seruus iussus est liber esse, & hoc amplius fundum sibi habere, si hæredi decem dederit mortuo hærede non acceptis decem, an fiet liber? Ac si paratam pecuniam morte hæredis non habuerit; dicemus legatum perimi, libertatem conseruari, non ex testamento, sed ex constituto iure. l. si seruus 19. cum l. seq. §. is cui de statuliberis. Similiter si seruus sit legatus testamento primum; deinde eodem testamento liber esse iussus sit, & legatum ei relictum, legatum adimetur, libertas præstabitur. Et contra primum liber esse iussus est, deinde legatus alteri, an vindicetur libertas? minime, nisi euidenter constet esse ademtam. Item Stichus liber esse iubetur; duo sunt Stichi, neuter liber erit l. ex piurib. 31. de manumiss. test. quia constitutiones nihil inducunt sine colore aliquo; Hic nullo colore defendi libertas potest, qui enim nomen expressit, de certo Sticho sensit, itaque noluit, duos libertos fieri: ius non deest, sed probatio; Propter incertam igitur voluntatem, neutri debetur. Eo modo licet causa tutoris sit fauorabilis, tamen si testator Titium dederit tutorem, & duo sint Titii, neuter erit; l. duo sunt Titij 30. de test. tut. non deficit fauor, sed color fauoris inducendi. Atque rursus quaeritur, si testator legauit Stichum & duos Stichos habuerit, quis debeatur? Et minorem deberi dicimus, l. si seruus §. vlt. de legat.
units.tr: Pomponius expressed the same opinion in other words in in l. quoties 20 sup., where this example is given: a slave is ordered to be free, and at the same time a legacy is handed over to him if his son reaches the age of 14. The son does not reach the age of 14. The legacy is extinguished, but liberty is due. Liberty is due not by virtue of the will, for the legacy would also have been due in that case; it is due by a special right, because we interpret in favour of liberty even though the legacy is not due. What if a slave is ordered to be free and, in addition, to have a farm for himself if he gives ten to the heir, and the heir dies without the ten having been received: will he become free? And if he did not have the money ready at the heir's death, we will say that the legacy is extinguished but liberty is preserved, not by the will but by the established law: l. si seruus 19, cum l. seq. §. is cui de statuliberis. Similarly, if a slave was first bequeathed by will, and then, in the same will, ordered to be free and a legacy left to him, the legacy is taken away and liberty is granted. And conversely, if he was first ordered to be free and then bequeathed to another, is liberty to be claimed? By no means, unless it is plainly clear that it has been revoked. Likewise, Stichus is ordered to be free, but there are two Stichi: neither will be free, l. ex piurib. 31. de manumiss. test., because constitutions introduce nothing without some ground; here liberty cannot be defended on any ground, for he who expressed the name thought of a particular Stichus, and so did not wish two to be made free. The right is not lacking, but the proof is. Because the will is uncertain, therefore neither is owed. In the same way, although the cause of a guardian is favourable, yet if the testator has given Titius as guardian, and there are two Titii, neither will be guardian: l. duo sunt Titij 30. de test. tut. The favour is not lacking, but the ground for applying the favour. And again the question arises: if the testator bequeathed Stichus and there were two Stichi, which one is owed? We say the lesser is owed: l. si seruus §. vlt. de legat.

units.la: 1. Sic etiam, testator legat Titio, duo sunt Titii eiusdem nominis, valet legatum, & praestabitur ei, cui haeres voluerit. l. 3. §. si duobus de alim leg. ratio diuersitatis est, quia libertas relinquitur directo, & competit ipso iure, non videtur venire ab haerede, & Orcinus ille libertus dicitur. Item de tutoris datione constitutum est, eam non tenere, nisi directis fiat verbis. l. 1. de confirm. tut. quae ait inutilem esse datio nem tutoris, si detur qui non potest dari; item inutilem, si non detur, quando oportet, male equidem, si detur rebus, non personis. Sed si illa tota lex legatur, patet inutiliter dari, hoc modo, rogo te, sis tutor. Nam precaria verba sunt: cum directis verbis sit vtendum, legati hæc causa est, vt præstetur ab hærede: itaque incertum explicare potest ipse hæres præstando legatum, eligeret, quem volet, vel dabit, cui volet, sed tutore dato, vel libertate, non est qui possit explicare. Cuia. in Recit.
units.tr: 1. Likewise, if a testator leaves something to Titius and there are two Titii of the same name, the legacy is valid, and it will be paid to whichever one the heir chooses: l. 3. §. si duobus de alim leg. The reason for the difference is that liberty is left directly and is due by law itself; it does not seem to come from the heir, and that freedman is called Orcinus. Likewise, it has been established concerning the appointment of a guardian that it does not hold unless it is made in direct words: l. 1. de confirm. tut., which says that the appointment of a guardian is invalid if one is appointed who cannot be appointed, and likewise invalid if none is appointed when it ought to be; indeed, badly, if it is given to things and not to persons. But if that whole law is read, it is clear that it is given in vain in this manner: "I ask you, be guardian, if you please." For these are entreating words; since direct words must be used, the purpose of the legacy is that it be paid by the heir. Thus, when the expression is uncertain, the heir himself, by paying the legacy, may explain it: he will choose whom he wishes, or give it to whom he wishes; but once a guardian has been appointed, or liberty granted, there is no one who can explain it. Cuia. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 180. De eo qui iussu alterius soluit.
units.tr: On the Law 180. On one who pays at another's order.

units.la: QVod iussu alterius soluitur, pro eo est, quasi ipsi solutum esset.
units.tr: What is paid at another's order is regarded as paid to himself.

units.la: Quod ] coniunge legem, si donaturus de condict. causa data.
units.tr: Quod ] join it with the law if he is about to give, on the condictio for a cause given.

units.la: Iussu ] v. l. 56. sup. de solut. ecl. ibid. c. 176.
units.tr: "At another's order": see law 56 above, de solut., same chapter, 176.

units.la: Quod iussu meo soluis alteri, mihi soluisse videris; ergo liberaris leg. cum iussu 64. de solut. certum est, etiam me teneri condictione indebiti, si per errorem indebitum solueris: Est & aliis effectus huius regulæ, in l. mortuo herede 15. §. vlt. de statu liber. Iunge l. si donaturus 9. de condict. causa dat. Cuia in Recit.
units.tr: If you pay another at my order, you seem to have paid me, and therefore I am discharged: leg. cum iussu 64. de solut. It is certain that I am also liable to the action for what was not owed, if you paid what was not owed through error. There are also other effects of this rule: in l. mortuo herede 15. §. vlt. de statu liber. Join l. si donaturus 9. de condict. causa dat. Cuia in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 181. Si nemo adierit ex testamento.
units.tr: On the Law 181. If no one has entered upon the inheritance under the will.

units.la: SI nemo subiit hæreditatem, omnis vis testamenti soluitur.
units.tr: If no one has taken up the inheritance, the whole force of the will is dissolved.

units.la: Nemo ] l 12. §. 5. sup. de bon. libert. l. 1. §. 1. sup. quis ordo in bonorum possess.
units.tr: Nemo ] law 12, §. 5, above, de bonis libertorum; law 1, §. 1, above, quis ordo in bonorum possessione.

units.la: Omnis vis ] omne ius.
units.tr: "The whole force": the whole right.

units.la: Soluitur ] & res ad intestati causam redit. d. §.1. l.89. sup. eod. l.9 sup. de test. tut. l. 10. §.4. in fine l,38. in sin. sup. de vulg. nisi hæredes pro adita habeant, & nisi testator pro adita esse velit, quod sæpissime euenit propter codicillos, vel similes clausulas. Goth.
units.tr: "Is dissolved": and the matter returns to the cause of intestacy. d. §.1. l. 89. sup. eod. l. 9 sup. de test. tut. l. 10. §. 4. in fine l. 38. in sin. sup. de vulg. unless the heirs hold that they have entered, and unless the testator wishes it to be regarded as entered, which very often happens on account of codicils or similar clauses. Goth.

units.la: Subiire est adire, vt docui in obseruat. Cum semel adita est hæreditas, omnis defuncti voluntas constituitur. l. si patroni 55. §. qui fideicommissum ad Senatusconf. Trebell. contra si nemo adierit, constituitur irrita l. 9. de test. tutel. Leam quam C. de fideicommiss. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: To take up is to enter upon, as I have explained in the observations. Once the inheritance has been entered upon, the whole will of the deceased is established: l. si patroni 55. §. qui fideicommissum ad Senatusconf. Trebell. On the contrary, if no one has entered, it is established as void: l. 9. de test. tutel. Leam quam C. de fideicommiss. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 182. De eo quod nullius esse potest.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 182. Concerning that which can belong to no one.

units.la: QVod nullius esse potest, id, vt alicuius fieret, nulla obligatio valet efficere.
units.tr: Whatever can belong to no one, no obligation has the power to make it belong to someone.

units.la: Nullius ] l. 82. §. 5. sup. de verborum obligat. 2. ecl. 3. c. 178.
units.tr: Of no one ] l. 82. §. 5. sup. de verborum obligat. 2. ecl. 3. c. 178.

units.la: Liber homo nullius esse potest, & ideo in obligationem deduci non potest, quia ea sola in obligatione consistere possunt, quæ pecunia lui darique possunt. L.1. §. penult. de statulib. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: A free man can belong to no one, and therefore cannot be brought into an obligation, because only those things can exist in an obligation that can be paid or given in money. L.1. §. penult. de statulib. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 183. Solemnia non facile mutanda.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 183. Solemn forms are not to be changed easily.

units.la: ETsi nihil facile mutandum est in solemnibus ; tamen vbi æquitas euidens poscit, subuenientendum est.
units.tr: Although nothing should easily be changed in solemn forms, nevertheless where evident equity demands it, help must be given.

units.la: Vbi] l. 85. in sin. l. 90. de in integ. l. 2. sup. de const. princip. de æquitate alibi dixi. Goth.
units.tr: Where ] l. 85. in sin. l. 90. de in integ. l. 2. sup. de const. princip. I have discussed equity elsewhere. Goth.

units.la: Repetita est ex leg. penultim. de in integ. restit. aliud addatur exemplum ex l. si seruus communis 8. de noxa. act. Cuiac.
units.tr: It is repeated from leg. penultim. de in integ. restit. Let another example be added from l. si seruus communis 8. de noxa. act. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 184. De vano timore.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 184. Concerning groundless fear.

units.la: VAni timoris iusta excusatio non est.
units.tr: A groundless fear is no lawful excuse.

units.la: Vani ] v. l. 4. sup. si cui plus, quam per legem; & l. 13. sup. de re indica. qui ἄλογος & μάταιος z. Eccl. 3. c. 180.
units.tr: Vain: see l. 4 above, si cui plus, quam per legem; and l. 13 above, de re iudicata, "qui"; [ἄλογος] unreasonable and [μάταιος] vain; see Eccl. 3, c. 180.

units.la: Bulgarus & Iohannes legunt: non iusta excusatio est; sed legendum, nulla æstimatio, ex l. si quis ab alio 13. de re iudicata, & illius legis inscriptio verior fortasse est, de specie vide Cuiac. in l. 98. de verb. obligat.
units.tr: Bulgarus and Iohannes read: it is not a lawful excuse; but it should be read: no estimation (nulla æstimatio), from l. si quis ab alio 13. de re iudicata. The inscription of that law is perhaps truer, concerning the kind of case; see Cuiac. on l. 98. de verb. obligat.

units.la: Ad Leg. 185. De impossibilibus.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 185. Concerning impossibilities.

units.la: IMpossibilium nulla obligatio est.
units.tr: There is no obligation to impossible things.

units.la: Impossibilium ] v. l. 135. l. 182. sup. eod. l. 35. l. 69. sup. de verbor. obligat. ecl. 9. d. loco c. 181. c. nemo potest ad impossibile obligari 6. de reg. in 6.
units.tr: Impossible: see l. 135 and l. 182 above in the same title, and l. 35 and l. 69 above, de verborum obligationibus; see 9, d. loco, c. 181; the canon "No one can be bound to the impossible", 6 de regulis iuris in 6.

units.la: Nulla obligatio, ciuilis aut naturalis {*}scil. l.31. sup. Qua de causa ex falsa confessione non teneor, nisi naturæ conueniat. l. confessionib. 13. §. 1. & l. seq. § vlt. de interrog. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: No obligation, civil or natural {*}namely l.31. sup. For this reason I am not bound by a false confession, unless it agrees with nature. l. confessionib. 13. §. 1. and the following law, final §. de interrog. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 186. Quando peti potest.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 186. When a thing may be demanded.

units.la: NIhil peti potest ante id tempus, quo per naturam solui possit; & cum soluendi tempus obligationi additur, nisi eo tempore præterito, peti non potest.
units.tr: Nothing can be demanded before the time at which it can by nature be paid; and when a time of payment is added to an obligation, it cannot be demanded unless that time has passed.

units.la: Ex stipulatione, cui tacite inest tractus temporis, agi non potest, antequam id tempus præterierit l. quoties 24. de oper. libert. l. interdum pura 73. de verb. obligat. similiter ex stipulatione, cui tempus palam additum est, agi non potest, nisi tempore præterito. §. omnis Instit. de verb. obligat. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: An action cannot be brought on a stipulation in which a tacit lapse of time is implied, before that time has passed. l. quoties 24. de oper. libert. l. interdum pura 73. de verb. obligat. Similarly, on a stipulation to which a time has been openly added, action cannot be brought unless the time has passed. §. omnis Instit. de verb. obligat. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 187. Qui uxorem prægnan- tem reliquit.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 187. Whoever leaves a pregnant wife.

units.la: SI quis uxorem prægnantem reliquit, non videtur sine liberis decessisse.
units.tr: If anyone leaves a pregnant wife, he is not regarded as having died without children.

units.la: Prægnantem] l. 18. sup. quando dies legati. ecl. ibid. c. 183. Sine liberis] de hac conditione adde l.77.§. 13.l.89.§.5.sup.de lega.2.l.17.§.4.sup.ad Trebell.l. 148.sup.de verb.signif.
units.tr: Pregnant: see l. 18 above, quando dies legati; ibid., c. 183. "Without children": on this condition add l. 77 §13, l. 89 §5 above, de legatis 2, l. 17 §4 above, ad Trebellianum, and l. 148 above, de verborum significatione.

units.la: Orbitatis olim erant poenae quaedam; orbi sunt, qui liberos non habent, sed qui vxorem praegnantem reliquit, non videtur orbus decessisse; consequenter & patronum habet is, cuius patronus mortuus est, relicta vxore praegnante, orba etiam non videtur, quae moritur pleno vtero, nam etsi mortuae filius extrahitur, videtur tempore mortis filium habuisse. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: Bereavement once carried certain penalties; those are bereaved who have no children. But he who leaves a pregnant wife is not regarded as having died bereaved; consequently, too, one whose patron has died, leaving a pregnant wife, does not seem to be bereaved either. Nor is she regarded as bereaved who dies with a full womb, for even if the child is taken from the dead mother, it is considered that the child existed at the time of death. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg.188. Si testator pugnantia iusse- rit. De impossibilibus.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 188. If a testator has ordered contradictory things. Concerning impossibilities.

units.la: VBi pugnantia inter se in testamento iubentur, neutrum ratum est.
units.tr: Where contradictory things are ordered in a will, neither is valid.

units.la: Quae rerum natura prohibentur, nulla lege confirmata sunt.
units.tr: Things which are forbidden by the nature of things have not been confirmed by any law.

units.la: Pugnantia] 2.Eccl.3.cap.184.l.16.sup.de condit.instit.l.13.§.3.l.27.sup.de reb.dub.v.l.14. C. de fide instrum.
units.tr: Contradictory ] 2. Eccl. 3. cap. 184. l. 16. sup. de condit. instit. l. 13. §. 3. l. 27. sup. de reb. dub. v. l. 14. C. de fide instrum.

units.la: Prohibentur] v.l.185.sup.eod. adde l.12.§.2. sup.de captivis. eclog.d.loco.
units.tr: Forbidden ] v. l. 185. sup. eod. add l. 12. §. 2. sup. de captivis. eclog. d. loco.

units.la: Vt, si iusserim agrum in familia retineri, ac deinde iusserim Titio eundem vendi certo pretio, neutrum valet; Atque dici solet, nouissimam simam scripturam spectari. Hoc cum sola legati causa mutatur; Cum enim adimitur, quod antea testatorem voluisse constat, neutrum ratum est. Qua de causa etsi iubeat seruum manumitti, ac deinde eundem seruum iubeat Titio praestari, si obscurum sit, an ante, vel post libertatem eam legauerit, neutrum valere videtur, hoc tamen fauore libertatis praevalere dicimus.
units.tr: For example, if I order that a field be kept in the family, and then order that the same field be sold to Titius for a certain price, neither order is valid. And it is customary to say that the last writing is regarded. This changes only where the matter is a legacy; for when something is taken away which the testator is known to have wished before, neither order stands. For this reason, even if he orders a slave to be manumitted and then orders the same slave to be delivered to Titius, if it is unclear whether he bequeathed him before or after the freedom, neither seems valid; yet we say that, out of favour to liberty, the freedom prevails.

units.la: Ad §. Quaererum, &c.
units.tr: Ad §. Quaererum, &c.

units.la: Si minor adoptauerit maiorem, haec adoptio nulla est, nec vlla lege confirmatur, alias adoptio non iure facta, a principe confirmari potest l. adoptio. 38. de adopt. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: If a younger man has adopted an older man, this adoption is void and is not confirmed by any law; otherwise an adoption not made lawfully may be confirmed by the prince. l. adoptio. 38. de adopt. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 189. De pupillo & authoritate tutoris.
units.tr: On Law 189. On the Pupil and the Authority of the Guardian.

units.la: Pupillus nec velle, nec nolle in ea aetate nisi apposita tutoris auctoritate creditur. Nam quod animi iudicio fit, in eo tutoris authoritas necessaria est.
units.tr: A pupil is not believed to will or to be unwilling at that age unless the guardian's authority is added. For what is done by the judgment of the mind requires the guardian's authority.

units.la: Pupillus] l. 43. sup. de oblig. ecl. ibidem. cap. 185.
units.tr: Pupillus] Law 43, above, on obligations, ecl. ibid. chap. 185.

units.la: Velle] v. l. 2. §. 19. sup. vi bonarum rapt.
units.tr: Velle] See law 2, §19, above, on violent seizure of goods.

units.la: De hac lege dixi in l. 3. sup. inscriptio suspecta est, quia non seruatur series librorum. Cuiac.
units.tr: I discussed this law in law 3, above. The inscription is suspect, because the order of the books is not kept. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 190. De evictione.
units.tr: On Law 190. On Eviction.

units.la: Quod evincitur, in bonis non est.
units.tr: What is evicted is not among the goods.

units.la: Evincitur] l. 52. sup. de acquir. rerum dominio l. 25. sup. de verborum signif.
units.tr: Evincitur] law 52, above, on the acquisition of ownership of things; law 25, above, on the meaning of words.

units.la: In bonis] v. l. 49. sup. de verb. signif.
units.tr: In bonis] see law 49, above, on the meaning of words.

units.la: Non est] Imo est, v. l. 15. §. 6. sup. qui satisdare.
units.tr: Non est] Rather it is; see law 15, §6, above, on who must give security.

units.la: Et ideo non liberatur, qui rem, quae evincitur, soluit. l. Si homo. 69. de sol. quae evincitur; etsi nondum evicta sit, vel etiam quae evinci possit. l. 139. §. vlt. nec etiam in bonis esse videtur, nisi quod retinere possumus. l. rem in bonis 52. de acquir. rerum domin. l. non videtur 22. de acquir. possess. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: And so one who pays a thing that is evicted is not released. Law "Si homo", 69, on payment. Which is evicted; even if it has not yet been evicted, or even which can be evicted. Law 139, §last. Nor does it seem to be among the goods, except what we can keep. Law "rem in bonis" 52, on the acquisition of ownership; law "non videtur" 22, on the acquisition of possession. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 191. De beneficio principis.
units.tr: On Law 191. On the Emperor's Favour.

units.la: Neratius consultus, an quod beneficium se dare quasi viventi Caesar rescripserat, iam defuncto dedisse existimaretur? respondit, non videri sibi principem, quod ei, quem viuere existimabat, concessisset, defuncto concessisse, quem tamen modum sui beneficii esse vellet, ipsius existimationem esse.
units.tr: Neratius, being asked whether a favour which the Emperor had granted by rescript to a man as if he were still living was to be thought granted to him after he was already dead, answered that it did not seem to him that the prince, having granted something to one whom he believed to be alive, had granted it to one who was dead; but what limit he wished his favour to have, that was a matter for the prince's own judgment.

units.la: Iam] Priuilegium alicui datum tanquam viuenti, ei mortuo non competit, id est, ad haeredes non extenditur eclo. ibid. cap. 187. facit lex 2. sup. qua sententia sine appellatione.
units.tr: Iam] A privilege given to someone as if he were living does not pass to him once he is dead; that is, it is not extended to his heirs. See the same, ibid. chap. 187. Compare law 2, above, on a sentence without appeal.

units.la: Ipsius] interpretatio priuilegii, vel beneficii spectat ad principem, qui concessit. l. 43. sup. de vulgari. ecl. ibid.
units.tr: Ipsius] The interpretation of a privilege or favour belongs to the prince who granted it. Law 43, above, on vulgar substitution, ibid.

units.la: Beneficium, quod princeps viuenti concessit (vt si quid largiatur viuenti) iam defuncto non concessisse videtur, argumento l. de qua re 74. de iudic. sed suum ipse beneficium interpretabitur ex animi sententia. l. ex facto quaeritur 43. de vulg. subst. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: A favour which the prince granted to a living person (for example, if he bestows something on one who is alive) is not considered to have been granted once that person is dead, by argument from law "de qua re" 74, on judgments; but he himself will interpret his own favour according to the sense of his mind. Law "ex facto quaeritur" 43, on vulgar substitution. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 192. De heredibus & obligatione indiuidua. De re dubia.
units.tr: On Law 192. On Heirs and Indivisible Obligation. On a Doubtful Matter.

units.la: EA, quae in partes diuidi non possunt, solida à singulis heredibus debentur. §. In re dubia benigniorem interpretationem sequi, non minus iustius est, quam tutius.
units.tr: Those things which cannot be divided into parts are owed in full by each of the heirs. To follow the more favourable interpretation in a doubtful matter is no less just than it is safer.

units.la: Non possunt ] vt via, vt actus : aquaeductus. L. 17. sup. de seruitutibus l. 11. §. 24. sup. de legat. 3. l. vlt. sup. de seruit. legat.
units.tr: Non possunt ] As a way, as an act: an aqueduct. Law 17, above, on servitudes; law 11, §24, above, on legacies; law 3, last, above, on legacies of servitudes.

units.la: Solida ] l. 2. §. 2. sup. de verb. obligat.
units.tr: Solida ] Law 2, §2, above, on the meaning of obligations.

units.la: Benigniorem ] v. L. 155. in sin. sup. eod. l. 54. sup. de acquirend. hereditate.
units.tr: Benigniorem ] See law 155, at the end, above, same title; law 54, above, on acquiring an inheritance.

units.la: Ea, quae diuidi possunt, debentur ab heredibus, portionibus hereditariis ex 12. Tabulis; quae diuidi non possunt, vt iura praediorum, solida debentur à singulis. l. heredes 25. §. 9. familiaris hercisc. l. 2. §. his de verb. obligat. Sumatur aliud exemplum ex l. si duo 22. deposit.
units.tr: Those things which can be divided are owed by heirs in proportion to their hereditary shares, under the Twelve Tables; those which cannot be divided, such as rights over estates, are owed in full by each of the heirs. Law "heredes" 25, §9, on partition of a family inheritance; law 2, §"his", on the meaning of obligations. Let another example be taken from law "si duo" 22, on deposit.

units.la: Ad §. In re dubia, &c.
units.tr: On §. In a doubtful matter, etc.

units.la: Vide sup. l. 58. Cuiac.
units.tr: See above, law 58. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 193. De aditione cum tempore mortis continuanda.
units.tr: Ad Leg. 193. On continuing the acceptance of the inheritance up to the time of death.

units.la: OMnia fere iura hæredum perinde habentur, ac si continuo sub tempus mortis hæredes extitissent.
units.tr: Almost all the rights of heirs are held as if they had become heirs continuously, right up to the time of death.

units.la: Continuo] v. l. 3. sup. de hered. petit. l 5. §. 1. sup. quod cum eo. l. 7. in sin. sup. de acquir. hered. l. 65. l. 70. sup. de verb. significatione l. ult. C. de hered. instituend. Goth.
units.tr: Continuously] See above, book 3, on the petition of inheritance, law 5, §1; above, on what is done with him, law 7 at the end; above, on the acquisition of inheritances, law 65, law 70, on the meaning of words; the last law of the Code, on the institution of heirs. Goth.

units.la: Quod hic dicitur, idem ex Paulo relatum est supra in l. 138. vbi vide Cuia.
units.tr: What is said here is also related from Paul above in law 138, where see Cujas.

units.la: Ad Leg. 194. De hæredibus hæredum.
units.tr: On Law 194. On the heirs of heirs.

units.la: QVi per successionem; quamuis longissimam, defuncto hæredes constituerunt, non minus hæredes intelliguntur, quam qui principaliter hæredes existunt.
units.tr: QThose who, by succession however remote, have appointed heirs after the death of the one who died are understood to be no less heirs than those who are heirs in the first place.

units.la: Successionem] cessionem.
units.tr: Successionem] cessionem.

units.la: Longissimam] nisi hæredis vocabulo adiecta sit restrictio, puta, lego hæredibus infra scriptis, nisi agatur de odio, nisi quædam specialis affectio defuncti aliud requirat. v. Decium hic Gothofr.
units.tr: Longissimam] unless a restriction is added to the word "heirs," for example, "I bequeath to the heirs written below," unless the matter concerns hatred, or unless some special affection of the deceased requires otherwise. See Decius here, and Gothofredus.

units.la: Constituerunt] alii exstiterunt.
units.tr: Constituerunt] others read exstiterunt (have arisen).

units.la: Hæres hæredis est hæres testatoris l. vlt. C. de hæred. instit. Hæres scriptus directe, principaliter suo nomine l. vlt. de legat. 3. Non hæres hæredis per successionem, nam hic alieno nomine, non suo, non ex iudicio defuncti venit. l. qui liberis 8. §. vlt. de vulg. & pupill. substit. nisi ab eo fideicommissum relinquatur, l. 5. §. 1. de legat. 3. sicut legitimus hæres remotior ex iudicio defuncti non venit, nisi ab eo fideicommissum relinquatur l. 1. §. 1. de legat. 3. & incertus est l. sciendum 70. de verborum signif. quæ differentiam facit in quibusdam speciebus, vbi hæredis appellatione non comprehendantur. Cuiac. in Recit.
units.tr: An heir of an heir is an heir of the testator, l. vlt. C. de hæred. instit. A directly written heir, principally, in his own name, l. vlt. de legat. 3. A remote heir by succession is not an heir of the heir, for he comes in another's name, not his own, and not by the judgment of the deceased, l. qui liberis 8. §. vlt. de vulg. & pupill. substit. unless a trust is left to him by the deceased, l. 5. §. 1. de legat. 3. Just as a more remote legitimate heir does not come by the judgment of the deceased, unless a trust is left to him by the deceased, l. 1. §. 1. de legat. 3. And the rule is uncertain, l. sciendum 70. de verborum signif. which makes a difference in certain kinds of cases where the term "heir" does not include them. Cuiac. in Recit.

units.la: Ad Leg. 195. De expressis & tacitis.
units.tr: On Law 195. On express and tacit matters.

units.la: EXpressa nocent; non expressa non nocent. Nocent] Interdum. l. 77 sup. eod. l. 77. inf. sup. de condit. & demonstr. Interdum vero magis prosunt, quam tacita. de quib. vide Decum hic. Goth.
units.tr: Express things harm; things not expressed do not harm. Harm] sometimes. l. 77 sup. eod. l. 77. inf. sup. de condit. & demonstr. Sometimes, indeed, they benefit more than tacit ones. On these, see Decius here. Goth.

units.la: Vim huius reg. exposui in l. actus legitimi 77. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: I have set out the force of this rule in l. actus legitimi 77. sup. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 196. De priuilegiis.
units.tr: On Law 196. On privileges.

units.la: PRiuilegia quædam causæ sunt, quædam personæ: & ideo quædam ad hæredem transftransmittuntur, quæ causæ sunt, quæ personæ sunt, ad hæredem non transeunt.
units.tr: Some privileges are attached to things, others to persons. Therefore some pass to the heir, those attached to things; those attached to persons do not pass to the heir.

units.la: Ad Leg. 197. De coniunctionibus, licito & honesto.
units.tr: On Law 197. On conjunctions, the lawful and the honourable.

units.la: Semper in coniunctionibus non solum quid liceat, considerandum est, sed quid & honestum sit.
units.tr: In conjunctions one must consider not only what is permitted, but also what is honourable.

units.la: Eandem sententiam retulit sup. leg. 144. in princip. ex Paulo, vbi vide Cuiac.
units.tr: He gave the same opinion above in law 144, at the beginning, drawn from Paul, where see Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 198. De dolo tutoris.
units.tr: On Law 198. On the fraud of a guardian.

units.la: Neque in interdicto, neque in cæteris causis pupillo nocere oportet dolum tutoris, siue soluendo est, siue non est.
units.tr: Neither in an interdict nor in other cases ought the fraud of a guardian to harm a ward, whether the guardian is solvent or not.

units.la: Siue ] 2. Ecl. 3. cap. 194.
units.tr: Whether] 2. Ecl. 3, chap. 194.

units.la: Ex dolo tutoris pupillus non tenetur interdicto, quod vi aut clam l. 11. §. si tutoris, quod vi aut clam. auctor huius regulæ illo loco nominatur Cassius, & sane inscriptio eruta est ex libris Cassii. Non tenetur etiam interdicto, de tabulis exhibendis. Huic regulæ locus est, siue solummodo tutor sit, siue non, videlicet, si pupillus ex dolo tutoris locupletior factus non sit. Nam si locupletior factus sit, tenetur l. sed & ex dolo 15. de dol. leg. apud 4. §. illa etiam 23. de dolo except. Et tenetur indistincte, siue soluendo tutor sit, siue non, cum scilicet dolus ex contractu descendit: Extra contractum non tenetur, nisi tutor soluendo sit. Cætera in l. Heredib. de dolo. vide apud. Cuiac.
units.tr: A ward is not liable under the interdict "concerning force or stealth" for the fraud of a guardian, l. 11. §. si tutoris, quod vi aut clam. The author of this rule is named in that passage as Cassius, and indeed the wording has been drawn from the books of Cassius. He is not liable under the interdict on the production of documents either. This rule applies whether the person is only a guardian or not, namely, if the ward has not become richer through the guardian's fraud. For if he has become richer, he is liable, l. sed & ex dolo 15. de dol. leg. apud 4. §. illa etiam 23. de dolo except. and he is liable without distinction, whether the guardian is solvent or not, since the fraud arises from a contract. Outside a contract he is not liable unless the guardian is solvent. For the rest, see in l. Heredib. de dolo, apud Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 199. De eo, qui imperio Magi- stratus non paruit.
units.tr: On Law 199. On one who did not obey the command of the magistrate.

units.la: Non potest dolo carere, qui imperio magistratus non paruit.
units.tr: One who has not obeyed the command of a magistrate cannot be free of fraud.

units.la: Non paruit ] l. unica sup. si quis ius dicenti l. 13. §. 2. sup. de iniuriis.
units.tr: Did not obey ] the single law si quis ius dicenti, above; and law 13, §2, above, de iniuriis.

units.la: Neque enim hoc quisquam ignorat, magistratui esse parendum, cum sit innatum unicuique, sicut & illud, parentibus & patriæ esse parendum. Igitur non potest non contumax videri, qui imperio Magistratus non paret. Dolo caret ignarus malitiæ, cuius malitiæ ignorantiam nemo prætendere potest, nisi demens sit, vel admodum impubes. Contumacia dolus est, qui in non faciendo consistit. Cuiac. in Recitat.
units.tr: For no one is ignorant that the magistrate must be obeyed, since this is innate in everyone, just as it is that parents and country must be obeyed. Therefore one who does not obey the command of a magistrate cannot fail to appear contumacious. He is free of fraud who is ignorant of wrongdoing, and no one can plead ignorance of such wrongdoing unless he is insane or quite under age. Contumacy is a fraud, which consists in not doing. Cuiac. in Recitat.

units.la: Ad Leg. 200. De minori iniquitate eligenda.
units.tr: On Law 200. On choosing the lesser injustice.

units.la: QVoties nihil sine captione inuestigari potest, dicendum est, quod minimum habet iniquitatis.
units.tr: Whenever nothing can be investigated without loss, one must say that which has the least injustice.

units.la: Sine captione] χωρὶς ἐλάττονος Ecl. ibid. c. 195. 6. Harmenop. 2.
units.tr: Without loss] [χωρὶς ἐλάττονος] Ecl. ibid. c. 195. 6. Harmenop. 2.

units.la: Inuestigari] fieri non potest. ecl. c. 195. 6. Harmenop. 2.
units.tr: Investigated] cannot be done. Ecl. c. 195. 6. Harmenop. 2.

units.la: Minimum] ἕλαττον ἀδικῶν 2. ecl. 3. cap. 195. hinc illæ regulæ; Ex duobus malis minus eligendum: odia restringi c. odia 15. de regul. in 6.
units.tr: The least] [ἕλαττον ἀδικῶν] 2. Ecl. 3, cap. 195. Hence those rules: of two evils the lesser is to be chosen; hatreds are restricted, c. odia 15, de regul. in 6.

units.la: Sumatur exemplum ex l. 4. de diuers. & temp. præscript. Seruus hæreditarius satis accepit in diem certum; postea adita est hæreditas, quæritur; an tempus satisdationis cedat & computetur ex die accepti fideiussoris, ex quo agi cum eo potuit; an ex adita hæreditate? Item quæritur: si seruus eius qui est apud hostes fideiussores acceperit, vtrum ex die accepti fideiussoris, an ex quo postliminio reuertitur, tempus satisdationis cedat? Si dixeris: ex die interpositæ stipulationis, captio erit actoris. Nam tempus cedit antequam agere possit. Contra si dixeris; ex die, quo dominus agere possit, captio erit rei, hoc est fideiussoris. Nam in longius tempus extenditur obligatio. Quid fiet? Eligamus, quod minimum in se habet iniquitatis; Iniquius autem est grauari reum, quam actorem, iniquius ex conditione actoris extendi obligationem rei. Itaque melius est ita constitui, Tepus cadere statim ex die interpositae stipulationis. Et hoc Iauolenus docte censuit. in d.l. 4. quae cum hac regula optime conuenit. Iauolenus ex Cassianis fuit, & Cassius idem censuit, vt refertur in l. si seruus 25. de stipul. seruorum. Cassius, inquam, existimat, tempus ex eo computandum, ex quo agi cum eis potuerit, cum iis scilicet fideiussoribus: licet nondum fuerit, qui agere possit, quod sequitur in d. l. si seruus, id est, ex quo adeatur hereditas, aut postliminio dominus reuertatur. Huic regulae simile quicquam habuimus in l. 85. §. vlt. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: Take an example from law 4, de diversis & temporalibus praescriptionibus. A slave of an inheritance has given security for a fixed day; afterwards the inheritance was entered upon. The question is whether the time for the security begins and is computed from the day the surety was accepted, from which day suit could be brought against him, or from the entry upon the inheritance? Likewise the question is: if the slave of one who is among the enemies has accepted sureties, does the time for security begin from the day the surety was accepted, or from the day he returns by postliminy? If you say: from the day the stipulation was made, the advantage will be the plaintiff's, for the time begins before he can sue. On the contrary, if you say: from the day the owner can sue, the disadvantage will be the defendant's, that is, the surety's, for the obligation is extended over a longer time. What is to be done? Let us choose what has the least injustice in it. But it is more unjust to burden the defendant than the plaintiff, and more unjust to extend the defendant's obligation by the plaintiff's condition. So it is better to settle it thus: that the time begins at once from the day the stipulation was made. And Iavolenus gave this opinion learnedly, in d. l. 4. which agrees very well with this rule. Iavolenus belonged to the school of the Cassians, and Cassius held the same view, as is reported in l. si seruus 25. de stipul. seruorum. Cassius, I say, thinks that the time is to be computed from the day on which suit could be brought against them, that is, against those sureties, although there is not yet anyone who can sue; which follows in d. l. si seruus, that is, from the day the inheritance is entered upon, or the owner returns by postliminy. We have had something similar to this rule in l. 85. §. vlt. sup. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 201. De his quae ex testamento proficiscuntur.
units.tr: On Law 201. Concerning those things that proceed from a will.

units.la: OMnia, quae ex testamento proficiscuntur, ita statum euentus capiunt, si initium quoque sine vitio ceperint.
units.tr: All things that proceed from a will take on the state of their outcome, provided they also began without defect.

units.la: Euentus ] id est, effectus ἀποτελέσματα 2. ecl. 3. cap. 197.
units.tr: Outcome ] that is, effect [ἀποτελέσματα] Ecl. 2, tit. 3, cap. 197.

units.la: Initium] l. 29. l. 178. sup. eod. l. 210. inf. eod. vide l. 1. sup. de reg. Catoniana.
units.tr: Beginning] law 29; law 178 above in the same title; law 210 below in the same title; see law 1 above, on the Catonian rule.

units.la: Vide l. 29. & l. 178. sup. eod. & l. 210. inf. hoc tit. Cuiac.
units.tr: See law 29 and law 178 above in the same title, and law 210 below in this title. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 262. Definitiones esse periculosas.
units.tr: On Law 262. That definitions are dangerous.

units.la: OMnis definitio in iure ciuili est periculosa, parum enim est, ut non subuerti possit.
units.tr: Every definition in civil law is dangerous, for it is scarcely such that it cannot be overturned.

units.la: Definitio] l. 1. sup. eod. adde l. 32. sup. eod. νομικὰς ecl. ibid. c. 198. 6. Harmenop. 2.
units.tr: Definition] see law 1 above in the same title; add law 32 above in the same title; [νομικὰς] Ecl. ibid. cap. 198, 6; Harmenop. 2.

units.la: Parum] id est, vix est, sic Graeci ὀλίγον ... Ecl. ibid. Harmenop.
units.tr: Scarcely] that is, hardly is; so the Greeks say [ὀλίγον]. Ecl. ibid.; Harmenop.

units.la: Etiam de hac lege in l. 1. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: This law is also treated in law 1 above. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 203. De damno & culpa.
units.tr: On Law 203. On damage and fault.

units.la: QVod quis ex sua culpa damnum sentit, non intelligitur damnum sentire.
units.tr: One who suffers damage through his own fault is not understood to suffer damage.

units.la: Damnum] c. damnum 86. de reg. in 6. ξημίαν Ecl. ibid. c. 199. l. 46. §. 5. sup. de procurat. l. 9. inf. l. 17. in f. princ. sup. de noxalib. l. 44. §. 5. ᵴ familiae l. 15. sup. qui omissa causa. Goth.
units.tr: Damnum] cf. the chapter "damnum" (86), De regulis iuris in VI; the Ecloga (ξημίαν), ibid.; chapter 199, law 46, §5 above, De procuratoribus; law 9 below; law 17, at the end of the opening, above, De noxalibus; law 44, §5, "familiae"; law 15 above, Qui omissa causa. Gothofredus.

units.la: Sentire] ab alio scilicet.
units.tr: To suffer] that is, from another.

units.la: Ideo si culpa emtoris res euincatur, non committitur stipulatio duplae. l. si ideo de euict. si ex delicto suo procurator poenam praestiterit, non recuperat eam contrario mandati iudicio. rio, l. qui proprio 46. §. item 5 de procurat. Idem in socio est, l. cum duobus §. vlt. pro socio, sumatur exemp. ex l. 44. de dam. infect. Cuiac.
units.tr: Hence, if goods are evicted through the buyer's fault, the stipulation for double is not incurred (law si ideo de euict.). If a procurator has paid a penalty through his own fault, he does not recover it by the contrary action of mandate (see law qui proprio 46, §item 5, de procurat.). The same holds for a partner (law cum duobus §vlt. pro socio); take the example from law 44 de dam. infect. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 204. De actione.
units.tr: On Law 204. On action.

units.la: MInus est, actionem habere, quam rem.
units.tr: Having an action is less than having a thing.

units.la: Qui actionem habet, videtur rem habere, l. 25. sup. videri est ὡλαςικὸν. Nam reuera minus est habere actionem, quam rem. Qua de causa, & qui actionem habet, non in rem condemnatur, satis namque est, actionem cedi. l. 20. §. bonae fid. de petit. hereditat. Cuiac.
units.tr: He who has an action is seen to have the thing (law 25 above; "to be seen" is [ὡλαςικὸν]). For in truth it is less to have an action than to have the thing. For this reason, one who has an action is not condemned in rem, since it is enough that the action be ceded (law 20 §bonae fid. de petit. hereditat.). Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 205. De his, quae à nobis abire possunt. De obligatis Fisco.
units.tr: On Law 205. On those things which can pass from us. On goods pledged to the Fisc.

units.la: PLerunq; fit, vt etiam ea, quae à nobis abire possunt, proinde in eo statu sint, atque si non essent eius conditionis, vt abire possent, & ideo quòd fisco obligamus & vindicare interdum, & alienare, & seruitutem praedio imponere possumus.
units.tr: It often happens that even those things which can pass from us are in the same state as if they were not of such a kind that they could pass; and therefore, because we pledge them to the fisc, we can sometimes both claim them back and alienate them, and impose a servitude on an estate.

units.la: Dixi in l. omnes actiones. 139. sup. Cuiac.
units.tr: I have spoken on this in law omnes actiones 139 above. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad Leg. 206. Ne quis lucretur cum iactura alterius.
units.tr: On Law 206. That no one should gain by another's loss.

units.la: IVre naturae aequum est, neminem cum alterius detrimento & iniuria fieri locupletiorem.
