units.la: §. 2. Re contrahitur quoties aliqua cuicunque mutuo dantur, quæ in his rebus contingunt, quæ pondere, numero, mensura continentur, hoc est, si pecunia numeretur, vel frumentum detur, vinum, aut oleum, aut æs, ferrum, argentum, vel aurum. Quæ omnia numerando, aut pensando, aut metiendo, ad hoc damus vt eorum fiant, qui ea accipiunt, & ad nos statuto tempore non ipsæ res, sed aliæ eius naturæ, quales datæ sunt, atque ipsius ponderis, numeri, vel mensuræ reddantur. Propter quod Mutuum appellatum est, quasi à me tibi ita datum sit, vt ex meo tuum fieret.
units.tr: §. 2. An obligation is contracted by a thing whenever things that are measured by weight, number or measure are given to someone as a loan. These are things such as money counted out, grain, wine, oil, bronze, iron, silver or gold. We give all of these by counting, weighing or measuring, so that they become the property of those who receive them, and at the agreed time they are returned to us not as the same things but as others of the same kind, and of the same weight, number or measure, as were given. For this reason it is called a loan (mutuum), as if it had been given by me to you on the condition that what was mine should become yours.

units.la: §. 3. Verbis contrahitur obligatio ex interrogatione dantis, & responsione accipientis, ita, vt si ille, qui dat, interroget, Hoc mihi dabis? qui accipiet, respondeat, Habeo. Aut in obligatione debitoris, si aliquis fideiussor accedat, ille, qui personam fideiussori tradit, interroget, Istum fide tua esse iubes? & ille respondeat: Fide mea esse iubeo. Hac conditione non solum ille qui debitor est, sed & is qui fideiussor existit, obligantur. Et non solum fideiussor, ipse, dum viuit, sed & hæredes ipsius si ille defecerit, tenentur obnoxij: creditor autem qui pecuniam dedit, in potestate habet ad reddendam pecuniam quem velit tenere, vtrum ipsum debitorem, an fideiussorem; sed si debitorem tenere elegerit, fideiussorem absoluit: si vero fideiussorem tenuerit, debitorem absoluit. Quia vno electo, quem idoneum creditor iudicat, alterum liberat.
units.tr: §. 3. An obligation is contracted by words through a question from the giver and an answer from the receiver. So if the one who gives asks, "Will you give me this?", and the one who receives answers, "I will," the obligation arises. Likewise, in the obligation of a debtor, if some surety joins, the one who hands over the person to the surety asks, "Do you command this man to be on your faith?", and the surety answers, "I command him to be on my faith." By this form not only the debtor but also the one who becomes surety is bound. And not only the surety himself, while he lives, but also his heirs, if he has died, are held liable. The creditor who has given the money, however, has the power to hold whichever he wishes for repayment of the money, either the debtor himself or the surety. But if he has chosen to hold the debtor, he releases the surety; if he has held the surety, he releases the debtor. For once the one whom the creditor judges sufficient has been chosen, the other is freed.

units.la: §. 4. Sunt & aliae obligationes, quae nulla praecedente interrogatione, contrahi possunt, id est, ut si mulier sive sponso vxor futura, sive iam marito, dotem dicat: quod tam de mobilibus rebus, quam de fundis fieri potest. Et non solum in hac obligatione ipsa mulier obligabitur, sed & pater eius, & debitor ipsius mulieris, si pecuniam, quam ille debebat sponso creditricis, ipse debitor in dotem dixerit. Hae tantum tres personae, nulla interrogatione praecedente, possunt dictione dotis legitime obligari. Aliae vero personae, si pro muliere dotem marito promiserint, communi iure obligari debent, id est, ut & interrogatae respondeant, & stipulatae promittant.
units.tr: §. 4. There are also other obligations that can be contracted without any preceding question, namely when a woman, either a bride-to-be to her betrothed or already a wife to her husband, declares a dowry. This can be done with movable goods as well as with lands. And the obligation binds not only the woman herself, but also her father and the debtor of the woman, if the debtor himself declares a dowry from the money which he owed to the betrothed creditor. These three persons alone can be lawfully bound by the mere declaration of a dowry, with no preceding question. Other persons, however, if they promised a dowry to the husband on behalf of the woman, must be bound by the common law, that is, they must answer when asked and promise when stipulated.

units.la: Quae nulla ] dotis dictio stipulationem non requirit.
units.tr: Without any] the declaration of a dowry does not require a stipulation.

units.la: Dotem dicat ] de dotis dictione vid. Vlpian. 6. §. 1. §. 2.
units.tr: Declares a dowry] on the declaration of a dowry see Ulpian 6 §. 1 §. 2.

units.la: Tres personae ] Vlp. 6. §. 2.
units.tr: Three persons] Ulp. 6 §. 2.

units.la: §. 5. Item & alio casu, vno loquente, & sine interinterrogatione alio promittente, contrahitur obligatio, id est, si libertus patrono aut donum, aut munus, aut operas se daturum esse iuraverit. Exponendum hic, quid sit donum, aut munus, aut operæ: in quare supradicti liberti, non tam verborum solemnitate, quam iurisiurandi religione tenentur. Sed nulla altera persona hoc ordine obligari potest.
units.tr: §. 5. Likewise, in another case, with one party speaking and the other promising without any mutual question, an obligation is contracted: for example, if a freedman has sworn to his patron that he will give a gift, a present or services. What a gift, a present or services is must be explained here. The aforesaid freedmen are bound in these matters not so much by the solemnity of the words as by the sanctity of the oath. But no other person can be bound in this way.

units.la: §. 6. Præterea inutilis est promissio, etiamsi stipulatione interveniente facta sit, si id aliquis daturum se promiserit, quod sui iuris non est, hoc est, si aut ingenuum hominem, quasi servum se daturum promittat. Aut si mortuum aliquis, quem viuum credebat, promiserit. Aut locum sacrum, aut sanctum, aut religiosum daturum se quicunque promiserit.
units.tr: §. 6. Moreover, a promise is invalid even if it was made with a stipulation, if someone promises to give what is not in his own power, that is, if he promises to give a free man as if he were a slave, or if he promises a dead man whom he believed to be alive, or if he promises to give any sacred, holy or religious place.

units.la: Ingenuum hominem ] id est, libertum. l. 103. de verb. obligat.
units.tr: A free man] that is, a freedman. l. 103. de verb. obligat.

units.la: Quasi seruum ] §. 2. Inst. d. inutil. stipul.
units.tr: As if a slave] §. 2. Inst. d. inutil. stipul.

units.la: Mortuum aliquis } d. l. 103. §. 1. Inst. de inutil. stipul. l. 69. ff. d. verb. obligat.
units.tr: Mortuum aliquis: the same law, §. 1 of the Institutes on useless stipulations; and the law 69, ff. on verbal obligations.

units.la: Locum sacrum aut sanctum ] l. 83. §. 3. ff. de verb. obligat. §. 2. Inst. de inutil. stipul.
units.tr: A sacred or holy place. Law 83, §. 3, Digest, On verbal obligations; §. 2, Institutes, On useless stipulations.

units.la: §. 7. Præterea inutilis est promissio si aliquis rem sub tali conditione promittat, quæ impleri pro rei difficultate non possit.
units.tr: §. 7. Moreover, a promise is invalid if someone promises a thing under such a condition that, because of the difficulty of the thing, it cannot be fulfilled.

units.la: Pro rei difficultate ] vid. l. 31. ff. de obligationib. leg. 35. ff. d. verb. obligat. §. 1. Institut. de inutil. stipul.
units.tr: Pro rei difficultate: see the law 31 in the Digest, de obligationibus et actionibus; law 35 in the Digest, de verborum obligationibus, §. 1; and the Institutes, de inutilibus stipulationibus.

units.la: §.8.Præterea inutilis est interrogatio, & promissio, si ita aliquis interroget debitorem, Post mortem meam vel tuam illud dari spondes? Quod propterea inutile visum est, quia à persona hæredis obligatio incipere non potest. Et ideo nec hæredi creditoris sub hac sponsione obligatur debitor, nec debitoris hæres creditori tenetur obnoxius.
units.tr: §. 8. Moreover, a question and a promise are invalid if someone asks the debtor, "Do you promise to give that after my death or after yours?" This was held invalid because an obligation cannot begin from the person of an heir. Therefore the debtor is not bound to the creditor's heir under this undertaking, nor is the debtor's heir held liable to the creditor.

units.la: Inutilis est interrogatio ] hodie non est §. 2. in pr. Inst. de inuti. stip.
units.tr: A question is invalid] today it is not so; §. 2 in pr. Inst. de inutil. stip.

units.la: §.9: Item inutilis est obligatio, si dicat creditor, Pridie quam moriar, dare spondes? vel interroget debitorem, Pridie quam moriaris? Similiter & hæc stipulatio inutilis iudicatur, quia non potest sciri, quando sit pridie, quam aliquis moriatur, nisi postquam mortuus fuerit.
units.tr: §. 9. Likewise, an obligation is invalid if the creditor says, "Do you promise to give on the day before I die?", or asks the debtor, "On the day before you die?" This stipulation too is judged invalid, because it cannot be known which day is the day before someone dies until after he has died.

units.la: Inutilis est obligatio ] Hodie non est. d. §. 12. verf. sed & si quis ita stipul. pridie, quam moriar, &c.
units.tr: An obligation is invalid] Today it is not so. d. §. 12. verse "but also if someone stipulates thus, on the day before I die," etc.

units.la: §. 10. Item si pure interrogat creditor, & debitor sub conditione promittat.
units.tr: §. 10. Likewise, if the creditor asks purely, and the debtor promises under a condition.

units.la: Si pure ] vid. §. 5. Inst. de inuti. stip.
units.tr: If purely] see §. 5 Inst. de inutil. stip.

units.la: §. 11. Vel si creditor decem solidos debitorem interroget, & debitor quinque promittat: hoc ordine integrum debitum vacillare cognoscitur.
units.tr: §. 11. Or if the creditor asks the debtor for ten shillings, and the debtor promises five. In this way the whole debt is known to waver.

units.la: Quinque promittat ] d. §. 5. in pr.
units.tr: Promises five] d. §. 5 in pr.

units.la: §.12.Si quis nobis pecuniam debeat, possumus debitorem nostrum compellere, ut pecuniam, quam nobis redditurus erat, alteri se cau-eat redditurum. Neque potest ei, cui pro nostro debito cauet, de cauto, & non numerato, sicut fieri solet, aliquid disputationis afferre, cum id, quod à nobis accepit, alteri cauerit redditurum.
units.tr: §. 12. If someone owes us money, we can compel our debtor to promise to another that he will repay the money which he was about to repay to us. And the one to whom he gives surety for our debt cannot raise any objection about the security being given and the money not counted out, as is usually done, since he has promised to repay to another what he received from us.

units.la: §. 13. Literis obligatio fit, aut à re in personam, aut à persona in personam. A re in personam, velut si id, quod ex emptione, aut conductione, aut societate debes, alii reddas. A persona in personam, veluti si id, quod mihi alter debet, alteri personae delegem, vt reddere debeat.
units.tr: §. 13. An obligation is made by writing either from a thing to a person, or from a person to a person. From a thing to a person, as when you pay to another what you owe from a purchase, a hiring or a partnership. From a person to a person, as when I assign to another person what another owes me, so that he must pay it.

units.la: §. 14. Consensu fiunt obligationes & emptionibus & venditionibus, locationibus, conductionibus, societatibus & mandatis. Quia in eiusmodi rebus consensus magis quam scriptura aut solennitas quaeritur. In quibus rebus etiam inter absentes obligatio contrahi potest, quod in aliis rebus fieri non potest.
units.tr: §. 14. Obligations are made by consent in purchases and sales, lettings, hirings, partnerships and mandates, because in such matters consent is sought rather than writing or formality. In these matters an obligation can also be contracted between absent parties, which cannot be done in other matters.

units.la: Consensu fiunt] vid. Inst. de oblig. ex consensu. l. 2. ff. de obligat.
units.tr: Consensu fiunt: see Inst. de oblig. ex consensu. l. 2. ff. de obligat.

units.la: Scriptura] d. l. 2. §. 1.
units.tr: Scriptura] d. l. 2. §. 1.

units.la: Inter absentes ] d. l. 2. § 2.
units.tr: Inter absentes] d. l. 2. § 2.

units.la: §. 15. Emptio igitur & venditio contrahitur, cum de pretio inter emptorem & venditorem fuerit definitum, etiamsi pretium non fuerit numeratum, & nec pars pretij, aut arrha data fuerit.
units.tr: §. 15. A contract of sale and purchase is therefore made once the price has been agreed between buyer and seller, even if the price has not been paid and no part of the price or earnest money has been given.

units.la: §. 16. Locatio & conductio simili ratione consistunt, ut consensu, etiam verbo definitio inter consentientes firma permaneat.
units.tr: §. 16. Lease and hire stand on a similar footing: once agreed by consent, even by word, the terms agreed between the consenting parties remain firm.

units.la: §. 17. Societatem inire possumus, aut omnium bonorum, aut unius alicuius negotiationis. Et potest ita initi societas, si tamen hoc inter socios convenit, ut unus pecuniam det, alter operam suam pro pecunia doner. Et huius rei definitio etiam verbo inita valet, ita, ut quicquid societatis tempore, quolibet modo fuerit acquisitum, sociis commune sit.
units.tr: §. 17. We may enter a partnership either in all our goods or in some one business. A partnership may be formed in this way, provided it is agreed among the partners that one contributes money and the other gives his labour in return for that money. The terms of this arrangement are valid even when agreed by word, so that whatever is acquired in any way during the partnership is common to the partners.

units.la: §. 18. Permanet autem inita societas, quamdiu in ipso consensu socii perseverant: quia sicut consensu contrahitur, etiam dissensu solvitur. Dissolvitur ergo societas aut morte unius socij, aut contraria voluntate, aut capitis deminutione, id est, si unus ex sociis, sicut frequenter supra diximus, capite fuerit deminutus.
units.tr: §. 18. A partnership entered into continues for as long as the partners remain in the same consent; for just as it is contracted by consent, so it is dissolved by dissent. A partnership is therefore dissolved either by the death of one partner, or by a change of will, or by loss of civil status (capitis deminutio), that is, if one of the partners has been diminished in status, as we have often said above.

units.la: Permanet autem]
units.tr: It continues

units.la: Morte vnius ]
units.tr: By the death of one partner

units.la: §. 19. Similiter & mandati verbo potest. Et cum verbis, mandatum fuerit, obligatio contrahitur. Possumus enim aut nostra negotia, aut aliena cuicunque agenda mandare, dummodo honestum aliquid agi mandemus. Nam si contra bonos mores aliquid mandare voluerimus: hoc est, si cuicunque mandemus, ut alicui furtum faciat, aut homicidium, aut adulterium admittat, in his rebus mandati obligatio non contrahitur.
units.tr: §. 19. Likewise an obligation can arise by the word of mandate. When a mandate has been given in words, an obligation is contracted. For we may commit to anyone our own affairs or those of others to be done, provided we commission something honest. But if we wish to commission something contrary to good morals, that is, if we order someone to commit theft for another, or murder, or to permit adultery, no obligation of mandate arises in those matters.

units.la: Mandati verbo ]
units.tr: By the word of mandate

units.la: Honestum aliquid ]
units.tr: Something honest

units.la: Contra mores ]
units.tr: Against good morals

units.la: Homicidium ]
units.tr: Homicide

units.la: §. 20. Soluitur autem mandatum aut morte, cui mandatum est, aut contraria illius voluntate, qui mandauit.
units.tr: §. 20. A mandate is ended either by the death of the one to whom it was given, or by the contrary will of the one who gave it.

units.la: Morte ]
units.tr: By death

units.la: Contraria illius voluntate ]
units.tr: By his contrary will

units.la: §. 21. Sed is, cui mandatur, mandati formam egredi non potest, aut si egressus fuerit, & mandatori teneatur obnoxius, & quod extra mandatum egit, non praeiudicet mandatori.
units.tr: §. 21. But the one to whom a mandate is given cannot go beyond the form of the mandate; or if he does go beyond it, he is bound to the mandator, and what he did outside the mandate does not prejudice the mandator.

units.la: Egredi non potest] l. 5. ff. mandati §. 8. Inst. de mandato.
units.tr: Cannot go beyond] l. 5. ff. mandati §. 8. Inst. de mandato.

units.la: Tit. X. Quibus modis obligatio tollatur.
units.tr: Title X. By what means an obligation is discharged.

units.la: TOllitur obligatio solutione debiti. Præterea aliquoties tollitur obligatio, etiam si aliud quam cautum fuerat à debitore creditori reddatur. Nam si quicunque pro pecunia quam creditori cauit, acquiescente creditore, aurum, aut argentum, aut manicipia, vel alias quaslibet species, habita æstimatione consentiente creditore dederit, obligatio euidenter tollitur.
units.tr: An obligation is discharged by payment of the debt. Moreover, an obligation is sometimes discharged even when something other than what was promised is rendered to the creditor by the debtor. For if anyone, instead of money which he promised to the creditor, gives gold, silver, slaves, or any other kind of goods, with the creditor's consent and after a valuation has been agreed, the obligation is plainly discharged.

units.la: Quia de obligationibus, quæ ex contractu nascuntur, diximus, superest vt de his obligationibus, quæ ex delicto nascuntur, simpliciter disputemus. Ex delicto nascuntur obligationes, si aliquis furtum fecerit, vel bona aliena rapuerit, vel damnum alteri dederit, aut iniuriam fecerit. Quarum omnium rerum vno genere ex delicto nascitur obligatio. Furtorum autem sunt genera quatuor: manifesti, nec manifesti, concepti, & oblati. Manifestum furtum dicitur, si quando fur cuiuscunque rem tollit, in ipso furto deprehenditur. Nec manifestum furtum appellatur, quod quamliber dum fieret, inuentum non est, tamen furtum factum fuisse probatur. Conceptum furtum dicitur, cum eum apud aliquem alterum res furtiua inueniatur. Oblatum furtum dicitur, cum res furtiua alicui ita à fure datur, vt apud ipsum furem inueniri non possit. Præterea, qui rem alienam inuito aut nesciente domino contingit, vel tollere, aut de loco mouere præsumit, furtum facit. Et si quis rem vtendam acceperit, aut commendatam apud se habuerit, & aliter ea vsus fuerit, quam acceperit, furti actione tenetur. Præterea, si quis iumentum alterius ad hoc accepit, vt eum quinque millibus duceret, si id decem millibus, aut longius quam ab illo qui dedit fuerit constitutum duxerit, furti reus erit. Et multa præterea quorumcunq; similia sunt: secundum quæ & ille furti tenetur, qui vt ferret opem, aut consilium, aut studium commodarit: velut si quis pecuniam, quam in manu aliquis tenebat, excusserit, vt alii eam rapere possent.
units.tr: Since we have spoken of obligations arising from contract, it remains that we briefly discuss those obligations which arise from delict. Obligations arise from delict if someone commits theft, or seizes another's goods, or causes harm to another, or commits an injury. All of these give rise to an obligation from delict under a single heading. There are four kinds of theft: manifest, non-manifest, conceived, and offered. Theft is called manifest when the thief is caught in the very act of taking another's property. It is called non-manifest when, although it was not discovered while it was being done, it is nevertheless proved that the theft took place. Theft is called conceived when the stolen goods are found in the possession of another person. Theft is called offered when the stolen goods are handed over to someone by the thief in such a way that they cannot be found with the thief himself. Moreover, whoever presumes to touch or to remove from its place another's property against the will or without the knowledge of the owner, commits theft. And if anyone has received a thing to use, or has kept a thing entrusted to him, and has used it otherwise than he received it, he is liable to the action for theft. Further, if anyone has taken another's beast of burden for the purpose of leading it five miles, and has led it ten miles, or further than the place fixed by the person who gave it, he will be guilty of theft. And there are many other similar cases, under which he is also liable for theft who has lent aid, counsel, or zeal to the act; for example, if someone has shaken loose money which another held in his hand, so that others might snatch it.

units.la: AD VLPIANI TIT. XXIX. NOTÆ EX CVIACIO, PACIO, & optimis quibusque ICtis selectæ.
units.tr: TO THE TITLE 29 OF ULPIAN: NOTES CHOSEN FROM CUJAS, PACIUS, AND THE BEST JURISTS.

units.la: Tit.1.De Libertis.
units.tr: Title 1. On Freedmen.

units.la: Libertorum genera sunt tria, Ciues Romani, Latini Iuniani, Dediticiorum numero. Ciues Romani, sunt liberti, qui vindicta, censu aut testamento nullo iure impediente manumissi sunt.
units.tr: Freedmen are of three kinds: Roman citizens, Junian Latins, and those counted among the dediticii. Roman citizens are freedmen who were manumitted by the vindicta, by the census, or by will, with no law preventing it.

units.la: Vindicta manumittuntur apud magistratum, velut Prætorem, Consulem, Proconsulem.
units.tr: Those are manumitted by the vindicta before a magistrate, such as the praetor, the consul, or the proconsul.

units.la: Censu manumittebantur olim, qui lustrali censu Romæ, iussu dominorum, inter ciues Romanos censum profitebantur.
units.tr: Formerly, those were manumitted by the census who, at the lustral census at Rome, declared themselves among the Roman citizens in the census, by order of their masters.

units.la: Vt testamento manumissi liberi sint, lex duodecim Tabularum facit; quæ confirmat, quod datum legatum est. Hodie autem ipso iure liberi sunt ex lege Iunia, qua lege Latini sunt nominati, inter amicos manumissi.
units.tr: The Twelve Tables law provides that those manumitted by will become free; it confirms what was left to them as a legacy. Today, however, those manumitted among friends are free by law itself, under the Junian law, by which they are called Latins.

units.la: Dediticiorum numero sunt, qui pœnæ causa vincti sunt à domino: quibus vestigia scripta fuerunt: qui propter noxam torti nocentesque inuenti sunt: quiue traditi sunt, vt ferro, aut cum bestiis depugnarent: vel in custodiam coniecti fuerunt: deinde quoquomodo manumissi sunt: idque lex Ælia Sentia facit.
units.tr: Among the dediticii are those who were bound by their master as a punishment, on whom marks had been written, who were tortured on account of a crime and found guilty, or who were handed over to fight with the sword or with wild beasts, or who were thrown into prison. Then, however they were manumitted, they are so counted; the Aelian Sentian law provides this.

units.la: Eadem lege cautum est, vt minor triginta annorum seruus vindicta manumissus, ciuis Romanus non fiat, nisi apud consilium causa probata fuerit: ideo sine consilio manumissum seruum manere putat. Testamento vero manumissum perinde haberi iubet, atque si domini voluntate in libertate esset, ideoque Latinus fit.
units.tr: By the same law it is provided that a slave under thirty years of age, manumitted by the vindicta, does not become a Roman citizen unless the cause has been approved before the council. Therefore he thinks a slave manumitted without the council remains a slave. But one manumitted by will he orders to be regarded as if he were free by the master's will, and so he becomes a Latin.

units.la: Eadem lex eum dominum, qui minor viginti annorum est prohibet seruum manumittere, præterquam si causam apud consilium probauerit. In consilium autem adhibentur Romæ quinque Senatores, & quinque Equites Romani, in prouincia viginti Recuperatores, ciues Romani.
units.tr: The same law forbids a master under twenty years of age to manumit a slave, unless he has first proved the cause before the council. Five senators and five Roman knights are called to the council at Rome; in a province, twenty recuperatores who are Roman citizens.

units.la: Ab eo domino, qui soluendo non est, seruus testamento liber esse iussus, & heres institutus, etsi minor sit triginta annis, vel in ea causa sit, vt dedititius fieri debeat, ciuis Romanus & heres fit: si tamen alius ex eo testamento nemo heres sit. Quod si duo pluresve liberi heredesque esse iussi sunt, primo loco scriptus liber & heres fit: quod & ipsum lex Ælia Sentia facit.
units.tr: A slave ordered by will to be free by a master who is insolvent, and instituted heir, becomes a Roman citizen and heir, even if he is under thirty years of age or in a case where he ought to become a dediticius, provided that no other heir is named in that will. But if two or more are ordered to be free and heirs, the one written first becomes free and heir. The Aelian Sentian law provides this as well.

units.la: Eadem lex in fraudem creditoris & patroni manumittere prohibet.
units.tr: The same law forbids manumission in fraud of a creditor or patron.

units.la: Qui tantum in bonis, non etiam ex iure QuiQuiritium seruum habet, manumittendo Latinum facit.
units.tr: One who has a slave only in goods, and not also by Quiritary right, makes him a Latin by manumitting him.

units.la: In bonis tantum alicuius seruus est, velut hoc modo, Si ciuis Rom. à ciue Romano seruum emerit, isque traditus ei sit, neque tamen mancipatus ei, neque in iure cessus, neque ab ipso anno possessus sit. Nam quamdiu horum quid fiat, is seruus in bonis quidem emptoris est, ex iure Quiritium autem venditoris est.
units.tr: A slave belongs to someone only in goods, for example in this way: if a Roman citizen buys a slave from a Roman citizen and the slave is delivered to him, but not mancipated to him, nor ceded in court, nor possessed by him for a year. For as long as none of these things happens, the slave is indeed in the buyer's goods, but by Quiritary right he remains the seller's.

units.la: Mulier quae in tutela est, item pupillus & pupilla manumittere non possunt.
units.tr: A woman under guardianship, and likewise a ward, boy or girl, cannot manumit.

units.la: Communem seruum vnus ex dominis manumittendo, partem suam amittit: eaque accrescit socio, maxime si eo modo manumiserit, quo, si proprium haberet, ciuem Romanum facturus esset. Nam si inter amicos eum manumiserit, plerisque placet eum nihil egisse.
units.tr: When one of several masters manumits a common slave, he loses his own share, and it accrues to his partner, especially if he manumitted in the way by which, had he owned the slave outright, he would have made him a Roman citizen. For if he manumitted him among friends, most hold that he has accomplished nothing.

units.la: Seruus in quo alterius est vsusfructus, alterius proprietas, à proprietatis domino manumissus, liber non fit, sed seruus sine domino est.
units.tr: A slave in whom one person has the usufruct and another the ownership, when manumitted by the owner of the ownership, does not become free but is a slave without a master.

units.la: Post mortem heredis, aut ante institutionem heredis, testamento libertas dari non potest, excepto testamento militis.
units.tr: Liberty cannot be given by will after the death of the heir, or before the institution of the heir, except in the will of a soldier.

units.la: Inter medias heredum institutiones libertas data, vtrisque adeuntibus non valet: solo autem priore adeunte, iure antiquo valet. Sed post legem Papiam Poppeam, quae partem non adeuntis caducam facit, siquidem primus heres vel ius antiquum habeat, valere eam posse placuit: quod si non habeat, non valere constat, quod loco non adeuntis, legatarii partis heredes fiunt. Sunt tamen qui & hoc casu valere eam posse dicunt.
units.tr: Liberty given between successive institutions of heirs is not valid if both accept; but if only the first accepts, it is valid under the old law. Since the Papian Poppaean law, which makes the share of a non-accepting heir caducous, it has been held that it can be valid if the first heir has the old right; but if he does not have it, it is clear that it is not valid, because the legatees of that share become heirs in place of the non-accepting heir. Yet some say that it can be valid even in this case.

units.la: Qui testamento liber esse iussus est, mox quam unus ex heredibus adierit hereditatem, liber fit.
units.tr: One ordered by will to be free becomes free as soon as one of the heirs has entered upon the inheritance.

units.la: Iusta libertas testamento potest dari his servis, qui testamenti faciendi, & mortis tempore, ex iure Quiritium testatores fuerunt.
units.tr: Valid liberty can be given by will to those slaves who were testators by Quiritary right at the time of making the will and at the time of death.

units.la: Lex Furia Caninia iuber testamento ex tribus seruis non plures quam duos manumitti, & usque ad decem, dimidiam partem manumittere concedit: a decimo usque ad triginta tertiam partem, ut tamen adhuc quinque manumittere liceat, aeque ut ex priori numero: a triginta usque ad centum quartam partem, aeque ut decem ex priori numero liberari possint: a centum usque ad quingentos, partem quintam similiter, ut ex antecedenti numero viginti quinque possint fieri liberi. Eandemque praecipit, ne plures omnino quam centum, ex cuiusquam testamento liberi fiant.
units.tr: The Furian Caninian law orders that not more than two out of three slaves be manumitted by will, and it permits half to be manumitted when there are up to ten; from ten up to thirty, a third, provided that five may still be manumitted, as from the earlier number; from thirty up to a hundred, a quarter, just as ten from the earlier number may be freed; from a hundred up to five hundred, likewise a fifth, so that twenty-five from the preceding number may become free. And it prescribes that no more than a hundred in all be made free by anyone's will.

units.la: Eadem lex cauet, ut libertates seruis testamento nominatim dentur.
units.tr: The same law provides that liberties be given to slaves by name in the will.

units.la: Dn. Pacius & alii hic praemittunt φελεγάνδρον quoddam, sub peculiari rubrica, DE LEGIBVS BVS & MORIBVS: quae tamen sub ea tradunt, haec pleraque Cuiacius suo, quem observavit, ordine ac loco, sub hoc, de LIBERTIS, titulo proposuit.
units.tr: Dn. Pacius and others place before this a certain preface [φελεγάνδρον], under a special heading, ON LAWS AND CUSTOMS: but what they teach under that heading, Cujas has set out in his own order and place under this title, ON FREEDMEN, as he observed.

units.la: Libertorum ] Libertorum divisio haec est. Adde Caium 1. Inst. 1. verb. libertorum. Libertorum status tripertitus §. 3. Inst. de libertinis.
units.tr: Freedmen] The division of freedmen is this. Add Gaius, Inst. 1, verb. libertorum. The threefold status of freedmen, §3, Inst. de libertinis.

units.la: Cives ] Cives Romani fiunt tribus modis. eod. §. 6. Caius 1. Inst. 2.
units.tr: Roman citizens] Roman citizens are made in three ways. Same place, §6; Gaius, Inst. 2.

units.la: Vindicta ] De manumissis vindicta. Adde §. 1. Inst. de Libertinis. Haec manumissio tribunal non exigit l. 7. ff. de manumiss. vindict. sitque hodie per tutorem, verbaque solennia: licet non dicantur ut dicta accipiuntur. l. 23. ff. d. tit. Porro Theophilus id genus manumissionis ex eo dictum putat, vel quod eo vindicaretur mancipium in naturalem libertatem, (& male. Nam si ita esset, qui censu vel testamento manumitteretur, vindicta quoque manumitti diceretur) vel a vindice quodam, qui, cum seruus esset, erupturam adversus Romanos coniurationem indicio suo patefecit, publiceque a Romanis manumissus est, & in honorem eius, quicunque apud magistratum manumittebatur, vindicta manumitti dicebatur. Theophil. §. Instit. de libert. Coniurationis a vindice detectae meminit quidem Liuius 2. Est etiam verisimile vindicta manumissionem dici, quod lictor l. 8. l. 23. ff. de manumiss. vindict. virgulam seruo manumittendo imponeret. Persius: Vindicta postquam meus à prætore recessi: & post, non in festuca lictor quam gestat inani, virgulam, inquam, quæ vindicta diceretur. Boët. in top. Plutarchus de sera numinis vindicta κάλφου λεπτὸν appellat. hinc vindictam imponere l.14. in sin. ff. de manumiss. l.12. §.2. ff. de liberali l.19. §.4. ff. de castrensi peculio. l.
units.tr: Vindicta] On those manumitted by the vindicta. Add §1, Inst. de Libertinis. This manumission does not require a tribunal, l. 7, ff. de manumiss. vindict. and today it is done through a guardian, with solemn words, which need not be spoken, provided they are understood. l. 23, ff. d. tit. Theophilus thinks this kind of manumission was so named either because the slave was claimed (vindicabatur) into natural liberty by it (and wrongly, for if that were so, one manumitted by the census or by will would also be said to be manumitted by the vindicta), or from a certain vindex who, while a slave, disclosed by his information a conspiracy about to break out against the Romans, and was publicly manumitted by the Romans; and in his honour, whoever was manumitted before a magistrate was said to be manumitted by the vindicta. Theophilus, §Instit. de libert. Livy, book 2, indeed mentions the conspiracy detected by a vindex. It is also likely that manumission was called by the vindicta because the lictor, in manumitting the slave, placed a little rod (virgula) on him, l. 8, l. 23, ff. de manumiss. vindict. Persius: "after I withdrew from my master's vindicta" and afterwards: "not the rod which the lictor carries in an empty festuca," that is, the little rod which would be called the vindicta. Boethius on the Topics. Plutarch, in On the Delay of Divine Justice, calls the vindicta a thin rod. Hence to place the vindicta: l. 14, in fin., ff. de manumiss.; l. 12, §2, ff. de liberali; l. 19, §4, ff. de castrensi peculio; l.

units.la: 2. C. si aduersus libertat. Gothofred. in not. ad tit. de legib. & morib. & libert. Inst. Vlpian.
units.tr: 2. C. si adversus libertat. Gothofredus, in notes on the title de legibus et moribus and de libertinis, Inst. Ulpian.

units.la: Prætorem ] l.1. l.8. ff. de manumiss. vindict. l.4. C. de manum. vindict. l. 1. ff. & C. de off. Prætor. Gothofr. ibid.
units.tr: Praetorem] Law 1 and law 8, Digest, on manumission by vindicta; law 4, Code, on manumission by vindicta; law 1, Digest and Code, on the office of the praetor. Gothofred, ibid.

units.la: Consulem] l.4. l.1. §.1. §.2. ff. de off. consul. l.20. in f. ff. de manumiss. vindict.
units.tr: Consulem] l. 4; l. 1, §1, §2, ff. de off. consul.; l. 20, in fin., ff. de manumiss. vindict.

units.la: Proconsulem ] l. 2. ff. de off. proconsul. l.17. ff. de manum. vind. Et ita legendum est in l. 4. non præsules. An & apud alios? Vtique apud magistratus ciuitatum, quibus huiusmodi ius est v. d. l.4. in sin. apud magistratus municipales. Hi habent legis actionem. Paul. 2. sentent. 25. §.4. apud præfectum Ægypti l.21. ff. de manum. vind. apud legatum proconsulis l. 17. in sin. ff. d. tit. quin apud ipsum Imperatorem l. 14. in sin. ff. de manumission. Goth. ibid.
units.tr: Proconsulem] l. 2, ff. de off. proconsul.; l. 17, ff. de manum. vindict. And so it should be read in l. 4, not praesules. Was it also before others? Certainly before the magistrates of cities who have such a right, as in the said l. 4 at the end, namely before municipal magistrates. These have the legal action, Paul, Sent. 2, 25, §4; before the prefect of Egypt, l. 21, ff. de manum. vindict.; before the legate of the proconsul, l. 17, at the end, ff. of this title; indeed even before the emperor himself, l. 14, at the end, ff. de manumission. Gothofredus, ibid.

units.la: Lustrali ] Lustrum, spatium quinque annorum, de forma censendi vid. tit. ff. de censib.
units.tr: Lustrali: a lustrum, a space of five years. On the form of the census, see the title in the Digest on the census.

units.la: Censum ] id est, facultatem & libertatem suam. vid. Theoph. d. loc. l. 10. ff. de probat. l. 64. ff. de acquir. rerum.
units.tr: Censum: that is, his faculty and liberty. See Theophilus, the same place; Digest, l. 10 De probationibus; Digest, l. 64 De acquirendo rerum dominio.

units.la: Testamento ] Dominus seruum testamento potest manumittere ff. de manumiss. testam. C. de testam. manumiss. ibid. Goth.
units.tr: Testamento: a master may manumit a slave by will. Digest, De manumissis testamento; Code, De testamentaria manumissione, the same place; Gothofredus.

units.la: Quæ confirmat ] desunt hæc verba, Testamento datas libertates, quæ deinde sequuntur, abundant, nam ad legem Furiam pertinent, cuius sententia mox clarius explicatur. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Quae confirmat: these words are missing. The liberties given by will that follow are superfluous, for they belong to the Furian law, whose meaning is explained more clearly below. Cuiacius, on this place.

units.la: Datum ] verba huius legis vide in tit. II. §. 14. inf. eod. & in l. 1. ff. ad l. Falcidiam l. 53 l. 120. ff. de verb. signif. in Novell. 22. cap. 2. vide etiam quasdam in notis Goth.
units.tr: Datum: for the words of this law, see below in the title, §14 of the same book; also Digest, l. 1 ad legem Falcidiam; Digest, ll. 53 and 120 De verborum significatione; Novel 22, cap. 2. See also some in Gothofredus' notes.

units.la: Quæ prohibet ] l. non est dubium. C. de legibus. No. Th. ne cur. pred. alt. cond. Macrob. in somn. Scip. ad finem, inter leges illa imperfecta dicitur, in qua nulla deuiantibus pœna sancitur. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Quae prohibet: Code, l. Non est dubium, De legibus; Novel of Theodosius, De curiis; Macrobius, on the Dream of Scipio, near the end. Among laws, a law is called imperfect when no penalty is laid down for those who transgress it. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Lex Furia ] vide in not. Goth. ad leg. 102. ff. ad l. Falcid.
units.tr: Lex Furia: see Gothofredus' note on Digest, l. 102, ad legem Falcidiam.

units.la: Id est pars prima tollitur ] Legendum opinor, Pars prima legis tollitur; vt derogare sit partem primæ legi detrahere. l. derogatur. de verb. sign. quod etiam exrogare est, auctore Sex. Pomp. Obrogare, legem primam alia lege lata aliqua ex parte commutare. quod M. Tullius his verbis complexus est. Deinde indignum de lege alialiquid derogari, aut legem abrogari, aut alia ex parte commutari, id est, vt ipse loquitur, aliis in locis legi obrogari. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Id est pars prima tollitur: I think one should read "Pars prima legis tollitur", so that to derogate means to take away part of an earlier law. Digest, l. Derogatur, De verborum significatione. To repeal in part (exrogare) is also the same, on the authority of Sextus Pompeius. To obrogate is to change a former law in some part by a later enacted law, which Marcus Tullius expressed in these words: "Next, it is unworthy for anything to be derogated from a law, or a law to be abrogated, or changed in some part"; that is, in his own words, to be obrogated in other places. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Hodie autem ] Hic talia quaedam desunt. Olim liberi non erant qui aliter quam vindicta, censu, vel testamento, manumittebantur. Cuiac.
units.tr: Hodie autem: here some such matters are missing. Formerly, those were not free who were manumitted otherwise than by vindicta, by census, or by will. Cuiacius.

units.la: Lege Iunia ] leg. unica C.de Latina libertate, Norbana scilicet. §.3. Inst. de libert. Nouell. 78. Alia est Iunia Patronia vel Petronia de libertate l.24.ff.de manumiss.
units.tr: Lege Iunia: Code, the single law De Latina libertate, namely the Norbanian law. Institutes, §3 De libertatibus; Novel 78. Another is the Junian Patronian or Petronian law on liberty, Digest, l. 24 De manumissis.

units.la: Inter amicos ] §. 1. Instit. de libert. Latini aut per epistolam, aut inter amicos, aut conuiuii adhibitione manumittebantur. vid. Caium 1. §.3. Hoscè manumittendi modos Theophil. d. §. ᾧ τρὸς appellat φυσικὰς, quibus apponit d. loco, ἀνομαν τεόπον ἱλαθείας. Goth.h.
units.tr: Inter amicos: Institutes, §1 De libertatibus. Latins were manumitted either by letter, among friends, or by admission to a banquet. See Gaius 1, §3. Theophilus, in the passage beginning "ᾧ τρὸς", calls these modes of manumission natural, and in the same place adds "an unwritten manner of freedom" [ἄγραφον τρόπον ἐλευθερίας]. Gothofredus, here.

units.la: Dediticiorum ] vid.C.de deditiua libertate.
units.tr: Dediticiorum: see the Code, De deditiua libertate.

units.la: Qui poenae causa vincti ] Huc pertinet l. fideicommissaria 2.de fid.lib. cuius sensus hic est. Fideicommissaria libertas non debetur ei, quem postea dominus ob delictum vinxit, quia Dediticiorum numero habetur. Secus est, si heres vinxerit, arg. l.caetera in f. de leg.1. & hoc Paulus tradit lib.4.sententiarum 2.tit. ex quo detorta videtur l.fideicommiss. Nam & sententiae speciem habet. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Qui poenae causa vincti: to this belongs the law Fideicommissaria 2, De fideicommissariis libertatibus, whose sense here is this: a fideicommissary liberty is not owed to a slave whom the master afterwards bound in chains for a crime, because he is counted among the dediticii. It is otherwise if the heir bound him; compare the law Caetera, in fine, De legatis 1. Paul hands this down in Sentences 4, title 2, from which the law Fideicommissaria seems to have been twisted, for it also has the form of a sentence. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Poenae causa ] Nam fugitiuos solebant plerunque poenae causa notis compungere.
units.tr: Poenae causa: for fugitives were commonly branded with marks by way of punishment.

units.la: A domino] l.43.ff. de fideicommiss. libert. vel alio eius iussu aut ratihabitione. Paul.4.sentent. 12. §.8. Aliud si ab hærede. Paulus. 4.sentent. 12. §.4. Quid si à communi domino? vid. Paul. ibid.§.5. Quid si à creditore? sunt quoque. Paul. ibid. §. 6. Quid si domini furiosi aut pupilli iussu? Non fient Dedititij. Paul. ibid. §. 7. Gothofr. h.
units.tr: A domino: Digest, l. 43, De fideicommissariis libertatibus; or by another's order or ratification. Paul, Sentences 4, 12, §8. Otherwise if it was done by the heir: Paul, Sentences 4, 12, §4. What if it was done by a co-owner? See Paul, ibid., §5. What if by a creditor? Those too are dediticii; Paul, ibid., §6. What if by the order of a furious or pupil owner? They do not become dediticii; Paul, ibid., §7. Gothofredus, here.

units.la: Quibus vestigia] Legendum videtur, Quibusve stigmata, nisi vestigia sunt noxæ. Seneca lib.1. de benefic. Sic non est beneficium, quod sub oculos venit, sed beneficii vestigium & nota. Ergo serui compuncti notis, manumissione Deditilij efficiuntur. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Quibus vestigia: it seems one should read "Quibusve stigmata", unless vestigia are the traces of an injury. Seneca, Book 1 De beneficiis: "So that is not a benefit which comes under the eyes, but the trace and mark of a benefit." Therefore slaves pricked with marks become dediticii by manumission. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Vestigia] σίγματα χξ τῶ μετὰ ὅπω. Theoph.§. τῶν ἀπελευθέρων. Inst.de libert. vid. Caium 1.§.3.
units.tr: Vestigia: marks [στίγματα]. Theophilus, on the passage "τῶν ἀπελευθέρων", Institutes, De libertatibus. See Gaius 1, §3.

units.la: Nocentesque inuenti] id est, confessi. Nam qui torti, nec confessi sunt, ciues Romani fieri possunt, vt Paul. in eod.lib. scribit.
units.tr: Nocentesque inventi: that is, confessed. For those who were tortured but did not confess can become Roman citizens, as Paul writes in the same book.

units.la: Nocentes] Aliud si innocentes. Paul. 4.sentent. 12. §.3.
units.tr: Nocentes: otherwise if they were innocent. Paul, Sentences 4, 12, §3.

units.la: Vel in cuius custodiam] In publicum carcerem. Igitur publicus carcer deditirium facit, non priuatus: nisi corpori vincula adhibita sint. Iverum.de verb.sign. Cuiac.h. Custodiam] publicam scilicet, alias priuatus carcer non impediret, nisi vincula fuissent injecta l.216.ff.de verb.sign.
units.tr: Vel in cuius custodiam: into the public prison. So a public prison makes them dediticii, not a private one, unless shackles were put on the body. Iverum, De verborum significatione; Cuiacius, here. "Custodiam": clearly the public one, since otherwise a private prison would not be an impediment unless chains had been put on; Digest, l. 216, De verborum significatione.

units.la: Coniecti] non idem fuit, si dominus seruum ab honore ministrandi vel administrandi removisset.l.81. in sin.ff.de manum.testam.
units.tr: Coniecti: it was not the same if the master had removed the slave from the honour of ministering or administering. Digest, l. 81 in fine, De manumissis testamento.

units.la: Ælia] §.3.Inst.de libert.
units.tr: Aelia: Institutes, §3 De libertatibus.

units.la: Eadem lege] Sentia.§.11.in sin. sup. eod.
units.tr: Eadem lege: the Sentian law, §11 near the end, above in the same title.

units.la: Seruus] Ita etiam manumittitur, cum ad statutam ætatem peruenerit l.vlt.ff.de reb. dubiis. id est, cum seruus erit 30. annorum liber esto l.39.§.2.ff.familiæ. Goth.h.
units.tr: Servus: so too he is manumitted when he reaches the age stated; Digest, last law De rebus dubiis; that is, when the slave is thirty years old, "let him be free"; Digest, l. 39, §2, De familiae erciscundae. Gothofredus, here.

units.la: Testamento vero manumissum] Et idcirco quos ad ciuitatem Romanam perduci volebant, iis testamento libertatem dabant, sic, LIBERI SVNTO CVM ANNORVM ERVNT xxx.l.ex parte §.Sticho fam.ercisc.l. Aristo.de manum. testam. l. vlt.de reb. dubiis l.si quis ita §. vlt. de statu lib. In eo qui censu liberatur, nulla ætatis habita est ratio.Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Testamento vero manumissum: and so those whom they wished to bring into Roman citizenship they gave liberty by will in these words: "let them be free when they are thirty years old." In one who is freed by census, no account is taken of age. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Eadem lex eum] §. 4. Instit. quib. ex causis manumitt.
units.tr: Eadem lex eum: Institutes, §4 De causis quibus manumittuntur.

units.la: In consilium] hæc eadem & Theophilus scribit in titul. qui & quib. ex causis manumit. non possunt.
units.tr: In consilium: Theophilus writes the same thing under the title "Who and by what causes may not manumit."

units.la: Consilium] Theophil. Inst. quib.ex causs. manumitt. Consilium definit συνέδριον seu consilium spectabilium virorum, statis diebus coëuntium. Consilium autem hic intellige Prætoris. ris, Romæ, Præsidum & Proconsulis in provinciis. Theophil. d. loco.
units.tr: Consilium: Theophilus, Institutes, De causis quibus manumittuntur. "Consilium" is defined as [συνέδριον], or a council of distinguished men meeting on fixed days. Here "consilium" should be understood as that of the praetor at Rome, and of the presidents and proconsuls in the provinces. Theophilus, the same place.

units.la: à prætore scilicet.
units.tr: Namely, of the praetor.

units.la: li ita est, turpe non fuit, senatorem Prætori adsidere.
units.tr: Whether it is so, it was not shameful for a senator to sit beside the praetor.

units.la: à præsidibus scilicet & proconsulibus.
units.tr: Namely, of the presidents and proconsuls.

units.la: Ita dicti, quod per eos quisque debitum, id est, ius suum, reciperet. Hi adsidebant Præsidi, aut Prætori sedenti pro tribunali in provinciis Theoph. d. loco.
units.tr: So called because through them each person recovered what was owed to him, that is, his right. These sat beside the president, or the praetor sitting on the tribunal in the provinces. Theophilus, the same place.

units.la: §. 1. Inst. quibus ex causis manum. Caius 1. Inst. 5.
units.tr: Institutes, §1 De causis quibus manumittuntur; Gaius, Institutes 1, 5.

units.la: Ratio dubitandi sumitur ex §. 12. sup. eod.
units.tr: The ground of doubt is taken from §12 above, in the same title.

units.la: §. 1. Inst. quib. ex causis manumitt. id autem species est ignominiæ l. 26. ff. de fideicommiss. libert.
units.tr: Institutes, §1 De causis quibus manumittuntur; but this is a kind of ignominy. Digest, l. 26, De fideicommissariis libertatibus.

units.la: Ordo scripturæ attenditur. l. 24. §. 17. ff. de fideicommiss. libert.
units.tr: The order of the writing is what is attended to. Digest, l. 24, §17, De fideicommissariis libertatibus.

units.la: Caius idem lib. 1. Inst. Porro in cæteris rebus alienatis in fraudem, Rescissoria actione utimur, Pauliana, & Fabiana: non etiam in libertatibus datis in fraudem: quæ ipso iure nullæ sunt, ex lege Æl. Sentia. Cuiac. b.
units.tr: Gaius, the same, Book 1 of the Institutes. Moreover, in other things alienated in fraud we use the rescissory action, the Pauline and the Fabian; but not in liberties given in fraud, which are null by law itself, under the Aelian Sentian law. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Hunc Theophilus Bonitarium vocat, sequentem Quiritarium.
units.tr: Theophilus calls this Bonitarian, and the following Quiritarian.

units.la: Quod civis à cive comparat, nec mancipatum, aut cessione in iure accipit, aut nec dum vsucepit, id in bonis non habet: sed iure Quiritium tantum, Goth.h. testam. Nam Iustiniani constitutio in contrarium scripta est. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: What a citizen acquires from a citizen, if it was not taken by mancipation or by cession in court, nor yet has been usucapted, he does not hold among his goods, but only by Quiritary right. Gothofredus, here, on the Code. For Justinian's constitution was written to the contrary. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Liber non fit ] veteri iure proprietarius servum manumittendo, dominum admittebat. Interim tamen dum usufructus durabat, status manumissi erat in pendenti. l.9.in sin. ff. de hared.instit. nisi ipse fructuarius manumissioni consensisset, (tunc enim servus fiebat liber. l.2. ff.de manum.vind.) aut si proprietarius proprietatem servi, ipsi usufructuario reliquisset, vna cum libertate. l.6.ff. de manum.testam. Hodie manumissus à proprietario servus, fit liber, usufructuario necessitatem habente manumittere, accepta prius sui usufructus iusta æstimatione. l.1.§.2.C.de communi seruo. Goth.h.
units.tr: Liber non fit: under the old law, a proprietor who manumitted a slave admitted the right of the usufructuary; meanwhile, as long as the usufruct lasted, the status of the manumitted slave was pending. Digest, l. 9 in fine, De heredibus instituendis; unless the usufructuary himself had consented to the manumission (for then the slave became free; Digest, l. 2, De manumissione vindicta), or unless the owner had left the ownership of the slave to the usufructuary himself together with the liberty (Digest, l. 6, De manumissis testamento). Today a slave manumitted by the owner becomes free, the usufructuary being under the necessity of manumitting, once he has first received a just estimate of his usufruct. Code, l. 1, §2, De communi servo. Gothofredus, here.

units.la: Post mortem haeredis ] quia nihil ab haerede haeredis relinqui potest. Paul.3.sent.§.2. & haec prima ratio fuit dubitandi veteribus.
units.tr: Post mortem haeredis] Because nothing can be left by the heir of an heir after his death. Paul. 3. sent. §.2. This was the first reason for doubt among the ancients.

units.la: Aut ante ] quia testamenta accipiunt vim ab institutione haeredis §.34.Inst.de legat. & haec fuit secunda ratio dubitandi veteribus.
units.tr: Aut ante] Because wills take their force from the institution of the heir. §.34. Inst. de legat. This was the second reason for doubt among the ancients.

units.la: Dari non potest] hodie hoc abrogatum est §. 34.Inst.de legat. Cur ita? Inciuile est scripturae ordinem sequi, testatoris autem voluntatem sperni.d.§.34.Goth.h.
units.tr: Dari non potest] Today this has been abrogated. §.34. Inst. de legat. Why so? It is uncivil to follow the order of the writing and to spurn the will of the testator. d. §.34. Goth. h.

units.la: Non valet ]hodie valet d.§.34.in sin.
units.tr: Non valet] Today it is valid. d. §.34. in fin.

units.la: Legatarii partis]hic locus admodum depravatus est: Crediderim legendum, Præf. ærarii. præfectorum enim ærarii est, bona quæ fisco defedeferuntur, spernere, vel agnoscere. l.ergo. §. plane de fid. l.edicto de iur. fisc. Ph. Geruasii liber habet, ea lege aerarium partis haeres fiat. Cuiac. & Pac. hic.
units.tr: Legatarii partis] This passage is very corrupt. I would think it should read "prefects of the treasury" (Præf. ærarii), for it belongs to the prefects of the treasury to reject or accept the goods that fall to the fisc. l. ergo §. plane de fid. l. edicto de iur. fisc. The book of Philip Gervasius reads: by this law the treasury becomes heir of a part. Cuiac. & Pac. hic.

units.la: Mox quam vnus ] l.23. l.25. l.58. ff. de manumiss. testam.
units.tr: Immediately after the words "as soon as one". l.23. l.25. l.58. ff. de manumiss. testam.

units.la: Qui testamenti ] vid. d. l. 58. tit. 22. §. 1. infr. eod.
units.tr: Those of the testament. vid. d. l. 58. tit. 22. §. 1. infr. eod.

units.la: Et mortis tempore ] vel intra diem cretionis. l. verum de manu. test. & inf. tit. 22. Nam & qui intra diem cretionis haereditatis fit, prope est, vt defuncti fuisse videatur mortis tempore. Paci.
units.tr: And at the time of death] Or within the day of cretion. l. verum de manu. test. and below, tit. 22. For one who becomes heir within the day of cretion is nearly as if he were regarded as having been of the deceased at the time of death. Pacius.

units.la: Lex Furia Caninia ] Quid fiet, si supra statutum numerum seruos in testamento manumittat? Et placet liberari eos, qui primo loco scripti sunt, vsque ad legitimum numerum, quod & in l. Ælia seruatur l.qui soluendo 2. l. si non lex §. 1. de haered. inst. Quid fiet si in orbe, si permixte seruorum nomina scripta sint? Et placet impediri omnium libertatem. l.qui soluendo 1. & l.prox. eod. tit. Quid fiet, si in Codicillis quidem scripti sint? Et Paul. lib. 4. sent. nouissimum eis locum tribuit? quod puto verius dici. Rursus quaero, cum per l. Furiam, totam familiam inter viuos liberare liceat, non etiam in testamento, facilius enim quis in testamento totam familiam manumittit, quam inter viuos. Et eadem ratione senatus obligatae mulieri succurrit, tit, non donanti: Lex Iulia hypothecam prædij dotalis inhibet, non alienationem: Constitutio Theodosij Decurionibus, venditionem, non donationem aut permutationem, Nouella Iustiniani intercessiones pro marito, non pro extraneo. Quæro, an recte, quis moribundus prætermisso testamento totam familiam manumittrat? Et recte Caius lib. 1. Instit. hoc tanquam in fraudem legis excogitatum respicit, cui simile est, quod ad leg. Caniniam Paul. scribens tractat in l. si quis eum de cond. & idem. Sed pugnat cum Paulo l. si quis quos de legat. 2. nisi dicamus, legati retentionem esse non petitionem, vt in l. Lucius §. codicillis eod. tit. Et hæc de lege Caninia ex iure antiquo adnotare libuit: quæ & si ea lex abrogata sit, nobis in aliis tamen partibus iuris magno visui esse possunt. Cuiac. & Paci. b.
units.tr: Lex Furia Caninia] What happens if, in a will, a man manumits slaves beyond the statutory number? It is held that those written first in the list are freed, up to the lawful number; this is also observed under the Lex Ælia. l. qui soluendo 2. l. si non lex §.1. de haered. inst. What happens if the names of slaves are written in a circle, that is, mixed together? It is held that the freedom of all is prevented. l. qui soluendo 1. & l. prox. eod. tit. What happens if they are written in codicils? Paul, in lib. 4 sent., gives them the last place, which I think is the more correct view. Again I ask: since by the Furian law it is permitted to free the whole household between the living, why is it not permitted in a will? For one more easily manumits the whole household in a will than between the living. And by the same reasoning the senatus-consult comes to the aid of a woman bound as surety, not of one giving a gift; the Julian law forbids a mortgage on a dotal estate, not its alienation; the constitution of Theodosius, for decurions, forbids sale, not gift or exchange; a Novel of Justinian forbids intercession for a husband, not for a stranger. I ask whether it is right that a dying man, passing over his will, manumits the whole household. And Gaius rightly, in lib. 1. Instit., regards this as devised in fraud of the law, to which is similar what Paul, writing on the lex Caninia, treats in l. si quis eum de cond. and the same. But it conflicts with Paul in l. si quis quos de legat. 2, unless we say that retaining a legacy is not a claim, as in l. Lucius §. codicillis eod. tit. And it has pleased me to note these things about the Caninian law from the ancient law; although that law has been abrogated, they can nevertheless be of great use to us in other parts of the law. Cuiac. & Paci. b.

units.la: Lex Furia] Fulia. vid. Paul. 4. sent. §. 14. ad l. Fus. Canin.
units.tr: Lex Furia] Read "Fufia". vid. Paul. 4. sent. §.14. ad l. Fus. Canin.

units.la: Extribus] de numero seruorum testamento manumittendorum vid. Caium 2. adde §. 7. Inst. quib. ex causis manumitt.
units.tr: From three] On the number of slaves to be manumitted by testament, see Gaius 2; add §.7 Inst. quib. ex causis manumitt.

units.la: Ne plures] Caius d. loco. Paul. d. loc. Vupiscus in Tacito. Seruos manumisit intra centum tamen, ne Caniniam transire videretur. Quid iuris, si supra statutum numerum, manumissi fuissent? receptum eos liberati, qui primo loco scripti fuissent. l. 83. in sin. ff. de hared. instit. Caius d.loc. §. 2. Quid si in orbe, id est, permixte scripti? omnium impediebatur libertas l.42.43.ff. d.tit. nulli erant liberi. Caius d. loc. §.
units.tr: Lest more] Gaius, d. loco. Paul, d. loc. Vopiscus in Tacitus. He manumitted slaves, but within a hundred, lest he seem to pass beyond the Caninian law. What is the law if more than the statutory number had been manumitted? It is received that those written first are freed. l. 83. in fin. ff. de hared. instit. Gaius d. loc. §.2. What if they were written in a circle, that is, mixed together? The freedom of all was prevented. l. 42, 43. ff. d. tit. None were free. Gaius d. loc. §.

units.la: 2. Quid si codicillis quibusdam libertates datæ? ius codicilli testamentario cedebat. Paul. 4. sentent. 14. §. 2. Gothofr. h. vrd: paulo ante ex Cuiac.
units.tr: 2. What if freedoms were given by certain codicils? The right of the codicil yielded to the testamentary right. Paul, 4 sent. 14. §.2. Gothofr. h. vrd.: a little before, from Cuiacius.

units.la: Eadem lex cauet] §. libertas. de legat.
units.tr: The same law provides. §. libertas. de legat.

units.la: Nominatim ] nominatim videtur liber esse iussus, qui vel ex artificio, vel officio, vel quoliber alio modo euidenter denominatus est, v. l.24.ff. de manumiss. testam. Paul. 4. sent. vlt. §.1. §. 25. in f. Inst. de legat.
units.tr: Nominatim] A slave seems to be ordered free by name when he has been clearly designated, whether by his craft, his office, or in any other way. See l.24 ff. de manumiss. testam. Paul. 4 sent. vlt. §.1. §.25 in fin. Inst. de legat.

units.la: Tit. II. De statu liberis.
units.tr: Title II. On the statuliber.

units.la: QVi sub conditione testamento liber esse iussus est, statu liber appellatur.
units.tr: He who is ordered in a will to be free under a condition is called a statuliber.

units.la: Statu liber quandiu pendet conditio seruus heredis est.
units.tr: While the condition is pending, the statuliber is the slave of the heir.

units.la: Statu liber seu alienetur ab herede, siue suscipiatur ab aliquo, libertatis conditionem secum trahit.
units.tr: Whether a statuliber is sold by the heir or taken over by someone else, he carries the condition of his freedom with him.

units.la: Sub hac conditione liber esse iussus, si decem millia heredi dederit, & si ab herede alienatus sit, emptori dando pecuniam, ad libertatem perueniet: idque lex duodecim Tabularum iubet.
units.tr: One ordered to be free under this condition, that he give ten thousand to the heir, if he has been sold by the heir, will attain liberty on giving the money to the buyer. The Law of the Twelve Tables orders this.

units.la: Si per hæredem factum sit, quo minus statu liber conditioni pareat, perinde fit liber, atque si conditio expleta fuisset.
units.tr: If the heir brings it about that the statuliber cannot comply with the condition, he becomes free just as if the condition had been fulfilled.

units.la: Extraneo pecuniam dare, iussus, & liber esse, si paratus sit dare, & is qui iussus est dare, aut noller accipere, aut antequam acceperit moriatur, perinde fit liber, ac si pecuniam dedisset.
units.tr: One ordered to give money to a stranger and to be free, if he is ready to give it, and the person who was ordered to receive it either refuses to accept it or dies before accepting, becomes free just as if he had paid the money.

units.la: Libertas & directo potest dari hoc modo, Liber esto, liber sit, Liberum esse iubeo: & per fideicommissum, vt puta, Rogo, fideicommitto heredis mei, ut Stichum seruum manumittat.
units.tr: Liberty can be given directly in this way: Let him be free, let him be free, I order that he be free; and by trust (fideicommissum), for example: I request, and I entrust to my heir, that he manumit the slave Stichus.

units.la: Is qui directo liber esse iussus est, horcinus fit libertus. Is autem cui per fideicommissum data est libertas, non testatoris, sed manumissoris fit libertus.
units.tr: One who is ordered directly to be free becomes a freedman of Horcus. But one to whom liberty is given by trust becomes a freedman not of the testator but of the one who manumits him.

units.la: Cuius fideicommissi potest ad rem aliquam praestandam, eiusdem etiam libertas fideicommissi potest.
units.tr: Whatever trust can be for the performance of some thing, the freedom given by that trust may also be.

units.la: Per fideicommissum libertas dari potest tam proprio seruo testatoris, quam heredis, aut legatarij, vel cuiuslibet extranei seruo.
units.tr: By trust, liberty can be given to the testator's own slave, or to the heir's, the legatee's, or any stranger's slave.

units.la: Alieno seruo per fideicommissum data libertate, si dominus eum iusto pretio non vendat, extinguitur libertas. quoniam nec pretii computatio pro libertate fieri potest.
units.tr: If liberty is given by trust to another's slave, and the owner does not sell him for a just price, the liberty is extinguished, since no reckoning of price can be made for liberty.

units.la: Libertas sicut dari, ita & adimi tam testamento, quam codicillis testamento confirmatis potest: vt tamen eodem modo adimatur, quo & data est. Statu liberis ] vid. Goth. ad l. 1. ff. eod.
units.tr: On the statuliber] see Gothofredus on l. 1 ff. eod. Liberty can be taken away as well as given, both by will and by codicils confirmed by the will; but it must be taken away in the same way in which it was given.

units.la: Conditionem secum ] statuliber vendi potest. l. 20. ff. eod. non tamen duris conditionibus in venditione onerandus est. l. 35. ff. eod. ne pacto haeredis, eius conditio fiat durior. leg. 33. ff. eod. Ideoque nec alienatio, nec vsucapio ei nocebit, quo minus existente conditione libertatem consequatur. l. 13. Cod. de testam. manum. Quid si legatus fuit? cum sua causa alienabitur. l. 45. in f. ff. de fidei. lib. Goth. h.
units.tr: Carries the condition with him] A statuliber can be sold, l. 20 ff. eod.; yet he must not be burdened with harsh conditions in the sale, l. 35 ff. eod.; nor is his condition made harsher by an agreement of the heir, l. 33 ff. eod. Hence neither alienation nor usucapion will harm him, so that when the condition is met he obtains his liberty, l. 13 Cod. de testam. manum. What if he was bequeathed? He will be alienated together with his own cause, l. 45 in f. ff. de fidei. lib. Gothofredus here.

units.la: Emptori ] aut similibus successoribus. l 27. in sin. ff. eod.
units.tr: To the buyer] or to similar successors. l 27. in sin. ff. eod.

units.la: Idque lex 12. tabularum iubet ] in hac lege emtoris nomine continentur omnes, qui quoquo iure dominium in statulibero nacti sunt. Et hoc Pomponius scribit in l. statuliberi a ceteris. de statu liber. Hac item l. significatur, vendi statuliberos posse. Et hoc est, quod Modestinus in eod. tit. statuliberos, ait, vaenundari posse ll. 12. tab. putauerunt: quasi haec fuerit sententia 12. tabular. sic sup. Vlpian. de l. Aelia Sentia. Ideo sine consilio manumissum, seruum manere putat. & M. Tullius lib. 4. de republ. Iurgare lex putat inter se vicinos, non litigare.
units.tr: The Law of the Twelve Tables orders this] Under the name of buyer in this law are included all who have acquired ownership of a statuliber by any right whatever. Pomponius writes this in l. statuliberi a ceteris, de statu liber. This law also indicates that statuliberi can be sold. And this is what Modestinus says in the same title, that the jurists thought statuliberi could be sold under the Twelve Tables, as if this were the meaning of the Twelve Tables; so above, Ulpian on the lex Aelia Sentia. Therefore he thinks a slave manumitted without advice remains a slave. And M. Tullius, book 4 de republica: the law holds that neighbours should bicker with one another, not go to law.

units.la: Si per haeredem ] l. 3. §. 1. ff. eod. aut haeredis tutorem & curatorem. l. 3. §. 10. ff. eod.
units.tr: If by the heir] l. 3. §. 1. ff. eod. or the heir's guardian and curator. l. 3. §. 10. ff. eod.

units.la: Extraneo ] cuiuis denique d. §. 10.
units.tr: To a stranger] to anyone at all, d. §. 10.

units.la: Et directo ] l. 43. ff. de manum. testam. Directo manumittitur, qui à nullo quam à testatore manumittitur. §. 2. Instit. de singul. reb. per fideicommiss.
units.tr: And directly] l. 43. ff. de manum. testam. One is manumitted directly who is manumitted by no one other than the testator. §. 2 Instit. de singul. reb. per fideicommiss.

units.la: Esse iubeo ] Iubeo est verbum directum.
units.tr: I order that he be free] Iubeo is a direct verb.

units.la: Et per fideicommissum ] l. 16. ff. de fideicomm. libert. Quibus verbis fideicommittatur vid. §. ultim. Instit. de sing. reb. per fideicommiss. Paul. 4. sent. 1. §. 6.
units.tr: And by trust (fideicommissum): see l. 16 ff. de fideicommissis libertatis. For the words by which a trust is created, see §. ultim. Instit. de singulis rebus per fideicommissum, and Paul. 4 sent. 1, §. 6.

units.la: Rogo ] Rogo & fidei committo, verbum obliquum.
units.tr: I request] I request and entrust; an indirect verb.

units.la: Horcinus fit libertus ] Non male Horcinus. Nam & horcum quidam dixere παρὰ τὸ ὤργος. Hic autem nullius est libertus l. si necem. de bonis libert. nisi Charontis, Plutonis, Orci, quamobrem & Charonianus à Theophilo dictus est, ea forma qua Orcini senatores (quorum meminit Sueto. Tranquillus) à Plutarcho in M. Antonio Charonitæ dicuntur.
units.tr: Becomes a freedman of Horcus] "Horcinus" is not a bad word. For some have also called it horcum, derived from the Greek [ὤργος]. But such a man is the freedman of no one except Charon, Pluto, or Orcus, l. si necem. de bonis libert. wherefore Theophilus also called him Charonian, in the same way that the Orcini senators (whom Suetonius Tranquillus mentions) are called Charonites by Plutarch in his life of Mark Antony.

units.la: Non testatoris sed ] §. 2. Inst. de sing. reb. per fideicomm.
units.tr: Not of the testator, but] §. 2. Instit. de sing. reb. per fideicomm.

units.la: Ad rem aliquam ] puta pecuniam.
units.tr: Some thing] for instance, money.

units.la: Eiusdem etiam ] Ex hoc loco, puto initium l. 24. ff. de fideicom. libert. passiue legendum esse: quod & seqq. d. l. §. satis ostendunt. Goth. h.
units.tr: Of the same] From this place I think the beginning of l. 24. ff. de fideicom. libert. should be read in the passive voice, as the following sentences of that law, §. satis, also show. Goth. h.

units.la: Alieno seruo ] si relinquatur res aliena, & si hæres non possit eam redimere, non tamen extinguitur legatum aut fideicommissum. Nam iustum rei pretium ex testamento debetur. Si relinquatur libertas seruo alieno, quem nulnulla hæres conditione redimere possit, extinguitur fideicommissum libertatis: propterea quod libertas inæstimabilis res est. Sed videamus an hoc sit perpetuum: quid enim si eius serui dominium hæres quandoque nanciscatur? Et hoc constitutiones introduxerunt, l. deberi C. de fid. lib.
units.tr: Another's slave] If a thing belonging to another is bequeathed, and the heir cannot redeem it, the legacy or trust is nonetheless not extinguished, for the just price of the thing is owed under the will. If liberty is bequeathed to another's slave whom the heir cannot redeem on any condition, the trust of liberty is extinguished, because liberty is a thing beyond price. But let us see whether this is permanent: for what if the heir at some later time acquires ownership of that slave? The imperial constitutions introduced this, l. deberi C. de fid. lib.

units.la: hoc abrogatum est. l. 6. C. de fideicommiss. libert.
units.tr: This was repealed. l. 6. C. de fideicommiss. libert.

units.la: libertas æstimari non potest.
units.tr: Liberty cannot be valued.

units.la: l. 50. ff. de fideicommiss. libert. & ff. de ademptione libert.
units.tr: l. 50. ff. de fideicommiss. libert. & ff. de ademptione libert.

units.la: vid. l. 35. ff. de regul. iuris.
units.tr: See l. 35. ff. de regul. iuris.

units.la: Tit. III. De Latinis.
units.tr: Title III. On the Latins.

units.la: LAtini ius Quiritium consequuntur his modis, beneficio principali, liberis, iteratione, militia, naue, ædificio, pistrino: præterea ex Senatusconsulto, veluti quæ sit rer enixa.
units.tr: Latins obtain Quiritary right in these ways: by princely favour, by children, by repeated manumission, by military service, by a ship, by a building, and by a mill or bakery. Besides these, by a senatus consultum, as in the case of a woman who has borne three children.

units.la: Beneficio principali Latinus ciuitatem Romanam accipit, si ab imperatore ius Quiritium impetrauerit.
units.tr: By princely favour a Latin receives Roman citizenship if he has obtained Quiritary right from the emperor.

units.la: Liberis ius Quiritium consequitur Latinus, qui minor triginta annorum manumissionis tempore fuit. Nam lege Iunia cautum est, vt si ciuem Romanam, vel Latinam vxorem duxerit testatione interposita, quod liberorum quæquærendorum causa vxorem duxerit, postea filio filiaue, nato natauè, & anniculo facto, possunt apud Prætorem vel Præsidem prouinciæ causam probare, & fieri ciuem Romanum tam ipse quam filius filiaue eius & vxor, scilicet si & ipsa Latina sit, nam si vxor ciuis Romana fit, partus quoque ciuis Romanus est, ex se- natusconsulto, quod auctore Diuo Adriano factum est.
units.tr: A Latin obtains Quiritary right through children if he was under thirty years of age at the time of his manumission. For the lex Iunia provides that if he has married a Roman citizen, or a Latin woman, with a declaration made for the purpose of having children, and afterwards a son or daughter has been born to them and has reached the age of one year, they may prove the case before the praetor or the governor of the province, and both he and his son or daughter and his wife become Roman citizens. This holds, of course, if she is also a Latin; for if the wife is a Roman citizen, the child is also a Roman citizen, by the senatus consultum made on the authority of the deified Hadrian.

units.la: Iteratione fit ciuis Romanus, qui post Latinitatem, quam acceperat maior triginta annorum, iterum iuste manumissus est ab eo, cuius ex iure Quiritium seruus fuit. Sed huic concessum est, ex senatusconsulto, etiam liberis ius Quiritium consequi.
units.tr: A Latin becomes a Roman citizen by repetition if, after receiving Latinity while over thirty years of age, he is manumitted a second time, lawfully, by the person whose slave he was under Quiritary law. But by a senatus consultum this man was also granted that his children obtain Quiritary right.

units.la: Militia ius Quiritium accipit Latinus, si inter vigiles Romæ sex annis militauerit, ex lege Visellia. Præterea ex senatusconsulto concefsum est ei, vt si triennio inter vigiles militauerit, ius Quiritium consequatur.
units.tr: A Latin receives Quiritary right by military service if he has served six years among the night watchmen at Rome, under the lex Visellia. Besides this, by a senatus consultum it was granted to him that if he has served three years among the watchmen, he obtains Quiritary right.

units.la: Naue Latinus ciuitatem Romanam accipit, si non minorem quam decem mille modiorum nauem fabricauerit, & Romam sex annis frumentum portauerit, ex edicto Diui Claudij.
units.tr: A Latin receives Roman citizenship by a ship if he has built a ship of not less than ten thousand modii, and has carried grain to Rome for six years, under the edict of the deified Claudius.

units.la: De Latinis] Latini fiebat ex lege Iunia. Nouel. 78. Latinorum conditio hodie abrogata l. vnic. C. de Latina libert. toll.
units.tr: On the Latins] The Latins arose from the lex Iunia. Nov. 78. The condition of the Latins is today abrogated, l. unica C. de Latina libertate tollenda.

units.la: Latinius Quiritium] Igitur meliore conditione sunt Latini quam Deditician. Nam Dediticii nullo prorsus modo ius Quiritium consequuntur. Sed & Latini commercium habent, & testamenti factionem: Deditician non item. Latini vera libertate potiuntur quamdiu viuunt. Deditician vmbra & imaginibus libertatis. Ciues autem Romani meliore conditione sunt, quam Latini. Connubium enim Latini, & patriam potestatem non habent: testamentum facere, tutoresve dari non possunt; denique moriuntur quasi serui.
units.tr: The Latins' Quiritary right] Therefore the Latins are in a better condition than the Dediticii. For the Dediticii obtain Quiritary right in no way at all. But the Latins also have commercium and testamentary capacity; the Dediticii do not. The Latins enjoy true liberty as long as they live; the Dediticii have only the shadow and image of liberty. Roman citizens, however, are in a better condition than Latins. For Latins have no conubium and no paternal power; they cannot make a will or be given tutors; and finally they die as if they were slaves.

units.la: Nam si uxor ciuis Romana ] Partum Latinum nasci, argumento erat lex Mensia, de qua in tit.ul. ritul. §. propterea quod Latini non valde distant à peregrinis.
units.tr: If a Roman woman is his wife] That the offspring of a Latin is born a Latin was shown by the lex Mensia, concerning which see in the title, §. because the Latins are not very far removed from foreigners.

units.la: Romana ] Ex matre, ciue Romana, patre Latino, qui nascitur, ciuis Romanus est, antea fiebat Latinus arg.§.&.in f.inf.tit.§.
units.tr: Roman] A child born of a Roman citizen mother and a Latin father is a Roman citizen; formerly he became a Latin. See §. and at the end of the following title, §.

units.la: Iteratione ] Plinius 7.epistola.
units.tr: By repetition] Pliny, Letter 7.

units.la: Iterum ] Latinus si iterato manumissus suisset, fiebat ciuis Romanus §.1.sup. eod.1. Caius 1. §.5. in sin.
units.tr: Again] If a Latin had been manumitted a second time, he became a Roman citizen. §. 1, above, same title. Gaius 1, §. 5, at the end.

units.la: Sed huic concessum] Qui minor 30.annorum Latinitatem accipit, liberis ius Quiritium consequitur, ex l. Iunia post hanc aetatem qui Latinitatem accipit, non nisi patroni beneficio, sed ex S.C. etiam liberis ius Quiritium consequitur,Cuiac.h.
units.tr: But this man was granted] A man who receives Latinity under thirty years of age obtains Quiritary right for his children by the lex Iunia. A man who receives Latinity after this age obtains it only by the patron's favour; but by a senatus consultum he also obtains Quiritary right for his children. Cuiacius, on the passage.

units.la: Etiam liberis ] §.3.sup.eod.
units.tr: Also for children] §. 3, above, same title.

units.la: Militia] Vigilum septem cohortes D. Augustus in urbe ita constituit, ut binas regiones urbis unaquæque cohors tueretur. Constat enim 14. fuisse regiones urbis.l.3.de off.præf. vigil. Inter eos qui Latinus sex annis militasset, ex l. Visellia ius Quiritium consequebatur: tandem senatui triennium visum est sufficere. Visellia malo quam Visillia: quæ D. Claudii temporibus lata est, rogante L. Vitellio Varrone.l.1. C. ad l. Visel. leg.1. Cod. quand. cin. act. cri. praind.
units.tr: Military service] The Emperor Augustus established seven cohorts of watchmen in the city, so that each cohort guarded two regions of the city. For the city is agreed to have had fourteen regions. l. 3, de officio praefecti vigilum. Among those Latins who had served six years, Quiritary right was obtained under the lex Visellia; at last the senate judged that three years was enough. Read "Visellia" rather than "Visillia": it was passed in the time of the deified Claudius, on the proposal of Lucius Vitellius Varro. l. 1 C. ad l. Visellam; l. 1 Cod. quando civiliter agere...

units.la: Inter vigiles ] nocturni vigiles militare censen-sensentur. vid. Gothofr. ad leg. 8. §. 4. §. 6. ff. de excusat. tut.
units.tr: Among the watchmen] Night watchmen are regarded as serving in the militia. See Gothofredus on the law 8, §. 4, §. 6, de excusationibus tutorum.

units.la: Visellia] lata anno 763. vid. Gothof. in C. ad l. Visel.
units.tr: Visellia] Passed in the year 763 (of the city). See Gothofredus, on the Code, ad l. Visellam.

units.la: Præterea] id est, postea.
units.tr: Besides] That is, afterwards.

units.la: Naue] Non est mirum priuilegia dari nauium ædificatoribus. Nauis enim exercitio ad summam reipub. pertiner. l. 1. §. 20. ff. de exercitor. adde & aliud priuilegium, nauis ædificatori datum ex leg. 5. leg. 6. ff. qui potior. Non, 97 cap. 2.
units.tr: A ship] It is no wonder that privileges are granted to shipbuilders, for the operation of ships pertains to the public good as a whole. l. 1, §. 20, de exercitoria. Add also another privilege given to the shipbuilder, from l. 5, l. 6, qui potiores in pignore habeantur; Non 97, cap. 2.

units.la: Si non minorem] magna capacitas nauis fuit. Senatoribus olim non licuit lege lata à Q. Claudio tribuno plebis, nauem maritimam maiorem 300. amphorarum habere. Liuius lib. 21. qua de re vid. Gothofr. ad l. 3. ff. de vacation. muner.
units.tr: If not less than] The capacity of the ship was large. Formerly senators were not permitted, under a law proposed by Quintus Claudius, tribune of the plebs, to own a sea-going ship larger than 300 amphorae. Livy, book 21. On this matter see Gothofredus on l. 3, de vacatione munerum.

units.la: Diui Claudij] Suetonius in Claudio c. 18. in sin. Naues mercaturæ causa fabricantibus magna commoda constituit. & cap. 19. fœminis (quæ naues mercaturæ causa fabricarent) ius tribuit quatuor liberorum.
units.tr: Of the deified Claudius] Suetonius, in Claudius, chapter 18, at the end: he established great advantages for those who built ships for trade. And chapter 19: he granted to women who built ships for trade the right of four children.

units.la: Tit. IV. De his qui sui iuris sunt.
units.tr: Tit. IV. On those who are sui iuris.
