units.la: Vid. in Inst. 8. in ff. 6. Cai. 3.
units.tr: See in Inst. 8, in Ff. 6, Cai. 3.

units.la: SVI iuris sunt familiarum suarum principes, id est, paterfamiliæ, itemque materfamiliæ.
units.tr: Those who are sui iuris are the heads of their own families, that is, the fathers of families, and likewise the mothers of families.

units.la: Qui matre quidem certa, patre autem incerto nati sunt, spurij appellantur. Principes ] quasi diceret. Non sunt in alterius familia, sui iuris sunt, l. 4. ff. hoc tit. puta morte parentum. Tunc enim singuli liberi, singulas familias inchoant, iure saltem, etiamsi sine pupilli. l. 95. §. 2. ff. de verb. signif. ac sine matrimonio & liberis. Tertullianus in lib. de veland. virginib. Materfamilias est, licet virgo: paterfamilias, licet iuuenis, nouarumque familiarum principes atque duces esse possunt. Festus, in voce familiæ. Quod patresfamilias, quam domini familiæ potius appellantur, ratione non caret. Gratius est enim nomen patris, quam domini. Tertull. in apologet. Seneca 6. epist. Macrob. 1. Saturnal. 11. Martial.
units.tr: Those born of a known mother but an uncertain father are called spurii. "Heads" is as if he said: they are not in another's family; they are sui iuris, l. 4 ff. hoc tit., namely by the death of their parents. For then each child begins a family of his own, at least in law, even if he is a minor and without marriage and children. Tertullian, in his book on the veiling of virgins: a woman is a mother of a family even though she is a virgin, and a man is a father of a family even though he is young, and they can be the heads and leaders of new families. Festus, under "familiae". That they are called "fathers of families" rather than "masters of the family" is not without reason, for the name of father is more gracious than that of master. Tertullian, in the Apologeticus. Seneca, letter 6. Macrobius, Saturnalia 1, 11. Martial, 1. Epigram.

units.la: 1. Epigram.
units.tr: 1. Epigram.

units.la: Materfamiliæ ] Ea familiæ suæ & caput, & finis est. L. 195. in f. ff. de verb. signif.
units.tr: Materfamiliae: she is both the head and the end of her family. L. 195, in f. ff. de verb. signif.

units.la: Spurij appellantur ] spurij sunt, qui legitime quæsiti non sunt. Originem verbi Iustinianus explicat his verbis, unde solent spurij appellari, vel à Græca voce, quasi ἀπογεγόνῳ concepti, vel quasi sine patre filij, in tit. de nupt. sic in leg. divus. de captiu. sic Caius lib. 1. inst. sic Theoph, sic libri scripti: impressi non sic, quibus non assentior. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Spurii appellantur: spurii are those who are not lawfully begotten. Justinian explains the origin of the word in these words, whence spurii are usually so called, either from the Greek word, as if conceived "apogegonoi", or as if sons without a father, in tit. de nupt.; so in l. divus, de captiv.; so Gaius, lib. 1 Inst.; so Theophilus; so the manuscripts, though not the printed books, to which I do not assent. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Spurij ] ita dicuntur ἀπὸ τὴν ἀπογεγὼν, id est, sationem. l. 23. ff. de statu. quasi ἀπογεγόνῳ, seu sparsim concepti. vel à literis Latinis S. P. quasi sine patre. Theoph. §. ἀὶ ἡ ἡ ἐπιναρτίων. quam postremam stremam originem probat Caius 4. §. 8. in sin. & Martianus l. 2. §. in sin. ff. de captiuis. Vtramque originem assumit Tribonianus §. 12. Instit. de nupt. dum vult spurios dici ἀπάτορας, & ὢ ἂ̓ ὦ τοκέων. Festus nothum appellat spurio patre natum. ἀπὸ ὑιὸς à Plutarcho ioculari dicto appellatur, quasi matris filius. Muliebrem enim naturam veteres spurium vocarunt. 9. Isidorus §. ἀπάτορα. Plutarch. in problem. Gothib.
units.tr: Spurii: they are so called from [ἀπογεγόνῳ], that is, sown, l. 23 ff. de statu, as if [apogegonoi], or sparsim conceived; or from the Latin letters S.P., as if sine patre (without a father). Theophilus. Gaius 4 §8 in fine proves the last origin, and Martianus l. 2 § in fine, ff. de captiv. Tribonian, Inst. de nupt. §12, takes up both origins, wishing spurii to be called [ἀπάτορες], fatherless. Festus calls nothus one born of a spurious father. Plutarch, in a jesting saying, derives it as if it meant a mother's son, for the ancients called the female nature spurium. Isidore. Plutarch, in the Problems. Gothofredus.

units.la: Tit. V. De his qui in potestate sunt.
units.tr: Tit. V. On those who are in power.

units.la: IN potestate sunt liberi, parentum ex iusto matrimonio nati.
units.tr: Children born of parents in lawful marriage are in power.

units.la: Iustum matrimonium est, si inter eos qui nuptias contrahunt connubium sit, & tam masculus pubes quam fœmina potens sit, & utrique consentiant, si sui iuris sunt, aut etiam parentes eorum, si in potestate sunt.
units.tr: A marriage is lawful if there is connubium between those who contract it, and the male is of age and the female able to bear children, and both consent, if they are sui iuris, or their parents consent if they are in power.

units.la: Connubium est uxoris iure ducendæ facultas.
units.tr: Connubium is the capacity to take a wife by right.

units.la: Connubium habent cives Romani cum civibus Romanis: cum Latinis autem & peregrinis ita, si concessum sit.
units.tr: Roman citizens have connubium with Roman citizens; with Latins and foreigners only if it has been granted.

units.la: Cum seruis nullum est connubium.
units.tr: There is no connubium with slaves.

units.la: In parentes & liberos infinite cuiuscunque gradus connubium non est. Inter cognatos autem ex transuerso gradu, olim quidem usque ad quartum gradum matrimonia contrahi non poterant: nunc autem etiam ex tertio gradu licet vxorem ducere. Si tamen fratris filia, non etiam sororis filia, aut amita, vel matertera, quamuis eodem gradu sit: eandemque vxore: nouerca, vel priuigna, vel nurus, vel socrus nostra fuit, ducere non possumus.
units.tr: Between parents and children, in the direct line of whatever degree, there is no connubium. Between kin in the collateral line, marriages formerly could not be contracted up to the fourth degree, but now one may take a wife even from the third degree. But we may not take as wife a brother's daughter (though not a sister's daughter), nor an aunt or maternal aunt, although of the same degree; nor may we take a stepmother, stepdaughter, daughter-in-law, or mother-in-law of ours.

units.la: Si quis eam quam non licet, vxorem duxerit, incestum matrimonium contrahit: ideoque liberi in potestate eius non fiunt, sed quasi vulgo concepti, spurij sunt.
units.tr: If anyone takes as wife one whom it is not allowed, he contracts an incestuous marriage; therefore the children do not become in his power, but, as if conceived promiscuously, they are spurii.

units.la: Connubio interueniente, liberi semper patrem sequuntur, non interueniente connubio, matris conditioni accedunt, excepto eo, qui ex peregrino & ciue Romana, peregrinus nascitur: quoniam lex Mensia ex alterutro peregrino natum deterioris parentis conditionem sequi iubet.
units.tr: Where there is connubium, children always follow the father; where there is none, they take the status of the mother, except for one who is born a foreigner from a foreigner and a Roman citizen, since the Mensian law orders that one born of either foreign parent follow the condition of the worse parent.

units.la: Ex ciue Romano & Latina Latinus nascitur: & ex libero & ancilla, seruus: quoniam cum his casibus connubia non sint, partus sequitur matrem.
units.tr: From a Roman citizen and a Latin woman a Latin is born; and from a free man and a female slave, a slave. Since in these cases there is no connubium, the offspring follows the mother.

units.la: In his qui iure contracto matrimonio nascuntur, conceptionis tempus spectatur. In his autem qui non legitime concipiuntur, editionis: veluti si ancilla conceperit, deinde manumissa pariat, liberum parit. Nam quanuis non legitime concepit, cum editionis tempore libera sit, partus quoque liber est. Iustum ] legitimum. Caius 4. §. 1. secundum præcepta legum. Inst. de nupt.
units.tr: For those born of a lawfully contracted marriage, the time of conception is considered. For those not lawfully conceived, the time of birth is considered: for example, if a slave woman conceives and is then manumitted and gives birth, she bears a free child. For although she did not conceive lawfully, since she is free at the time of birth, the offspring is also free. Iustum: that is, lawful. Gaius 4 §1: according to the precepts of the laws. Inst. de nupt.

units.la: Inter eos ] id est, inter ciues. Legitimæ enim nuptiæ sunt si Romanus Romanam ducat. Caius 4. §. 1.
units.tr: Inter eos: that is, between citizens. For a marriage is lawful if a Roman takes a Roman woman as wife. Gaius 4 §1.

units.la: Fœmina potens ] id est, pubes. Masculus pubes esse debet, virgo viriporens. Inst. de nupt. l. 13. ff. de verb. sign. l. 101. ff. de condit. & demonstr. nubilis ætatis l. 10 ff. de condit. & demonst. maior annis 12. leg. 4. ff. de ritu. ἐφηβος παρθένος. 2. Eclog. 2. 13.
units.tr: Foemina potens: that is, of marriageable age. The male must be of age; the virgin must be able to bear children. Inst. de nupt.; l. 13 ff. de verb. sign.; l. 101 ff. de condit. et demonstr., of nubile age; l. 10 ff. de condit. et demonst., over 12 years of age; l. 4 ff. de ritu. [ἔφηβος παρθένος]. 2 Eclog. 2, 13.

units.la: Consentiant ] Tria requiruntur in iusto matrimonio. Primum vt qui contrahunt sint ciues Romani. sup. eod. ibi, connubium: vt sint puberes. sup. eod. ibi potens: Tertio vt consentiant, si sint sui iuris: vel parentes eorum, si in potestate, vt hic & l. 2. ff. de ritu. Instit. de nupt. Quartum Caius addidit, nuptias. d. §. 1. quo vocabulo, vt opinor, ritum solennem intelligit. vid. l. 24. C. de nupt.
units.tr: Consentiant: Three things are required for a lawful marriage. First, that those who contract it be Roman citizens (see above, ibid., connubium); second, that they be of age (see above, ibid., potens); third, that they consent, if they are sui iuris, or their parents if they are in power, as here and l. 2 ff. de ritu; Inst. de nupt. Gaius added a fourth, nuptials, in the said §1, by which word, I think, he means the solemn rite. See l. 24 C. de nupt.

units.la: Connubium ] Definitio connubij. Quidam scribunt Connubium per vnicum n.
units.tr: Connubium: the definition of connubium. Some write Connubium with a single n.

units.la: Habent ciues ] Isidorus 10. Etym. vlt. addit æquales eo sensu. Connubium esse, cum æquales nuptiis coëunt, vt puta ciues Romani, pari vtique dignitate. Idem receptum fuit aliquando ab Atheniensibus, apud quos lege Periclis pro notho habebatur qui natus non fuisset ex duobus Athenienšibus. Vid. Demosthenem in oratione ξ. Nεαρα.
units.tr: Habent cives: Isidore, Etym. 10 at the end, adds "equals" in this sense: connubium exists when equals come together in marriage, as Roman citizens do, of equal dignity. The same was at one time received among the Athenians, among whom by the law of Pericles one who was not born of two Athenians was considered a bastard. See Demosthenes in his oration against Neaera.

units.la: ] Boëtius in topicis, Non omnibus erat connubium cum Romanis, nec erant nuptiæ iure contractæ, quæ non aut inter ciuem Romanum ciuemque Romanam inhibantur; aut cui princeps populusve ciuitatem vel connubium permisisset: eo scilicet modo in potestatem parentum liberi redigu ntur. Hæc ille. Sic Hernicis permissum, Anagnignis ademtum connubium. Livius lib. 9.
units.tr: Boethius, in the Topics: Not everyone had connubium with the Romans, and marriages were not lawfully contracted unless they were not forbidden between a Roman citizen and a Roman woman, or unless the prince or the people had granted citizenship or connubium; in that way children are brought back into their parents' power. Thus far he. So connubium was granted to the Hernici and taken away from the Anagnini. Livy, book 9.

units.la: ] cum ancillis. l. 3. C. de incestis. inter servos & liberos Paul. 2. sent. 19. §. 3. Quid ergo? contubernium fuit. l. 14. §. 3. ff. de ritu.
units.tr: With female slaves: l. 3 C. de incestis. Between slaves and free persons, Paul, Sent. 2, 19 §3. What then? There was contubernium. l. 14 §3 ff. de ritu.

units.la: ] & tamen inter servos cognatio. Inst. de servili cognat. l. 10. §. 5. ff. de grad. Et quidem talis vt inter ascendentes & descendentes impediantur nuptiæ. Servilis enim cognatio impedimento nuptiis est. §. 10. Inst. de nupt. l. 8. l. 14. ff. de ritu. Est igitur connubium inter servos? Non est. Quoties connubium negamus esse inter servos, hoc intellige; Natos ex eiusmodi coniunctione cives non esse; iureque civium non frui, nec esse in parentum suorum potestate, servos esse. l. 3. C. de incestis. Et tamen quibus in negotiis summus pudor summaque honestas esse debet (vt in nuptiis d. §. 2.) non parcimus his nominibus: vt ita sit cognatio etiam inter servos. d. §. 5.
units.tr: And yet there is kinship among slaves: Inst. de servili cognat.; l. 10 §5 ff. de gradib. And indeed of such a kind that marriages between ascendants and descendants are impeded; for servile kinship is an impediment to marriage. §10 Inst. de nupt.; l. 8, l. 14 ff. de ritu. Is there therefore connubium among slaves? There is not. Whenever we say there is no connubium among slaves, understand this: that children born of such a union are not citizens, do not enjoy the rights of citizens, are not in their parents' power, but are slaves. l. 3 C. de incestis. And yet in those matters in which the highest modesty and honour ought to be (as in marriages, d. §2), we do not spare these names, so that there is kinship even among slaves. d. §5.

units.la: Ii l. 14 l. 14. §. 2 §. 3 ff. de ritu. Sic conniuentibus oculis seruos dicimus habere bona propria. l. 4. §. 1. ff. de manumission. & quasi testamenta facere, Plin. 8. epist. 16. eaque ut legitima custodi mandant, rogantque quod vilum est, pareo ocyus, res suas diuidunt, donant, relinquunt, duntaxat intra domum. Nam seruis respublica quaedam & quasi ciuitas, domus est. Goth.h.
units.tr: These: l. 14 §§2, 3 ff. de ritu. Thus, with eyes half closed, we say that slaves have their own goods, l. 4 §1 ff. de manumiss., and, as it were, make wills, Plin. 8 epist. 16; they entrust these as if they were lawful to be kept, and ask for what is cheap, and obey more quickly; they divide, give, and leave their goods, but only within the house. For for slaves the household is a kind of commonwealth and city. Goth. h.

units.la: Inter parentes ]l. 17. C. de nupt.
units.tr: Between parents: law 17, C. de nuptiis.

units.la: Nunc autem etiam ex tertio ] Hic locus sic meo iudicio restituendus est. Nunc autem etiam ex quarto gradu licet uxorem ducere. Sed tamen fratris aut sororis filiam, neptemve eorum, quamuis eodem gradu sit, amitam vel materteram, eamque uxorem, quae nouerca vel priuigna, vel nurus, vel socrus nostra fuit, ducere non possumus. Olim igitur inter se patrueles, amitini, consobrini, matrimonio iungi non poterant: id quod & Caius scribit lib.
units.tr: Nunc autem etiam ex tertio ]: In my judgment this passage should be restored to read: "Now, however, one may also marry from the fourth degree. But one may not marry a daughter of a brother or sister, or their granddaughter, even though she is in the same degree; nor an aunt or niece; nor a woman who was once our stepmother, stepdaughter, daughter-in-law or mother-in-law." Accordingly, in the past, paternal cousins, first cousins on the father's side, and first cousins on the mother's side could not be joined in marriage to one another. Gaius also writes this in book 1 of the Institutes. Today they can, by the imperial constitutions.

units.la: 1. Inst. Hodie ex constitutionibus possunt. Perperam ex tertio gradu, nam iure ciuili ex tertio gradu uxorem ducere numquam licuit: neque vero nunc licet. Caetera quam Inepte descripta fuerint ex Caij & Iustiniani institutionibus, ex graduum ratione deprehendi potest. sed vid. obserue 13. c. 16.
units.tr: Today by the constitutions they can. The phrase "from the third degree" is wrongly written, for by civil law marriage from the third degree was never permitted, and it is not permitted now either. How the rest was badly described can be seen from the Institutes of Gaius and Justinian, and from the system of degrees. But see the note on book 13, chapter 16.

units.la: Si tamen ] Fratris vel sororis neptem (& sic deinceps) duci non posse constat, etiamsi quarto gradu, §. 3. Inst. de nupt. Multo minus filiam fratris, quæ est tertio gradu. Caius 4. §. 3. Quid amitini vel consobrini inter se? Iure veteri hæ personæ iungi inter se non potuerunt. Caius 4. §. 6. Possunt hodie novis constitutionibus §. 4. Inst. de nupt. l. 19. C. de nupt.
units.tr: Si tamen ]: It is established that a granddaughter of a brother or sister (and so on in the line) cannot be married, even in the fourth degree (Inst. de nupt. §3). Much less a daughter of a brother, who is in the third degree (Gaius 4, §3). What of first cousins, paternal or maternal, between themselves? By the old law these persons could not be joined in marriage (Gaius 4, §6). Today they can, by new constitutions (Inst. de nupt. §4; l. 19, C. de nupt.).

units.la: Incestum matrimonium] Ergo non tantum inter parentes & liberos incestæ sunt nuptiæ, sed & inter eos qui ex transverso, vel qui assinitate, coniuncti sunt: quod & Caius scribit lib. 1. Inst. & Paulus in l. sororis. de ritu nupt. Et præterquam quod iure gentium inter parentes & liberos, cæterum iure ciuili incestæ sunt nuptiæ.
units.tr: Incestum matrimonium ]: So marriages are incestuous not only between parents and children, but also between those joined in the collateral line or by affinity. Gaius writes this in book 1 of the Institutes, and Paul in the law sororis, de ritu nupt. Moreover, marriage between parents and children is incestuous by the law of nations, while the other cases are incestuous by civil law.

units.la: ita ex incestis nuptiis nati.
units.tr: Thus those born of incestuous marriages.

units.la: Quoniam lex Mensia] l. lex natura. de statu homin. seruus est.d. §. 9. natus vulgo, matrem sequitur; l. 1. in sin. ff. ad municipalem. vt & is qui illegitimo matrimonio, nisi lex specialis aliud inducat. l. 24. ff. de statu. Et hoc obseruandum quod interpretes notant, Bastardos patrum suorum nobilitate, eorumque priuilegiis frui ; sed & nomine & insignibus gentis & familiae. Guido Papae quaest. 580. Papon. 3. Notar. 6. c. de legitimation. de Bastards. eosque adipiscendarum dignitatum quoque capaces. l. 3. §. 2. ff. de Decurionibus. Ex duobus ingenuis natus, patrem sequitur, quod ad honores l. 19. ff. de statu. Ideoque natus ex patre Campano, municeps erit Campanus. Quae regula vera est, nisi priuilegio aliquo materna origine censeantur liberi. Tunc enim liberi maternae originis municipes erunt; exempli gratia: Ilienfibus concessum est, vt qui matre Ilienfi esset, Ilienfium municipium sortiretur l. 1. §. 2. ff. ad municip. Idem Delphensibus & Ponticis mulieribus tributum. d. §. 2. & Antiochenis l. 22. Cod. de decurion. In Campania Galliae, natus ex nobili muliere & ignobili patre, fit nobilis, eo scilicet priuilegio. En Champaigne le ventre ennoblit. vid. Goth. ad l. 1. in sin. ff. ad municip. Ex duobus diuersorum dominorum adscriptitiis natus impar, matris: par vero, patris conditionem sequitur. Nouel. 156. Ex libera & seruo vel adscriptitio olim fiebat seruus & adscriptitius. l. 27. ff. depos. quod merito sublatum. l. unic. C. de S. C. Claudiano. ex ingenua & murilegula conditionem paternam sequitur l. 3. C. de murilegulis. Adde & hoc, Natum in Gallia ex peregrino & Galla muliere, Gallici iuris censeri, patri succedere & ab intestato & testato, fisco nullum ius albinagij competere, hæreditatem paternam ad liberos eius in infinitum, & cognatos in ead. Gallia commorantes deferri, quod est contra ius ciuile, quo peregrini sine beneficio principali testari non poterant. l. 11. ff. qui testam. l. 31. 32 ff. de iure fisci. vid. Papon. 3: Notar. 6. cap. des lettres de Naturalite. Idem ius esse puto: si Galli apud peregrinas gentes morentur, ibique liberos suscipiant: fruentur enim eius liberi iure Gallico: si tamen apud fœderatos Galliæ populos eos susceperint. l. 32. ff. de iure fisci l. 7. ff. de captiu. ideoque nedum hæreditatis paternæ dominium retinebunt d. l. 7. sed & hæredes poterunt instituì. Goth. h.
units.tr: Quoniam lex Mensia ]: Since by the law lex natura, de statu homin. a child is a slave, and by §9 (d.) a child born out of wedlock follows the mother's condition (l. 1 in fine, ff. ad municipalem), as does one born of an illegitimate marriage, unless a special law provides otherwise (l. 24, ff. de statu). This must be observed, as the interpreters note: bastards share in the nobility of their fathers and their privileges, and also in the name and insignia of the clan and family (Guido Papae, quaest. 580; Papon, 3 Notar. 6; c. de legitimation; de Bastards), and they are also capable of attaining dignities (l. 3, §2, ff. de Decurionibus). A child born of two free-born parents follows the father as regards honours (l. 19, ff. de statu). Hence a child born of a Campanian father will be a citizen of Campania. This rule is true, unless by some privilege children are reckoned by their maternal origin. For then children of maternal origin will be citizens there. For example, it was granted to the Ilienses that whoever was born of an Ilian mother should belong to the municipality of Ilium (l. 1, §2, ff. ad municip.). The same was granted to the Delphians and to Pontic women by tribute (d. §2), and to the Antiochenes (l. 22, Cod. de decurion.). In Campania of Gaul, a child born of a noble mother and an ignoble father becomes noble, by that privilege, as the saying goes in Champagne: the belly ennobles (see Goth. on l. 1, in fine, ff. ad municip.). A child born of two adscripti of different masters follows the condition of the mother if it is unequal, and of the father if it is equal (Nov. 156). Formerly, a child of a free woman and a slave or adscriptus became a slave and adscriptus (l. 27, ff. depos.), which was rightly abolished (l. unic. C. de S.C. Claudiano). A child of a free woman and a murilegula follows the father's condition (l. 3, C. de murilegulis). Add this too: a child born in Gaul of a foreign man and a Gallic woman is held to be under Gallic law; he succeeds his father both intestate and by will; the fisc has no right of albinagium; the paternal inheritance passes to his children without limit, and to kinsmen dwelling in the same Gaul. This is contrary to civil law, by which foreigners could not make a will without special imperial grant (l. 11, ff. qui testam.; l. 31, 32, ff. de iure fisci; see Papon, 3 Notar. 6, cap. des lettres de Naturalite). I think the same law holds if Gauls stay among foreign peoples and have children there, for such children will enjoy Gallic law, provided however that they were born among the allied peoples of Gaul (l. 32, ff. de iure fisci; l. 7, ff. de captiu.). Therefore they will not only keep ownership of the paternal inheritance (d. l. 7), but may also be instituted heirs. Goth. h.

units.la: Conceptionis tempus ] Mulier quæ libera vel concepit, vel vtero libera partum gestauit, vel libera peperit, liberum parit. Vel ita, cuius mater libera fuerit vel conceptionis, vel partus, vel intermedio tempore, liber nascitur. l. 5. §. 2. ff. de statu. Paul. 2. sentent. 24. §. 1. 2. 3. Censetur autem libera quæ manumissa debuit, nec est manumissa. l. 1. §. 1. ff. de suis. Paul. ibid. §. 4. Ad eundem modum conceptus ex concubinatu, natus in matrimonio, fit legitimus: Nouel. 7. Tentari potest, eum esse ciuem Romanum, qui patre ciue conceptus est, licet patre postea peregrino nascatur: & nobilem, qui tempore conceptionis, patrem nobilem habuerit, quamtumuis postea pater nobilitatem amiserit. Goth.h.
units.tr: Conceptionis tempus ]: A woman who was free either at conception, or carried the child free in her womb, or gave birth while free, bears a free child. Or put thus: a child whose mother was free at conception, or at birth, or in the intervening time, is born free (l. 5, §2, ff. de statu; Paul, Sent. 2, 24, §§1–3). A woman is considered free if she ought to have been manumitted and has not been manumitted (l. 1, §1, ff. de suis; Paul, ibid., §4). In the same way, a child conceived in concubinage but born in marriage becomes legitimate (Nov. 7). It may be held that one conceived by a citizen father is a Roman citizen, although the father is later a foreigner when the child is born; and that one who at conception had a noble father is noble, although the father afterwards lost his nobility. Goth. h.

units.la: Veluti si ancilla conceperit ] Quod si libera conceperit, deinde ancilla peperit, partus quoque seruus est: si hanc iuris ciuilis regulam sequamur: quod & Caius scribit lib.1. Inst. Sed fauore libertatis placuit eum liberum nasci, & ita Marc. scribit in l. & seruorum, de statu hom. & Paul. lib.11. sentent.
units.tr: Veluti si ancilla conceperit ]: But if a free woman conceived, and afterwards gave birth as a slave, the offspring is also a slave, if we follow this rule of civil law. Gaius also writes this in book 1 of the Institutes. But out of favour to liberty it was decided that the child be born free; so Marcian writes in the law et seruorum, de statu hom., and Paul in book 11 of the Sentences.

units.la: Tit. VI. De Dotibus.
units.tr: Title VI. On Dowries.

units.la: DOs aut datur, aut dicitur, aut promittitur.
units.tr: A dowry is either given, or declared, or promised.

units.la: Dotem dicere potest mulier, quae nuptura est: & debitor mulieris, si iussu eius dicat institurus.
units.tr: A woman who is about to marry may declare a dowry, and so may her debtor, if he declares it at her direction, as her appointed agent.

units.la: Parens mulieris virilis sexus per virilem sexum cognatione iunctus, velut pater, auus paternus. Dare promittere dotem omnes possunt.
units.tr: A parent of the woman who is male and related to her through the male line, such as her father or paternal grandfather. Anyone at all may give or promise a dowry.

units.la: Dos aut profectitia dicitur, id est, quam pater mulieri dedit: aut aduentitia, id est, ea quae a quouis alio data est. Mortua in matrimonio muliere, dos à patre profecta, ad patrem reuertitur, quintis in singulos liberos in infinitum relictis penes virum. Quod si pater non sit, apud maritum remanet.
units.tr: A dowry is either called profectitia, that is, one which the father gave to the woman, or adventitia, that is, one given by anyone else. If the woman dies during the marriage, a profectitia dowry returns to the father, while the husband keeps a fifth for each child, without limit. But if there is no father, it remains with the husband.

units.la: Aduentitia autem dos semper penes maritum remanet, præterquam si is qui dedit, vt sibi redderetur stipulatus fuit: quæ dos specialiter receptitia dicitur.
units.tr: An adventitia dowry always remains with the husband, unless the giver stipulated that it be returned to him; such a dowry is specially called receptitia.

units.la: Diuortio facto, si quidem sui iuris sit, mulier ipsa habet actionem, id est, doris repetitionem: quod si in potestate patris sit, pater adiuncta filiepersona habet actionem reuera: nec interest aduentitia sit dos, an profectitia.
units.tr: After a divorce, if the woman is sui iuris, she herself has the action, that is, the recovery of the dowry. If she is in her father's power, the father has the action in fact, with the daughter joined as a party. It makes no difference whether the dowry is adventitia or profectitia.

units.la: Post diuortium defuncta muliere, hæredi eius actio non aliter datur, quam si moram in dote mulieri reddenda maritus fecerit.
units.tr: After a divorce, when the woman has died, her heir has no action unless the husband delayed in returning the dowry to her.

units.la: Dos si pondere, numero, mensura contineatur, annua, bima, trima die reddetur: nisi si, vt præsens reddatur, conuenerit. Reliquæ dotes statim redduntur.
units.tr: If the dowry consists of weight, number or measure, it is returned in annual, biennial or triennial instalments, unless it was agreed that it be returned at once. Other dowries are returned immediately.

units.la: Retentiones ex dote fiunt, aut propter liberos, aut propter mores, aut propter impensas, aut propter res donatas, aut propter res amotas.
units.tr: Deductions may be made from a dowry on account of children, of conduct, of expenses, of gifts, or of goods removed.

units.la: Propter liberos retentio fit, si culpa mulieris aut patris, cuius in potestate est, diuortium factum sit. Tunc enim singulorum liberorum nomine sextæ retinentur ex dote: non plures tamen quam tres sextæ in retentione sunt, non in petitione.
units.tr: A deduction on account of children is made if the divorce came about through the fault of the woman or of the father in whose power she is. In that case a sixth is deducted from the dowry for each child, but not more than three sixths may be deducted, and this applies to the deduction, not to the claim.

units.la: Dos quæ semel functa est, amplius fungi non poterit, nisi aliud matrimonium sit. Morum nomine, grauiorum quidem sexta retinentur: leuiorum item octaua. Grauiores mores sunt, adulteria tantum: leuiores, omnes reliqui.
units.tr: A dowry that has once been paid out cannot be paid out again, unless there is another marriage. On account of conduct, a sixth is deducted for more serious faults, and likewise an eighth for lesser ones. Adultery alone counts as a more serious fault; all the rest are lesser.

units.la: Mariti mores puniuntur, in ea quidem dote, quæ à die reddi debet. Ita propter maiores mores præsentem dotem reddit: propter minores senûm mensum die. In ea autem quæ præsens reddi solet, tantum ex fructibus iubetur reddere, quantum in illa dote quadriennio redditur: quod repræsentatio facit.
units.tr: The husband's misconduct is punished in that dowry which ought to be returned on the day. Thus, for the greater faults he returns the present dowry; for the lesser, the dowry is returned on the day, with six months' delay. In the dowry which is usually returned in kind, he is ordered to return from the fruits only as much as would be returned from that dowry over four years; the presentation effects this.

units.la: Impensarum species sunt tres: aut enim necessariæ dicuntur, aut utiles, aut voluptuosæ.
units.tr: There are three kinds of expenses: they are called necessary, useful, or voluptuary.

units.la: Necessariæ sunt impensæ, quibus non factis dos deterior futura est: veluti si quis ruinosas æde s refecerit.
units.tr: Necessary expenses are those without which the dowry would be worse: for example, if someone repaired ruinous buildings.

units.la: Utiles sunt, quibus non factis quidem deterior dos non fuerit: factis autem fructuosior dos effecta est: veluti si vineta & oliueta fecerit.
units.tr: Useful expenses are those without which the dowry would not indeed be worse, but with which it has been made more productive: for example, if he planted vineyards and olive groves.

units.la: Voluptuosæ sunt, quibus neque omissis deterior dos fieret: neque factis, fructuosior effecta est: quod euenit in viridariis, & pictoriis, similibusque rebus.
units.tr: Voluptuary expenses are those without which the dowry would not be worse, and with which it has not been made more productive. This happens with pleasure gardens, paintings, and similar things.

units.la: Dos aut datur ] Dos dicitur solennibus verbis sine interrogatione. Dotis actio tam ex dictione nascitur, quam ex stipulatione : hodie etiam ex nuda pollicitatione & nudo pacto l. 2. C. Theodos. de ince. nupt. l. ult. C. Theodos. de dotib. Sublata autem est dicendæ dotis solennitas: ideoque à l. ad actionem C. de dotis promiss. vt ex C. Theod. apparet, Tribonianus amouit hæc verba, Dictio vel & quibus in locis prudentes scripserant, Doti dicere, subscripsit, Doti promittere, inusitata loquendi for- ma, l. si rem §. ult. de novat. l. annus de iur. dot. l. si marito. §. 1. l. si socer. §. Lucius solut. matr. Denique in l. 1. C. de iur. dot. cum Seuerus Imperator scripsisset, Dictio vel promissio, & paulo post ex dictione vel ex stipulatione, ( nec dum enim ex pollicitatione dotis actio erat ) pollicitationem Tribon. adscripsit, & condictionem ex pollicitatione : cum tamen ex pactis, vel pollicitationibus, præscriptis verbis, non condictio dari soleat.
units.tr: A dowry is either given ] A dowry is declared in solemn words, without a question. An action on a dowry arises from a declaration as much as from a stipulation, and today also from a bare promise and a bare pact, l. 2. C. Theodos. de ince. nupt. l. ult. C. Theodos. de dotib. The solemnity of declaring a dowry, however, was abolished. Therefore, as appears from the Theodosian Code in l. ad actionem C. de dotis promiss., Tribonian removed these words, dictio vel, and wherever the jurists had written doti dicere he substituted doti promittere, an unusual form of expression: l. si rem §. ult. de novat. l. annus de iur. dot. l. si marito. §. 1. l. si socer. §. Lucius solut. matr. Finally, in l. 1. C. de iur. dot., where the Emperor Severus had written dictio vel promissio, and a little later ex dictione vel ex stipulatione (for an action from a pollicitatio did not yet exist), Tribonian added pollicitationem and a condictio from a pollicitatio, although a condictio is not usually given from pacts or pollicitations by praescriptis verbis.

units.la: Dotem dicere ] Dotis dictio, l. 3. C. Theodosiano, eod. solenniter fiebat, l. 2. C. Theodos. de incestis, id est, solennibus verbis. Hodie qualiacunque verba sufficiunt, l. 6. C. de dotis promiss. Doti dicere veteres dicebant, cuius forte loco Tribonianus hanc formulam vsurpauit, Doti promittere. vid. Goth. ad l. 79. ff. de iure dotium.
units.tr: To declare a dowry ] The declaration of a dowry was made solemnly, l. 3. C. Theodosiano, eod., that is, in solemn words, l. 2. C. Theodos. de incestis. Today any words whatever suffice, l. 6. C. de dotis promiss. The older writers said doti dicere, and perhaps in its place Tribonian used this phrase, doti promittere. See Gothofredus on l. 79. ff. de iure dotium.

units.la: Mulier ] Tres personæ tantum poterant doti dicere.2. Caius9.§.4. mulier nuptura, vt hic: procurator specialis inf.eod.parens nupturæinf. eod. Dotem vero promittere poterant omnes cuiuscunque sexus & conditionis. leg. 41. ff. de iur. dot.
units.tr: Woman ] Only three persons could declare a dowry: 2. Caius 9. §. 4. the woman about to marry, as here; a specially appointed procurator, inf. eod.; and the parent of the bride, inf. eod. But anyone of either sex and any condition could promise a dowry, leg. 41. ff. de iur. dot.

units.la: Institutus ] ad hanc rem constitutus.
units.tr: Appointed ] Established for this matter.

units.la: Dare promittere ] Idem Paul. in l.promittendo de iur. dot. Dicendo igitur tres duntaxat personæ obligantur, promittendo omnes.
units.tr: To give, to promise ] The same Paul in the law promittendo, de iur. dot. Therefore, by declaring, only three persons are bound; by promising, all.

units.la: Quam pater mulieris] Adde vel parens virilis sexus, per virilem sexum cognatione iunctus.
units.tr: Which the father of the woman ] Add: or a parent of the male sex, related through the male sex.

units.la: Dedit ] per se vel per alium l. 5. §. 1. ff. de iur. dot. & breuiter, non ius potestatis, sed parentum nomen, dotem profectitiam facit. d. leg. 5. §. 1.
units.tr: Gave ] in person or through another, l. 5. §. 1. ff. de iur. dot. In short, it is not the power of authority but the name of parent that makes a dowry profectitia. d. leg. 5. §. 1.

units.la: A quouis alio ] d.l.5.§.9. etiam matre.d.§.9.
units.tr: From any other person ] d. l. 5. §. 9. even the mother, d. §. 9.

units.la: Ad patrem reuertitur ] Nobilis est quæstio, & à multis agitata, ad quem Dos profectitia, (de adventitia §.5.inf.) mortua muliere reuertatur. Paucis ita definio, dotem profectitiam morte mulieris ad eius patrem reuerti, vt hic: & l.17.ff.de S.C.Macedon.l.4.§.13.ff. de iur.dot. siue filiafamilias fuit l.4.C.soluto. siue materfam. vt Theodorus Græcus interpres adnotauit ad d.l.4. Hic difficiles occurrunt quæstiones, quid si non morte, sed diuortio, matrimonium dis-soluatur? si filiafamilias sit, ad patrem reuertitur: ad eam tamen recuperandam sine consensu filiæ agere non potest. l.34. ff. soluto l.14.ff.ad l. Falcid. l. 34. §. 6. ff. de solut. l. 2. l. 7. in sin. C. hoc tit. Si emancipata, vno casu ad patrem reuertitur. l. 71. ff. de euict. puta si ideo filia diuertit, vt maritum lucro dotis afficeret, patrem defraudaret, l. 5. ff. de diuort. l. 59. ff. soluto. Quid si capta ab hostibus, perinde dicendum est, ac si nupta decessisset: ideoque dos ad patrem reuertitur. l. 10. ff. soluto. Quid si mortua liberos reliquit? Bulgarus dotem ad patrem filiæ reuerti existimat. Martianus contra: cuius opinio communi interpretum sententia defensa est. Accurs. ad l. 4. C. soluto. Num ex iure Romano? iure veteri non puto, hic enim dos profectitia ad patrem filiæ reuertitur, quintis in singulos liberos relictis penes virum: si pater non sit, apud maritum remanet, adde l. 6. ff. de iur. dot. 29. Ecl. 1. c. 3. scio tamen subtiliter quædam dici in contrariam sententiam posse, quale est illud, dotis repetitionem patri competere, mortua in matrimonio puella. leg. 17. ff. de S. C. Macedon. ergo à contrario, si non puella, id est, non virgo mortua, sed mater relictis liberis, dos ad eius patrem non reuertetur. Ad hæc, innui potest ex l. vlt. §. 1. ff. vt legator. vel vnius filij superstitis nomine dotem apud maritum remanere, non ad patrem reuerti. Colligunt etiam nonnulli ex l. 26. §. 2. ff. de pact. dotal. dotem pertinuisse prius ad liberos defunctos: ab his ad maritum, nisi maritus suo iuri in fauorem patris defunctæ expresse renunciasset.
units.tr: Returns to the father ] It is a noble question, and much debated, to whom a profectitia dowry returns when the woman dies (for an adventitia dowry, see §. 5 below). In brief I define it thus: on the woman's death the profectitia dowry returns to her father, as here, & l. 17. ff. de S. C. Macedon. l. 4. §. 13. ff. de iur. dot., whether she was a filiafamilias, l. 4. C. soluto, or a materfamilias, as the Greek interpreter Theodorus noted on d. l. 4. Here difficult questions arise. What if the marriage is dissolved not by death but by divorce? If she is a filiafamilias, the dowry returns to the father, but he cannot sue to recover it without the daughter's consent, l. 34. ff. soluto, l. 14. ff. ad l. Falcid., l. 34. §. 6. ff. de solut., l. 2., l. 7. in fin. C. hoc tit. If she has been emancipated, it returns to the father in one case, l. 71. ff. de evict., namely if the daughter divorced in order to enrich her husband with the dowry and defraud her father, l. 5. ff. de divort., l. 59. ff. soluto. What if she was taken by enemies? It must be said just as if she had died married, and so the dowry returns to the father, l. 10. ff. soluto. What if she died leaving children? Bulgarus thought the dowry returns to the daughter's father; Martinus held the contrary, and his opinion has been defended by the common consensus of the interpreters, Accursius on l. 4. C. soluto. Is this so under Roman law? I do not think so under the old law, for here the profectitia dowry returns to the father of the girl, with a fifth left with the husband for each child, and if there is no father it remains with the husband; add l. 6. ff. de iur. dot., 29. Ecl. 1. c. 3. Yet I know that some subtle arguments can be made for the contrary view, such as that the father has a claim to recover the dowry when the girl dies in marriage, leg. 17. ff. de S. C. Macedon. So by contrast, if it is not a girl, that is, not an unmarried woman, who dies, but a mother leaving children, the dowry will not return to her father. Further, it may be implied from l. ult. §. 1. ff. ut legator. that the dowry remains with the husband, not returning to the father, on account of a single surviving son. Some also infer from l. 26. §. 2. ff. de pact. dotal. that the dowry first belonged to the children who died, and from them passed to the husband, unless the husband had expressly renounced his right in favour of the father of the deceased woman.

units.la: Sed præstat Martini opinionem defendere liberorum fauore: eoque magis quod vsu sit recepta Accurs. ad l.4. C.soluto. Bald. ad l.post dotem 40. ff.soluto. Ferrariensis in forma libelli qua uxor agit ad dotem. 33. in verb. dictæ dominæ. nn.1. adde Anto. Fabrum 1.conject.16.
units.tr: But it is better to defend Martin's opinion out of favour to the children, all the more because it has been received in practice: Accurs. ad l.4. C.soluto. Bald. ad l.post dotem 40. ff.soluto. Ferrariensis, in the form of the libel by which a wife sues for her dowry, 33. in verb. dictae dominae. nn.1. Add Anto. Fabrum 1.conject.16.

units.la: Quintis in singulos] Nota de quintæ retentione. Sextæ retentionis fit mentio in §.10. inf. vtraque abrogata l. unic. §. 5. verf. licet ob liberos retentio. C.de rei uxoriæ act.
units.tr: Quintis in singulos] Note on the retention of a fifth. Mention of the retention of a sixth is made in §10 below. Both were abrogated by l. unic. §. 5. verf. licet ob liberos retentio. C.de rei uxoriae act.

units.la: Quod si pater non sit ]l.cum patrem C. de rei vxo. act.
units.tr: But if the father is not living: l.cum patrem C. de rei vxo. act.

units.la: Aduentitia] Aduentitia dos ea est, quæ ab alio quam parente constituitur. l.1. §.13. verf. extraneum. C.de rei vxor. act.
units.tr: Aduentitia] An adventitious dowry is one constituted by someone other than a parent. l.1. §.13. verf. extraneum. C.de rei vxor. act.

units.la: Semper] siue sint liberi, siue non.
units.tr: Semper] whether there are children or not.

units.la: Receptitia ] l. mortis causa §. sed & si dos. de donation. causa mortis. seruus autem receptitius, de quo Aul. Gellius & Non. Marcellus scribunt, neque doralis est, neque ex paraphernis: quia ad virum non defertur. Sunt hæc omnia diuersa, bona receptitia, dotes, Διάφερνα, ἀντίφερ-να, προϊέμενα [?] & ὑπόβολα. Διάφερνα [?] sunt, quæ extra dotem (peculij nomine) ad virum deferuntur. Ἀντίφερνα sunt donationes propter nuptias. l. vlt. C. de donat. ant. nupt, quib. proxima sunt προϊέμενα [?] & ὑπόβολα, de quibus Constantinus Harmenopulus scribit. Vnde & Hypobolica instrumenta apud Sid. Apol. l.7. epist. quanquam sunt qui legant Hyperbolica, alij quidam Paraphernica, omnino male.
units.tr: Receptitious ] l. mortis causa §. sed & si dos. de donation. causa mortis. A receptitious slave, of whom Aulus Gellius and Nonius Marcellus write, is neither dotal nor from the paraphernalia, because he is not conveyed to the husband. All these are different: receptitious goods, dowries, Διάφερνα [?], ἀντίφερνα, προϊέμενα [?] and ὑπόβολα. Διάφερνα [?] are those which are conveyed to the husband outside the dowry, under the name of peculium. Ἀντίφερνα are gifts on account of marriage, l. vlt. C. de donat. ant. nupt. Closely related to these are προϊέμενα [?] and ὑπόβολα, of which Constantinus Harmenopulus writes. Hence also the hypobolic instruments in Sid. Apol. l.7. epist. Although some read "Hyperbolica" and others "Paraphernica", both are altogether wrong.

units.la: Reuera] Legendum, rei vxoriæ.
units.tr: Reuera] Read: of the wife's dowry (rei uxoriae).

units.la: Nec interest] Obstare videtur l.2. §. quod si in partis sol. matr. Goueanus in li. var. lect. Tribon. in eo §. facinus adnotauit: Ant. Goueanus, cui ex omnibus quotquot sunt aut fuere, Iustinianei iuris interpretibus, si quæramus quis unus excellat, palma deferenda est. Proinde dos aduentitia communis est ex iure antiquo, mulieris propria ex iure nouo. Actio dotis aduentitiæ communis est etiam iure nouo. l. ult. C. de bon. quæ lib. neque vero propriam esse actionem recte colligitur ex l. Caius. solut. mat. quia non dicit, soli filiæ actionem dari: verum ideo filiæ dicit, non patri, quia filiæ cautum fuit, non patri, cæterum per filiam patri quæritur actio.
units.tr: Nec interest] l.2. §. quod si in partis sol. matr. seems to stand in the way. Goveanus in his Var. lect. and Tribonian in eo §. facinus have noted this. Antonius Govea, if we ask which one of all the interpreters of Justinian's law, past or present, excels, must be awarded the palm. Therefore the adventitious dowry was common under the old law and is the wife's own under the new. The action for an adventitious dowry is common also under the new law, l. ult. C. de bon. quae lib. Nor is it rightly inferred from l. Caius. solut. mat. that the action is proper to the wife, because it does not say that the action is given to the daughter alone. It says "to the daughter" rather than "to the father" because the provision was made for the daughter, not the father; but through the daughter the action is acquired for the father.

units.la: Post diuortium] inde si post diuortium maritus in reddenda dote moram fecerit, & hæredi vxoris competit actio: si moram non fecerit, secus est. Quamobrem & mortua in matrimonio vxore, hæredi non competit actio. l. usufruct. sol. mat. l. cum in fundo. §. si autem usufruct. de iur. dot.
units.tr: Post diuortium] Hence, if after divorce the husband delays in returning the dowry, the heir of the wife has the action; if he has not delayed, it is otherwise. Wherefore, even if the wife dies during the marriage, the heir has no action. l. usufruct. sol. mat. l. cum in fundo. §. si autem usufruct. de iur. dot.

units.la: Annua, bima]Hodie annua die ex constitutione Iustiniani: cui à Triboniano aptata est l. 1. de dot. preleg. in qua legitur, annua die pecuniam dotalem reddi.
units.tr: Annua, bima] Today it is yearly, by the constitution of Justinian, to which Tribonian adapted l. 1. de dot. preleg., in which it is read that the dotal money is to be returned yearly.

units.la: Reddetur] Hic paragraphus abrogatur. Nam hodie res mobiles, se mouentes, incorporales dotales, intra annum redduntur: res soli, illico. l. vn. §. 7. verf. exactè autem dotis, Cod. de rei vxor. act.
units.tr: Reddetur] This paragraph is abrogated. For today movable, self-moving and incorporeal dotal goods are returned within a year, and land goods at once. l. vn. §. 7. verf. exactè autem dotis, Cod. de rei vxor. act.

units.la: Ex dote fiunt ] Hic paragraphus abrogatus est l. vn. C. de rei vxor. act. §. 5.
units.tr: Ex dote fiunt ] This paragraph has been abrogated: Code, On the action for recovery of the wife's property, law 7, §5.

units.la: Aut propter liberos ] d. §. 5. verf. sileat ob liberos retentio.
units.tr: Aut propter liberos ] Same law, §5, words: "let retention on account of children be passed over."

units.la: Aut propter mores ] d. §. 5. quid enim opus est inducere ob mores retentionem.
units.tr: Aut propter mores] d. §. 5. For what need is there to introduce a retention on account of morals?

units.la: Aut propter impensas] d. §. 5. verf. sed nec ob impensas.
units.tr: Aut propter impensas] d. §. 5. verf. sed nec ob impensas.

units.la: Propter res donatas ] d. §. 5. verf. vel ex qua causa ob rem donatam. Adde l. 1. §. 3. ff. de dote relegata.
units.tr: Propter res donatas ] Same law, §5, words: "or for any cause arising from a gift made." Add Digest, On the dowry that was ordered returned, law 1, §3.

units.la: Propter res amotas]d. §. 5. verf. sed nec retentio ob res amotas.
units.tr: Propter res amotas] d. §. 5. verf. sed nec retentio ob res amotas.

units.la: Retentio fit]Hodie non fit.d. §. 5. verf. sileat ob liberos retentio.
units.tr: Retentio fit ]Today it is not done. Same law, §5, words: "let retention on account of children be passed over."

units.la: Nomine sextæ]nota de sextæ retentione. vid. §. 4. sup. eod. Vtraeque retentiones abrogatæ sunt d. verf. sileat ob liberos.
units.tr: Nomine sextæ] Note on the retention of a sixth; see §4 above in this title. Both retentions were abrogated, d. verf. sileat ob liberos.

units.la: Non plures tamen quam tres ] id est media pars, vt Paul. ait lib. II. Inst. tit. de dot. cuius verba Boëtius Seuerinus refert. Nam sex sextæ, integrum conficiunt.
units.tr: Non plures tamen quam tres] that is, the half, as Paulus says in lib. II. Inst. tit. de dot., whose words Boëtius Severinus cites. For six sixths make a whole.

units.la: Non in petitione]Quę ex aliis causis retinentur, & in petitione sunt. Sustulit vero Iustinianus quintas & sextas, & alia omnia retentionum genera. Sunt tamen compensationum ex eis causis leges quam plurimæ. l. fructus. §. ob donationes. l. rei. §. 1. l. si constante. §. si uxor. l. penult. §. 1. sol. matr. l. utilium. de impens. in res dotal. l. neq; C. de impens. l. 1. C. rerum amot. Sed & de moribus actionem sustulit. l. ult. C. de repud. de qua in l. 5. ff. de pact. dot. l. ult. C. Theodos. de inc. nuptiis. l.
units.tr: Non in petitione] Those retained on other grounds are in the petition. Justinian, however, abolished the fifths and sixths and all other kinds of retention. There are nonetheless very many laws on compensations from those causes: l. fructus. §. ob donationes. l. rei. §. 1. l. si constante. §. si uxor. l. penult. §. 1. sol. matr. l. utilium. de impens. in res dotal. l. neq; C. de impens. l. 1. C. rerum amot. But he also abolished the action concerning morals: l. ult. C. de repud., of which we read in l. 5. ff. de pact. dot. l. ult. C. Theodos. de inc. nuptiis. l.

units.la: 1. C. Theod. vic. civ. cri. ag. non poss quæ & accusatio dicitur in l. viro. l. cum mulier. ff. sol. matrim. quemadmodum actio suspecti, actio ingrati, actio inofficiosi, suis locis. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: 1. C. Theod. vic. civ. cri. ag. non poss which is also called an accusation, in l. viro. l. cum mulier. ff. sol. matrim., just as the action of suspicion, the action of ingratitude and the action of inofficiousness, in their places. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Dos quæ semel ]Nisi redintegratum sit matrimonium, dos quæ semel dos esse desiit, dos effici amplius non poterit. Redintegrato matrimonio, tacite redintegratur dos, nisi sit receptitia. l. si mulier diuerterit. l. in insulam. §. ult. sol. matr. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Dos quæ semel] Unless the marriage has been restored, a dowry which has once ceased to be a dowry cannot become a dowry again. When the marriage is restored, the dowry is tacitly restored too, unless it is receptitious. l. si mulier diuerterit. l. in insulam. §. ult. sol. matr. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Nisi aliud matrimonium sit ]id est, nisi matrimonium redintegratum sit. Redintegrato matrimonio, dos tacite redintegratur. l. 64. ff. de iur. dot. l. 19. ff. soluto. Tacite, inquam: quia semper hoc agi intelligitur, nisi aliud convenerit. l. 30. ff. d. iur. dot. id est, nisi dos sit receptitia l. 42. in sin. ff. soluto. Porro, non dicitur redintegrari matrimonium, si post leue iurgium uxor rediit. Est enim aliud leue fribusculum, aliud diuortium. l. 31. ff. de iur. dot. l. 31. §. 11. 12. ff. de donat. inter vir. si diuortium non fuit, redintegrari non potuit. Vix estenim vt id redintegratum dicamus, quod dissolutum non fuit.
units.tr: Nisi aliud matrimonium sit] that is, unless the marriage has been restored. When the marriage is restored, the dowry is tacitly restored: l. 64. ff. de iur. dot. l. 19. ff. soluto. Tacitly, I say, because it is always understood to be done unless something else has been agreed: l. 30. ff. d. iur. dot. that is, unless the dowry is receptitious, l. 42. in sin. ff. soluto. Moreover, a marriage is not said to be restored if the wife returns after a slight quarrel, for a small squabble is one thing and divorce another: l. 31. ff. de iur. dot. l. 31. §. 11. 12. ff. de donat. inter vir. If there was no divorce, it could not be restored; for we can scarcely say that something is restored which was never dissolved.

units.la: Item octana ] Legendum, octana, sexta, &c. Cuiac.
units.tr: Item octana] Read octana, sexta, &c. Cuiac.

units.la: Grauiores mores ] Adde l.39. l.47. ff. soluto.
units.tr: Grauiores mores] Adde l.39. l.47. ff. soluto.

units.la: Adulteria ] An pars aliqua bonorum adulterae, eius marito hodie cedat. vid. ad Novell. 117. cap. 13. & ad Nov. 134. cap. 10. Dn. Gothofr.
units.tr: Adulteria] Whether some part of the goods of an adulterous wife now passes to her husband. Vid. ad Novell. 117. cap. 13. & ad Nov. 134. cap. 10. Dn. Gothofr.

units.la: Quae à die reddi debet. Ita propter ] Legendum, quae annua, bina, trina die reddi debet, propter. Cuiac.
units.tr: Quae à die reddi debet. Ita propter] Read: which ought to be returned yearly, biennially, triennially, on account of. Cuiac.

units.la: Maiores mores ] id est, propter adulterium §. 12. supra eod.
units.tr: Maiores mores] that is, on account of adultery, §. 12 above in this title.

units.la: Praesentem ] id est, illico.
units.tr: Praesentem] that is, at once.

units.la: Propter minores ] quam adulterij scilicet.
units.tr: Propter minores] than adultery, that is.

units.la: Quod repraesentatio ] cuius magnum est commodum l.1. §. 2. ff. de dote prælegata.
units.tr: Quod repraesentatio] whose great advantage is shown in l.1. §. 2. ff. de dote prælegata.

units.la: Species sunt tres ] l.1. ff. de impensis.
units.tr: Species sunt tres ] l.1. ff. de impensis.

units.la: Quibus non factis dos ] aut res quaelibet l. 79. ff. de verb. signif.
units.tr: Quibus non factis dos ] or any other thing: Digest, On the meaning of words, law 79.

units.la: Deterior ] id est quibus non factis dos minueretur, l.14. de impensis.
units.tr: Deterior] that is, without which the dowry would be diminished, l.14. de impensis.

units.la: Ruinosas ] aedificium ruens vid. d. l. 1. §.3. l.4. ff. de impensis.
units.tr: Ruinosas] a building falling down; see d. l. 1. §.3. l.4. ff. de impensis.

units.la: Fructuosior ] melior d. l. 79. §. 1. l. 5. in sin. ff. de impensis.
units.tr: Fructuosior] better, d. l. 79. §. 1. l. 5. in sin. ff. de impensis.

units.la: Voluptuosa ] ita appellantur in l. 14. in sin. ff. de impensis. voluptariae l. 7. §. 9. 10. 11. ff. de impensis impensas 2. eclog. c. 79.
units.tr: Voluptuosa] So they are called in l. 14. in sin. ff. de impensis; voluptariae in l. 7. §. 9. 10. 11. ff. de impensis; impensas in the second Eclogue, chapter 79.

units.la: Pisto-
units.tr: Pisto-

units.la: Pictoriis] Lego picturis: & paulo ante, deterior dos fuerit.
units.tr: Pictoriis: read picturis; and a little before, deterior dos fuerit.

units.la: Viridariis] vid. Gothofr. ad l. 79. in sin. ff. de verb. signif.
units.tr: Viridariis: see Gothofredus on l. 79. in sin. ff. de verb. signif.

units.la: Similibusque] vid. d. l. 79. in fine.
units.tr: Similibusque: see the said l. 79. in fine.

units.la: Tit. VII. De iure donationum inter vi- rum & uxorem.
units.tr: Title VII. On the law of gifts between husband and wife.

units.la: INter virum & uxorem donatio non valet, nisi certis ex causis: mortis causa; diuortii causa, seruii manumittendi gratia. Hoc amplius principalibus constitutionibus concessum est mulieri, in hoc donare viro suo, ut is ab Imperatore, latoclauo, vel equo publico, similive honore honoretur.
units.tr: A gift between husband and wife is not valid, except for certain reasons: in case of death, in case of divorce, or for the purpose of manumitting a slave. Moreover, by imperial constitutions it has been granted to a wife that she may give to her husband, so that he may be honoured by the Emperor with the broad stripe, or with the public horse, or with some similar honour.

units.la: Si maritus diuortii causa res mouerit, rerum quoque amotarum actione tenebitur.
units.tr: If a husband removes goods on account of divorce, he will also be liable to the action for things removed.

units.la: Si maritus pro muliere se obligauerit: vel in rem eius impenderit, diuortio facto, eo nomine cauere sibi solet stipulatione tribunitia.
units.tr: If a husband has bound himself on behalf of his wife, or has spent money on her property, then, once the divorce has taken place, he is accustomed to secure himself on that account by a tribunician stipulation.

units.la: In potestate parentum sunt etiam ii liberi quorum causa probata est, per errorem contracto matrimonio inter dispares condignis personas. Nam seu ciuis Romanus Latinam, aut peregrinam, vel eam, quae Dediticiorum numero est quasi per ignorantiam vxorem duxerit: siue ciuis Romana per errorem peregrino vel ei qui Dediticiorum numero est, aut etiam si Latino ex lege Ælia Sentia nupta fuerit, causa probata, ciuitas redditur tam liberis quam parentibus, praeter eos qui Dediticiorum numero sunt, & ex eo fiunt in potestate parentum liberi.
units.tr: Those children also are in the power of their parents for whom the cause has been proved, when a marriage has been contracted through error between persons of unequal rank who are nonetheless suitable for each other. For whether a Roman citizen has taken as wife, through ignorance, a Latin woman, or a foreigner, or one who belongs to the class of the surrendered (dediticii); or whether a Roman citizen woman, through error, has married a foreigner or one of the dediticii, or even a Latin who was married under the Aelian Sentian law, once the cause has been proved, citizenship is restored both to the children and to the parents, except for those who belong to the class of the dediticii, and children who are born from that union come into the power of their parents.

units.la: Mortis causa donatio fit impendente metu mortis. Mors impendet quidem omnibus, eaque semper certa est, etiamsi incertum diem habeat. l.68. in sin. ff. de leg. 1. l.1. §.2. ff. de cond. & demonstr. Metum tamen hic, instantem intelligere l.6. ff. de mort. causa. Instat autem non tantum infirmo, sed peregrinaturo, navigaturo, militi. Paul. 2. sentent. 24. §.1. iter facturo per insidiosa loca, seni. l.3. 4.5. ff. de mort. causa. Id genus donationis mortis donatoris convalescit. Paul. d. loco §. ultim. Morte donatarij res redit ad eum qui donavit. Paul. d. loco §.5. Est autem hoc genus donationis permissum, quia in id tempus excurrit, quo qui donat & cui donatum est, vir & vxor esse desidesinunt. leg. 10. ff. eod. leg. 22. Cod. de donat. int. vir. &c.
units.tr: A gift in case of death is made when the fear of death is imminent. Death indeed hangs over everyone, and it is always certain, even if the day is uncertain. See l. 68, at the end, ff. de legatis 1; l. 1, §2, ff. de conditionibus et demonstrationibus. Yet here the fear must be understood as pressing, see l. 6, ff. de mortis causa. It presses not only on the sick, but on one about to travel abroad, about to go to sea, or on a soldier. Paulus, Sententiae 2, 24, §1; on one about to make a journey through dangerous places; on an old man, see ll. 3, 4, 5, ff. de mortis causa. A gift of this kind becomes valid if the donor dies. Paulus, in the place cited, last §. If the donee dies, the property returns to the one who gave it. Paulus, in the place cited, §5. This kind of gift is, however, permitted, because it extends to the time at which the giver and the recipient cease to be husband and wife. See l. 10, ff. eodem; l. 22, Cod. de donationibus inter virum et uxorem, etc.

units.la: Manumittendi gratia] Cur ita? Fauore libertatis id receptum est, vel potius quod nemo huiusmodi re donata fiat locupletior. Paul. d. loco §. 2. add. l. 7. §. 8. §. vlt. l. 8. l. 9. ff. eod.
units.tr: For the purpose of manumission: Why so? This has been received out of favour to liberty, or rather because no one becomes richer by such a gift of property. Paulus, in the place cited, §2; add l. 7, §8, and the last §; l. 8; l. 9, ff. eodem.

units.la: Principalibus] Antonini Imperat. l. nuper de donat. int. vir. & vx.
units.tr: By the emperors: the constitution of the Emperor Antoninus, l. nuper, de donationibus inter virum et uxorem.

units.la: Veleqño] id est, vt equestris conditionis fieret. l. 42. ff. eod.
units.tr: Or the public horse: that is, so that he may become of equestrian rank. l. 42, ff. eodem.

units.la: Similiter] Idem dicendum est de rebus donatis sepulturæ causa. l. 5. §. 8. 9. 10. 11. ff. eod. ad oblationem Dei d. l. 5. §. 12. ad processus d. l. 42.
units.tr: Similarly: The same must be said of goods given for the sake of burial. l. 5, §§8, 9, 10, 11, ff. eodem; for the offering to God, the same l. 5, §12; for the funeral processions, l. 42 cited.

units.la: Si maritus divortij] Non tantum in vxorem, sed & in virum retunì amotarum actio est. leg. contra l. item. rer. amot.
units.tr: If a husband, on account of divorce: The action for things removed lies not only against the wife but also against the husband, on the contrary, l. Item, de rebus amotis.

units.la: Se obligauerit] vid. leg. 2. ff. de negotiis leg. 28. ff. soluto.
units.tr: Has bound himself: see l. 2, ff. de negotiis gestis; l. 28, ff. solutionibus.

units.la: Eo nomine cauere] l. 25. in sin. l. 55. ff. soluto.
units.tr: On that account to secure himself: l. 25, at the end; l. 55, ff. solutionibus.

units.la: Stipulatione tribunitia] vt in l. cum mulier de dote sol. matr. Hæc stipulatio honoraria est, quia ex iurisdictione tribunorum venit: vt prætoria, & ædilitia, ex iurisdictione prætoris, & ex iurisdictione ædilium. In Institutionibus de ædilitijs vulgo male scriptum est, quia ex iurisdictione prætoris veniunt. Superest enim vox, prætoris, auctore Theoph. & Pompon. in l. 5. de verb. oblig.
units.tr: By a tribunician stipulation: as in l. Cum mulier, de dotis solutione matrimonio. This stipulation is honorary, because it comes from the jurisdiction of the tribunes, just as the praetorian and aedilician (stipulations) come from the jurisdiction of the praetor and from the jurisdiction of the aediles. In the Institutes, under the heading of aedilician actions, it is commonly and wrongly written that they come from the jurisdiction of the praetor, for the word "praetoris" is retained, on the authority of Theophilus and Pomponius in l. 5, de verborum obligationibus.

units.la: Disparesq; condignis ] Lego, disparis conditionis. Cuiac.
units.tr: Unequal yet suitable: I read "of unequal rank" (disparis conditionis). Cujas.

units.la: Aut peregrinam ] vid. Gothofr. ad tit.5. §.8. sup.eod.
units.tr: Or a foreigner: see Gothofredus on title 5, §8 above, same title.

units.la: Per ignorantiam ] Ignorantia errorem in nuptiis commissum excusat. facit l.57.§.1.ff.de ritu l.22.in f.ff.soluto. Nou. 12.c.1.sin.
units.tr: Through ignorance: Ignorance excuses an error committed in marriage. Compare l. 57, §1, ff. de ritu nuptiarum; l. 22, at the end, ff. solutionibus; Novella 12, c. 1, at the end.

units.la: Ex lege Ælia Sentia ] vt in tit.de Latinis ex l. Iunia, id est, vti l. Iunia comprehensum est. Est autem ab hac sententia non abslimilie id, quod Impp.rescripserunt in l.qui in prouincia §. Diuus de rit.nupt.
units.tr: Under the Aelian Sentian law: as in the title on the Latins under the Junian law, that is, as it is comprehended in the Junian law. Nor is what the Emperors rescribed in l. qui in provincia, §Divus, de ritu nuptiarum, far from this opinion.

units.la: Lege Ælia ] Adde tit.3.§.3.sup.eod.
units.tr: Under the Aelian law: add title 3, §3, above, same title.

units.la: Tit. VIII. De Adoptionibus.
units.tr: Title 8. On Adoptions.

units.la: Vid.l.1.ff.eod.8.C.48.Inst.eod.in pr.Cai.5.
units.tr: See l.1 ff. eod.; 8 C. 48; Inst. eod. in pr.; Gaius 5.

units.la: NOn tantum naturales liberi in potestate parentum sunt, sed etiam adoptiui.
units.tr: Not only natural children are in the power of their parents, but adopted children too.

units.la: Adoptio fit, aut per populum, aut per Praetorem, vel Praesidem prouinciae. Illa adoptio quae per populum fit, specialiter arrogatio dicitur.
units.tr: Adoption takes place either through the people, or through the Praetor, or through the governor of a province. The adoption that takes place through the people is specifically called arrogation.

units.la: Per populum qui sui iuris sunt arrogantur: Per Praetorem autem, filiisfamiliae a parentibus dantur in adoptionem.
units.tr: Those who are their own masters (sui iuris) are adrogated through the people; but through the Praetor, sons under power (filiifamilias) are given in adoption by their parents.

units.la: Arrogatio Romae tantum fit: adoptio autem, etiam in prouincia apud Praesidem.
units.tr: Arrogation takes place only at Rome; adoption, however, also in a province, before the governor.

units.la: Per Praetorem vel Praesidem prouinciae adoptari optrari tam masculi quam fœminæ, & tam puberes quam impuberes possunt: per populum vero Romanum, fœminæ quidem non arrogant. Pupilli antea quidem non poterant arrogari: nunc autem possunt ex constitutione Divi Antonini.
units.tr: Both males and females, and both those of full age and those under age, can be adopted through the Praetor or the governor of a province; but through the Roman people, women indeed cannot be adrogated. Wards formerly could not be adrogated, but now they can, by the constitution of the deified Antoninus.

units.la: Hi qui generare non possunt, velut spado, utroque modo possunt adoptare. Idem iuris est in persona cœlibe.
units.tr: Those who cannot beget children, such as a eunuch, can adopt in either way. The same law applies to an unmarried person.

units.la: Item is qui filium non habet, in locum nepotis adoptare potest.
units.tr: Likewise, one who has no son can adopt in the place of a grandson.

units.la: Si paterfamiliæ arrogandum se dederit, liberi quoque eius quasi nepotes, in potestate fiunt arrogatoris. Fœminæ vero neutro modo possunt adoptare, quoniam nec naturales liberos in potestate habent.
units.tr: If a head of a household has given himself up to be adrogated, his children too, as if grandchildren, pass into the power of the adrogator. Women, however, cannot adopt in either way, since they do not even have their natural children in their power.

units.la: {a} Aut per populum] l. 2. C. de adopt. Hodie per imperatorem. Paci.
units.tr: {a} Through the people] l. 2 C. de adopt. Today it is done through the emperor. Pacius.

units.la: Per populum qui sui] §. 2. sup. eod. §. 5. infr. eod. leg. 2 sin. Cod. eod. leg. 1. in sin. ff. eod. d. §. 1. Inst. inf. eod.
units.tr: Through the people which is sui iuris] §. 2 sup. eod.; §. 5 infr. eod.; leg. 2 sin. Cod. eod.; leg. 1 in sin. ff. eod.; d. §. 1 Inst.; inf. eod.

units.la: Sui iuris sunt] Hodie ex indulgentia principis. d. l. 1.
units.tr: Are sui iuris] Today by the indulgence of the prince. d. l. 1.

units.la: Per prætorem] §. 2. supra eod. id est magistratus imperio. l. 2. ff. eod. §. 1. Inst. eod.
units.tr: Through the praetor] §. 2 supra eod., that is, by the authority of the magistrate. l. 2 ff. eod.; §. 1 Inst. eod.

units.la: Filiifamilias] id est, qui sui iuris non sunt, sed in potestate patris positi d. l. 2. vers. imperio. Et breviter, qui patrem habebat, adoprabatur, qui non habebat, adrogabatur. Caius 5. §. 2.
units.tr: Filiifamilias] that is, those who are not sui iuris but placed in the power of a father, d. l. 2, verse "imperio". And briefly: one who had a father was adopted, one who had none was adrogated. Gaius 5. §. 2.

units.la: Adrogatio tantum Romæ fit] Quoniam curiatis comitiis fit. 5. Gell. 19.
units.tr: Adrogation takes place only at Rome] Because it is done by the curiate assemblies. Gellius 5, 19.

units.la: Romæ tantum fit] Quia fiebat apud populum, Nullibi autem populus Romanus extra Romam quærendus erat.
units.tr: It takes place only at Rome] Because it was done before the people, and the Roman people was never to be sought outside Rome.

units.la: Etiam in provincia ] Quia in provinciis erant præsides.
units.tr: Even in a province] Because there were governors in the provinces.

units.la: Fœminæ quidem non adrogant] Legendum, adrogantur. Causa illa est, quia nulla cum fœminis comitiorum communio est. Cæterum per principem fœminæ adrogantur. l. nam fœminæ ff. de adopt.
units.tr: Women indeed cannot adrogate] One should read "are adrogated." The reason is that women have no share in the assemblies. Otherwise women are adrogated through the prince. l. nam feminae ff. de adopt.

units.la: Non poterant arrogari] Quia tutoribus in pupillos tantam esse authoritatem fas non erat, ut caput liberorum fidei suæ commissum, alienæ ditioni subijcerent. 20 Gell. 19.
units.tr: Could not be adrogated] Because it was not lawful for guardians to have such authority over their wards that they could subject the head of the children entrusted to their good faith to another's dominion. Gellius 20, 19.

units.la: Spado] l. 2. §. 1. l. 40. in sin. ff. eod. §. 9. Inst. eod.
units.tr: Eunuch l. 2 §. 1; l. 40 in sin. ff. eod.; §. 9 Inst. eod.

units.la: In cœlibe] l. 30 ff. eod. Cœlebs est qui vxorem non habet.
units.tr: In an unmarried person] l. 30 ff. eod. A caelebs is one who does not have a wife.

units.la: Neutro modo possunt ] possunt tamen iussu principis adoptare. l. 29. §. 3. ff. de inofficioso.
units.tr: Cannot adopt in either way] They can, however, adopt by order of the prince. l. 29 §. 3 ff. de inofficioso.

units.la: Tit. IX. De his qui in manu sunt.
units.tr: Tit. IX. Concerning those who are in manus.

units.la: FArre conuenitur in manum, certis verbis, & testibus X. præsentibus, & solenni sacrificio facto, in quo panis quoque farreus adhibetur.
units.tr: A woman passes into manus by fixed words, with ten witnesses present, and a solemn sacrifice being made, in which a cake of spelt [panis farreus] is also used.

units.la: In manu est uxor, quæ convenit in manum. In manum aut confarreatione convenitur, aut coëmptione, sed omissa est conferendi adsuetudo; ut Cornel. Tacitus lib. 4. Annalium scribit. Omissa tandem quoque coemptio. Denique omissa est omnis conventio in manum. Quamobrem Tribonianus in l. uxorem de ritu nupt. l. ex parte §. 1. de verb. oblig. scripsit, in matrimonium convenire, cum tamen Pap. scripsisset, in manum convenire, & in l. si concubina rerum amot. convenit, pro in manu convenit. Cuiac h.
units.tr: A wife who passes into manus is in manus. Passage into manus took place either by confarreatio or by coemptio, but the custom of the former was dropped; as Cornelius Tacitus writes in the fourth book of the Annals. Finally coemptio was dropped too, and at last every form of conventio in manum was dropped. For this reason Tribonian, in l. uxorem de ritu nupt. and l. ex parte §. 1 de verb. oblig., wrote "in matrimonium convenire," whereas Papinian had written "in manum convenire"; and in l. si concubina rerum amot. "convenit" is used for "in manu convenit". Cujas on this passage.

units.la: Farre] Tribus modis apud veteres fiebant nuptiæ. Vsu, si mulier anno cum viro fuisset: Farre & coëmtione, seu in manum conventione. Adde Seruium 1. Georg. Goth. h.
units.tr: Farre: Among the ancients marriages were contracted in three ways: by usus, if a woman had lived with a man for a year; by farreum and coemptio, or conventio in manum. Add Servius on the first Georgic. Gothofredus on this passage.

units.la: Conuenitur] Convenire in manum, pro quo Tribonianus dixit, convenire. l. 17. ff. rer amot. convenire in matrimonium l. 13. ff. de ritu. l. 121. §. 1. ff. de verb. oblig. quo genere loquendi vsus est etiam Gellius 18. cap. 6. conventio in manum etiam fiebat coëmtione. Cicero pro L. Flacco. In manum convenerant: nunc audio, sed quæro utrum vsu an coëmptione? Farre (unde confarreatio, vel ut Plinius 18. cap. 3. loquitur, confarratio: cui contraria diffarreatio. Fest. in voce Diffarreatio) quo tantum genere Flamen Dialis Flaminiæ iungebatur. Seru. 4. Æneid. ex eo matrimonio quæ nascebantur. patrimi & matrimi dicebantur. Fest. in voce Flaminia, Seru. 1. Georg. Gell. 12. Ex patrimis tres simul nominabantur, ut ex iis unus Flamen Dialis legeretur. Tacit. 4. Annal. sed quia confarreandi adsuetudo omissa, aut inter paucos retenta propter incuriam virorum & foeminarum, & ipsius ceremoniae difficultatem: tum quod qui ita conveniebant, de patria exibant potestate; placuit Tiberij tempore, ut Flaminica Dialis in potestate esset viri, ceteri promiscue genere Foeminarum agerent. Et hoc quidem genere nuptiarum postea non soli Flamines usi videntur, sed & alij: quod hic innuitur, ibi, in quo panis quoque farreus. Coemptione vero fiebat matrimonium, Seru.
units.tr: Conuenitur: convenire in manum, for which Tribonian said simply convenire (l. 17 ff. rer. amot.), and convenire in matrimonium (l. 13 ff. de ritu; l. 121 §. 1 ff. de verb. oblig.). Gellius also used this manner of speaking in book 18, chapter 6. Conventio in manum was also effected by coemptio. Cicero, in defence of L. Flaccus: "They had come together into manus; now I hear it, but I ask whether by usus or by coemptio?" By farreum (whence confarreatio, or, as Pliny says in book 18, chapter 3, confarratio; its opposite is diffarreatio; see Festus under "Diffarreatio"), which was the only manner by which the Flamen Dialis was joined to a Flaminica. Servius on the fourth Aeneid. The children born of that marriage were called patrimi and matrimi. Festus under "Flaminia", Servius on the first Georgic, Gellius book 12. Of the patrimi three were named together, so that one of them might be chosen as Flamen Dialis. Tacitus, Annals book 4: but since the custom of confarreatio was dropped, or kept among a few because of the carelessness of men and women and the difficulty of the ceremony itself, and because those who so came together passed out of their father's power, it was decided in the time of Tiberius that the Flaminica Dialis should be in the power of her husband, while the others lived under the common condition of women. Afterwards this kind of marriage seems to have been used not only by the Flamines but by others too; which is hinted at here, where it says "in which a cake of spelt is also used". Marriage was effected by coemptio, Servius.

units.la: 1. Georg. libra & aere adhibitis. Seru. 4. Aeneid. Eaque solennitate praeunte uxor quasi emebatur: eiusque coemptionis is erat effectus, ut quae ita in manum viri convenisset, ea viro sua haeres esset. Caius 3. Instit. apud Ruffinum authorem collationis legum Mosaicarum tit. 16. add. Gell. 18. c. 6. in sin. adde notas Goth. ad tit. C. de sponsalibus: & Petrum Pitheum 16. Notar. Mosaic. Goth. hic.
units.tr: On the first Georgic: with a balance and bronze being brought in. Servius on the fourth Aeneid. With this solemnity leading, the wife was as it were bought; and the effect of this coemptio was that she who had so come into the manus of her husband should be his heir. Gaius, third Institutes, in Rufinus, author of the collation of the Mosaic laws, title 16; add Gellius 18, chapter 6, at the end; add the notes of Gothofredus on the title C. de sponsalibus; and Petrus Pithoeus, Notes on the Mosaic law, book 16; Gothofredus here.

units.la: Solenni sacrificio ] Videtur innui ritus aquae & ignis, de quo Seru. 4. Aeneid. Dotalesque uas Tyrios committere dextras. Quid aliud dextras committere, quam in manum convenire? Quae conventio eo ritu perficitur, ut aqua & igni adhibitis, natura coniuncta habeat. Goth. ibid.
units.tr: Solenni sacrificio: The rite of water and fire seems to be hinted at, of which Servius on the fourth Aeneid: "and to join the right hands of Tyrians through a dowry". For what else is joining right hands than coming into manus? This conventio is accomplished by that rite, so that with water and fire employed it holds the natural union. Gothofredus, ibid.

units.la: Panis quoque farreus] Panis farreus, qui & farreum Festo & Plinio 18. cap. 3. genus libi ex farre compositum.
units.tr: Panis quoque farreus: a farreus cake, which Festus and Pliny (book 18, chapter 3) call a kind of cake made of spelt.

units.la: Tit. X. Qui in potestate mancipiove sunt, quemadmodum eo iure libe- rentur.
units.tr: Title X. Who are in the power of another or in mancipium, and how they are freed by that law.

units.la: Liberi parentum potestate liberantur, emancipatione, id est, si postea quam mancipati fuerint, manumissi sint. Sed filius quidem ter mancipatus, ter manumissus, sui iuris fit. Id enim lex duodecim Tabularum iubet his verbis, Si pater filium ter venundarit, filius à patre liber esto. Cæteri autem liberi præter filium tam masculi quam fœminæ, vna mancipatione manumissioneque sui iuris fiunt.
units.tr: Children are freed from the power of their parents by emancipation, that is, if after they have been mancipated they are manumitted. But a son mancipated three times and manumitted three times becomes sui iuris. For the law of the Twelve Tables commands this in these words: "If a father sells his son three times, let the son be free from his father." The other children, however, apart from the son, whether male or female, become sui iuris by a single mancipation and manumission.

units.la: Morte patris filius & filia sui iuris fiunt: morte autem aui nepotes ita demum sui iuris fiunt, si post mortem aui in potestate patris suturi non sunt: veluti si moriente auo pater eorum aut iam decessit, aut de potestate dimissus est. Nam si mortis aui tempore, pater eorum in potestate eius sit, mortuo auo, in patris sui potestate fiunt.
units.tr: By the death of the father, the son and the daughter become sui iuris; but by the death of the grandfather, the grandchildren become sui iuris only if after the grandfather's death they are not going to be in the power of their father: for example, if at the grandfather's death their father has either already died or has been released from power. For if at the time of the grandfather's death their father is in his power, then when the grandfather dies they pass into the power of their father.

units.la: Si patri, vel filio, aqua & igni interdictum sit, patria potestas tollitur: quia peregrinus fit, cui is, cui aqua & igni interdictum est. Neque autem peregrinus ciuem Romanum, neque ciuis Romanus peregrinum in potestate habere potest.
units.tr: If interdiction by fire and water is pronounced against the father or the son, paternal power is lost, because he against whom fire and water is interdicted becomes a foreigner. Nor can a foreigner have a Roman citizen in his power, nor can a Roman citizen have a foreigner in his power.

units.la: Si pater ab hostibus captus sit, quanuis seruus hostium fiat: tamen cum reuersus fuerit, omnia pristina iura recipit, iure postliminii. Sed quandiu apud hostes est, patria potestas in filio eius interim pendebit: & cum reuersus fuerit ab hostibus, in potestate filium habebit. Si vero ibi decesserit, sui iuris filius erit. Filius quoque si captus fuerit ab hostibus, similiter propter ius postliminii, patria potestas interim pendebit.
units.tr: If the father is taken by enemies, although he becomes a slave of the enemies, nevertheless when he returns he recovers all his former rights, by the right of postliminium. But as long as he is among the enemies, paternal power over his son remains in suspense in the meantime; and when he returns from the enemies, he will have the son in his power. But if he dies there, the son will be sui iuris. If the son also is taken by enemies, likewise, on account of the right of postliminium, paternal power remains in suspense in the meantime.

units.la: In potestate parentum esse desinunt & hi, qui Flamines Diales inaugurantur, & quæ virgines Vestæ capiuntur.
units.tr: Those also cease to be in the power of their parents who are installed as Flamines Diales, and the virgins who are taken as Vestals.

units.la: De hac materia vide Caium 1. t. 6. Nouel. 81. 31. Inst. 12. 8. C. 49. 2. Paul. sent. 25.
units.tr: On this matter see Gaius, 1. t. 6; Novel. 81; Inst. 12.8; C. 49.2; Paul, Sent. 25.

units.la: Liberantur emancipatione] §. 6. Instit. quib. mod. ius patria l. 5. C. de dolo & C. de emancipationib. liber.
