units.tr: They are freed by emancipation] §. 6 Inst. by which means paternal power is ended; l. 5 C. de dolo, and C. de emancipationibus liberorum.

units.la: Ter mancipatus] id est, venditus (Caius 10. §. 1.
units.tr: Mancipated three times] that is, sold (Gaius 10 §. 1).

units.la: Lex duodecim tabularum] Idem fuit constituturum à Romulo. Dionys. Halicarnass. 2.
units.tr: The law of the Twelve Tables] The same was established earlier by Romulus. Dionysius of Halicarnassus, 2.

units.la: Ter venundarit] olim liberos etiam interficere parentibus permissum erat. vid. l. 11. in sin. ff. de liber. & posthum.
units.tr: Sells three times] Formerly it was even permitted to parents to kill their children. See l. 11 in fine, ff. de liberis et posthumis.

units.la: Praeter filium] ut nepotes, pronepotes. Sensus est, filios factos sui iuris trina emancipatione fuisse: filias, nepotes, pronepotes, & deinceps, vnica. l.8.inf.ff.de iniusto Caius 6.§.2. verf. fœmina vel nepotes. vid.Goth. hoc.tit.
units.tr: Apart from the son] as grandchildren, great-grandchildren. The sense is that sons made sui iuris required a triple emancipation, but daughters, grandchildren, great-grandchildren and so on, a single one. l. 8 inf. ff. de iniusto; Gaius 6 §. 2, verb. "fœmina vel nepotes". See Gothofredus on this title.

units.la: Vna mancipatione
units.tr: By a single mancipation

units.la: quæ morte soluantur, vid.Goth.ad Nouel.22.c.20. lio. sine capitis deminutione.l. 3. in sin. ff. de S.C. Macedon. Goth. hic.
units.tr: which are dissolved by death; see Gothofredus on Novel. 22 c. 20. sine capitis deminutione (without loss of status); l. 3 in fine ff. de S.C. Macedoniano; Gothofredus here.

units.la: Qui flamines ] qui flaminium Diale adipiscebatur, iure patrio exibat. Tacit. 4. Annal. anno 776.
units.tr: Who are Flamines] he who attains the flaminate of Jupiter leaves his father's power. Tacitus, Annals 4, year 776.

units.la: Diales ] id est, Iouis.
units.tr: Diales] that is, of Jupiter.

units.la: Flamines Diales ] Qui morte parentis sui iuris fit, capite non minuitur.l. 3. §. vlt. ad Macedon. Adiungo etiam eum qui Flaminio Diali, aut Vestali sacerdotio sui iuris fit. l. 2. quod cum eo leg. 1. §. sed etsi alio, quando de pecul. auctore Gellio lib. 1. c. 13. Et hoc nimirum est quod ait Vlpianus in d.l. 3. vel altas sui iuris, &c. Idem & in eo Iustinianus constituit, qui dignitate sui iuris fit Novel. 18. At is profecto qui emancipatione sui iuris fit, capite minuitur; credo, quia in imaginariam seruitutis formam deducitur. l. liberos de cap. minutis. Immo quia sublata est legitima emancipatio, vigetque aut Anastasiana, aut Iustinianea emancipatio, qui emancipatur hodie, capite non minuitur. Proinde merito ex Iustiniani constitutionibus suo exæquatur emancipatus. Vlusfructus emancipatione non finitur. Id denique restat, ut capite non minuantur hodie, qui cum alieni iuris forent, sui iuris efficiuntur. His autem, quæ hoc loco dicuntur ab Vlpiano, addenda est quę in manum flaminis conuenit. Cornel. Tacit. lib. 4. quando exiret è iure patrio qui id flaminium apilceapiceretur, quæque in manum flaminis conuenirer. Pacius & Cuiacius hic.
units.tr: Flamines Diales] He who becomes sui iuris by the death of his parent does not suffer loss of status (l. 3 §. ult. ad Macedonianum). I add also one who becomes sui iuris by taking up the priesthood of the Flamen Dialis or of the Vestals (l. 2 quod cum eo; l. 1 §. sed etsi alio, quando de peculio), on the authority of Gellius, book 1, c. 13. And this is surely what Ulpian means in the said l. 3, "or are sui iuris", etc. Justinian also established the same for one who becomes sui iuris by dignity (Novel. 18). But he who becomes sui iuris by emancipation certainly suffers loss of status; I believe because he is brought into an imaginary form of slavery (l. liberos de capitis minutione). Indeed, since legitimate emancipation has been abolished, and either the Anastasian or the Justinianic emancipation holds, he who is emancipated today does not suffer loss of status. Hence the emancipated person is rightly made equal to a sui iuris person by Justinian's constitutions. Usufruct is not ended by emancipation. Finally, it remains that those who, though previously under another's power, become sui iuris, do not today suffer loss of status. To what Ulpian says in this place must be added what came under the hand of the flamen: Cornelius, Tacitus, book 4, when one who was designated to that flaminate would leave the paternal right, and what was brought under the hand of the flamen. Pacius and Cujas here.

units.la: Gell. l. 12. c. 12. virgo Vestalis, mulatque capta in atrium Vestæ deducta, pontificibusque tradita est, eo statim tempore, sine emancipatione, ac sine capitis minutione, è patria potestate exibat. Goth. h.
units.tr: Gellius, l. 12, c. 12: a Vestal virgin, once taken, was led into the atrium of Vesta and handed over to the pontiffs; at that very moment, without emancipation and without loss of status, she left paternal power. Gothofredus here.

units.la: Tit. XI. De Tutelis.
units.tr: Title XI. On Guardianships.

units.la: TVtores constituuntur tam masculis, quam fœminis: sed masculis quidem impuberibus duntaxat propter ætatis infirmitatem. fœminis autem tam impuberibus, quam puberibus, & propter sexus infirmitatem, & propter forensium rerum ignorantiam.
units.tr: Guardians are appointed both for males and for females, but for males only while they are under puberty, because of the weakness of their age. Females are given guardians both before and after puberty, both because of the weakness of their sex and because of their ignorance of legal business.

units.la: Tutores autem legitimi sunt aut senatusconsultis constituti, aut moribus introducti.
units.tr: Guardians are either legitimate, or appointed by senatus-consulta, or introduced by custom.

units.la: Legitimi tutores sunt, qui ex lege aliqua descendunt. Per eminentiam autem legitimi dicuntur, qui ex lege duodecim Tabularum introducuntur, seu propalam, quales sunt agnati: seu per consequentiam, quales sunt patroni.
units.tr: Legitimate guardians are those who arise from some law. Those are called legitimate in the strict sense who are introduced by the Law of the Twelve Tables, either openly, as agnates are, or by consequence, as patrons are.

units.la: Agnati sunt, à patre cognati virilis sexus, per virilem sexum descendentes eiusdem familiæ: veluti patrui, fratres, filii fratris patruelis.
units.tr: Agnates are blood relatives on the father's side of the male sex, descending through males of the same family: such as paternal uncles, brothers, and the sons of a paternal cousin.

units.la: Qui liberum caput manciparum sibi, vel à parente, vel à coemptore manumisit per similitudinem patroni tutor efficitur, qui fiduciarius tutor appellatur.
units.tr: A man who has manumitted a free person whom he held in mancipium for himself, whether from a parent or from a coemptionator, becomes by analogy that person's patron-guardian; this is called a fiduciary guardian.

units.la: • Legitimi tutores; alii tutela in iure cedere possunt.
units.tr: Legitimate guardians; others can surrender guardianship in court.

units.la: Is cui tutela in iure cessa est, Cessicius tutor appellatur: qui siue mortuus fuerit, siue capite minutus, siue alii tutela cesserit, redit ad legitimum tutorem tutela. Sed & si legitimus decesserit; aut capite minutus fuerit, cessitia quoque tutela extinguitur.
units.tr: The person to whom guardianship has been surrendered in court is called a cessician guardian. If he dies, or suffers loss of status, or surrenders the guardianship to another, the guardianship returns to the legitimate guardian. But if the legitimate guardian dies or suffers loss of status, the ceded guardianship is also extinguished.

units.la: Quantum ad agnatos pertinet, hodie cessitia tutela non procedit: quoniam permissum erat in iure cedere tutela foeminarum tantum, non etiam masculorum foeminarum autem legitimas tutelas lex Claudia sustinet.
units.tr: As far as agnates are concerned, ceded guardianship does not hold today, since it was permitted to surrender guardianship in court only for women and not also for men. The Claudian law, however, upholds the legitimate guardianships of women.

units.la: Excepta tutela patronorum legitima tutela capitis diminutione amittitur.
units.tr: Apart from the guardianship of patrons, legitimate guardianship is lost by loss of status.

units.la: Capitis minutionis species sunt tres, maxima, media, minima.
units.tr: There are three kinds of loss of status: the greatest, the middle, and the least.

units.la: Maxima capitis deminutio est, per quam & ciuitas; & libertas amittitur. veluti cum incensus aliquis venierit: aut cum mulier alieno seruo se iunxerit, denuntiante domino, & ancilla facta fuerit, ex senatusconsulto Claudiano:
units.tr: The greatest loss of status is that by which both citizenship and liberty are lost, as when someone is sold as one not enrolled in the census, or when a woman has joined herself to another's slave, the owner having given notice, and has become a slave, under the Claudian senatus-consultum.

units.la: Media capitis deminutio dicitur, per quam sola ciuitate amissa, libertas retinetur: quod fit in eo, cui aqua & igni interdicitur.
units.tr: The middle loss of status is said to be that by which citizenship alone is lost while liberty is retained; this happens to one who is interdicted from water and fire.

units.la: Minima capitis deminutio est, per quam & ciuitate & libertate salua, status duntaxat hominis minus minis mutatur: quod fit adoptione, & in ma-num conuentione.
units.tr: The least loss of status is that by which, citizenship and liberty remaining safe, only the man's standing is changed in a lesser degree. This happens by adoption and by conventio in manum.

units.la: Testamento quoque nominatim tutores dati confirmantur eadem lege duodecim Tabularum, his verbis: Vti legassit super pecunia tutelave suæ rei, ita ius esto: qui tutores datiui appellantur.
units.tr: Guardians named by name in a will are also confirmed by the same law of the Twelve Tables, in these words: "As he shall have bequeathed concerning money or the guardianship of his property, so let it be law." These are called guardians given by will (datiui).

units.la: Dari testamento tutores possunt liberis qui in potestate sunt.
units.tr: Guardians can be given by will to children who are in power.

units.la: Testamento tutores dari possunt hi, cum quibus testamenti faciendi ius est, præter Latinum Iunianum. Nam Latinus habet quidem testamenti factionem, sed tamen tutor dari non potest: id enim lex Iunia prohibet.
units.tr: Those who have the right of making a will can be given as guardians by will, except a Junian Latin. For a Latin has testamentary capacity, but cannot be given as a guardian, since the Lex Junia forbids it.

units.la: Si capite deminutus fuerit tutor testamento datus, non amittit tutelam: sed si abdicaverit se tutela, desinit esse tutor. Abdicare autem est, dicere nolle se tutorem esse in iure. Cedere autem tutela testamento datus non potest: nam & legitimus in iure cedere potest, abdicare se non potest.
units.tr: If a guardian given by will suffers loss of status, he does not lose the guardianship; but if he renounces the guardianship, he ceases to be guardian. To renounce is to say in court that one is unwilling to be guardian. A guardian given by will cannot, however, surrender the guardianship; for even a legitimate guardian can surrender in court, but cannot renounce.

units.la: Lex Attilia iubet mulieribus, pupillisve non habentibus tutores, dari a Prætore & maiore parte Tribunorum plebis: quos tutores Attilianos appellamus. Sed quia lex Attilia Romæ tantum locum habet, lege Iulia & Titia perfectum est, ut in prouincia quoque similiter a præsidibus earum dentur tutores.
units.tr: The Lex Attilia orders that guardians be given to women, or to pupils who have no guardians, by the praetor and the majority of the tribunes of the plebs; we call these Attilian guardians. But because the Lex Attilia has force only at Rome, it was provided by the Lex Julia and Titia that in the provinces too guardians should similarly be given by the governors.

units.la: Lex Iunia tutorem fieri iubet Latino, vel Latinis impuberibus eum, qui etiam ante manumissionem ex iure Quiritium fuit.
units.tr: The Lex Junia orders that a guardian be made for a Latin, or for Latin pupils under puberty, namely the one who was of Quiritary right even before manumission.

units.la: Ex lege Iulia de maritandis ordinibus, tutor datur à Prætore vrbis ei mulieri virginive, quam ex hac ipsa lege nubere oportet, ad dotem dandam, dicendam, promittendamve, si legitimum tutorem pupilla non habeat. Sed postea Senatus censuit, vt etiam in prouincia quoque, similiter à præsidibus earum ex eadem causa tutores dentur.
units.tr: By the Lex Julia on marrying the orders, a guardian is given by the praetor of the city to a woman or maiden whom this same law requires to marry, for giving, declaring, or promising a dowry, if the pupil has no legitimate guardian. But afterwards the Senate decreed that in the provinces too guardians should similarly be given by the governors for the same cause.

units.la: Præterea etiam in locum muti, furiosive tutoris, alterum dandum esse tutorem ad dotem constituendam Senatus censuit.
units.tr: Moreover, the Senate decreed that, in place of a mute or insane guardian, another guardian should be given for the constitution of a dowry.

units.la: Item ex Senatusconsulto tutor datur mulieri ei, cuius tutor abest, præterquam si patronus sit, qui abest. Nam in locum patronii absentis alter peti non potest, nisi ad hereditatem adeundam, & nuptias contrahendas. Idemque permisit in pupillo patroni filio.
units.tr: Likewise, by senatus-consultum, a guardian is given to a woman whose guardian is absent, unless the absent guardian is a patron. For in place of an absent patron another cannot be sought, except for entering an inheritance and contracting marriage. The same was permitted for the son of a patron as a pupil.

units.la: Hoc amplius Senatus censuit, vt si tutor pupilli pupillæve suspectus à tutela submotus fuerit, vel etiam iusta de causa excusatus in locum eius tutor alius detur.
units.tr: Furthermore, the Senate decreed that if the guardian of a male or female pupil is suspected and removed from the guardianship, or is even excused for a just cause, another guardian be given in his place.

units.la: Moribus tutor datur mulieri pupillove, qui cum tutore suo lege aut legitimo iudicio agere vult, vt auctore eo agat (ipse enim tutor in rem suam auctor fieri non potest) qui Prætorianus tutor dicitur, quia à prætore vrbis dari consueuit.
units.tr: By custom a guardian is given to a woman or pupil who wishes to proceed against their own guardian by law or by legitimate judgment, so that they may act with his authorization (for the guardian cannot himself authorize an action in his own affair). This is called a Praetorian guardian, because he was customarily given by the praetor of the city.

units.la: Pupillorum pupillarumque tutores & negotia gerunt, & auctoritatem interponunt. Mulierum autem tutores auctoritatem duntaxat interponunt.
units.tr: Guardians of male and female pupils both conduct business and interpose authority. Guardians of women, however, only interpose authority.

units.la: Si plures sunt tutores, omnes in omni re debent auctoritatem accommodare, præter eos qui tunc dati sunt: nam ex his vel vnius auctoritas sufficit.
units.tr: If there are several guardians, all must lend their authority in every matter, except those who were then given; for among these the authority of one alone suffices.

units.la: Tutoris auctoritas necessaria est, mulieribus quidem in his rebus, si lege aut legitimo iudicio agant, si se obligent, si ciuile negotium gerant, si libertæ suæ periiurtant in contubernio alieni serui morari, si mancipia alienent. Pupillis autem hoc amplius, etiam in rerum nec mancipi alienatione tutoris auctoritate opus est.
units.tr: A guardian's authority is necessary for women in these matters: if they act by law or legitimate judgment, if they bind themselves, if they conduct civil business, if they swear that their freedwoman lives in cohabitation with another's slave, and if they alienate slaves. For pupils, however, in addition, the guardian's authority is needed even for the alienation of things not mancipable.

units.la: Liberantur tutela, masculi quidem pubertate: Puberem autem Cassiani quidem eum esse dicunt; qui habitu corporis pubes apparet, id est, qui generare potest: Proculeij autem, eum qui quatuordecim annos expleuit: verum Priscus eum puberem esse, in quem vtrumque concurrit, & habitus corporis, & numerus annorum. Fœminæ autem tutela liberantur.
units.tr: Males are released from guardianship by puberty. The Cassians say that one is pubes when puberty appears in the bodily habit, that is, when he can beget; the Proculians say one who has completed fourteen years; but Priscus held that one is pubes in whom both the bodily habit and the number of years concur. Females are released from guardianship.

units.la: Vide Caium 7. in Inst. 1. 26. ff. 1.
units.tr: See Gaius 7. in Inst. 1. 26. ff. 1.

units.la: Tam masculis] l. 1. §. 3. ff. eod. l. 1. ff. de legit. tut.
units.tr: Tam masculis] l. 1. §. 3. ff. eod. l. 1. ff. de legit. tut.

units.la: Propter ætatis infirmitatem ] propter ætatem. §. 1. Inst. eod. l. 1. ff. eod. Δια τὸ τῆς ἡλικίας ἀσθενὲς. Theoph. eod.
units.tr: On account of the weakness of age] on account of age. §. 1. Inst. eod. l. 1. ff. eod. Because of the weakness of age [Δια τὸ τῆς ἡλικίας ἀσθενὲς]. Theoph. eod.

units.la: Aut moribus] l. 1. ff. de curatore furiosi: Ex lege aliqua] l. 5. de tutor.
units.tr: Or by conduct] Dig. 1.tit. de curatore furioso, l. 1; By some law] Dig. de tutoribus, l. 5.

units.la: Per consequentiam] hæreditarum. l. 3. ff. de legitim. tutor. perinterpretationem, acsi verbis legis introducti essent. Inst. de legitima patron. vt qui sperarent successionem, ijdem bona consequerentur. Inst. d. tit. l. 1. ff. de legitim. tutor: vid. l. 72. ff. de regul. iur. Goth. h.
units.tr: By consequence (of inheritances). l. 3. ff. de legitim. tutor. by interpretation, as if they had been introduced by the words of the law. Inst. de legitima patron. so that those who hoped for the succession would obtain the goods. Inst. d. tit. l. 1. ff. de legitim. tutor: see l. 72. ff. de regul. iur. Goth. h.

units.la: Virilis sexus] In tutelarum quæstione ita definiuntur agnati: proprerea quod tutela virile munus est. Cæteroquin & fœminæ agnatæ sunt. Eadem est agnatorum definitio in quæstione intestatæ successionis. leg. 2. §. agnati de suis & l. hæred. & inf. tit. 26. quia etsi consanguinea consanguineo intestato hæres existat, agnata tamen agnato cuiquam intestato ex lege Voconia hæres non est, §. caterum, de legit. agnat. succeff. sic in l. Vellea, qui testamentum facier, is omneis virilis sexus, qui ei sui hæredes futuri erunt, &c. etiamsi viuo parente nascantur. Ideo ait, virilis sexus, quia sequuntur hæc verba, vt nominatim eos exhæredet, vel instituat §. posthumorum. in sin. de exhæred. lib. Soli autem mares posthumi exhæredandi sunt. §. posthumi quoque §. posthumorum de exhæred. lib. unde & in l. 3. de iniusto rupt. aio, sic Vlpianum scripsisse, Posthumi virilis sexus: & ex Iustiniani constitutione id Tribonianum immurasse. Pacius & Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Of the male sex] In the question of guardianships, agnates are defined in this way, because guardianship is a male office. Otherwise, females too are agnates. The same definition of agnates is used in the question of intestate succession. leg. 2. §. agnati de suis & l. hæred. & inf. tit. 26. because, although a blood relative (consanguinea) is heir to a blood relative who dies intestate, an agnate woman is not heir to any agnate who dies intestate, by the Lex Voconia. §. caeterum, de legit. agnat. success. So in the Lex Vellea: he who makes a will, all those of the male sex who will be his heirs under him, etc., even if they are born while the parent is alive. He says "of the male sex" because these words follow: so that he disinherits or institutes them by name. §. posthumorum. in sin. de exhaered. lib. Only male posthumous children are to be disinherited. §. posthumi quoque, §. posthumorum de exhaered. lib. Whence also in l. 3. de iniusto rupt. I say that Ulpian wrote thus, "posthumi virilis sexus"; and that, from Justinian's constitution, Tribonian inserted this. Pacius and Cuiacius here.

units.la: Per virilem sexum ] per virilis sexus cognationem §.1. Inst. de legit. agnator. tut. per virilis sexus personas. l.7. ff. de legit. tut. per patrem cognati ex eadem familia l.10. §.2. ff. de gradib.
units.tr: By the male sex: by the kinship of the male sex (Inst. de legit. agnator. tut. §.1); by male persons (l.7. ff. de legit. tut.); by kinsmen from the same family through the father (l.10. §.2. ff. de gradib.).

units.la: Eiusdemque familiæ ] l. pronunciatio §. communi de verb. significat. adde d. §. 2. communi enim iure familiam dicimus omnium agnatorum l.195. §.2. verf. communi ff. de verb. sig.
units.tr: Eiusdemque familiae: see the law "pronunciatio", section "communi", on the meaning of words; add the same section "communi" just cited. For in law we call "family" all the agnates, as in the law 195, section 2, "communi", on the meaning of words.

units.la: Veluti patrui ] veluti fratres, patrueles, filij fratris patruelis. Cuiac Pacius. Goth.b.
units.tr: Such as paternal uncles: such as brothers, cousins on the father's side, and the sons of a paternal cousin. Cuiac., Pacius, Goth. b.

units.la: Qui liberum caput ] Agnatus est tutor ex l.12. tabularum, patronus ex interpretatione legis: parens ex contractu fiduciæ. Cur non & parens ex interpretatione legis? Quia nulla talis in lege interpretatio adhiberi potuit. Nec enim vt patronis, sic parentibus nominatim lege defertur hæreditas. Igitur duæ tantum sunt species legitimæ tutelæ, Agnatorum & patronorum: id quod Vlpianus tradit in l. 1. de legit. tut. Verum in l.3. §. vlt. eod. tit. parentem emancipatorem non legitimum, sed vicem ait legitimi tutoris obtinere, id est, fiduciarium tutorem esse. Non nego moribus inde receptum, vt nominetur legitima, quæ proprie est fiduciaria. tit. de l. par. tut. fiduciariæ tutelæ nomen ad liberos transmitti, legitimæ non transmitti: denique liberos patronorum distare à liberis parentum. Cæterum ratio differentiæ traditæ à Iustiniano in titul. de fiduciar. tut. falsa est in patre & auo: certe subtilior est quam verior. An igitur, quia non vt liberis patroni, ita liberis emancipatoris lege debetur hereditas. l.1. §. Liberos si quis à par. fuerit manu. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Who are of free condition: An agnate is a guardian by the Twelve Tables (l.12.); a patron is one by interpretation of the law; a parent by the contract of fiducia. Why not a parent by interpretation of the law too? Because no such interpretation could be applied in the law. For inheritance is not granted by name by law to parents as it is to patrons. Therefore there are only two kinds of legitimate guardianship, of agnates and of patrons, as Ulpian teaches in l. 1. de legit. tut. Yet in l.3. §. vlt. eod. tit. he says that a parent who emancipates does not act as a legitimate guardian but takes the place of one, that is, that he is a fiduciary guardian. I do not deny that by custom it has come to be called legitimate, though strictly it is fiduciary (tit. de l. par. tut.). The name of fiduciary guardianship passes to the children, the legitimate does not pass; and finally, the children of patrons differ from the children of parents. Moreover, the reason for the difference given by Justinian in the title de fiduciar. tut. is false in the case of father and grandfather; it is certainly more subtle than true. Or is it because inheritance is not owed by law to the children of an emancipator as it is to the children of a patron? (l.1. §. Liberos si quis à par. fuerit manu.) Cuiac. h.

units.la: Vel à parente vel coemptore] Qui à parente, is est pater fiduciarius: qui à coemptore, is est pater naturalis.
units.tr: Either from a parent or from a purchaser: he who is from a parent is the fiduciary father; he who is from a purchaser is the natural father.

units.la: Per similitudinem] patroni ad tutelam libertorum quos manumiserunt, vocati sunt l. 12. tab. ex consequentia. §. 4. supra eod. Eadem igitur similitudine patres vocari oportuit ad liberorum, quos emanciparunt, & manumiserunt tutelam.
units.tr: By likeness: patrons were called to the guardianship of freedmen whom they had manumitted, by the Twelve Tables by consequence (§. 4. supra eod.). By the same likeness, then, fathers ought to be called to the guardianship of the children whom they had emancipated and manumitted.

units.la: Qui fiduciarius] vid. 6. Caii. 5. vers. mancipat. In iure cedere] vid. §. 7. infr. eod.
units.tr: Who is fiduciary: see Gaius 6, verse mancipat. To yield in law: see §. 7 infra eod.

units.la: Cessicus ] nota de cessico tutore, vt hic, & cessitia tutela: infr. eod. & §. 8. §. 17. infra.
units.tr: Cessicius: note the cessician guardian, as here, and cessitian guardianship: infra eod. and §. 8, §. 17 infra.

units.la: Lex Claudia ] de qua vide l.3. C. de legitim. tut.
units.tr: The Claudian law: on which see l.3. C. de legitim. tut.

units.la: Lex Claudia sustinet] lege, sustulit. Rursus vero lex Claudia sublata est constitutione Constantini l.3. C. de legit. tut. l.2. Theod. Cod. de tut. & cur. crea. Ait Constantinus, in foeminis tutelam legitimam consanguineus vel patruus non recuser. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: The Claudian law upholds: by law, it abolished. Conversely, the Claudian law was again repealed by a constitution of Constantine (l.3. C. de legit. tut.; l.2. Theod. Cod. de tut. & cur. crea.). Constantine says that a blood relation or paternal uncle should not refuse legitimate guardianship over women. Cuiac. and Pacius here.

units.la: Excepta tutela] Hoc est quod ait l. tutelas. de capit. minut. Tutelas etiam non amittit capitis deminutio, exceptis his quae I.A.P.P. deferuntur, id est, quae iure agnationis proximis potissimum deferuntur. Tribonianus non sic. Equidem scio Tribonianum, cum multa in libris prudentum notis perscripta essent, auctore Iustiniano, in l. 2, C. de vet. iur. enucl. in iis explicandis cadere frequenter & labi. Caeterum tutela patronorum, minima capitis deminutione non perit, quia nec ius patronatus perit. Aeque testamentaria & datiua tutela non perit. At quia minima capitis deminutione ius agnationis perit, & legitima agnatorum tutela perit. Dixi, proximis potissimum, vt in edicto translaticio Verris, Tum vti proximum quemque potissimum haeredem esse oporteret, si is intestato mortuus esset. Vnde eximenda non sunt posteriora verba l. 1. unde legit. Quinimo in Ascanio ita male leguntur, quasi si Asconii essent, non Tullii. Item alio edicto, Sec. tab. testamenti potissimum haereditatem dabo. Cuiacius hic & Paci.
units.tr: Except guardianship: this is what the law tutelas, de capit. minut., says: "Guardianships are not lost even by a change of status, except those which by the praetor's edict are given to the nearest kin, that is, those which by right of agnation are given chiefly to the nearest." Tribonian does not say so. Indeed I know that Tribonian, when many things had been written in the notes of the jurists, at the instigation of Justinian (in l. 2, C. de vet. iur. enucl.), often fell and stumbled in explaining them. Moreover, guardianship of patrons is not lost by the smallest change of status, because the right of patronage is not lost either. Likewise testamentary and dative guardianship is not lost. But because the right of agnation is lost by the smallest change of status, so too is legitimate guardianship of agnates lost. I said "chiefly to the nearest" as in Verres' translated edict: "Then, as the nearest person should be chiefly heir, if he had died intestate." Hence the later words of l. 1, unde legit., must not be removed. Indeed in Ascanius they are read badly, as if they were Asconius's and not Tullius's. Likewise by another edict: "I will give the inheritance chiefly to the second rank of a will." Cuiacius here and Pacius.

units.la: Excepta tutela] Tribonianus hunc locum ita interpretatus est, exceptis his quae in iure alieno positis personis deferuntur. l. 7. ff. de cap. minutis. Hottom. 3. observ. 9. legit, exceptis his quae in nomine alieno positis personis deferuntur. Gothofredus hic.
units.tr: Except guardianship: Tribonian interpreted this passage thus: "except those which are conferred on persons placed under another's authority" (l. 7. ff. de cap. minutis.). Hottomannus, 3 observ. 9 legit: "except those which are conferred on persons placed in another's name." Gothofredus here.

units.la: Species sunt tres] l. vlt. ff. de cap. minutis.
units.tr: There are three kinds: l. vlt. ff. de cap. minutis.

units.la: Veluti cum incensus aliquis venierit] Hoc M. Tullius explicat in extremo orationis pro Caecinna, Dionysius IIII.
units.tr: As when some person who was not enrolled in the census is sold: Marcus Tullius explains this at the end of the speech for Caecina, Dionysius 4.

units.la: Cicero pro Cæcinna in fine. Iam populus cum eum vendit, qui miles factus non est (id est, quia ad delictum non respondit, qua de re vid. Goth. ad l. 20. ff. comm. præd. l. 40. §. 10. ff. de re militari) non adimit ei libertatem, sed indicat eum non esse liberum, qui cum liber esset, adire periculum noluit. Cum autem incensum (id est eum qui censum vitavit) hoc indicat: cum ii qui in seruitute iusta fuerint, censu liberentur, eum, qui, cum liber esset, censeri noluerit, ipsum sibi libertatem abiudicasse. Quod si maxime hisce rebus adimi libertas aut amitti potest, &c. Halicarnasseus etiam lib. 4. refert, Seruii Tullii iussu bona omnium ciuium censita, eis qui non censerent, pœna proposita, ut bonis in fiscum redactis, cæsi virgis sub hasta venirent: eamque diu legem Romanis seruatam fuisse. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Cicero, for Caecina, at the end: "When the people sells a man who has not become a soldier (that is, because he did not answer for the offence, on which see Goth. ad l. 20. ff. comm. praed., l. 40. §. 10. ff. de re militari), it does not take away his freedom, but shows that he is not free, since, though he was free, he was unwilling to face the danger. When it shows this of one who was not enrolled (that is, one who avoided the census), since those who were in lawful servitude are freed by the census, the man who, though free, was unwilling to be enrolled has himself stripped himself of freedom. But if by such things liberty can be taken away or lost, etc." Halicarnassus also reports in book 4 that, by the order of Servius Tullius, the goods of all citizens were assessed, with a penalty set for those who did not register, so that, once their goods were brought into the treasury, they were beaten with rods and sold under the spear; and that this law was long observed among the Romans. Gothofredus here.

units.la: Cum mulier] l. 27. ff. depositi.
units.tr: When a woman: l. 27. ff. depositi.

units.la: Denunciante domino ] Trina denunciatione opus est: denunciari etiam restato oportet, idque denunciari ut seruo abstineat. Denunciationem sequitur prætoris, aut præsidis sententia. Inde Tertull. lib. 2. ad uxorem. Nonne insuper censuerunt seruituti vindicandos, qui cum alieno seruo post dominorum denunciationem in consuetudine perseuerarunt? Exemplo S.C. si ingenuæ, quæ ad gynæciarium se vel monetarium applicat, similis denunciatio fiat, nisi dicto audiens fuerit, eiusdem ipsa conditionis ex constitutionibus efficitur. l. edicimus C.Theod.de murilegul.l.Senatusconsult. C.Theod. de decur. Sed hæc à Iustiniano mutata sunt in tit.de S. C.Claud.toll. Cuiac.hic.
units.tr: The owner giving notice: Notice must be given three times; it is also necessary that notice be given to the person in question, and given so that he may abstain from the slave. The notice is followed by the sentence of the praetor or the governor. Hence Tertullian, book 2 ad uxorem: "Have they not also decided that those who continued in the habit of living with another's slave, after the owners had given notice, were to be claimed as slaves?" By the example of the senatusconsult: if notice of this kind is given to a freewoman who applies herself to the weaving-shop or the mint, and she does not obey the command, she is by the constitutions made of the same condition. (l. edicimus C.Theod. de murilegul.; l. Senatusconsult. C.Theod. de decur.). But these things were changed by Justinian in the title de S. C. Claud. toll. Cuiac. here.

units.la: Senatusconsulto Claudiano ] Id hodie abrogatum est.C.de S.C.Claud.toll.& Institut.de succession.sublat.quæ fiebant per bon.vend. &c.
units.tr: By the Claudian senatusconsult: this has today been abrogated (C. de S.C. Claud. toll. & Inst. de succession. sublat., which were done through sale of goods, etc.).

units.la: Minima capitis diminutio ] Minima capitis deminutione familiam : media familiam & ciuitatem : maxima familiam, ciuitatem, & libertatem amittimus d.l.vlt. Adde Inst.de capit.diminut.
units.tr: The smallest change of status: by the smallest change of status we lose the family; by a middle change, family and citizenship; by the greatest, family, citizenship and freedom (d.l.vlt.). Add Inst. de capit. diminut.

units.la: Status duntaxat hominis] saluo statu publici iuris.l.1. §.capitis.ad S.C.Tertyll. priuatus hominis status commutatur.Cuiac.b.
units.tr: The status of the person only: with the status of public law preserved (l.1. §. capitis ad S.C. Tertyll.). The private status of the person is changed. Cuiac. b.

units.la: In manum conuentionem ] Quæ conuenit in manum mariti, capite minuitur: quia in familiam eius,& sui hæredis locum venit, vt in tit. 23.& apud Gellium lib.18.cap.6.
units.tr: Marriage by which a woman comes under the hand of her husband: she who comes into the hand of a husband suffers a change of status, because she passes into his family and takes the place of a daughter-heir, as in title 23 and in Gellius, book 18, chapter 6.

units.la: Confirmantur eadem lege ] Testamento dati tutores lege confirmantur, vt hic.
units.tr: Confirmed by the same law: guardians appointed by testament are confirmed by law, as here.

units.la: Vti legassit] Integra lex est. Paterfamilias vti legassit, auctore Cornificio lib.1. ad Herennium. Ait, super pecunia, tutelave suæ rei, quæ verba coniunctim accipienda sunt. Nam tutorem instituere filiis suis pater, nisi in testamento, non potest, in quo & pecuniæ suæ hæredem instituat.L.sæpe.de verb.sign.Cuiac.hic.
units.tr: As he has bequeathed: the law is complete: "The head of the family, as he has bequeathed..." as Cornificius, book 1, to Herennius, states it: concerning money or the guardianship of his own affairs. These words are to be taken together. For a father cannot appoint guardians for his sons except in a will, in which he also appoints an heir to his money. L. saepe, de verb. sign. Cuiac. here.

units.la: Vti legassit] Hoc caput ad hæreditates etiam & legata refertur, vti quisque legassit, suæ rei ius esto. l.120. ff. de verb. sign. vti quisq; legassit de re sua, ita ius esto. Nov. 22. c. 2. Paterfamilias vti super pecunia tutelave sua legassit, ita ius esto. Author ad Herennium: super pecunia, tutelave suæ rei. l. 53. ff. de verb. signif. vt eam pecuniam, easve res, quibusque dare legare voler, ius potestasque esto. l.1. ff. ad l. Falcidiam. & Vlpian. tit. 1. §. 9. sup. eod. Lex 12. tabularum confirmat quod datum, legatum est. Goth. hic.
units.tr: As he has bequeathed: this clause is also referred to inheritances and legacies: "as each has bequeathed, so let his right over his own property be" (l.120. ff. de verb. sign.). "As each has bequeathed concerning his own property, so let it be his right" (Nov. 22, c. 2). "As the head of the family has bequeathed concerning his money and guardianship, so let it be his right" (the author to Herennius: concerning money, or the guardianship of his own affairs; l. 53. ff. de verb. signif.: "let it be his right and power to give or bequeath that money or those things to whomever he wishes"; l.1. ff. ad l. Falcidiam; and Ulpian tit. 1 §. 9 sup. eod.). The Law of the Twelve Tables confirms that what has been given is a legacy. Goth. here.

units.la: Tutelave ] melius quam in l. 53. ff. de verb. signific. super pecuniæ, tutelève suæ.
units.tr: Tutelave: better than in l. 53. ff. de verb. signific., which reads "super pecuniae, tutelaeve suae."

units.la: Qui tutores datiui] Legitimi non dantur, sed ipso iure fiunt tutores. l. legitimos. ff. de legit. tutor. Testamentarii, Attiliani, Iuliani, datione tutores fiunt. Plerunque autem Attiliani, & Iuliani datiui tutores appellantur. l. datiuus. C. rem pup. satu. for. l. generaliter. (. de episc. & cler. l. vlt. C. de legit. tutor. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Qui tutores datiui: Legitimate tutors are not appointed; they become tutors by the law itself. l. legitimos. ff. de legit. tutor. Testamentary, Attilian and Julian tutors become tutors by appointment. Attilian and Julian tutors are usually called dative tutors. l. datiuus. C. rem pup. salv. fore; l. generaliter. § de episc. & cler.; l. vlt. C. de legit. tutor. Cuiacius and Pacius here.

units.la: Qui tutores datiui] verba quæ sequuntur esse quasi argumentum sententiæ sequentis videntur. alias improprie legitimi tutores datiui dicuntur. l. 5. ff. de legib. quod tamen ex hoc §. sequitur. Goth. h.
units.tr: Qui tutores datiui: The words that follow seem to be a kind of argument for the sentence that follows; otherwise legitimate tutors are improperly called dative tutors. l. 5. ff. de legib. This, however, follows from this §. Goth. h.

units.la: Liberis qui in potestate] l.3. ff. de tutel. l.1. ff. de testam. tut.
units.tr: Liberis qui in potestate: l. 3. ff. de tutel.; l. 1. ff. de testam. tut.

units.la: Cum quibus] l.21. ff. de testam. tut.
units.tr: Cum quibus: l. 21. ff. de testam. tut.

units.la: Nam Latinus] de quo vid. s tit. 3. de Latinis. Si abdicauerit] id est, se excusauerit. l.ii. §.2. ff.de testament.
units.tr: Nam Latinus: of which see tit. 3. de Latinis. Si abdicauerit: that is, if he has excused himself. l. ii. §. 2. ff. de testament.

units.la: Desinit esse tutor] eiusque loco non legitimus sed datiuus constituetur. d.§.2.
units.tr: Desinit esse tutor: and in his place a dative tutor, not a legitimate one, is appointed. d. §. 2.

units.la: Abdicare autem] M. Tullius lib.6. ad Atticum. Itaque aut tutela cogito me abdicare, aut vt pro Glabrione Scæuola, fœnus & impendium recusare. Nihil ab abdicatione distat excusatio. Excusatione datiui duntaxat vtuntur. l.ειδνας. ff.de exc.tut.§.qui excusare. Inst.eod. Nullum vero in iure ciuili excusationis proximis agnatis datæ extat exemplum. Proinde recte ait, legitimos tutela se abdicare non posse. Ratio illa est, quia ipso iure tutores existunt. Quæ ratio etiam efficit, vt sui hæredes repudiare hæreditatem non possint. Verum enim vt in iure, hi se hæreditate abstinere, ita & illi in iure, id est, apud prætorem, tutela fœminarum cedere possunt.] In pupillis maribus, vt iam superius ab Vlpiano dictum est, cessitia tutela non procedit. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Abdicare autem: M. Tullius, lib. 6. ad Atticum: "So I am thinking of either renouncing the guardianship, or, as in the case of Glabrio on behalf of Scaevola, refusing the interest and the outlay." Excuse differs in no way from renunciation. Only dative tutors make use of excuse. l. ειδνας. ff. de exc. tut.; § qui excusare. Inst. eod. In civil law there is no recorded instance of an excuse granted to the nearest agnates. Therefore he rightly says that legitimate tutors cannot renounce the guardianship, the reason being that they become tutors by the law itself. This same reason also means that heirs-in-law cannot refuse an inheritance. Yet, just as these abstain from the inheritance in law, so those may cede the guardianship of women in law, that is, before the praetor. In the case of male pupils, as Ulpian has already said above, cession of guardianship does not apply. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.

units.la: Cedere] ad hanc cessionem in iure refer §. 3. sup. eod.
units.tr: Cedere: for this cession in law, refer to §. 3, sup. eod.

units.la: Lex Attilia] vid. Inst. de Attiliano tutore.
units.tr: Lex Attilia: see Inst. de Attiliano tutore.

units.la: Et inaiore] Inst. d. loco.
units.tr: Et in maiore: Inst. d. loco.

units.la: Præsidibus earum] ijsque qui sunt eius provinciæ, vel ibidem domicilium habent. l.1.in f. ff.de tutorib. dat.
units.tr: Praesidibus earum: and to those who belong to that province or have their domicile there. l. 1. in f. ff. de tutorib. dat.

units.la: Qui etiam ante manumissionem] Non eum solum L 1 5 solum qui in bonis, sed etiam qui ex iure Quiritium dominus fuit. Cuiac.
units.tr: Qui etiam ante manumissionem: not only one who was owner in bonis, but also one who was owner by Quiritary right. Cuiac.

units.la: Ad dotem dandam ] leg. 5. §. 4. l. 61. ff. de inr. dot. leg. 22. §. 10. ff. soluto. adde leg. 7. ff. de tutoribus dat.
units.tr: Ad dotem dandam: l. 5. §. 4; l. 61. ff. de iur. dot.; l. 22. §. 10. ff. soluto. Add l. 7. ff. de tutoribus dat.

units.la: Dicendam ] Dos olim dicebatur, qua de re vid. tit. 6. §. 1. §. 2. supr. eodem.
units.tr: Dicendam: the dowry was formerly called dos; on this see tit. 6. §. 1, §. 2, supra eodem.

units.la: Promittendamve ] d. §. 2. in sin. adde & augendam & minuendam d. l. 7.
units.tr: Promittendamve: d. §. 2, in sin. Add also augendam and minuendam, d. l. 7.

units.la: Si legitimum tutorem pupilla non habeat ] delenda est vox, pupilla: nam de pubere hic agitur, non de pupilla. Caeterum quamuis regula iuris haec sit, certae rei vel causae tutorem non dari, ex l. tamen Iulia & Senatusconsultis tutor ex causa datur ad dotem constituendam. Item ut paulo post tradit, ad adeundam hereditatem specialis tutor datur: quod etiam confirmat l. impuberi. ff. de tut. & curat. dat. l. cum in una §. tutor de appellat. Cuiac. & Paci. b.
units.tr: Si legitimum tutorem pupilla non habeat: the word pupilla should be deleted, for this concerns a pubescent, not a pupil. Moreover, although the rule of law is that a tutor is not given for a particular thing or cause, by the Julian law and the senatusconsults a tutor is given for a cause, namely to constitute a dowry. Likewise, as he teaches a little later, a special tutor is given for entering an inheritance; this too is confirmed by l. impuberi. ff. de tut. & curat. dat.; l. cum in una, §. tutor, de appellat. Cuiac. & Paci. b.

units.la: In locum muti ] l. 17. ff. de tutelis l. 11. l. 40. ff. de excus. tut.
units.tr: In locum muti: l. 17. ff. de tutelis; l. 11; l. 40. ff. de excus. tut.

units.la: Ad dotem constituendam ] si ad dotem constituendam, erit hoc contrarium superiori regulae iuris, quae dictat, certae rei tutorem non dari: si generaliter (quod & ipsum, si mutus aut furiosus sit, legitimus datur, ex S. C. fieri potest, l. penult. ff. de tutel.) obstat illa regula, qua cauetur, Tutorem habenti tutorem non dari: ideoque senatusconsulto opus fuit. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Ad dotem constituendam: if it is for constituting a dowry, this will be contrary to the rule of law above, which dictates that a tutor is not given for a particular thing. If it is given generally (which can also happen, when the pupil is mute or insane, that a legitimate tutor is given by senatusconsult, l. penult. ff. de tutel.), then that rule stands in the way, by which it is provided that a tutor is not given to one who already has a tutor; therefore a senatusconsult was needed. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.

units.la: Ad dotem constituendam ] Et ad res alias. d. l. 17. l. 11. l. 40.
units.tr: Ad dotem constituendam: and for other matters. d. l. 17; l. 11; l. 40.

units.la: Senatus censuit ] d. l. 17.
units.tr: Senatus censuit: d. l. 17.

units.la: Cuius tutor abest ] adde l. 15. ff. de tutel. l. 10. ff. de tutor. datis.
units.tr: Whose tutor is absent: add the law 15 of the Digest, de tutelis, and the law 10 of the Digest, de tutoribus datis.

units.la: Ad hæreditatem adeundam ] l. 9. sup. de tutor. datis.
units.tr: Ad hereditatem adeundam: l. 9. sup. de tutor. datis.

units.la: Idemque permisit in pupillo patroni filio ] Malo, Idemque permisit in patroni filio, nimirum ut in eius locum non nisi ad adeundam hæreditatem, vel dotem constituendam, tutor detur. Quod & generaliter in tutoribus pupillorum iure ciuili locum obtinet. Vel hic est sensus, ut in locum pupilli filij patroni, & tutoris legitimi liberti paterni alius tutor detur. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Idemque permisit in pupillo patroni filio: I prefer: "and he permitted the same in the son of a patron," namely that in his place a tutor be appointed only for entering an inheritance or constituting a dowry. This generally holds in civil law for the tutors of pupils as well. Or the sense here is that, in place of a pupil who is the patron's son, and a legitimate tutor of a paternal freedman, another tutor is appointed. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.

units.la: Hoc amplius ] Huius S. C. fit mentio in leg. si quis sub conditione de testam. tut. & hi quidem sunt tutores, qui ex S.C. dantur: de quibus intelligenda est lex tutelas de cap. minutis. Sequuntur hi, qui moribus dantur. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Hoc amplius: mention of this senatusconsult is made in leg. si quis sub conditione, de testam. tut. These are the tutors who are given by senatusconsult, and the law tutelas de cap. minutis must be understood of them. There follow those who are given by custom. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Pupilli pupillæ suspectus ] l. 14. §. 4. ff. de tutel. l. 11. §. 1. ff. de legit. tutor.
units.tr: Suspect of a ward, male or female: l. 14. §. 4. ff. de tutel. l. 11. §. 1. ff. de legit. tutor.

units.la: Iusta de causa excusatus ] d. l. 11. §. 1.
units.tr: Iusta de causa excusatus: d. l. 11. §. 1.

units.la: Moribus tutor ] Hodie quia extraordinaria sunt iudicia, curator datur, §. vlt. de aucto. tut.
units.tr: Moribus tutor: today, because trials are extraordinary, a curator is appointed; §. vlt. de auctor. tut.

units.la: In ordinarijs iudicijs tutor exigitur l.curatorem ff.eod. l.vlt. C.de in lit. dand. tut. Cuiac.b.
units.tr: In ordinary trials a guardian is required: l. curatorem ff. eod. l. vlt. C. de in lit. dand. tut. Cuiac. b.

units.la: Datur mulieri] vid. Goth. ad leges 12. tabularum lib.2. adde §.27. inf. eod.
units.tr: Datur mulieri: see Goth. on the laws of the Twelve Tables, lib. 2. Add §. 27, inf. eod.

units.la: Qui cum tutore] vid. l.1. C. de in litem dando.
units.tr: Qui cum tutore: see l. 1. C. de in litem dando.

units.la: Lege aut legitimo iudicio] Lege agere latius patet, quam legitimo iudicio agere. nam sine iudicio lege agi potest.
units.tr: Lege aut legitimo iudicio: to act by law extends more widely than to act by legitimate judgment, for an action can be brought by law without a judgment.

units.la: Praetorianus tutor] Praetorius §. vlt. Instit. de author. tut. Hodie tutorem habenti tutor non datur, sed curator.
units.tr: The praetorian guardian: Praetorius §. vlt. Instit. de author. tut. Today, where someone already has a guardian, no guardian is given but a curator.

units.la: Auctoritatem interponunt] l. 1. ff. de administ. tut.
units.tr: Auctoritatem interponunt: l. 1. ff. de administ. tut.

units.la: Auctoritatem duntaxat] vid. ff. C. Inst. de author. tut. vide Cuiac. 7. obseru. 11.
units.tr: Auctoritatem duntaxat: see ff. C. Inst. de author. tut.; see Cuiac. 7 obseru. 11.

units.la: Prater eos] Hodie id immutatum. vid. l. vlt. C. de authoritate praestanda.
units.tr: Praeter eos: today this has been changed; see l. vlt. C. de authoritate praestanda.

units.la: Qui tunc dati sunt] Legendum, qui testamento dati sunt. l. vlt. C. de auctor praestanda l.4. l.5. in princ. & §. item ipse. l. quod dicimus §. 1. ff. eod. Marcus Tullius pro Flacco, nihil potest de legitima tutela sine omnium tutorum auctoritate deminui. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Qui tunc dati sunt: read, "who were given by will." l. vlt. C. de auctor. praestanda; l. 4; l. 5, in princ. & §. item ipse; l. quod dicimus, §. 1. ff. eod. Marcus Tullius, in pro Flacco: nothing can be taken away from legitimate guardianship without the authority of all the tutors. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.

units.la: Vnius auctoritas] d.l.vlt. add. l.4. l.5. l.7. §.1. ff. de auctoritat. tut.
units.tr: Unius auctoritas: d. l. vlt.; add l. 4; l. 5; l. 7, §. 1. ff. de auctoritat. tut.

units.la: Mulieribus quidem] §.4. sup. eod.
units.tr: Mulieribus quidem: §. 4, sup. eod.

units.la: Masculi quidem pubertate] Inst. quib. mod. tutela.
units.tr: Masculi quidem pubertate: Inst. quib. mod. tutela.

units.la: Cassiani] veteres Inst. quib. mod. tut.
units.tr: Cassiani: the ancient jurists; Inst. quib. mod. tut.

units.la: Tit. XII. De Curatoribus.
units.tr: Tit. XII. Concerning Curators.

units.la: CVratores aut legitimi sunt, id est, qui ex lege duodecim Tabularum dantur: aut honorarii, id est, qui à Prætore constituuntur.
units.tr: Curators are either legitimate, that is, those appointed by the law of the Twelve Tables, or honorary, that is, those appointed by the praetor.

units.la: Lex duodecim Tabularum furiosum, itemque prodigum, cui bonis interdictum est, in curatione iuber esse agnatorum.
units.tr: The law of the Twelve Tables orders that a madman, and likewise a prodigal who has been forbidden to manage his goods, be placed under the guardianship of his agnates.

units.la: A Prætore constituitur curator, quem ipse Prætor voluerit, libertinis prodigis, itemque ingenuis, qui ex testamento parentis heredes facti, male dissipant bona: his enim ex lege, curator dari non poterat: cum ingenuus quidem non ab intestato, sed ex testamento heres factus sit patri: libertinus autem nullo modo patri heres fieri possit, qui nec patrem habuisse videtur; cum servilis cognatio nulla sit.
units.tr: A curator is appointed by the praetor, whomever the praetor himself chooses, for prodigal freedmen, and likewise for freeborn men who, having been made heirs by their parent's will, squander the estate. For by law no curator could be given to these. A freeborn man becomes his father's heir not on intestacy but by will, whereas a freedman can in no way become his father's heir, since he seems not to have a father at all, and servile kinship is nothing.

units.la: Praeterea dat curatorem ei etiam, qui nuper pubes factus, idoneè negotia sua tueri non potest.
units.tr: Moreover, he also gives a curator to one who, having recently reached puberty, cannot adequately manage his own affairs.

units.la: Vide l. Caium 8. l. Inst. 23. §. C. 70. 27. ff. eod.
units.tr: See l. Caium 8. l. Inst. 23. §. C. 70. 27. ff. eod.

units.la: Aut honorarij ] dantur etiam testamento, postea confirmandi à praeside. §. 1. Inst. eod.
units.tr: Aut honorarii ] are also given by will, afterwards to be confirmed by the praetor. §. 1. Inst. eod.

units.la: Lex duodecim tabularum ] l. 1. ff. de curator.
units.tr: Lex duodecim tabularum ] l. 1. ff. de curator.

units.la: Dissipant bona ] qui neque tempus, neque finem expensarum habent d. l. 1.
units.tr: Dissipant bona ] who have neither a limit nor an end to their expenses. d. l. 1.

units.la: Qui nec patrem ] utitur Iurisconsultus argumento à priuatione ducto, vt & alibi, Nemo cogitur reddere quod non habet. l. 22. §. 3. ff. ad Trebel. Non repudiat, qui negat nuptam. Novel. 74. c. 5. Non latitat, qui sibi non est idoneus defensor. l. 5. de reb. autor. servus capite minui non potest, qui nullum caput habet. l. 3. in sin. ff. de capite minut. Goth. b.
units.tr: Qui nec patrem ] The jurist uses an argument drawn from privation, as he does elsewhere: no one is compelled to return what he does not have. l. 22. §. 3. ff. ad Trebel. One does not repudiate who denies that she was married. Novel. 74. c. 5. One does not hide who is not a suitable defender. l. 5. de reb. autor. A slave cannot suffer capitis deminutio who has no caput. l. 3. in sin. ff. de capite minut. Goth. b.

units.la: Cognatio nulla sit ] Imo aliqua Instit. de servili cognat.
units.tr: Cognatio nulla sit ] On the contrary, there is some. Instit. de servili cognat.

units.la: Sua tueri non potest ] l. 2. ff. eod.
units.tr: Sua tueri non potest ] l. 2. ff. eod.

units.la: Tit. XIII. De cœlibe, orbo, & solitario patre.
units.tr: Tit. XIII. On the unmarried, the childless, and the solitary father.

units.la: LEge Iulia prohibentur vxores ducere, senatores quidem liberique eorum, libertinas, & quæ ipsæ, quarumve pater materve artem ludicram fecerit: item corpore quæstum facientem:
units.tr: By the Julian law, senators and their children are forbidden to marry freedwomen, or women who have themselves practised the stage art, or whose father or mother has done so, and likewise women who make money from their bodies.

units.la: Cæteri autem ingenui prohibentur ducere lenam, à lenone lenave manumissam, & in adulterio deprehensam, & iudicio publico damnatam, & quæ artem ludicram fecerit: adiicit Mauricianus, & à senatu damnatam.
units.tr: Other freeborn men are forbidden to marry a procuress, a woman manumitted by a procurer, a woman caught in adultery, a woman condemned in a public trial, or a woman who has practised the stage art. Marcianus adds: or one condemned by the senate.

units.la: De] Hæc epigraphe convenit melius titulo sequenti.
units.tr: De: this heading fits better with the following title.

units.la: Cœlibe] Dion. 54. refert, legem Iuliam τοῖς πρεσβύταις καὶ τοῖς ἀνάνδροις graues pœnas irrogasse: Intelligit autem id pœnæ genus, quo cœlebs vetatur quidquam extranei testamento capere: nisi intra centum dies nuptias contraxerit, tit.17.§.1.inf.eod.1.Sozom.9.l.35.ff.de mortis causal.12.ff.de vulgari. Tertull.lib.de Monogamia. Aliud est si apud Christum, legibus Iuliis agi credunt & existimant cœlibes & orbos ex testamento Dei solidum capere non posse. Tacit. 3. Annal. Relatum de moderanda Papia Poppæa, quam senior Augustus post Iulias rogatas incitandis cœlibum pœnis, & augendo ærario sanxerat, &c. ad has pœnas respexit Plutarchus chius libro ἀπὸ φιλοσοφίας, χωμάων πολλοί, inquit: χαμῶσι, καὶ ἡ γυνὴ, ὅχ ἵνα κληρονόμως ἔχωσιν, ἀλλ' ἵνα κληρονομῶσιν δύνωνται. Author Panegyrici Maximino & Constantino dictari leges Iulias ita commendat. Leges, inquam, quæ multa cœlibes notarunt; parentes præmiis honorarunt; vere dicuntur esse fundamenta reipublicæ, quia seminarium iuuentutis & quasi fontem humani corporis semper Romanis exercitibus ministrarunt. Goth.h.
units.tr: Cœlibe: Dio (54) reports that the Julian law imposed severe penalties on τοῖς πρεσβύταις καὶ τοῖς ἀνάνδροις [the elderly and the unmarried]. He means by this kind of penalty that the unmarried is forbidden to take anything by a stranger's will, unless he has contracted marriage within a hundred days: tit.17.§.1.inf.eod.1.Sozom.9.l.35.ff.de mortis causal.12.ff.de vulgari. Tertull.lib.de Monogamia. It is another matter if, in the case of Christ, they believe and think that by the Julian laws the unmarried and the childless cannot take the whole of an inheritance under God's testament. Tacit. 3. Annal. The proposal concerning the moderating of the Papian Poppaean law, which the elder Augustus had sanctioned after the Julian laws were proposed, to increase the penalties on the unmarried and to enlarge the treasury, etc. Plutarch of Chios, in his book on philosophy, looked to these penalties when he said: "Many men marry, and women too, not so that they may have heirs, but so that they may be able to be heirs" [χαμῶσι, καὶ ἡ γυνὴ, ὅχ ἵνα κληρονόμως ἔχωσιν, ἀλλ' ἵνα κληρονομῶσιν δύνωνται]. The author of the Panegyric to Maximian and Constantine commends the Julian laws, which are said to have been enacted for them, in this way: "The laws, I say, which marked the many unmarried, honoured parents with rewards; they are rightly said to be the foundations of the commonwealth, because they always supplied the Roman armies with a seedbed of youth and, as it were, a fountain of the human body." Goth.h.

units.la: Orbo] Orbus semissis capiendi capax erat, non solidi: l. 6. ff. de vulgari l. 42. ff. de legat. l. 116. §. 15. ff. ad Trebell. l. 13. in sin. ff. de iur. fisci. hinc illæ instituendi leges in tempus capiendæ hereditatis. l. 62. ff. de hæred. instituend. Ex parte quam quis per leges capere possit. l. 78. sin. de hared. instit. Et ita melior orbi quam cœlibis conditio; quia maritus orbus, saltem dimidium capit: cœlebs nihil. Goth.h.
units.tr: Orbo: The childless man was able to take only half of an inheritance, not the whole: l. 6. ff. de vulgari l. 42. ff. de legat. l. 116. §. 15. ff. ad Trebell. l. 13. in sin. ff. de iur. fisci. Hence those laws of institution for a time limit on taking the inheritance: l. 62. ff. de hæred. instituend. For the part which someone can take by the laws: l. 78. sin. de hared. instit. And so the condition of the childless is better than that of the unmarried, because a childless married man takes at least half, while the unmarried takes nothing. Goth.h.

units.la: Et solitario patre] solitarius hic dicitur, qui unicum & solum filium habet μόνον παλυγενῆ υἱὸν μονογενῆ, vt Aquila loquitur: quasi medius inter orbum & cœlibem, & multorum liberorum parentem. Priorum pœnas vt non patitur, ita posteriorum præmijs non fruitur. Gothofred. hic.
units.tr: Et solitario patre: Here "solitary" is said of one who has a single and only son, μόνον παλυγενῆ υἱὸν μονογενῆ, as Aquila puts it: as if midway between the childless and the unmarried, and the parent of many children. As he does not suffer the penalties of the former, so he does not enjoy the rewards of the latter. Gothofred. hic.

units.la: Lege Iulia] quæ & Papia. l. 44. ff. de ritu l. 28. C. de nupt.
units.tr: Lege Iulia: which is also called the Papian law. l. 44. ff. de ritu l. 28. C. de nupt.

units.la: Senatores quidem] l. 16. l. 31. l. 32. l. 34. in sin. l. 44. l.44.ff. de ritu. Id hodie senatoribus remissum est. Nou. 78. c.3.
units.tr: Senatores quidem: l. 16. l. 31. l. 32. l. 34. in sin. l. 44. ff. de ritu. This has now been remitted to senators. Nou. 78. c.3.

units.la: Libertinas ] l. 23. ff. de ritu l. 28. C. de nupt. l.7, C. de incestis.
units.tr: Libertinas: l. 23. ff. de ritu l. 28. C. de nupt. l.7, C. de incestis.

units.la: Artem ludicram ] d.l.7.l.42.§.1.ff.de ritu.
units.tr: Artem ludicram: stage art. d.l.7.l.42.§.1.ff.de ritu.

units.la: Item corpore ] l.41.l.43.ff. de ritu.l.7. in sin.ff. de incestis.
units.tr: Likewise, "body" ] l.41, l.43 ff. de ritu; l.7 in fin. ff. de incestis.

units.la: Ceteri autem ingenui ] Et has quoque senatores non ducent l. Iulia §. vlt. de ritu nupt. non tamen idem est contrario: nam ingenui libertinas ducent. l.lege Papia eod. Est in eandem rem auctoritate Marci & Commodi factum plenius S. C. de quo in l. oratio. de Sponsal. l. oratione l. palam §. senatus de ritu nupt. Extat & de eadem re Constantini constitutio. l. 1. C. de nat. lib. & Nou. Marciani, de mat.senat. quæ tamen ambæ sublatæ sunt in Novel. Iustiniani 117. & 89. ex qua id etiam didicimus, corrupte in d.l. scriptum esse, Præfectos, legendum enim est, Perfectissimos ; id est , ἀξιομυητότατος[?] arque ita constanter habent omnes veteres Codices. Error manauit ex errore Nou. Marciani. Lex quoque Iulia de senatorum & libertinarum nuptiis à Iustiniano sublata est. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Ceteri autem ingenui: These senators also are not to marry, l. Iulia §. vlt. de ritu nupt. but the converse does not hold, for freeborn men may marry freedwomen. l. lege Papia eod. A fuller provision on the same matter was made by the authority of Marcus and Commodus, S. C. de quo in l. oratio. de Sponsal. l. oratione l. palam §. senatus de ritu nupt. and there is also a constitution of Constantine on the same subject. l. 1. C. de nat. lib. & Nou. Marcian, de mat.senat. Both, however, were abolished in the Novels of Justinian, 117 and 89, from which we have also learned that in the law the word "Præfectos" is wrongly written; it should read "Perfectissimos", that is, ἀξιομυητότατος [?], and all the old codices consistently have this. The error came from an error in the Novel of Marcian. The Julian law on the marriages of senators and freedwomen was also abolished by Justinian. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.

units.la: Ducere lenam ] d.l.43.§.6.7.8.
units.tr: Ducere lenam: to marry a procuress. d.l.43.§.6.7.8.

units.la: In adulterio ] d.l.43.§.12.13.
units.tr: In adulterio: caught in adultery. d.l.43.§.12.13.

units.la: Iudicio publico damnatam ] d.l.43,§.10.11.
units.tr: Iudicio publico damnatam: condemned in a public trial. d.l.43,§.10.11.

units.la: Artem ludicram ] d.l.44.ff.de ritu.
units.tr: Artem ludicram: stage art. d.l.44.ff.de ritu.

units.la: ] Qui ad leges Iulias libros scri-psit.
units.tr: Who wrote books on the Julian laws.

units.la: ] leg. 16. l. 43. §. 10 ff. de ritu.
units.tr: leg. 16. l. 43. §. 10 ff. de ritu.

units.la: Tit. XIIII. De pœna legis Iuliæ.
units.tr: Title 14. On the penalty of the Julian law.

units.la: FOeminis lex Iulia à morte viri anni tribuit vacationem: à diuortio, sex mensium: lex autem Papia à morte viri, biennii: à repudio, anni & sex mensium.
units.tr: The Julian law granted women a period of exemption of one year after the death of a husband, and of six months after divorce; but the Papian law granted two years after the death of a husband, and one year and six months after repudiation.

units.la: Pœna legis Iuliæ, hæc est, ne cœlibes, ne orbi, ex ciuium Romanorum testamentis capiant. l. si is qui heres de vulg. subst. Tertull. in lib. de monogamia. Aliud est si & apud Christum legibus Iulijs agi credunt, & existimant cœlibes & orbos, ex testamento Dei solidum capere non posse. Sed hæc pœna sublata est à l. 1. C. de infir. pœn. cœl. & orbit. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: The penalty of the Julian law is this: the unmarried and the childless may not take under the wills of Roman citizens. l. si is qui heres de vulg. subst. Tertull. in lib. de monogamia. It is another matter whether they believe that under the Julian laws the same applies with Christ, and think that the unmarried and the childless cannot take the whole of an inheritance under God's testament. But this penalty has been abolished by l. 1. C. de infir. pœn. cœl. & orbit. Cuiac. h.

units.la: ] Orbis, cœlibus, & solitarijs iniectæ.
units.tr: Imposed on the childless, the unmarried and the solitary.

units.la: ] Quid maritis? triennij videtur fuisse ex l. Iulia Sueton. anni, lege Papia. Nam ipse Augustus, apud Dionem 56. dicitur ijs qui cœlibes essent, primum dedisse triennium, deinde biennium, (lege Iulia, vt est credibile) tum annum, lege Papia. Sed hoc tempus currebat à lege lata. An à die diuortij vel mortis eius temporis esset vacatio, incertum forte, quoquoniam de fœminis Vlpianus hic tantum loquitur: in quas, leges quam in viros mitiores fuere semper. vid. Cuiac. 6. obseru. 37. Goth. h.
units.tr: Why was it for husbands? It seems to have been three years under the Julian law, as Suetonius reports, and one year under the Papian law. For Augustus himself, according to Dio, book 56, is said to have first given three years to the unmarried, then two (under the Julian law, as is credible), and then one year under the Papian law. But this period ran from the passing of the law. Whether the exemption ran from the day of divorce or of death is perhaps uncertain, since Ulpian here speaks only of women, against whom the laws were always milder than against men. See Cuiac. 6. obseru. 37. Goth. h.

units.la: Tribuit vacationem] Hoc est, vt interim, etiam si cœlibem vitam agant, capere ex alterius testamento possint. Lex enim Iulia vetat cœlibes quidquam testamento extranei capere. leg. 11. ff. de vulgari. leg. 35. ff. de mort. causa. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Granted an exemption: that is, so that meanwhile, even if they live unmarried, they may take under another's will. For the Julian law forbids the unmarried to take anything under the will of a stranger. leg. 11. ff. de vulgari. leg. 35. ff. de mort. causa. Gothofr. hic.

units.la: Biennij] Legendum, Triennij, vt enim altero tanto à morte viri vacatio, quæ lege Iulia tribuitur, eam superat, quæ à diuortio tribuitur, eadem vt sit proportio necesse est in lege Papia, quæ tempora legis Iuliæ prorogauit. Denique triennium Augusti lege tribui, Suetonius auctor est: nimirum enim lex Papia Popæa lata est autore D. Augusto post Iulias rogationes, M. Papio, Q. Popæo coss. suffectis, non ordinariis, vt Dion & Isidorus scribunt. Cuiac. hic & Paci.
units.tr: Two years: read three years. For just as the exemption from the husband's death granted by the Julian law is twice that from divorce, so the same proportion must hold under the Papian law, which extended the Julian periods. Finally, Suetonius records that the three years were granted by a law of Augustus. Indeed the Papian-Poppaean law was passed on the authority of the deified Augustus after the Julian proposals, in the consulship of M. Papius and Q. Poppaeus, who were suffect and not ordinary consuls, as Dio and Isidore write. Cuiac. hic & Paci.

units.la: Tit. XV. De decimis.
units.tr: Title XV. On tenths.

units.la: VIr & vxor inter se matrimonii nomine decimam capere possunt.
units.tr: A husband and wife may take a tenth between themselves in the name of marriage.

units.la: Quod si ex alio matrimonio liberos superstites habeant, præter decimam quam matrimonii nomine capiunt, totidem decimas pro numero liberorum accipiunt. Item communis
units.tr: But if they have surviving children from another marriage, then besides the tenth they take in the name of marriage, they receive as many tenths as there are children. Likewise a common

units.la: filius,filiave,post nonum diem amissus, amissave, unam decimam adiicit. duo autem, post nonum diem amissi, duas decimas adiiciunt. Præter decimam, etiam usumfructum tertiæ partis bonorum eius capere possunt: & quotcunque liberos habuerint, eiusdem partis proprietatem. Hoc amplius mulier petere præter decimam dotem potest legatam sibi.
units.tr: son or daughter, lost after the ninth day, adds one tenth; two lost after the ninth day add two tenths. Besides the tenth, they may also take the usufruct of a third part of his goods, and the ownership of that same part, however many children they have. Moreover, a woman may claim, besides the tenth, the dowry bequeathed to her.

units.la: Lege Iulia coniuges, præter ea quæ in hoc titulo enumerantur, inter se capere nihil possunt, & hoc in uxore manifesto tradit l. i. C. de his qui se defendere lib. 10. Sunt & multa huius rei vestigia in C. Theod. l. ult. de inoff. dot. l. ult. de leg. hæred. l.1. l. si aliquis de bon. proscr. l. pro commoditate de nauicul. & in Nou. Valent. de testament. Sed in l. pro commoditate, pro liberis, perperam scriptum est, lucris. Interdum vero ne decimas quidem capere possunt: contra interdum & solidum capere possunt, hodie omnimodo l.2.C. de infir. pæn. cæl. & orbi. & decimis sublatis. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: By the Julian law spouses may take nothing from each other beyond what is listed in this title, and this is clearly stated for a wife in l. i. C. de his qui se defendere lib. 10. There are also many traces of this matter in the Theodosian Code: l. ult. de inoff. dot. l. ult. de leg. hæred. l.1. l. si aliquis de bon. proscr. l. pro commoditate de nauicul. and in the Novels of Valentinian, de testament. But in the law pro commoditate, the word lucris has been wrongly written for liberis. Sometimes, however, they cannot even take the tenths; on the other hand, sometimes they can take the whole, as is now always the case, l.2.C. de infir. pæn. cæl. & orbi. and with the tenths abolished. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Matrimonij nomine] id est, in honorem matrimonij.
units.tr: In the name of marriage] that is, in honour of marriage.

units.la: Capere possunt] l.18. ff. de auro. add. l.6. ff. de vulgari l. 42. ff. de legat. 2. respexit huc orator vetus: Placet ergo, o leges diligentissimæ pudoris custodes, decimas uxoribus, quartas meretricibus dari? Porro decimaria ea lex sublata l. 2. C. de infirm. pæn. cælib. Goth. hic.
units.tr: May take] l.18. ff. de auro. add. l.6. ff. de vulgari l. 42. ff. de legat. 2. An old orator had this in view: "Is it agreed, then, O laws most diligent guardians of modesty, that tenths are given to wives and quarters to prostitutes?" Moreover, that tenths law was abolished, l. 2. C. de infirm. pæn. cælib. Goth. hic.

units.la: Totidem] Aliæ decimæ erant, quæ nomine matrimonij, aliæ, quæ propter singulos liberos percipiebantur.
units.tr: Totidem] Some tenths were those granted in the name of marriage; others were those received on account of each individual child.

units.la: Duo autem] Tres post nonum diem amissi solidum adiiciunt. tit. prox.
units.tr: Duo autem] Three who die after the ninth day add the whole. tit. prox.

units.la: Post] Nam defuncti ante nominis suscepti-onem, pro non susceптis habentur.
units.tr: Post] For those who die before the name is taken up are regarded as not having been received.

units.la: Tit. XVI. De solidi capacitate inter vi-rum & uxorem.
units.tr: Title XVI. On the capacity to take the whole (solidum) between husband and wife.

units.la: ALiquando vir & vxor inter se solidum capere possunt: velut si vterque, vel alter-uter eorum nondum eius ætatis sit, quæ quidem liberos exigit: id est, si vir minor annorum viginti quinque sit, aut vxor annorum viginti minor. item si vtrique lege Papia finitos in matrimonio annos excesserint, id est, vir sexaginta annos, vxor quinquaginta. item si cognati inter se coierunt vsque ad sextum gradum: aut si vir absit, & donec abesset, intra annum postquam abesse desierit, libera inter eos testamenti factio est. Si ius liberorum à principe impetrauerint: aut si filium filiamve communem habeant: aut quatuordecim annorum filium, vel filiam duodecim amiserint: vel si duos trimos, vel si tres post nonum diem amiserint, vt intra annum tamen & sex menses. Etiam vnus cuiuscunque ætatis impubes amissus solidi capienpiendi ius præstat. Item si post mortem viri intra decem menses vxor ex eo peperit, solidum ex bonis eius capit.
units.tr: Sometimes husband and wife can take the whole (solidum) from each other. This happens, for example, if either of them, or both, has not yet reached the age that requires children: that is, if the husband is under twenty-five, or the wife under twenty. Likewise, if both have passed the years of marriage fixed by the Lex Papia, that is, the husband sixty and the wife fifty. Likewise, if relatives have married one another up to the sixth degree. Or, if the husband is absent, then for as long as he is absent, and within a year after he has ceased to be absent, there is free testamentary capacity between them. If they have obtained the right of children (ius liberorum) from the prince; or if they have a common son or daughter; or if they have lost a son of fourteen or a daughter of twelve; or if they have lost two children aged three, or three after the ninth day, provided this happens within a year and six months. Also, the loss of a single prepubescent child of any age confers the right to take the whole. Likewise, if the wife bears a child by her husband within ten months after his death, she takes the whole from his goods.

units.la: Aliquando nihil inter se capiunt, id est, si contra Legem Iuliam, Papiamque Poppæam contraxerint matrimonium: verbi gratia, si famosam quis vxorem duxerit, aut libertinam senator.
units.tr: Sometimes they take nothing from each other. This is the case if they have contracted marriage against the Lex Iulia and the Lex Papia Poppaea: for example, if someone has married a woman of infamous reputation, or a senator has married a freedwoman.

units.la: Qui intra sexagesimum, vel quæ intra quinquagesimum annum neutri legi paruerit, licet ipsis legibus post hanc ætatem liberatus esset; perpetuis tamen pœnis tenebitur, ex senatusconsulto Perniciano. Sed Claudiano senatusconsulto maior sexagenario, si minorem quinquagenaria duxerit, perinde habebitur, ac si minor sexaginta annorum duxisset vxorem.
units.tr: A man who, before his sixtieth year, or a woman who, before her fiftieth year, has obeyed neither law, even though he or she would have been released from the laws themselves after that age, will nevertheless be liable to perpetual penalties under the Senatus consultum Pernicianum. But under the Senatus consultum Claudianum, a man over sixty who has married a woman under fifty is treated just as if a man under sixty had married a wife.

units.la: Quod si maior quinquagenaria minori sexagenario nupserit, impar matrimonium appellatur: & senatusconsulto Caluisiano iubetur non proficere ad capiendas hereditates, & legatas dotes. Itaque mortua muliere, dos caduca erit.
units.tr: But if a woman over fifty has married a man under sixty, the marriage is called unequal (impar matrimonium). By the Senatus consultum Calvisianum it is ordered that it does not avail for taking inheritances or legacies and dowries. Therefore, if the woman dies, the dowry will lapse (caducum).

units.la: Solidi] l. 6. ff. de vulgari. vid. sup. in epigraphe tit. 13.
units.tr: Solidi] Law 6, Digest, de vulgari. See above, in the heading of title 13.

units.la: Liberos exigit] Huc refer d. locum Tertullianic. 4. Apologet. Nonne vanissimæ leges Papiæ, quæ ante liberos suscipi cogunt, quam Iuliæ matrimonium contrahi?
units.tr: Liberos exigit] Refer here to the passage of Tertullian, Apologeticus 4. Are not the most vain are the laws of Papia, which compel people to have children before a marriage is contracted under the Julian law?

units.la: Ad sextum gradum] Nam à sexto gradu cognatio nulla est. §. vltim. de successione cognat. Paci hic.
units.tr: Ad sextum gradum] For from the sixth degree there is no kinship. Last paragraph, de successione cognatorum. Pacius here.

units.la: Ad sextum gradum ] vid. Instit. de success. cognat. in fine.
units.tr: Ad sextum gradum: see the Institutes, de successione cognatorum, at the end.

units.la: Abesset intra ] Lege, abest & intra. Credo hæc vera esse, si absit Reipubl. causa. Nam annus eis tantum dari solet, qui reipubl. causa abesse desierunt. Cuiac. & Pacius.
units.tr: Abesset intra] Read, abest & intra. I believe these things are true if he is absent for the sake of the commonwealth. For a year is usually granted only to those who have ceased to be absent on public business. Cuiacius & Pacius.

units.la: Si ius liberorum ] Isidorus, auctor sane vel eo nomine probandus, quod, vt ex hoc libello nonnulla, ita ex optimis auctoribus, quibus nunc destituti sumus, descripta quam plurima contineat. lib. v. ius, inquit, liberorum est coniugum sine liberis inuicem pro loco pignorum hereditatis alterna conscriptio, quam definitionem confirmat Novel. Valent. de testam. & l. valeat. C. Theodos. de infir. his quæ sub tyran. Et hoc quidem ius liberorum imperatores omnibus dant in l. 1. C. de iur. lib. Nec enim se ius trium dicunt, aut quatuor liberorum dare, sed ius liberorum: id nempe quod superius exposuimus, idemque coniuncta ea lege cum l. 2. C. de infir. pæn. ex qua ea l. pendet, vt perspici ex inscriptionibus & subscriptionibus potest, clarius demonstratur: alioquin superuacua est, constitutio Iustiniani de iure trium aut quatuor liberorum. l. 2. C. de iur. liber. Si igitur ius liberorum à principe impetrauerint, liberam inter se coniuges, vt Vlpianus noster ait, testamenti factionem habent. Denique vno filio filiaue communi superstite, aut vno filio 14. filiaue 12. annorum amisso amissaue, tribus post nonum diem amissis, duobus trimis amissis, vno cuiuscunque aetatis impubere amisso intra annum matrimonij & sex menses, idem ius habent.Cuiac. h. v. Duar. 1. diss. 40.
units.tr: Si ius liberorum] Isidore, an author certainly to be approved, if only for this reason: that, as he has described a good number of things from this little book, so he contains very many things taken from the best authors, whom we now lack. In book 5, he says: the right of children is the mutual conscription of spouses without children as the heirs of each other, in place of pledges; this definition is confirmed by Novel of Valentinian, de testamentis, and l. valeat, C. Theodosian, de infirmandis his quae sub tyrannis. And the emperors grant this right of children to everyone, in l. 1, C. de iure liberorum. For they do not say that they grant the right of three or four children, but the right of children, namely what we have set out above; and this is shown more clearly by the same law, joined with l. 2, C. de infirmandis poenis, on which that law depends, as can be seen from the inscriptions and subscriptions. Otherwise the constitution of Justinian on the right of three or four children would be superfluous, l. 2, C. de iure liberorum. If therefore they have obtained the right of children from the prince, the spouses have, as our Ulpian says, free testamentary capacity between themselves. Finally, if one common son or daughter survives, or one son of fourteen or daughter of twelve has died, or three after the ninth day, or two three-year-olds, or one prepubescent child of any age, within a year and six months of the marriage, they have the same right. Cuiacius, on this passage. Duaren, 1 Disputation, 40.

units.la: Intra decem menses ] l. 29. ff. de liberis. quinquagesimum annum non gignit. l. si sterilis in princ. de act. empt. in moribus non probatur: nam & sexagenarij idonei sunt ad generandum. Aristot. lib. 7. de generatione animalium Γεννᾶ δὲ ἄνθρωπος τὸ ἐχόμενον μέχρι ἐξηκονταετοῦς ἐτῶν ὁ ἄρρην, γυνὴ δὲ μέχρι πεντηκονταετοῦς. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Intra decem menses] l. 29, Digest, de liberis. does not beget in the fiftieth year. l. si sterilis in princ., de actionibus empti. This is not approved in custom; for even men of sixty are fit for begetting. Aristotle, book 7, On the Generation of Animals: "Man is productive up to sixty years of age, the male; the woman up to fifty." [Γεννᾶ δὲ ἄνθρωπος τὸ ἐχόμενον μέχρι ἐξηκονταετοῦς ἐτῶν ὁ ἄρρην, γυνὴ δὲ μέχρι πεντηκονταετοῦς.] Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Licet ipsis legibus ] Augustin. 3. contra Iul. Iure etiam fuit constitutum, ne quisquam ius liberorum haberet, nisi cum amborum anni computati & simul ducti, centum non transisse docerentur. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Licet ipsis legibus] Augustine, 3 Contra Julianum. By law it was also established that no one should have the right of children unless it was shown that the years of both, counted together and added, did not exceed one hundred. Cuiacius, here.

units.la: Maior sexagenario ] Lege Iulia, si maior sexagenario, aut maior quinquagenaria, nuptias contraxissent, ius ab extraneo testamento capiendi amittebant: quasi operam matrimonio dare non possent. l. 15. §. 2 ff. de adopt. Lactant. 1. Quid ergo est, quare apud poetas salacissimus Jupiter desierit liberos tollere? Utrum sexagenarius factus est; & illi lex Papia fibulam imposuit? an impetrauit ius trium liberorum? & Apuleio 2. Apologet. in iudicio obiectum, quod Pudentilla ei anno aetatis 60. ad libidinem nupsisset. Hodie maior sexagenario minorem quinquagenaria ducere potest. l. 27. C. de nupt. l. 12. C. de legit. hared. adde Suetonium in Claudio c. 23. Goth. hic.
units.tr: Maior sexagenario] By the Lex Iulia, if a man over sixty, or a woman over fifty, had contracted marriage, they lost the right to take by testament from a stranger, as if they were unable to devote themselves to marriage. l. 15, §2, Digest, de adoptionibus.
