But if he has neither made cretio nor acted as heir, he is himself excluded, and the substitute becomes heir to the whole estate.

units.la: Testamenti factionem ] l. 52. ff. de hered in- stituendis.
units.tr: "Testamentary capacity": see Dig. 28.5.52, de heredibus instituendis.

units.la: Quia Peregrinus est ] Ex his quæ diximus in tit. XVII. apparet, ita hunc locum emendariportere, quia peregrinus est, cum quo testamenti factio non est. Latinus Iulianus siquidem mortis, &c. Nam cum Latino proculdubio testamenti factio est: alioquin nec si intra diem cretionis ciuis Romanus fiat, recte hæres instituitur §. in extraneis de hared. qual. & diff. aut Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: "Because he is a foreigner": from what we have said under title XVII, it appears that this passage should be emended to read "because he is a foreigner, with whom there is no testamentary capacity. For with a Latin, undoubtedly, there is testamentary capacity; otherwise, not even if he becomes a Roman citizen within the day of cretio is he rightly instituted heir." See in extraneis, de hared. qual. & diff. or Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Quia peregrinus ] Peregrinus institui non potest, vt hic, sed nec instituere. tit. 20. §. 14. supr. eod.
units.tr: Because he is a foreigner ] A foreigner cannot be instituted heir, as here, nor can he institute one. tit. 20. §. 14. supr. eod.

units.la: Latinus Iunianus ] d. § 14.
units.tr: Latinus Junianus ] d. § 14.

units.la: Intra diem cretionis ] §. 4. Institut. de hæred. qualitate.
units.tr: Within the day of cretion ] §. 4. Institut. de hæred. qualitate.

units.la: In persona cœlibis ] vid. tit. 14. 15. 16, supr. eod.
units.tr: In the person of a celibate ] see tit. 14, 15, 16, supr. eod.

units.la: Incerta persona ] §. 25. Instit. de legat. l. 69. §. 4. ff. de iure dot. Paul. 3. sentent. 6. §. 13.
units.tr: Uncertain person ] §. 25. Instit. de legat.; l. 69. §. 4. ff. de iure dot.; Paul. 3. sentent. 6. §. 13.

units.la: Nec municipia nec municipes ] Plinius lib. 5. Epistol. nec hæredem instituii nec præcipere posse, Remp. constat. Pac. hic & Cuiac.
units.tr: Neither municipalities nor their members ] Pliny, lib. 5, Epistles, it is agreed that the state can neither institute nor be instituted heir. Pac. here and Cuiac.

units.la: Hæredes institui possunt ] poterit tamen eis legari. v. l. 122 ff. de legat. 1 l. 1. §. 5 ff. ad l. Falcid.
units.tr: Can be instituted heirs ] Yet a legacy may be left to them. see l. 122 ff. de legat.; l. 1. §. 5 ff. ad l. Falcid.

units.la: Incertum corpus ] ratio petita ex §. 4. supr. eodem.
units.tr: An uncertain body ] The reason is taken from §. 4. supr. eodem.

units.la: Neque pro libito de hærede cernere ] videtur legendum, neque pro hærede gerere: nam aut cretione aut pro hærede gestione hæredes fiunt vid. Cuiac. & Pacium hic.
units.tr: Nor may one take up the inheritance at will ] It seems we should read: nor may one act as heir; for heirs become such either by cretion or by acting as heir. See Cuiac. and Pacius here.

units.la: Senatusconsulto tamen ] leg. 1. de libert. univers.
units.tr: By senatus consultum, however ] l. 1. de libert. univers.

units.la: Restitui potest ] l. 26. ff. de negociis l. 26. ff. ad Trebell.
units.tr: May be restored ] l. 26. ff. de negociis; l. 26. ff. ad Trebell.

units.la: Idque hoc S. C. ] Aproniano, quod factum est temporibus D. Marci l. omnibus ad Trebel.
units.tr: And this by the senatus consultum ] The Aproniaan, which was made in the time of the divine Marcus; l. omnibus ad Trebel.

units.la: Deos haredes instituere non possumus ] Deo tamen relinqui potuit. l. 5. §. 12. ff. de donat. inter virum l. 1. §. 5. ff. ad l. Fald. Paul. 4. sentent. 3. §. 7. Quemadmodum & apud Christianos Christus institui potest. leg. 26. C. de sacrosanct. ecclesiis. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: We cannot institute gods as heirs ] Yet something may be left to a god. l. 5. §. 12. ff. de donat. inter virum; l. 1. §. 5. ff. ad l. Falcid.; Paul. 4. sentent. 3. §. 7. Just as among Christians Christ may be instituted. leg. 26. C. de sacrosanct. ecclesiis. Gothofredus here.

units.la: Sicuti Iouem Tarpeium ] Ita dictus a Tarpeio monte. Tarpeius autem appellatus fuit a Tarpeia virgine vestali a Sabinis necata, ibique sepulta. Antea Saturnius mons, & in eo oppidum Saturnium, unde Saturnia terra. Postremo mons Capitolinus dictus, quod cum fundamenta foderentur aedis Iouis, caput humanum inuentum fuit. Varro 4. de lingua. vid. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Like Jupiter Tarpeius ] So called from the Tarpeian rock. Tarpeius, moreover, was named after Tarpeia, a Vestal virgin, killed by the Sabines and buried there. Earlier it was the Saturnian mount, and on it the town of Saturnium, whence the land of Saturnia. Finally it was called the Capitoline mount, because when the foundations of Jupiter's temple were being dug, a human head was found. Varro, book 4, On the Latin language. See Gothofredus here.

units.la: Apollinem Didymaeum ] Apollinis templum & oraculum quod Didymis fuit antiquum. Pausanias 7. in Achaicis, eiusdem facit mentionem in 2. seu Corinthiacis. Adde Strabonem 9. & 11. Goth. ibid.
units.tr: Apollo of Didyma ] The temple and oracle of Apollo, which was ancient at Didyma. Pausanias, book 7, in the Achaica; he makes mention of it also in book 2, or Corinthiaca. Add Strabo, books 9 and 11. Gothofredus, ibid.

units.la: Martem in Gallia ] Galli quondam Mercurium coluere maxime, post hunc Apollinem, & Martem & Iouem & Mineruam. Martem bella regere. Marti, cum proelio dimicare constituissent, ea quae bello coepissent plerunque deuouebant: quae supererant animalia capra, immolabant, reliquas res in unum locum con-
units.tr: Mars in Gaul ] The Gauls of old worshipped Mercury most of all, after him Apollo, Mars, Jupiter and Minerva. Mars rules wars. When they had resolved to fight a battle with Mars, they usually devoted to him the things they had gained in war; the animals that remained they sacrificed, and the other things they gathered into one place

units.la: cf. Gothofr. hic. conferebant.vid. Cæsar. 6. de bello Gallico.
units.tr: see Gothofredus here. they heaped together. See Caesar, book 6, on the Gallic War.

units.la: Minervam Melien(em ] Melitensem, aut à Melio vrbe non procul ab Euphrate. Cuiac. Paci.
units.tr: Minerva of Melis ] Either Melitensis, or from Melis, a town not far from the Euphrates. Cuiac. Pacius.

units.la: Herculem Gaditanum ] de Gadibus & Herc-ule vid. Strabonem 3. in sin. fuit & alius cognomento Gallus & Ogmius, de quo Lucianus in Hercule.
units.tr: Hercules of Gades ] On Gades and Hercules, see Strabo, book 3, near the end. There was also another, surnamed Gallus and Ogmius, of whom Lucian speaks in Hercules.

units.la: Dianam Ephesiam ] vid. act. 19. verf. 26, 27. de templo Dianæ Euseb. 36. Plin. 14.
units.tr: Diana of Ephesus ] See Acts 19, verses 26, 27. On the temple of Diana, Eusebius 36; Pliny 14.

units.la: Et Cœlestum Salinensem] Tertull. 23. Apolog. Vnicuique, inquit, etiam prouinciæ & ciuitati suus Deus est, vt Syriæ Astartis, vt Arabiæ Diasares, vt Norico Tibelenus, vt Africæ Cœlestus, vt Mauritaniæ reguli sui. & post. Crustuminensium Delventinus, Narniensium Viridianus, Asculanorum Ancaria, Volsiniensium Nursia, Otriculanorum Valentia, Sutrinorum Nortia, Faliscorum Iuno Curilis, & pater Curis. Sed nos soliarcemur à religionis proprietate. Hæc ille. Cui loco visum illud Arnobij 8. adiungere, inde adeo per vniuersa imperia, prouincias, oppida, videmus singulos sacrorum ritus gentiles habere, & Deos colere municipes, vt Eleusinos Cererem, Phrygas Magnam matrem, Epidaurios Æsculapium, Caldæos Belum, Assartem Syros, Dianam Tauros, Gallos Mercurium, vniuersa Romanos. Porro quis fuerit Cœlestus, an Deus, an Dea, ambigitur. Petrus Pitheus 1. aduersf. 4. Deam fuisse ait. Ammianus lib. 22. Asclepiades Philosophus cum visendi gratia Iuliani ad id suburbanum venisset, deæ Cœlestis argenteum breue sigmentum quocunque ibat secum solitus efferre, ante pedes statuit simulachri sublimes, accensisque cereis ex visu, fecit. Philastrius Brixiensis in catalogo hæresi. Alia, inquit, hæresis in Iudæis, quæ Reginam, quam & Fortunam cœli nuncupant, quam & Cœlestem vocant in Africa. Tertull. in Apologet. 29. Ista ipsa virgo Cœlestis, pluuiarum pollicitatrix. Saluianus de Gubernatione, Cœlestis illa. Idem 8. de prouidentia. Apul. 4. Floridor. Carthago Africæ Musa Cœlestis. ut non iniusta ratione possis dicere legendum esse apud Tertullianum in libro de virginibus; Cœlestis Africæ, non Ceres. Ambros. 1. epist. ad Valent. vid. Gothofr. Cuiac. Pacium hic. &c.
units.tr: And Caelestus of Salinae ] Tertullian, Apology 23. Every province and city, he says, has its own god: Astarte for Syria, Diasares for Arabia, Tibelenus for Noricum, Caelestus for Africa, and its petty kings for Mauritania. And afterwards: Delventinus for the Crustuminians, Viridianus for the Narnians, Ancaria for the Asculans, Nursia for the Volsinians, Valentia for the Otriculans, Nortia for the Sutrians, Juno Curilis and father Curis for the Faliscans. But we are spared the peculiarities of religion. So he. To this passage I thought to add that of Arnobius, book 8: from this we see that throughout all empires, provinces and towns individual peoples have their own rites of worship and honour gods as their local patrons, as the Eleusinians Ceres, the Phrygians the Great Mother, the Epidaurians Aesculapius, the Chaldeans Belus, the Assyrians Astarte, the Syrians the Dea, the Taurians Diana, the Gauls Mercury, and all things the Romans. Moreover, it is uncertain who Caelestus was, whether a god or a goddess. Petrus Pithoeus, 1. adversaria 4. says she was a goddess. Ammianus, book 22: when the philosopher Asclepiades came to that suburb to see Julian, he set before the feet of the lofty image of the goddess Caelestis a small silver figure which he habitually carried with him wherever he went, and having lit candles according to the custom, made a sacrifice. Philastrius of Brescia, in his catalogue of heresies: another heresy, he says, is among the Jews, who call the Queen, whom they also name Fortune of heaven, and whom they call Caelestis in Africa. Tertullian, Apology 29. That very virgin Caelestis, promiser of rains. Salvian, On the Governance of God: that Caelestis. The same, On Providence, book 8. Apuleius, Florida 4: Carthage, the Muse Caelestis of Africa. So one may reasonably say that in Tertullian's book on virgins one should read "Caelestis of Africa," not "Ceres." Ambrose, epistle 1 to Valentinian. See Gothofredus, Cuiac., Pacius here, etc.

units.la: Cum libertate ] Hodie etiam sine libertate instituere possumus. Inst. de hæred. instituend. l. penult. C. de necessariis.
units.tr: With freedom ] Today we may also institute someone without freedom. Inst. de hæred. instituend.; l. penult. C. de necessariis.

units.la: Cum libertate vel sine libertate ] si cum libertate socio adcrescit: si sine libertate, seruus communis est hæredis & socii. l. verum §. si seruum. pro socio. §. 9. l. 49. ad l. Falcid. Paul. 3. sent. 6. §. 4. Cuiac. Ad hereditatem capiendam ] nisi intra dies cretionis ciuis Romanus fiat.
units.tr: With or without freedom ] If with freedom, he accrues to the co-heir; if without freedom, the slave is common to the heir and the co-heir. l. verum §. si seruum. pro socio; §. 9. l. 49. ad l. Falcid.; Paul. 3. sent. 6. §. 4. Cuiac. To take up the inheritance ] unless within the days of cretion he becomes a Roman citizen.

units.la: Eos tamen quorum cum dominis ] si cum domino est testamenti factio, est & cum seruo: vice versa, si cum domino non est testamenti factio, nec item est cum seruo l. seruus hereditarius. l. non minus. de hered. instit. Caeterum ex persona serui id quod relinquitur, valet, id est, si ei libero relictum valeat. Ex quo efficitur, vt seruo legari non possit seruitus ad fundum domini. l. etsi maxime. de seruitut. leg. contra vt ei possit legari res domini, quamuis res sua domino legari non possit. l. debitor. §. seruo. de leg. 2. vide Goth. hic.
units.tr: Those, however, with whose masters ] If there is testamentary capacity with the master, there is also with the slave; conversely, if there is no testamentary capacity with the master, neither is there with the slave. l. seruus hereditarius; l. non minus. de hered. instit. Moreover, from the slave's person what is left is valid, that is, if it would be valid to leave it to a free person. From this it follows that a servitude over the master's estate cannot be left to a slave; on the other hand, the master's property can be left to the slave, although the master's own property cannot be left to him. l. debitor. §. seruo. de leg. 2; see Gothofredus here.

units.la: Siquidem ] §. 2. Inst. de hered. inst.
units.tr: Since indeed ] §. 2. Inst. de hered. inst.

units.la: Quod si ab ipso testatore ] Alienatione, manumissione libertas revocatur, non hereditas: cui rei non obstat regula l. si ita scriptum de lib. & posthum. talis namque est: seruo cum libertate ex asse herede instituto, libertatem seruo eodem testamento a semetipso adimi non posse, vt in l. sed & si conditioni in sin. de hered. instit. Ibidem scriptum est, hereditatem adimi non posse, quod falsum est, at lego, Qua constitutum est, libertatem. In libertatis & hereditatis nominibus saepius legum auctores errare contingit. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: But if by the testator himself ] Liberty, not the inheritance, is revoked by alienation or manumission; the rule l. si ita scriptum de lib. et posthum. does not stand in the way of this. For its wording is: where a slave with freedom has been instituted heir to the whole estate, the same will cannot take away his freedom by the testator's own act, as in l. sed & si conditioni in sin. de hered. instit. In the same place it is written that the inheritance cannot be taken away, which is false; but I read, "by which it is established, freedom." It often happens that the authors of the laws err in the terms "freedom" and "inheritance." Cuiac. here.

units.la: Vel alienatus sit ] Haec verba, vel alienatus, desiderantur apud Iustinianum §. 1. verf. si vero à vino testatore. Inst. de hared. instituend.
units.tr: Or has been alienated ] These words, "or alienated," are wanting in Justinian, §. 1, verse "si vero a vivo testatore," Inst. de hered. instituend.

units.la: ] Hodie constat ex constitutione Iustiniani l. penult. C. de necessariis.
units.tr: ] Today it is established by a constitution of Justinian, l. penult. C. de necessariis.

units.la: ] d. §. 1. verf. alienus quoque.
units.tr: ] The said §. 1, verse "alienus quoque."

units.la: ] l. 1. ff. de hared. inst. Instit. de exhæredat. liberor.
units.tr: ] l. 1. ff. de hered. inst.; Instit. de exheredat. liberorum.

units.la: ] Hi sunt sui naturales, reliqui sui non naturales, vt inf. tit. vlt. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: ] These are natural sui heredes; the others are non-natural sui heredes, as below, tit. last. Cuiac. and Pacius here.

units.la: ] Caius tertio Inst. apud Ruffinum tit. 16. Vxor inquit, quæ in manu eius est, Is sua hæres est: quia filiæ loco est: Item nurus quæ in filij manu est, nam & hæc neptis loco est. Sed ita demum erit sua hæres, si filius cuius in manu erit, dum pater moritur, in potestate eius non sit. Idemque dicimus & de ea, quæ in neporis manu matrimonij causa sit, quia proneptris loco est. Goth. h.
units.tr: ] Gaius, book 3, Institutes, as preserved by Rufinus, title 16: a wife, he says, who is in her husband's hand, he is her sua hæres, because she stands in the place of a daughter; likewise a daughter-in-law who is in her son's hand, for she too stands in the place of a granddaughter. But she will be a sua hæres only if the son in whose hand she is is not in his father's power at the time the father dies. And we say the same of one who is in her grandson's hand for the sake of marriage, because she stands in the place of a great-granddaughter. Gothofredus here.

units.la: ] Posthumi quoque qui si vivo patre nati essent, in potestate eius futuri forent, sui hæredes sunt Caius d. loc.
units.tr: ] Posthumous children too, who, had they been born while their father was alive, would have been in his power, are sui heredes. Caius d. loc.

units.la: ] Legendum est, sed scriptis eo sensu: iure antiquo, filiarum nepotes, prætereiri potuisse, sed nec testamentum ex causa prætereritionis infirmasse, cum illis consultum ita foret. Nam scriptis concurrebant: suis quidem in virilem: extraneis in dimidiam. Et hoc est, quod à Triboniano obscure scriptum ptum est, ius adcrescendi eis ad certam portionem præstitum. Inst. de exhæred. liber. vers. sed non ita vid. Goth. hic.
units.tr: ] The text should be read thus, but understood in this sense: under the old law, the grandchildren through daughters could be passed over, yet the will was not invalidated on the ground of their being passed over, since provision was made for them in that way. For the written heirs competed: with the sui in equal shares, with outsiders in a half. This is what Tribonian wrote obscurely, that the right of accrual was granted to them up to a fixed portion. Inst. de exhæred. liber. vers. sed non ita; vid. Goth. hic.

units.la: Posthumi quoque liberi cuiuscunque ] In natis differentia est sexus & personarum, in posthumis non item. Denique omnes posthumi præteriti si nascantur rumpunt, filij statim ab initio iniustum faciunt: utrunque fit iure ciuili: iure prætorio utrisque datur contra tabulas. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Posthumi quoque liberi cuiuscunque] In children there is a difference of sex and of persons; in posthumous children there is not. Indeed, if all posthumous children who were passed over are born, they break the will; the sons make it unjust from the very beginning. Both things happen by civil law; by praetorian law both are given the action against the tablets. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.

units.la: Posthumi quoque liberi cuiuscunque] Vt in eo par sit masculorum & fœminarum conditio. §. 1. Inst. de exhæredat. liberor.
units.tr: Posthumi quoque liberi cuiuscunque] So that in this respect the condition of males and females is equal. §. 1. Inst. de exhæredat. liberor.

units.la: Rumpitur ] legendum, rumpunt.
units.tr: Rumpitur] Read rumpunt.

units.la: Eos qui in utero ] Posthumi sui sunt, qui post mortem, aut post testamentum sui nascuntur, vel quasi nascuntur: nati post mortem ex iure antiquo instituuntur, nati post testamentum ex iure novo, id est, l. Iulia Vellea. De his qui quasi nascuntur non est quæstio an institui possint, quia nati sunt tempore testamenti, de quibus lex Iulia tractat in 2. cap. at nati non sui post testamentum, succedentes tamen in locum sui, moribus institui possunt, id est, ex Iuliani sententia. l. Gallus de liber. & posthum. Posthumi alieni, iure ciuili, id est, xii. tab. institui non possunt, sed neque eis legari potest: iure prætorio institui possunt: iure prætorio legata capere non possunt, quia prætori curæ legata gata non fuere: at fideicommissa capere possunt: ex Iustiniani constitutione cum eis, quasi ex iure ciuili, testamenti factio est. Haec vero breuia ita absoluta sunt: Ait Cuiac. hic. posthumi haeredes instituti possunt: leg. 4. l. 5. l. 24. l. 27. l. 29. ff. de liber. & posthumis.
units.tr: Eos qui in utero] Posthumous sui are those who are born after the death or after the will of the sui, or who are as it were born: those born after death were instituted under the old law, those born after the will under the new law, that is, the lex Iulia Vellea. About those who are as it were born there is no question whether they can be instituted, since they were born at the time of the will, of whom the Lex Iulia treats in cap. 2. But those born after the will who are not sui, yet succeed in the place of the sui, can be instituted by custom, that is, according to Julian's opinion. l. Gallus de liber. & posthum. Posthumous children of others cannot be instituted under civil law, that is, the Twelve Tables, nor can anything be bequeathed to them; under praetorian law they can be instituted; under praetorian law they cannot take legacies, since legacies were not a concern of the praetor; but they can take fideicommissa, since by Justinian's constitution they have testamentary capacity as if under civil law. These matters are summarised briefly thus: Cuiacius here says that posthumous heirs can be instituted. l. 4, l. 5, l. 24, l. 27, l. 29 ff. de liber. & posthumis.

units.la: Si quidem post mortem ] Duae posthumorum species: Alij enim post mortem testatoris nascuntur: alij post testamentum viuo testatore: l. 3. §. 2. ff. de iniusto.
units.tr: Si quidem post mortem] There are two kinds of posthumous children: some are born after the death of the testator, others after the will while the testator is still alive. l. 3. §. 2. ff. de iniusto.

units.la: Ex iure ciuili ] id est, legibus 12. tabular. quod ius antiquum a Scaeuola dicitur in l. 29. §. 7. ff. de liber. & posthum. Habita ratione ad l. Velleam: vide Gothofred. hic:
units.tr: Ex iure ciuili] that is, by the laws of the Twelve Tables, which old law Scaevola calls such in l. 29. §. 7. ff. de liber. & posthum. Taking into account the lex Velleia: see Gothofredus here.

units.la: Ex l. Iulia ] Vellea scilicet §. 2. Inst. de exhaered. liber: l. 29 ff. de liberis:
units.tr: Ex l. Iulia] Namely the Vellean law. §. 2. Inst. de exhaered. liber; l. 29 ff. de liberis.

units.la: Aut inter caeteros ] Inst. de exhared. lib. vers. sed non ita, in sin. Inter caeteros exhaeredare; est ἀορίστως siue indefinite exhaeredare: Fuit autem haec formula, Caeteri exhaeredes sunto: Theoph. Inst. de exhaeredat. lib: l. 23. ff. de liberis, & opponitur Inter caeteros exhaeredatio et quae nominatim fit. §. 1. inf. eod. Nominatim exhaeredatio longe diuersa ab indefinita, & generali exhaeredatione, de qua vid. l. 2. 3. ff. de liber: vt Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Aut inter caeteros] Inst. de exhared. lib. vers. sed non ita, in fin. To disinherit among the others is indefinitely [ἀορίστως], that is, to disinherit without definition. The formula was: "let the other heirs be disinherited." Theoph. Inst. de exhaeredat. lib.; l. 23 ff. de liberis. It is opposed to disinheritance that is made by name. §. 1. inf. eod. Disinheritance by name is far different from indefinite and general disinheritance, on which see l. 2, 3 ff. de liber.; as Gothofredus here.

units.la: Sed tutius est ] Ergo posthumae foeminae inter caeteros cum adiectione legati, ne per obliuionem omissae videantur: posthumi mares culus cuiuscunque gradus nominatim. §. posthumi quoque de exheredat. liber. superstites, præter filium, inter cæteros sine adiectione legari, quia superstitum non æque obliuiscimur. Sed hæc Iustinianus emendauit. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Sed tutius est] Therefore posthumous daughters should be included among the others with the addition of a legacy, lest they seem to have been left out through forgetfulness; posthumous sons of whatever degree should be named individually. §. posthumi quoque de exheredat. liber. Surviving sons, apart from the son, may be left among the others without addition, since we do not forget survivors so easily. But Justinian corrected these things. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Mancipatos ] Emancipati, & mancipati recte dicuntur: sed mancipari nomen in malam partem accipi potest. Plinius libr. 4. Epist. Filium regulus emancipauit, vt hæres matris exifteret. Mancipatum ( ita vulgo ex moribus hominis loquebantur ) fœda & insolita parentibus indulgentiæ simulatione captabat. Cuiac. & Pac. hic.
units.tr: Mancipatos] "Emancipati" and "mancipati" are rightly said, but the word mancipari can be taken in a bad sense. Pliny, book 4 of the Letters: "Regulus emancipated his son so that he might become his mother's heir." A mancipatus (so people commonly spoke, from the custom of the man) caught at his parents' affection with a foul and unusual pretence of indulgence. Cuiac. & Pac. hic.

units.la: Inter necessarios ] sui beneficium abstentionis habent: necessarij beneficium separationis, abstentionis non æque. Separatio facit, vt ne væneant quæ postea sibi hæres adquisierit; abstentio, vt ne sit hæredis loco. Goth.b.
units.tr: Inter necessarios] The sui have the benefit of abstention; necessary heirs have the benefit of separation, not equally of abstention. Separation ensures that goods the heir later acquires may not be sold for his debts; abstention ensures that he is not in the position of an heir. Goth. b.

units.la: A parentis hæreditate permittitur] §. 2. vers. sed hic prætor. Inst. de exher. lib.
units.tr: It is permitted to refuse a parent's inheritance ] §. 2. vers. sed hic prætor. Inst. de exher. lib.

units.la: Cum cretione ] id vt fiat vid. §. 27 inf.
units.tr: Cum cretione] On how this comes about, see §. 27 below.

units.la: Pro hærede ] vid. l. 20. ff. de acquir. hared.
units.tr: Pro hærede] See l. 20 ff. de acquir. hared.

units.la: Actionem ] id est, auctionem vid. l. 2. in sin. ff. de collat. bonor. l. 48. ff. de vsurp. leg. 2. §. 8. ff. pro emptore.
units.tr: Actionem ] that is, an auction; see l. 2 in fin. ff. de collat. bonor., l. 48 ff. de usurp. leg., l. 2 §. 8 ff. pro emptore.

units.la: - Cretio est ] Hæreditas acquiritur cretione, aditione, pro hærede geritione, immixtione, agnitione. Cretio, est eorum qui sub cretione hæredes instituuntur. Pro hærede geritio, eorum corum qui sine cretione, vel etiam cum cretione imperfecta, ex constitutione D. Marci Immixtio est necessariorum & suorum. Agnitio nuda hodie & in vsu, tam in ciuili, quam in praetorio iure. §. vlt. de haered. qual. & differ. §. vlt. de bon. poss. Sublata est cretio à Constantino in maternis successionibus. l. 1. C. Theod. de matern. bon. & mat. gen. cret. sub. à Theodosio penitus. l. cretionum C. de iur. deliberandi. leg. 1. C. Theodos. de cret. vel bon. poss. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Cretio est] An inheritance is acquired by cretion, adition, conduct as heir, intermeddling, or acknowledgement. Cretion belongs to those instituted heirs under cretion. Conduct as heir belongs to those who take without cretion, or even with an imperfect cretion, by the constitution of the Divine Marcus. Intermeddling belongs to necessary and own heirs. Acknowledgement is bare, and today in use both in civil and in praetorian law. §. vlt. de haered. qual. & differ. §. vlt. de bon. poss. Cretion was abolished by Constantine in maternal successions. l. 1 C. Theod. de matern. bon. & mat. gen. cret. sub. It was wholly abolished by Theodosius. l. cretionum C. de iur. deliberandi; leg. 1 C. Theodos. de cret. vel bon. poss. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Sic Varro interpretatur in lib. 5. de lingua Latin. Itaque inquit, in cretione iubent adhiberi testes.
units.tr: So Varro explains it in book 5 of On the Latin Language: "Thus," he says, "in cretion they order witnesses to be present."

units.la: sunt igitur vtiles dies, non continui. l. 2. quis ord. in bon. poss. ser. Inde M. Tullius lib. 1. de oratore de his, credo, rebus, inquit Crassus, vt in cretionibus scribi solet, quibus sciam poteroque. quem foelicitèr nobis locum Francisc. Hotoman. emendauit, vir ingenij probi & recti. Et similis error in lib. Gratiani, can. ius Quiritium 1. dist. vbi loco horum verborum, vel curationibus, vel de contractibus, scribendum est, vel cretionibus. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Therefore the days are useful, not continuous. l. 2 quis ord. in bon. poss. ser. Hence M. Tullius, book 1 De oratore: "About these things, I believe," says Crassus, "as is usually written in cretions, by which I may know and be able." Francis Hotman has happily emended this passage, a man of upright and honest talent. A similar error occurs in Gratian's book, can. ius Quiritium, dist. 1, where instead of these words, "or by curations, or about contracts," one must write "or cretions." Cuiac. hic.

units.la: In suo, aut emancipato haerede non scripto exhaeredatio valet, quia hic praetorio, ille ciuili iure haeres est: in extraneo. heo hærede non scripto exhæredatio inanis est l. quidam de verb. oblig. l. non putauit. §. si quis e-mancipatum de bon. poss. contrab. in scripto valet, vt in hac formula, & in l. paterfam. de hæred. instit. l. Seius ad l. Falcid. l. uxorem §. hæres de legar. 3. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: In the case of a suus or emancipated heir who is not instituted, disinheritance is valid, since the former is heir under praetorian law and the latter under civil law. In the case of an outsider who is not instituted, disinheritance is void. If he is instituted, it is valid, as in this formula. l. quidam de verb. oblig.; l. non putavit; §. si quis emancipatum de bon. poss. contrab.; l. paterfam. de hered. instit.; l. Seius ad l. Falcid.; l. uxorem §. hæres de legar. 3. Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Cernere est] Cernere est quasi decernere, se hæredem esse velle. l. 13. §. penult. ff. de adquir. hereditat.
units.tr: Cernere est] To cern is as it were to decide, that is, to wish to be heir. l. 13 §. penult. ff. de adquir. hereditat.

units.la: Ad hunc modum] Formula cernendi. Huius loci vestigia sunt apud Varronem 5. de lingua. In cretione adhiberi iubet testes, & lib. 6. Hæres cum constituit se hæredem esse, dicitur cernere: & cum id fecerit, creuisse. Varroni respondet Cicero 13. ad Atticum, Cretionem fieri testibus præsentibus. Fiebat etiam verbis solennibus, vt hic: & l. 51. in sin. ff. de adquirend. hæredit. pure fit: Est enim actus legitimus. l. 77. de reg. iur. & semel l. 80. sin. de acquir. hæred. non per alium l. 90. ff. de adquir. hæredit. Eius symbolum, digitorum percussio vid. Goth. ad epigraphen tit. de verb. oblig. & hic.
units.tr: Ad hunc modum] The formula of cerning. Traces of this passage are found in Varro, book 5 De lingua, where he orders witnesses to be present at cretion, and book 6: "When an heir declares that he is heir, he is said to cern; and when he has done this, he is said to have cerned." Cicero answers Varro in book 13 to Atticus: cretion is made with witnesses present. It was also done with solemn words, as here; and l. 51 in fin. ff. de adquirend. hæredit. It is done purely, since it is a legitimate act. l. 77 de reg. iur. and once only, l. 80 in fin. de acquir. hared. and not through another, l. 90 ff. de adquir. hæredit. Its symbol is the striking of the fingers. See Goth. on the heading tit. de verb. oblig. and here.

units.la: Non aliter] dixi superius, sublatam cretionis scrupulositatem. l. 17. C. de iur. deliberandi.
units.tr: Non aliter] I have said above that the scrupulous strictness of cretio has been removed. l. 17. C. de iur. deliberandi.

units.la: Vulgaris] Legitima, & vtilis, de cuius effectu vid. §. 32. in sin. inf. eod.
units.tr: Vulgaris] Legitimate and effective; on its effect see §. 32. at the end below, same title.

units.la: Continua] Et hoc ideo quod in institutione vulgari cretionis hæc verba adiunguntur, quibus scieris poterisque §. 27. & 31. sup. eod. §. 34. inf. eod.
units.tr: Continua] And this is so because in a vulgar institution of cretio these words are added: "by which you shall know and be able" (quibus scieris poterisque), see §. 27 and 31 above, same title; §. 34 below, same title.

units.la: Quibus ignorauit ] In continua cretione dies currunt ignoranti: in vulgari non currunt.
units.tr: Quibus ignorauit] In continuous cretio the days run against one who is ignorant; in vulgar cretio they do not run.

units.la: Aut instituti ] l.1. ff. de vulgari & pupill. Paul. 3. sent. 4. §. 27.
units.tr: Aut instituti] l. 1. ff. de vulgari & pupill.; Paul. 3. sent. 4. §. 27.

units.la: Veluti ] Formula haeredis scribendi.
units.tr: Veluti] The formula for writing an heir.

units.la: Sub imperfectam ] Imperfecta cretio, quoties non expressim exhaeredatur, sed alius eius loco instituitur.
units.tr: Sub imperfectam] Imperfect cretio occurs whenever the heir is not expressly disinherited, but another is instituted in his place.

units.la: His verbis ] Formula perfectae cretionis.
units.tr: His verbis] The formula of perfect cretio.

units.la: Sed sista ] Formula imperfectae cretionis.
units.tr: Sed sista] The formula of imperfect cretio.

units.la: Non cernendo autem ] Nota veterem differentiam cernendi, & pro haerede gerendi. Qui cernebat, excludebat inferiorem: qui pro haerede gerebat, in partem admittebat substitutum.
units.tr: Non cernendo autem] Note the old distinction between cernere and pro herede gerere. He who made cretio (cernebat) excluded the inferior heir; he who acted as heir (pro herede gerebat) admitted the substitute to a share.

units.la: Ex asse ] Qui pro haerede gerit ex asse fit haeres.
units.tr: Ex asse] He who acts as heir (pro herede gerit) becomes heir to the whole estate.

units.la: Tit. XXIII. Quemadmodum Testa- menta rumpuntur.
units.tr: Title XXIII. How Wills Are Broken.

units.la: TEstamentum iure factum infirmatur duobus modis, si ruptum, aut irritum factum sit.
units.tr: A will made in due form of law is invalidated in two ways: if it is broken, or if it is made void.

units.la: Rumpitur testamentum mutatione, id est, si postea aliud testamentum iure factum sit: item agnatione, id est, si suus heres agnascatur, qui neq; heres institutus, neque vt oportet, exheredatus sit.
units.tr: A will is broken by a later change, that is, if another will validly made afterwards exists. Likewise by the birth of a child, that is, if a suus heres is born who was neither instituted heir nor properly disinherited.

units.la: Adnascitur suus heres, aut agnascendo, aut adoptando, aut in manum conueniendo, aut in locum sui heredis succedendo: velut nepos mortuo filio, vel emancipato: aut manumissione, id est, si filius ex prima secundave mancipatione manumissus, reuersus sit in patris potestatem.
units.tr: A suus heres is added either by being born, by adoption, by coming into the hand of the husband, or by succeeding into the place of a suus heres, as when a grandson is born after his father has died or been emancipated. Or by manumission, that is, if a son manumitted after the first or second mancipation returns into his father's power.

units.la: Irritum fit testamentum, si testator capite deminutus fuerit, aut si iure facto testamento nemo extiterit heres.
units.tr: A will becomes void if the testator suffers loss of status (capitis deminutio), or if, although a will was validly made, no one comes forward as heir.

units.la: Si is qui testamentum fecit, ab hostibus captus sit, testamentum eius valet: siquidem reuersus fuerit, iure postliminij: si non ibi decesserit, ex lege Corneliana, quæ perinde successionem eius confirmat, atque si in ciuitate decessisset.
units.tr: If the person who made a will is taken by the enemy, his will remains valid. If he returns, this is by the law of postliminy; if he dies there, the Cornelian law applies, which confirms the succession just as if he had died within the city.

units.la: Si septem signis testium signatum sit testamentum, licet iure ciuili ruptum vel irritum factum sit, Prætor scriptis heredibus iuxta tabulas bonorum possessionem dat, si testator & ciuis Romanus, & suæ potestatis cum moreretur fuit, quæ bonorum possessio cum re, id est, cum effectu habetur, si nemo alius iure heres sit.
units.tr: If a will was sealed with the seals of seven witnesses, then even though it has been broken or made void by the civil law, the Praetor grants possession of the goods according to the tablets to the written heirs, provided the testator was a Roman citizen and was under his own power when he died. This possession of goods is held to be effective (cum re), that is, to have effect, if no one else is heir by law.

units.la: Liberis impuberibus in potestate manentibus, tam natis quam posthumis, heredes substituere parentes possunt duplici modo: id est, aut eo quo extraneus, vt si heredes non exti-terint liberi, substitutus heres fiat: aut proprio iure, id est, si post mortem parentis heredes facti intra pubertatem decesserint, substitutus heres fiat.
units.tr: While children below the age of puberty, whether born or posthumous, remain under power, parents may substitute heirs for them in two ways: either in the manner of a stranger, so that if the children do not become heirs, the substitute becomes heir; or in their own right, so that if the children have become heirs after the parent's death and die before puberty, the substitute becomes heir.

units.la: Etiam exheredatis filiis substituere parentibus licet.
units.tr: Parents may also substitute heirs for children who have been disinherited.

units.la: Non aliter impuberi filio substituere quis heredem potest, quam si sibi quis heredem institueret, vel ipsum filium, vel quemlibet alium.
units.tr: One can substitute an heir for a son below puberty only on the same terms as one would institute an heir for oneself, whether the son himself or some other person.

units.la: Milites quomodocunque fecerint testamenta, valent, id est, etiam sine legitima obseruatione. Nam principalibus constitutionibus permissum est illis, quomodocunque vellent, quomodocunque possent restari: idque testamentum, quod miles contra iuris regulam fecit, ita demum valet, si vel in castris mortuus sit, vel post missionem intra annum.
units.tr: Soldiers' wills are valid however they were made, that is, even without the lawful formalities. For by imperial constitutions they were permitted to make their wills however they wished and however they could. And a will which a soldier made contrary to the rule of law is valid only if he died in camp, or within a year after his discharge.

units.la: De hac materia vid. l. 28. ff. 3. §.
units.tr: On this subject see l. 28. ff. 3. §.

units.la: 1. Institut. quib. mod. testam.
units.tr: 1. Institut. quib. mod. testam.

units.la: Aliud testamentum]
units.tr: Another will]

units.la: Alio. l. 1. ff. de iniusto, seu posteriore testamento prius rumpitur §. 2. & 3. Inst. quib. mod. testam. §. 2. Inst. d. tit.
units.tr: Another law: in the Digest, "On an unjust or later will": the earlier will is broken by a later one, Inst. Quibus modis testamenta, §§ 2 and 3; Inst. same title, § 2.

units.la: Item agnatione] Agnatione ex iure antiquo, si nascantur post mortem ex iure nouo: si in vita: successione, ex iure nouo: nam iure antiquo sui nascuntur, non fiunt. Ait vero lex no-ua, in ua, in locum suorum sui hæredes succedunto. uilis est: illa iuris gentium: hæc retro fingit tempore captiuitatis eum decessisse, qui non rediit; illa vero in ciuitate fuisse eum, qui rediit. Lex 12. tab. ciuibus Romanis constituit hæredes testamentarios & legitimos: Lex Cornelia captiuis. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Item agnatione] A birth by agnation: under the old law, if children are born after death, and under the new law, if born during life, the succession is under the new law. For under the old law the sui are born, not made. The new law, however, says that the sui heredes succeed into the place of the sui. The former is the law of nations; the latter feigns that he who did not return had died at the time of captivity, whereas the former holds that he who returned had been in the city. Lex 12. tab. established testamentary and legitimate heirs for Roman citizens; the Lex Cornelia does so for captives. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Si nemo alius ] Iure legitimo, vel ab intestato. Quod si alius iure hæres sit, vt si existat filius præteritus, secundum tab. bonorum possess. erit sine re. Verum enim quia vtcunque secundum tab. dari potest, quamuis iure ciuili nullum sit testam. iure prætor. necessaria est filio contra tab. bonor. possessio. Restat autem ex iniusto, nullo, rupto agnatione, detur bonor. possess. item ex irrito, si modo reuersus testator in antiquum statum, non mutata voluntate è vita decesserit. Nam tria exigit prætor: vt non minus quam septem testium signis obsignatum sit testamentum: vt is cuius bonorum possessio datur, mortis & testamenti tempore testamenti factionem habuerit: denique vt supremum testamentum sit. §. non tamen. quib. mod. test. infirm. l. 1. de bonor. poss. secundum tab. Cuiac. hic. & Pacius.
units.tr: Si nemo alius] By lawful right, or intestate. But if another is heir by law, as when a passed-over son appears, the possession according to the tablets will be without effect. Yet because the possession according to the tablets can be given in any case, even though a will made by the civil law is null, the Praetor's possession according to the tablets is necessary for the son. It remains to ask whether the possession of goods is given from an unjust will, a null one, or one broken by agnation; likewise from a void one, if the testator, having returned to his former state and without changing his mind, died. For the Praetor requires three things: that the will was sealed with the seals of at least seven witnesses; that he whose possession is granted had the capacity to make a will at the time of death and of the will; and finally that it was the last will. §. non tamen. quib. mod. test. infirm. l. 1. de bonor. poss. secundum tab. Cuiac. hic. & Pacius.

units.la: Cum re ] Hoc explicatur in tit. 28. l. filius C. de inofficioso.
units.tr: Cum re] This is explained in tit. 28. l. filius C. de inofficioso.

units.la: Liberis ] v. Inst. de pupillari substit.
units.tr: Children] v. Inst. de pupillari substit.

units.la: Proprio iure] Hæc est pupillaris substitutio, illa vulgaris: hæc moribus, illa 12.tab. introducta est: hæc pubertate. illa aditione finitur: Hac succeditur pupillo, illa testatori, hæc fit in euentum adquisitæ hæreditatis & mortis, aut in euentum mortis duntaxat: illa in euentum non adquisitæ hæreditatis. Ex constitutione autem duorum fratrum omnis substitutio facta pupillo, duplex est.vid. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Proprio iure] This is pupillary substitution; that is vulgar substitution. The former was introduced by custom, the latter by the Twelve Tables. The former ends at puberty, the latter at acceptance of the inheritance. The former succeeds to the pupil, the latter to the testator; the former takes effect upon the event of an acquired inheritance and of death, or upon death alone; the latter upon the event of an inheritance not acquired. Under the constitution of the two brothers, every substitution made for a pupil is double. vid. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Exheredatis filiis] substitutio plerumque æstimatur ex ratione successionis: hæc ex ratione scripturæ æstimatur, non successionis. Proinde in ea ordo scripturæ obseruatur: & ita intelligendum est initium §.prius l. moribus, utpote cum pendeat ex §. quisquis.& §. interdum, quos si quidem quis diligenter excutiat, inueniet ad eam duntaxat substitutionem pertinere, quæ fit exhæredato. Ac inde in sin. §. prius. ait, quod igitur dictum est, etiam exheredatis liberis (sic enim legendum esse scio) substituere licet, ideo adiectum est, ut declaretur, non esse à filij impuberis testamento incipiendum: quandoquidem si ab eo incipias exhæredato, hoc non est substituere. Denique odiosa hæc substitutio estl. cum quidam. C. de legatis. & ideo rigor iuris, id est, ordo scripturæ, qui in cæteris relaxatur, in ea diligenter custoditur. Sunt & quam plurima alia exempla substitutionum, quæ ex scriptura æstimantur, non successione: vt in formula Galli, in specie l. cum ex filio §. vlt. l. sed si plures §. vlt. l. vlt. §. 1. de vulgari substit. vt vere quis ita statuere possit. Substitutus est is, qui secundo loco scriptus est, quamuis ei non succedat qui primo loco heres scriptus est. Substitutus est is, qui secundo loco scriptus est, etiamsi ei post mortem testatoris primo deferatur hereditas. Substitutus est is, qui semel atq; iterum heres scriptus est, quamuis ei non nisi semel deferatur hereditas. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Exheredatis filiis] Substitution is generally judged by the order of succession, but this one is judged by the order of the writing, not of succession. Accordingly, the order of the writing is observed in it, and the beginning of the paragraph prius must be understood in this way, since it depends on the paragraph quisquis and the paragraph interdum. If anyone examines these carefully, he will find that they pertain only to that substitution which is made for a disinherited child. And so, at the end of the paragraph prius, the text says: "what has therefore been said, that one may substitute even for disinherited children (for so I know it should be read), has been added to make clear that it should not begin from the will of a son below puberty, since if you begin with a disinherited son, this is not substitution." Finally, this substitution is odious (l. cum quidam. C. de legatis.), and therefore the strictness of the law, that is, the order of the writing, which is relaxed in other cases, is carefully preserved in this one. There are also very many other examples of substitutions judged by the writing and not by succession, as in the formula of Gallus, and in the cases l. cum ex filio §. vlt. l. sed si plures §. vlt. l. vlt. §. 1. de vulgari substit. So one may truly lay down that: he is substitute who is written in the second place, although the one written first as heir does not succeed to him; he is substitute who is written in the second place, even if the inheritance is first deferred to him after the testator's death; he is substitute who is written as heir once and again, although the inheritance is deferred to him only once. Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Exheredatis ] l. 1. §. 2. ff. de vulgari §. 4. Inst. de pupillari.
units.tr: Exheredatis] l. 1. §. 2. ff. de vulgari §. 4. Inst. de pupillari.

units.la: Quam si sibi ] d. l. 1. §. ultim. §. 5. Instit. de pupillari.
units.tr: Quam si sibi] d. l. 1. §. ultim. §. 5. Instit. de pupillari.

units.la: Quomodocunque fecerint ] vers. quoquo enim modo, & §. 1. Instit. de militari. l. 1. ff. de testament. milit.
units.tr: However they may have made it: the wording "quoquo enim modo", and Inst. De militari, § 1; Dig. De testamentis militum, law 1.

units.la: Principalibus ] Iulij Caesaris: Titi, Domiciani, Neruae, Traiani. d. l. 1.
units.tr: Principalibus] Of Julius Caesar, Titus, Domitian, Nerva, Trajan. d. l. 1.

units.la: In castris ] §. 3. Inst. de militari.
units.tr: In castris] §. 3. Inst. de militari.

units.la: Intra annum ] d. §. 3. vers. & quod in castris in sin. l. 21. ff. de testam. milit.
units.tr: Within a year: the same § 3, the words "and whereas in the camp" at the end; Dig. De testamentis militum, law 21.

units.la: T- it. XXIV. De Legatis.
units.tr: Title XXIV. On Legacies.

units.la: LEgatum est, quod legis modo, id est, imperatiue, testamento relinquitur. Nam ea quae quiæ precatiuo modo relinquuntur, fideicommissi vocantur.
units.tr: A legacy is what is left by will in the imperative mode, that is, by command. Those things which are left in the precative mode are called fideicommissa.

units.la: Legamus autem quatuor modis, per vindicationem, per damnationem, sinendi modo, per præceptionem.
units.tr: There are four ways of bequeathing: by vindication, by damnation, by the mode of permitting, and by preception.

units.la: Per vindicationem, his verbis legamus, Do, lego, capito, sumito, sive habeto.
units.tr: By vindication, the words of bequest are: I give, I bequeath, let him take, let him acquire, or let him have.

units.la: Per damnationem his verbis: Heres meus damnas esto dare, dato, facito, heredem meum dare iubeo.
units.tr: By damnation, in these words: "Let my heir be bound to give; let him give, do, make; I order my heir to give."

units.la: Sinendi modo ita, Heres meus damnas esto sinere, Lucium Titium sumere illam rem, sibique habere.
units.tr: By permission, thus: "Let my heir be bound to allow Lucius Titius to take that thing and to have it for himself."

units.la: Per præceptionem sic, Lucius Titius illam rem præcipito.
units.tr: By preception, thus: "Let Lucius Titius take that thing beforehand."

units.la: Per vindicationem legari possunt res, quæ vtroque tempore ex iure Quiritium testatoris fuerunt, mortis, & quando testamentum faciebat: præterquam si pondere, mensura, numero continentur: in his enim satis est, si vel mortis duntaxat tempore fuerint ex iure Quiritium.
units.tr: By vindication, those things may be bequeathed which belonged to the testator under Quiritary law at both times, that of his death and when he made the will; except where they are reckoned by weight, measure or number, for in these it is enough that they belonged to him under Quiritary law at the time of death alone.

units.la: Per damnationem omnes res legari possunt, etiam quæ non sunt testatoris, dummodo tales sint, quæ dari possint.
units.tr: By damnation, all things may be bequeathed, even those which are not the testator's, provided they are such as can be given.

units.la: Liber homo, aut res populi, aut sacra, aut religiosa, nec per damnationem legari potest: quoniam dari non potest.
units.tr: A free man, or public property, or sacred or religious things cannot be bequeathed by damnation, since they cannot be given.

units.la: Sinendi modo legari possunt res propriæ testatoris, & heredis eius.
units.tr: By the mode of permitting, the testator's own things and those of his heir may be bequeathed.

units.la: Per præceptionem legari possunt res quæ etiam per vindicationem. Si ea res quæ non fuit utroque tempore testatoris ex iure Quiritium, per vindicationem legata sit, licet iure ciuili non valeat legatum, tamen senatusconsulto Neroniano firmatur: quo cautum est, ut quod minus pactis verbis legatum est, perinde sit, ac si optimo iure legatum esset.
units.tr: By preception, the things which may be bequeathed by vindication may be bequeathed. If a thing which did not belong to the testator under Quiritary law at both times was bequeathed by vindication, then although the legacy is invalid under civil law, it is nevertheless confirmed by the Senatus consultum Neronianum, by which it is provided that a legacy given in less formal words is to have the same effect as if it had been given by the best law.

units.la: Optimum autem ius legati per damnationem est. Si duobus eadem res per vindicationem legata sit: siquidem disiunctim, singulis in solidum debentur: si vero coniunctim, velut Titio & Seio, hominem Stichum do, lego, iure ciuili concursu partes fiebant. Non concurrente altero pars eius alteri adcrescebat. Sed post legem Papiam Poppæam, non capientis pars caduca fit.
units.tr: The best law of a legacy, however, is that by damnation. If the same thing is bequeathed by vindication to two persons: if they are bequeathed disjunctively, each is owed the whole; but if jointly, as in I give and bequeath the slave Stichus to Titius and Seius, then under civil law the shares arose by concurrence. If one did not take, his share accrued to the other. But since the Lex Papia Poppaea, the share of one who cannot take becomes caducous.

units.la: Si per damnationem eadem res duobus legata sit, siquidem coniunctim singulis partes debentur, & non capientis pars iure ciuili in hereditatem remanebat, nunc autem caduca fit: quod si disiunctim, singulis in solidum debetur.
units.tr: If the same thing is bequeathed by damnation to two persons: if jointly, each is owed a share, and the share of one who cannot take remained under civil law in the inheritance, but now it becomes caducous; but if disjunctively, each is owed the whole.

units.la: Optione autem legati, per vindicationem data, legatarii electio est, veluti, Hominem optimo, eligito. Idemque est, & si tacite legauerim, Titium hominem aut decem heres meus dato: ho- minem dare heredis electio est.
units.tr: Moreover, where a legacy is given by vindication with an option, the choice belongs to the legatee, as in: Let him choose the best slave. The same holds if I have bequeathed tacitly: My heir shall give Titius a slave or ten; the choice of which slave to give belongs to the heir.

units.la: Ante heredis institutionem legari non potest: quoniam & potestas testamenti ab heredis institutione incipit.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made before the institution of an heir, since the power of a will begins with the institution of the heir.

units.la: Post mortem heredis legari non potest, nec ab heredis herede legari videatur: quod iuris civilis ratio non patitur. In mortis autem heredis tempus legari potest: velut cum heres moriatur.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made after the death of the heir, nor is it held to be bequeathed from the heir of the heir, which the principle of civil law does not permit. But a legacy may be made for the time of the death of the heir, as in: when my heir dies.

units.la: Poenae causa legari non potest. Poenae autem causa legatur: quod coercendi heredis causa relinquitur, ut faciat quidem aut non faciat, non ut legatum pertineat: ut puta hoc modo, Si filiam tuam in matrimonio Titio collocaveris, decem millia Scio dato.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made as a penalty. A legacy is made as a penalty when it is left to compel the heir to do or not to do something, and not so that the legacy itself takes effect; for example, in this way: If you marry your daughter to Titius, give ten thousand to Scius.

units.la: Incertae personae legari non potest: veluti, Quicunque filio meo filiam suam in matrimonio collocaverit, ei homini tot millia dato. Sub certa tamen demonstratione incertae personae legari potest velut, Ex cognatis meis qui nunc sunt, qui primo ad funus meum venerit, ei heres meus illud dato.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made to an uncertain person, as in: Whoever marries his daughter to my son, give that man so many thousand. But a legacy may be made to an uncertain person under a certain designation, as in: Of my relatives now living, let my heir give that to the one who first comes to my funeral.

units.la: Neque ex falsa demonstratione, neque ex falsa causa legatum infirmatur. Falsa demonstratio est, velut, Titio fundum, quem a Titio emi, do lego, cum fundus a Tirio emptus non sit, falsa causa est: velut, Titio, quoniam negotia mea exprocurauit fundum do, lego, vt negotia eius nunquam Titius curasset.
units.tr: A legacy is not invalidated either by a false designation or by a false cause. A false designation is, for example: I give and bequeath to Titius the farm which I bought from Titius, when the farm was not bought from Titius; a false cause is, for example: I give the farm to Titius because he has managed my affairs, when Titius had never managed his affairs.

units.la: A legatario legari non potest.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made by a legatee.

units.la: Legatum ei tantum dari potest, qui extraneus est. Ideoque filio familiae heredi insti-tuto, vel seruo, neque à patre, neque à domino legari potest.
units.tr: A legacy can be given only to one who is a stranger. Therefore it cannot be bequeathed to a son under power, once instituted heir, nor to a slave, neither by the father nor by the master.

units.la: Heredi à semetipso legari non potest.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made to an heir by himself.

units.la: Ei qui in potestate, manu, mancipiove est scripti heredis, sub conditione legari potest, sed requiritur vt quo tempore dies legati cedit, in potestate heredis non sit.
units.tr: A legacy may be made, under a condition, to one who is in the power, hand or ownership of the instituted heir, but it is required that at the time when the day of the legacy falls due, he is not in the power of the heir.

units.la: Ei cuius in potestate, manu, mancipiove est heres scriptus, legari non potest.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be made to one in whose power, hand or ownership the heir is instituted.

units.la: Sicut singulae res legari possunt, ita vniuersarum quoque summa legari potest: vt puta, Maeuius heres meus cum Titio hereditatem meam partito, diuidito: quo casu dimidia pars bonorum legata videtur. Potest autem & alia pars, velut tertia vel quarta legari: quae species Partitio appellatur.
units.tr: Just as single things may be bequeathed, so also the sum of the whole estate may be bequeathed; for example: Let Maevius, my heir, divide and apportion my inheritance with Titius: in which case half of the goods appears to be bequeathed. Another part, such as a third or a quarter, may also be bequeathed; this kind is called partition.

units.la: Vsusfructus iure ciuili legari potest earum rerum, quarum salua substantia vtendi fruendi potest esse facultas, & tam singularum rerum, quam plurium, id est, partis.
units.tr: Under civil law the usufruct may be bequeathed of those things whose substance being preserved, the power of using and enjoying them can exist, whether of single things or of several, that is, of a part.

units.la: Senatusconsulto cautum est, vt etiamsi earum rerum quae in abusu continentur, vt puta vini, olei, tritici, vsusfructus legatus sit, legatario res tradantur cautionibus interpositis de restituendis eis, cum vsusfructus ad legatarium pertinere desierit.
units.tr: By senatus consultum it was provided that even where the usufruct of things which are consumed by use, such as wine, oil or wheat, is bequeathed, the things are to be handed over to the legatee on securities given for their restoration when the usufruct ceases to belong to the legatee.

units.la: Ciuitatibus omnibus, quæ sub imperio Prætoriani sunt, legari potest: idque à Diuo Nerua introductum, postea à Senatu autore Adriano diligentius constitutum est.
units.tr: A legacy may be made to all the cities which are under the rule of the Praetorian prefect; this was introduced by the deified Nerva and later more carefully settled by the Senate, on the authority of Hadrian.

units.la: Legatum quod datum est, adimi potest, vel eodem testamento, vel codicillis testamento confirmatis: dum tamen eodem modo adimatur, quo modo datum est.
units.tr: A legacy which has been given may be revoked, either in the same will or in codicils confirmed by the will, provided only that it is revoked in the same manner in which it was given.

units.la: Ad heredem legatarii legata non aliter transeunt, nisi si iam die legatorum cedente, legatarius decesserit.
units.tr: Legacies pass to the heir of the legatee only if the legatee has died after the day of the legacy has already fallen due.

units.la: Legatorum quæ pure vel in diem certum relicta sunt, dies cedit: antiquo quidem iure, ex mortis testatoris tempore: per legem autem Papiam Poppæam, ex apertis tabulis testamenti: eorum vero quæ sub conditione relicta sunt, cum conditio exstiterit. Lex Falcidia iuber, non plus quam dodrantem totius patrimonii legari, ut omni modo quadrans integer apud heredem remaneat.
units.tr: The day of legacies left purely or for a certain day falls due: under the old law, from the time of the testator's death; but under the Lex Papia Poppaea, from the opening of the tablets of the will; and of those left under a condition, when the condition is fulfilled. The Lex Falcidia orders that not more than three quarters of the whole estate be bequeathed, so that in every case a full quarter remains with the heir.

units.la: Legatorum perperam solutorum repetitio non est.
units.tr: There is no recovery of legacies wrongly paid.

units.la: De legatis] vid. 2. Instit. 20. Caius 2. tit. 5. §. Harm. 18.
units.tr: On legacies: see 2 Institutes, 20; Gaius 2, tit. 5, §. Harm. 18.

units.la: Id est imperative] Imperativa verba, directa, Heredem facio, instituo. l. 15. C. de testam. eadem ciuilia dicuntur. l. 7. ff. de vulgari. oppohuntur precariis, inflexis, & obliquis, fideicommissariis, quæ & <bl>ꝏ</bl> de quibus vid. Paul. 4 sent. 1. §. 6. Goth. h.
units.tr: That is, imperative: imperative words, direct ones, "I make heir", "I appoint", are called civil in the same way (l. 15 C. de testam.; l. 7 ff. de vulgari). They are opposed to precative, inflected and oblique words, which are fideicommissary; on these see Paul, 4 sent. 1, §. 6; Goth. h.

units.la: Quatuor modis] §. 1. Inst. de legat. 2. Caius 5. §. 1. 2. 3. &c.
units.tr: Four ways: §. 1 Inst. de legat.; 2 Gaius 5, §§. 1, 2, 3, etc.

units.la: Per præceptionem] Hoc modo hæredibus le-gatur, vt in iudicio id familiæ ercisцundæ, quod legatum est, præcipiant; hoc & prælegatum dicitur, & præcipuum. Sid. Apol. lib. 6. Epist. Il-lud autem deberi tibi quodam, vt Iurisconsulti dicunt, præcipui titulo. Cuiac. hic & Pac. vid.
units.tr: By preception: in this way a thing is bequeathed to heirs that they may take beforehand, in the action for partition of the family, what has been bequeathed; this is also called a prelegacy, and a preferred share. See Sidonius, Apol. lib. 6, Epist.: That is owed to you, as the jurists say, by a title of preference. See Cujas here and Pacius.

units.la: 2. Cai. 5. §. 8. & 2. Institut. de legat. Paul. 3. sen-tent. §. 5.
units.tr: 2 Gaius 5, §. 8; 2 Institutes, de legat.; Paul 3 sent., §. 5.

units.la: Per vindicationem] 2. Caius 5. §. 2. §. 2. Inst. de legat. Paul. 3 sent. 6. §. 3. & 7.
units.tr: By vindication: 2 Gaius 5, §. 2; §. 2 Inst. de legat.; Paul 3 sent. 6, §§. 3 and 7.

units.la: Per damnationem] 2. Caius 5. §. 3. 4. 5. 6. §.
units.tr: By damnation: 2 Gaius 5, §§. 3, 4, 5, 6.

units.la: 2. Inst. de legat. Paul. 3. sent. 6. §. 3. & 10
units.tr: 2 Inst. de legat.; Paul 3 sent. 6, §§. 3 and 10.

units.la: Sinendi modo] 2. Caius 2. §. 7. §. 2. Inst. de le-gat. Paul. 3. sent. 6. §. 11.
units.tr: By permission: 2 Gaius 2, §. 7; §. 2 Inst. de legat.; Paul 3 sent. 6, §. 11.

units.la: Vtroque tempore] §. 11. inf. eod.
units.tr: At both times: §. 11 inf. eod. below, same title.

units.la: Testatoris fuerunt] Et ita per vindicationem res aliena relinqui non potest. 2. Caius 5. §. 3.
units.tr: Testatoris fuerunt] And so a thing belonging to another cannot be left by vindication. 2. Caius 5. §. 3.

units.la: Etiam quæ non sunt testatoris] id est, alienæ. 2. Caius 5. §. 3.
units.tr: Etiam quæ non sunt testatoris] that is, belonging to others. 2. Caius 5. §. 3.

units.la: Quoniam dari] Quod dari non potest, per damnationem relinqui non potest.
units.tr: Quoniam dari] What cannot be given cannot be left by damnation.

units.la: Et hæredes eius] non etiam alienæ: quod tamen perperam additum est apud Caium lib. 2. Inst. tit. de legatis.
units.tr: Et hæredes eius] not also of others. This, however, was wrongly added in Caius, book 2 of the Institutes, title on legacies.

units.la: Quae etiam per vindicationem ] Hæc ita distinguenda sunt, quæ etiam per vindicationem. Si ea res, &c. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Quae etiam per vindicationem] These words must be distinguished thus: "which also by vindication. If that thing," etc. Cuiacius here.

units.la: Vt quod minus pactis ] id est, solennibus conceptis & legitimis verbis: Cicero pro Rosc. Comœ. Non enim ex pactione verborum, quibus iusiurandum comprehenditur. Arnob. lib.7.contra gentes. Quam cum pactionibus adorat & formulis. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Vt quod minus pactis] that is, with solemn, set and legal words. Cicero, Pro Roscio Comoedo: "For not from the agreement of words, by which an oath is comprised." Arnobius, book 7 Against the Gentiles: "which they worship with agreements and formulas." Cuiacius here.

units.la: Optimum autem ius ] Nempe quia laxius & expeditius est, Sic optimum ius vluratum, in l.1.C.de vsur. optimum ius possessionis. l fideiussor.§.pater de vsur.l.26.§.1.ff.de pignoribus. Cuiac. & Goth.hic.
units.tr: Optimum autem ius] Namely, because it is looser and more convenient. So "optimum ius" is used in the law 1 C. de usuris, "optimum ius possessionis," l. fideiussor, §. pater, de usuris; l. 26 §. 1 ff. de pignoribus. Cuiacius and Gothofredus here.

units.la: Si duobus eadem res ] Hæc quoque diuelli debent à superiore sententia.
units.tr: Si duobus eadem res] These words too must be separated from the preceding sentence.

units.la: Si quidem disiunctim ] Disiunctim legatur, si re tantum legatarij iungantur: coniunctim, si re & verbis. §.si eadem de leg. tit. C. de cad. tollend. tit. de vsufr. adcresc. verborum coniunctio aut pro nihilo, aut pro duplici coniunctione accipitur. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Si quidem disiunctim] Read "disiunctim" if the legatees are joined only in the thing; "coniunctim" if they are joined in both thing and words. §. si eadem, de legatis; tit. C. de caducis tollendis; tit. de usufructu accrescendo. The joining of words is taken either as nothing or as a double joining. Cuiacius here.

units.la: Singulis in solidum ] Legendum, singulis partes debentur: & hoc Iustinianus indicat in §. sni autem disiunctim C. de caduc. toll. Paul. in sent. Caius in Instit.
units.tr: Singulis in solidum] Read: shares are owed to each. Justinian indicates this in the section sin autem disiunctim, C. de caducis tollendis. Paulus in the Sentences; Caius in the Institutes.

units.la: Non currente ] Legendum ; non concurrente.
units.tr: Non currente] Read: non concurrente.

units.la: Siper damnationem ] Re coniuncti sunt quibus eadem res distinctim per vindicationem legatur, quoniam à principio solidum concursu partes habent. proinde re coniunctis accrescit deficientium portio, idque sine onere. Re coniuncti non sunt, quibus eadem res disiunctim per damnationem legatur, quoniam solidum singulis debetur, vni res, alteri precium: ideoque nec ius adcrescendi inter se habent. Sed ex constitutione Iustiniani eodem iure est damnationis, quo & vindicationis, legatum. Re & verbis coniuncti sunt quibus eadem res coniunctim per vindicationem legatur. nam & concursu partes habent, & ideo ius inter eos accrescendi est, cum onere tamen. Re & verbis coniuncti non sunt, quibus eadem res coniunctim per damnationem legatur: quoniam singulis ab initio partes debentur: proinde siue disiunctim, siue coniunctim per damnationem legatum sit, nunquam inter eos versatur ius accrescendi. Ius accrescendi cum dicimus, ius antiquum dicimus. Ius caduci, ius nouum est; & haec est sententia huius loci. Hinc vero apparet l. coniunctim de legat. 3. de legato vindicationis l. plane §. si coniunctim de legat. 1. de legato damnationis, accipiendam esse. Sed hoc ideo in eis locis suppressum est, quod iam sublatae essent a Iustiniano legatorum differentiae: non tamen ita ab eis locis sublatae sunt, ut haec manifesto non supersint huius differentiæ vestigia, quæ prima specie, quasi contra se stare videantur, vt plane iam ex eo appareat, quam hebetes aut indiligentes fuerint hi, quibus studium fuit Pandectarum capita ex veterum Iurisconsultorum libris decerpere. Cæterum & id quod diximus de legato damnationis, nominatim traditur in l. 7. de legat. 2. vnde & in l. huiusmodi. §. si Titio. l. si duobus. de legat. 1. optimo iure legatum fuisse necesse est vt statuamus: alioquin pars vacans adcrescit coniuncto, cum quo partes per concursum fiunt. Quod deinde sequitur in §. si coniunctim, sed si in pupillari, ad re coniunctos pertinet, qui concursu partes habent, vnde in extremo ita scriptum oportuit, interim igitur totum. Quod & Azo & Hugolinus intellexere. vid. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Siper damnationem] Those are joined by the thing to whom the same thing is left separately by vindication, since from the beginning they have shares by concurrence; therefore, for those joined by the thing, the share of those who fail accrues, and that without burden. Those are not joined by the thing to whom the same thing is left separately by damnation, since the whole is owed to each separately: to one the thing, to the other the price; therefore they have no right of accrual among themselves. But by a constitution of Justinian, a legacy by damnation has the same law as one by vindication. Those are joined by thing and words to whom the same thing is left jointly by vindication, for they have shares by concurrence, and therefore there is a right of accrual among them, though with a burden. Those are not joined by thing and words to whom the same thing is left jointly by damnation, since shares are owed to each from the beginning; therefore, whether the legacy is left by damnation separately or jointly, a right of accrual never arises among them. When we speak of a right of accrual, we speak of the old law; the right of caducity is the new law, and this is the sense of this passage. Hence it appears that l. coniunctim, 3, de legato vindicationis; l. plane §. si coniunctim, 1, de legato damnationis, must be understood in this way. But this was passed over in those places because Justinian had already abolished the differences between legacies; yet they were not so abolished from those places that traces of this difference do not manifestly remain, which at first sight seem to stand against themselves. From this it is plain how dull or careless those were who devoted themselves to picking out the heads of the Pandects from the books of the older jurists. Moreover, what we have said about a legacy by damnation is stated by name in l. 7, de legatis 2, whence also in l. huiusmodi, §. si Titio; l. si duobus, de legatis 1, we must conclude that the legacy was of the best law; otherwise the vacant share accrues to the joint legatee, with whom shares arise by concurrence. What follows next in §. si coniunctim, but if in a pupillary substitution, pertains to those joined by the thing, who have shares by concurrence; hence at the end it had to be written thus: "meanwhile therefore the whole." Azo and Hugolinus also understood it so. See Cuiacius here.

units.la: Siquidem coniunctim] 2. Caius 5. §. 5.
units.tr: Siquidem coniunctim] 2. Caius 5. §. 5.

units.la: Quod si disiunctim] 2 Caius 5. §. 6.
units.tr: Quod si disiunctim] 2 Caius 5. §. 6.

units.la: In solidum debetur] Hoc innuit in legato per vindicationem disiunctim facto singulis partes deberi: in damnationis legato, singulis solidum deberi. vid. Paul. 3. sent. 6. §. 3. in sin. Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: In solidum debetur] This implies that in a legacy by vindication made separately, shares are owed to each; in a legacy by damnation, the whole is owed to each. See Paulus, 3 Sent. 6 §. 3 in fin.; Gothofredus here.

units.la: Optione autem legati] Hic locus mirum in modum deformatus est. Ipse ratione iuris ductus sic emendaui. Optione autem legati per vindicationem data, legatarii electio est: veluti, Hominem optato, eligito. Idemque estsi tacite legata legauerim Titio hominem. At si ita, Hæres meus damnas esto hominem dare, electio est. Si tacite, id est, non data optione. Homine igitur per vindicationem generaliter legato, legatarii electio est.l. legato. de legat. 1. per damnationem heredis. l. si à substituto. § 1. eod. similiter in disiunctiuis legatis electio est legatarij, si per vindicationem l. plane §. penult. de legat. 1. l. Lucio de legat. 2. heredis, si per damnationem. l. si is cui. l. si ita relictum. §. ult. de legat. 2. Et hæ quidem duæ differentiæ non sunt sublatæ, quia inducuntur ex voluntate testatoris. Cuiac. & Pac. hic.
units.tr: Optione autem legati] This passage has been strangely deformed. Guided by reason of law, I have emended it thus: "Where the choice of the legacy is given by vindication, the choice belongs to the legatee: for example, 'Let him choose a man whom he likes.' And the same holds if I have left a man to Titius tacitly. But if it is thus, 'Let my heir be bound to give a man,' the choice is his [the heir's]. If tacitly, that is, with no choice given. Therefore, where a man is left generally by vindication, the choice belongs to the legatee: l. legato, de legatis 1; per damnationem heredis; l. si a substituto §. 1, eod. Similarly, in disjunctive legacies the choice belongs to the legatee if by vindication, l. plane §. penult., de legatis 1; l. Lucio, de legatis 2; to the heir if by damnation, l. si is cui; l. si ita relictum §. ult., de legatis 2. And these two differences have not been abolished, because they arise from the will of the testator." Cuiacius and Pacius here.

units.la: Legari non potest ] Paul. 3. sent. 6. §. 2. hodie potest. § .34. Inst. de legat.
units.tr: Legari non potest] Paulus, 3 Sent. 6 §. 2. Today it can be done: §. 34 Inst. de legatis.

units.la: Institutione ] l. 1. in sin. ff. de vulgar. l. ult. ff. de iur. Codic.
units.tr: Institutione] l. 1 in fin. ff. de vulgari; l. ult. ff. de iure codicillorum.

units.la: Legari non potest ] Paul. 3. sentent. 6. §. 6. Hodie potest, §. 35. Inst. de legat.
units.tr: Legari non potest] Paulus, 3 Sent. 6 §. 6. Today it can be done: §. 35 Inst. de legatis.

units.la: Heredis ] & suæ. Paul. 3. sent. 6. § 6.
units.tr: Heredis] and his own. Paulus, 3 Sent. 6 §. 6.

units.la: Cum heres moriatur ] Morietur. Paul. d. loco.
units.tr: Cum heres moriatur] "Will die." Paulus, the place cited above.

units.la: Pœna causa ] Quemadmodum superiores duæ sententiæ, ita ut hæc à Iustiniano sublata est. Hodie igitur valet legatum tale, Hæres meus si Stichum alienauerit, Caio centum dato. Non idem est, si impossibile, probrosum, illicitum sit legatum: Veluti, si mare non ebibéris, Titio centum dato. Si sororem uxorem non duxeris, aut si pupillo filiam nuptum non collocaueris, Titio centum dato. §. sin. de legat. in l. 1. de his quæ pœn. caus. relin. Hæc verba, Illicite vel probrose, sunt Triboniani. Cuiac. hic & Pac.
units.tr: Pœna causa] As the two preceding opinions were, so this one was abolished by Justinian. Today, therefore, a legacy of this kind is valid: "If my heir sells Stichus, let him give a hundred to Gaius." It is not the same if the legacy is impossible, shameful or unlawful: for example, "If you do not drink up the sea, let him give a hundred to Titius"; "If you do not marry your sister, or if you do not give your ward's daughter in marriage, let him give a hundred to Titius." §. sin. de legatis; in l. 1, de his quae poenae causa relinquuntur. The words "unlawfully or shamefully" are Tribonian's. Cuiacius here and Pacius.

units.la: Pœnæ causa] §. 36. Inst. de legat. l. unic. C. de his quæ pœnæ nomin. l. 1. l. 2. & seqq. ff. de his quæ pœnæ causa.
units.tr: Pœnæ causa] §. 36 Inst. de legatis; l. unic. C. de his quae poenae nomine; l. 1, l. 2 and following, ff. de his quae poenae causa.

units.la: Coercendi hæredis causa] Pœnæ nomine relinquitur, non in gratiam legatarij, sed in odium hæredis.
units.tr: Coercendi hæredis causa] It is left by way of penalty, not for the benefit of the legatee, but in the hatred of the heir.

units.la: Ut faciat quidem] Puto legi debere, Quid, non quidem.
units.tr: Ut faciat quidem] I think it should be read, "What, not indeed."

units.la: Incerta persona legari] vt & fideicommitti, tit. 25. §. 13. inf. eod. d. §. 36. Paul. 5. sentent. 6. § 13.
units.tr: Incerta persona legari] as also a fideicommissum, tit. 25 §. 13 inf. eod.; the said §. 36; Paulus, 5 Sent. 6 §. 13.

units.la: Non potest] hodie potest. §. 25. Inst. de legat.
units.tr: Non potest] Today it can be done. §. 25 Inst. de legatis.

units.la: Incerta legari] id est, ex certis personis incertæ. d. vers. sub. certa.
units.tr: Incerta legari] that is, from certain persons, uncertain ones. The said words "sub certa."

units.la: Falsa demonstratione] §. 30. Inst. de legat. vid. l. 33 ff. de condit. & demonstr.
units.tr: Falsa demonstratione] §. 30 Inst. de legatis; see l. 33 ff. de conditionibus et demonstrationibus.

units.la: Falsa causa] §. 31. Instit. de legat. l. 72. §. 6. ff. de condit. & demonstr.
units.tr: Falsa causa] §. 31 Inst. de legatis; l. 72 §. 6 ff. de conditionibus et demonstrationibus.

units.la: Ut negocia] Lege, cum negocia.
units.tr: Ut negocia: read "cum negocia" (when the business).

units.la: Legatario legari non potest] Hodie potest. leg. 69. l. 91. §. 4. ff. de legat 1. leg. 2. in sin. Cod. comm. de legat.
units.tr: A legacy cannot be left to a legatee: Today it can. Dig. 69; Dig. 91 §. 4 (de legatis 1); Cod. comm. de legatis, l. 2 in fine.

units.la: Legatum ei tantum dari potest] Hic quoque locus valde corruptus est: Lego, Legatum ab eo tantum dari potest, qui ex sua persona hæres est, Ideoque, &c. quæ sequuntur Cuiac. & Paci. hic.
units.tr: Legatum ei tantum dari potest: This passage too is badly corrupted. I read: "A legacy can be given only by one who is heir in his own person; therefore, etc., and what follows." Cuiac. & Paci. hic.

units.la: Hæredi à semetipso ] l. 18. l. 34. §. 11. l. 116. §. 1. ff. de legat. 1. l. 34. §. 1. in f. ff. de legat. 2.
units.tr: To an heir from himself: l. 18; l. 34 §. 11; l. 116 §. 1 ff. de legat. 1; l. 34 §. 1 in fine ff. de legat. 2.

units.la: Qui in potestate manu mancipiove ] In potestate est filius familias tit. 5. & 10. sup. eod. in manu vxor, materfamilias. tit. 9. sup. eod. in mancipio seruus §. 24. Instit. de legat. Cuiac. & Gothofred. hic.
units.tr: Who is under power, in hand, or in mancipium: A son is under power (see titles 5 and 10 above, same title); a wife is in hand, as a materfamilias (title 9 above, same title); a slave is in mancipium (tit. 9. sup. eod. in mancipio seruus §. 24 Instit. de legat. Cuiac. & Gothofred. hic.).

units.la: Legari non potest ] tit. 25. §. 12. inf. eod. aut id mutatum est l. 25. ff. de legat 1. aut expungenda negatio.
units.tr: Cannot be left by legacy: tit. 25 §. 12 inf. eod. Or else this has been altered: l. 25 ff. de legat. 1. Or else the negation must be struck out.

units.la: Singulæ res ] vid. Inst. de sing. reb. per fideicommiss. relict.
units.tr: Single things: see Inst. de sing. reb. per fideicommiss. relict.

units.la: Partitò diuidito ] Malim Partito, diuidito. Quo casu dimidia pars bonorum. leg. nomen §. partitionis de verb. signif. Partitarius legatarius, partis suæ commodo, & pro parte sua onera sustinere debet. l. cum filius §. 1. l. si quis seruum §. sin. de legat. 3. & in eam rem partis, & pro parte stipulationes interponuntur. §. sed quia: de fideicommissariis hæreditat. & in tit. prox. Quod si ita legatum sit, Bonorum meorum partem tertiam, non est partitio. Non affero capita legum quæ sunt notissima. aut Cuiacius hic & Paci.
units.tr: Divide by parts: I would prefer "Partito, diuidito" (divide by parts). In that case the legacy is half of the goods. leg. nomen §. partitionis de verb. signif. A legatee by partition must bear the burdens in proportion to his share and according to his part. l. cum filius §. 1; l. si quis seruum §. sin. de legat. 3. For this purpose stipulations concerning the share and in proportion to it are entered into. §. sed quia, de fideicommissariis hereditat. and in the next title. But if the legacy is worded, "a third part of my goods," it is not a partition. I do not cite the chapters of the laws, which are very well known, or Cuiacius hic & Paci.

units.la: Partitio appellatur ] de Partitione vid. Goth. ad l.164.§ 1.ff. de verb.significat.
units.tr: Called a partition: on partition see Goth. ad l. 164 §. 1 ff. de verb. significat.

units.la: Vsusfructus iure ciuili ] vid.ff. de vsu & vsufruct. legat. §. 1. Institut. de vsufruct.leg. 3.ff. de vsufruct.
units.tr: Usufruct under civil law: see ff. de usu & usufruct. legat. §. 1; Institutes de usufructu; leg. 3 ff. de usufructu.

units.la: Salua substantia ] hoc enim vsus fructus definitione continetur Inst.de vsufr.l.1.ff.eod.
units.tr: With the substance preserved: for this is contained in the definition of usufruct. Inst. de usufr.; l. 1 ff. eod.

units.la: Id est partis ] l.42.ff.de vsufr. & quemadm.
units.tr: That is, of the part: l. 42 ff. de usufr. & quemadm.

units.la: Senatusconsulto ] Huius S. C. sit mentio in tit. de vsufruct. ear.rer.l.1.l.uxorem de vsufruct.legat. l. vlt. vsufruct. quemadm. caueat. l. vsufruct.ad l. Falcid. l.1. C.de vsufruct. §. constituitur. Inst. eod.
units.tr: Senatusconsultum: mention of this decree is made in the title de usufructu earum rerum; l. 1; l. uxorem de usufructu legat.; l. ult. usufruct. quemadm. caueat.; l. usufructu ad l. Falcid.; l. 1 C. de usufructu; §. constituitur, Inst. eod.

units.la: S. C. opus fuit; quia neque naturali, neque ciuili iure earum rerum est vsufr. quae sunt in abusu. Senatus autem id sanctionibus explicat: quae in rebus difficillimis certissima sunt iuris subsidia. leg. vsufructu solut. matrimon. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: A decree of the Senate was needed, because by neither natural nor civil law is there usufruct in those things which are consumed by use.
