The Senate, however, sets this out by its enactments, which in very difficult matters are the most certain legal aids. leg. usufructu solut. matrimon.; Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Ciuitatibus ] vid. Gothofred. ad l. 122. ff. de legat. 1.
units.tr: Cities: see Gothofred. ad l. 122 ff. de legat. 1.

units.la: Pratoriani ] Legendum, P. Romani. l.omnibus ad Trebell.
units.tr: Praetorians: read "P. Romani" (the Roman people). l. omnibus ad Trebell.

units.la: Authore Adriano ] Imo fortasse Marco l. cum Senatus de rebus dub. Etenim in Propriis nominibus facillimus auctorum lapsus. Non male tamen videtur legendum post; Senatusconsulto Aproniano, vt & Paulus libro singulari de Senatusconsultis scribit in l. 26.ff. ad Trebell. Cuiac. & Gothofr. hic.
units.tr: Under the author Hadrian: indeed perhaps it should be Marcus; l. cum Senatus de rebus dub. For errors of authors in proper names are very easy. It is not badly thought, however, that one should read after "Senatusconsulto" the word "Aproniano," as Paulus also writes in his single book on senatus-consulta, in l. 26 ff. ad Trebell.; Cuiac. & Gothofr. hic.

units.la: vid. Inst. de adempt. legator. ff. de adimen. legat.
units.tr: See Inst. de adempt. legator.; ff. de adimen. legat.

units.la: Inst. de adempt. legator. in princ. l. pen. §. 1. ff. de adimend.
units.tr: Inst. de adempt. legator. in princ.; l. pen. §. 1 ff. de adimend.

units.la: Dum tamen eodem modo ] sic de libertate in tit. 2. exempla haec sunto, Do, lego, non do, non lego, haeres dato, haeres ne dato. l. nisi de accept. ergo nec alij vlli quam cui datum est l. legatum. de adi. leg. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Provided only it be done in the same manner: thus on liberty, in title 2, these are the examples: "I give, I bequeath; I do not give, I do not bequeath; let him be heir; let him not be heir." l. nisi de accept. Therefore not to any other than to him to whom it was given. l. legatum de adi. leg.; Cuiac. h.

units.la: Dum tamen eodem modo ] Nihil hodie interest, an contrariis verbis, an quibuscunque fiat. Inst. d. loco.
units.tr: Provided only it be done in the same manner: Today it makes no difference whether it is done with contrary words or with any words at all. Inst. d. loco.

units.la: Nisi li iam ] vid. tit. ff. quando dies legator.
units.tr: Unless: see title ff. quando dies legator.

units.la: Legatorum quae pure ] Legati conditionalis polt euentum conditionis : puri vel in diem antiquo iure, a morte testatoris: ex lege Papia, ab apertis tabulis dies cedit. Hodie ius vetus sequimur ex regula Catoniana quae ad nouas leges, id est, Iuliam & Papiam non pertineut. l. vlt. ff. de regul. Catoniana. Goth. h.
units.tr: Of legacies which are pure: a conditional legacy falls due after the event of the condition; under the old law, a pure legacy or one at a fixed day fell due from the death of the testator; under the Papian law, it falls due from the opening of the tablets. Today we follow the old law by the Catonian rule, which does not pertain to the new laws, that is, the Julian and Papian. l. ult. ff. de regul. Catoniana; Goth. h.

units.la: Ex apertis tabulis ] sunt huius iuris vestigia quaedam in l. eum qui post. l. in testamento. de condit. & demonstr. l. sin. de donat. caus. mort. l. 3. §. fi-nal. l. qui soluendo, de hared. instit. Hodie vero ius antiquum sequimur, cuius iuris regula quaedam est Catonis regula: ad ea namque pertinet, quae a morte testatoris cedunt: ad nouas leges, id est, ad leges Papias non pertinet, ex quibus ex apertura tabularum legata cedunt. l. vlt. de regul. Caton. nam neque ad ea pertinet, quæ ab adiitione, vel ab euentu conditionis cedunt. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: From the opening of the tablets: there are some traces of this law in l. eum qui post; l. in testamento de condit. & demonstr.; l. sin. de donat. caus. mort.; l. 3 §. final; l. qui soluendo, de hared. instit. Today, however, we follow the old law, of which the rule is a certain rule of Cato, for it pertains to those things which fall due from the death of the testator; it does not pertain to the new laws, that is, the Papian laws, by which legacies fall due from the opening of the tablets. l. ult. de regul. Caton. For it does not pertain to those things which fall due from acceptance of the inheritance or from the event of a condition. Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Dodrantem ] vid. l. 1. ff. ad l. Falcid.
units.tr: Three-quarters: see l. 1 ff. ad l. Falcid.

units.la: Repetitio non est ] Imo repetitio est. l. 2. & 3. de condicti. indeb. l. fideicommissum. C. eod. l. error. C. ad l. Falcid. & in Paul. sentent. lib. 3. tit. 6. Aut igitur hæc sententia accipienda est de legatis damnationis: quibus adiici possunt legata incertis personis soluta. §. final. de obligat. quæ ex cont. §. incertis de leg. aut quod magis est negatione abundat. vid. Goth. & Cuiac. h.
units.tr: There is no repetition: Indeed there is repetition. l. 2 & 3 de condicti. indeb.; l. fideicommissum C. eod.; l. error C. ad l. Falcid.; and in Paul's Sentences, book 3, title 6. Either therefore this sentence must be taken of legacies of condemnation, to which may be added legacies paid to uncertain persons. §. final. de obligat. quae ex cont.; §. incertis de leg. Or, what is more likely, the negation is superfluous. See Goth. & Cuiac. h.

units.la: Tit. XXV. De Fideicommissis.
units.tr: Title XXV. Of Trust Bequests.

units.la: FIdeicommissum est, quod non ciuilibus verbis, sed precatiue relinquitur: nec ex rigore iuris ciuilis proficiscitur, sed ex voluntate datur relinquentis.
units.tr: A trust bequest (fideicommissum) is one that is left not in civil words but by way of request, and it does not arise from the strict rule of civil law but is given by the will of the one leaving it.

units.la: Verba fideicommissorum in vsu fere sunt hæc, Fideicommitto, peto, volo dari, & similia.
units.tr: The words of trust bequests in common use are these: "I entrust," "I ask," "I wish it to be given," and similar ones.

units.la: Etiam nutu relinquere fideicommissum in vsu receptum est.
units.tr: It is also an accepted practice to leave a trust bequest by a nod.

units.la: Fideicommissum relinquere possunt, qui testamentum facere possunt; licet non secerint. Nam intestatus quis moriturus, fideicommissum relinquere potest:
units.tr: Those who can make a will can leave a trust bequest, even if they have not made one. For a person who is about to die intestate can leave a trust bequest.

units.la: Res per fideicommissum relinqui possunt, quæ etiam per damnationem legari possunt.
units.tr: Things that can be left as a legacy by damnation (per damnationem) can be left by trust bequest.

units.la: Fideicommissa dari possunt his, quibus legari potest.
units.tr: Trust bequests can be given to those to whom a legacy can be given.

units.la: Latini Iuniani fideicommissum capere possunt, licet legatum capere non possint. Fideicommissum & ante heredis institutionem, & post mortem heredis, & codicillis, etiam non confirmatis testamento, dari potest, licet legari non possit.
units.tr: Latini Juniani can take a trust bequest, although they cannot take a legacy. A trust bequest can be given both before the institution of the heir and after the heir's death, and in codicils, even if the codicils are not confirmed by the will, although a legacy cannot be given in that way.

units.la: Item Græce fideicommissum scriptum valet, licet legatum Græce scriptum valeat.
units.tr: Likewise, a trust bequest written in Greek is valid, although a legacy written in Greek is valid.

units.la: Filio qui in potestate est, seruoue heredibus institutus, seu si his legatum sit, patris vel domini fidei committi potest, quamuis ab eo legari non possit. Qui testamento heres institutus est, codicillis etiam non confirmatis rogari potest, velut hereditatem totam, vel ex parte alii restituat, quamuis ex directo heres institui, ne quidem confirmatis codicillis possit.
units.tr: A trust bequest can be entrusted to a son who is under his father's authority, or to a slave instituted heir, or if a legacy has been made to them, to the father or master, even though a legacy cannot be left by him. One who has been instituted heir by will can be asked, even by unconfirmed codicils, to hand over the whole inheritance or part of it to another; although an heir cannot be instituted directly even by confirmed codicils.

units.la: Fideicommissa non per formulam petuntur, vt legata: sed cognitio est Romæ quidem Consulum, aut Prætoris, qui fideicommissarius vocatur: in prouinciis vero, Præsidum prouinciarum.
units.tr: Trust bequests are not sought by a formula, as legacies are; rather, cognizance belongs at Rome to the Consuls or the Praetor, who is called the trust-bequest praetor (fideicommissarius); but in the provinces, to the governors of the provinces.

units.la: Pœnæ causa certæ vel incertæ personæ, ne quidem fideicommissa dari possunt.
units.tr: Trust bequests cannot be given as a penalty to a certain or uncertain person.

units.la: Is qui rogatus est alii restituere hereditatem, lege quidem Faicidia locum non habent, quoniam non plus, puta quam dodrantem, restituere rogatus est, ex Trebelliano senatusconsulto restituit, vt ei & in eum dentur actiones, cui restituta est hereditas. Lege autem Falcidia intervenient, quoniam plus quam dodrantem, vel etiam totam hereditatem restituere rogatus sit, ex Pegasiano senatusconsulto restituit, vel deducta parte quarta, ipse qui scriptus est heres, hereditatem restituat, & in ipsum actiones conseruentur, is autem qui recipit hereditatem legatarii loco habeatur.
units.tr: One who has been asked to hand over an inheritance to another is not covered by the Falcidian law, since he has been asked to restore no more than, say, three-quarters (dodrans); he restores under the Trebellian senatus-consultum, so that actions are given both to him and against him to whom the inheritance is restored. But the Falcidian law comes into play when he has been asked to restore more than three-quarters, or even the whole inheritance; he restores under the Pegasian senatus-consultum, or, with the fourth part deducted, the heir himself who was named restores the inheritance, and the actions are preserved against him; and the one who receives the inheritance is regarded as in the position of a legatee.

units.la: Ex Pegasiano senatusconsulto restituta hereditate, commoda & incommoda hereditatis communicantur. Inter heredem, & eum cui reliquæ partes restitutæ sunt interpositis stipulationibus ad exemplum partis & pro parte stipulationum. Partis autem & pro parte stipulationes proprie dicuntur, quæ de lucro & damno communicando solent interponi inter heredem & legatarium partiarium, id est, cum quo partitus est heres.
units.tr: When an inheritance has been restored under the Pegasian senatus-consultum, the advantages and disadvantages of the inheritance are shared. Between the heir and the one to whom the remaining parts have been restored, stipulations are entered into on the model of partnership and as stipulations for a share. Stipulations "of a part" and "for a part" are properly so called, which are customarily entered into to share gain and loss between the heir and the partner legatee, that is, the one with whom the heir has shared.

units.la: Si heres damnosam hereditatem dicat, cogetur à Prætore adire & restituere totam, ita vt ei & in eum qui recipit hereditatem actiones dentur, perinde atque si ex Trebelliano senatusconsulto restituta fuisset: idque vt ita fiat, Pegasiano senatusconsulto cautum est.
units.tr: If the heir declares the inheritance to be burdensome, he shall be compelled by the Praetor to enter upon it and restore the whole, so that actions are given both to him and against the one who receives the inheritance, just as if it had been restored under the Trebellian senatus-consultum; and the Pegasian senatus-consultum provides that this shall be done.

units.la: Si quis in fraudem tacitam fidem adcommodauerit, vt non capienti fideicommissum restituat, nec quadrantem eum deducere Senatus censuit: nec caducum vindicare ex eo testamento, si liberos habeat.
units.tr: If anyone has pledged a tacit trust to restore a fideicommissum to one who is not capable of taking it, the Senate has ruled that he may not deduct a quarter, nor may he claim the caducous share under that will if he has children.

units.la: Libertas dari potest per fideicommissum.
units.tr: Liberty can be given by trust bequest.

units.la: De fideicommissis] 6. Cod. 42. 2. Caius 7. & Paul. 4. sent. 1. adde §. 2. Inst. 2 1. de sing reb.
units.tr: On trust bequests: 6. Cod. 42. 2. Caius 7. & Paul. 4. sent. 1. add §. 2. Inst. 2 1. de sing reb.

units.la: Non ciuilibus] directis verbis, vt in l. 7. ff. de vulgar. substit.
units.tr: Not civil: that is, not in direct words, as in l. 7. ff. de vulgar. substit.

units.la: In vsu fere haec sunt] adde Paul. 4. sent. 1. §. 6. & vlt. Inst. de sing. reb.
units.tr: In common use these are: add Paul. 4. sent. 1. §. 6. and last Inst. de sing. reb.

units.la: Etiam nutu] l. 21. ff. de legat. 3. l. 22. Cod. de fideicommissis. Secus tamen est in legato iure antiquo. Nutu quae fieri possint vid. Goth. ad l. 52. in sin. ff. de obligat.
units.tr: Even by a nod: l. 21. ff. de legat. 3. l. 22. Cod. de fideicommissis. It is otherwise, however, with a legacy under the old law. On what may be done by a nod, see Goth. on l. 52. at the end, ff. de obligat.

units.la: Fideicommissum relinquere] Idem Vlpianus in l. 2. de legat. 1. quae si quaerantur exempla, coniungenda est cum l. 1. de legat. 3. nam ex eodem libro sunt ambae.
units.tr: To leave a trust bequest: Ulpian himself says the same in l. 2. de legat. 1. If examples are sought, it must be joined with l. 1. de legat. 3., for both come from the same book.

units.la: Qui testamentum facere] Qui testari potest, fideicommittere potest. Gothofred. ad l. 2. ff. de legat. 1.
units.tr: Who can make a will: One who can make a will can make a trust bequest. Gothofred on l. 2. ff. de legat. 1.

units.la: Intestatus quis] Paul. 4. sent. 1. §. 4. Inst. de fideicommiss. hared.
units.tr: A person who is intestate: Paul. 4. sent. 1. §. 4. Inst. de fideicommiss. hered.

units.la: Quaecumque per damnationem] tit. 24. §. 8. 9. sup. eod.
units.tr: Whatever by damnation: title 24. §. 8. 9. above, same title.

units.la: Latini Iuniani] de quib. vid. sup. tit. 3. eod.
units.tr: Latini Juniani: on whom see above, title 3, same place.

units.la: Ante hæredis institutionem ] Quod olim non fuit in legato. tit.24.§.15 sup.eod.
units.tr: Before the institution of the heir: which was not formerly the case with a legacy. Title 24. §. 15 above, same place.

units.la: Post mortem hæredis ] leg.si fuerit de legat.3. hoc autem tacite fieri potest, non nominatim, vtputa à Titio substituto, exhæredati legatarij. l.cum quidem C. de legat.
units.tr: After the death of the heir: l. si fuerit de legat. 3. This may be done tacitly, not by name, for instance when a legatee disinherited has been substituted by Titius. l. cum quidem C. de legat.

units.la: Post mortem hæredis ] Quod olim non fuit in legatis.tit.24.§.8.sup.eod.
units.tr: After the death of the heir: which formerly was not the case with legacies. Title 24. §. 8. above, same title.

units.la: Etiam non confirmatis ] 2.Caius 7.§.9.Paul. 4.sent.1.§.10.
units.tr: Even without confirmed codicils: 2. Caius 7. §. 9. Paul. 4. sent. 1. §. 10.

units.la: Item Græce ] l.fideicommissa in princ.de legat. 2.Goth.ad l.11.de legat.3.
units.tr: Likewise in Greek: l. fideicommissa in princ. de legat. 2. Goth. on l. 11. de legat. 3.

units.la: Licet legatum Græce ] Quæ sunt iuris ciuilis, Latine ; quæ iuris gentium qualibet lingua. l. an utilis in sin. de accept. Testamenta igitur Latine fiunt, unde merito dubitatur in l.quires tamento §.veteres de testam. an testes ad testamentum adhibiti Latine scribere debeant. Sed hoc Impp. emendarunt, l. hac consultissima. §.final. C.de testam. l.vlt. C. de testam.tut.l.directas C. de testam.man. Si quandoque stipulationem contendas esse iuris gentium, hæc vere mascula erit ratio: nam stipulatio qualibet lingua semper fieri potuit. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Although a legacy written in Greek: things that belong to civil law are in Latin; things of the law of nations may be in any language. l. an utilis at the end, de accept. Wills, therefore, are made in Latin, whence it is rightly doubted in l. quires tamento §. veteres de testam. whether witnesses called to a will ought to write in Latin. But the emperors corrected this: l. hac consultissima, §. final. C. de testam. l. vlt. C. de testam. tut. l. directas C. de testam. man. If at any time you contend that stipulation belongs to the law of nations, this will be a truly manly argument, for a stipulation could always be made in any language. Cuiacius here.

units.la: Quamuis ab eo ] & in eo differt fideicommissum à legato.
units.tr: Although by him: and in this a trust bequest differs from a legacy.

units.la: Legari non possit ] tit.24.§.24.sup.eod.
units.tr: Cannot be left as a legacy: title 24. §. 24. above, same title.

units.la: Quamuis ex directo hæres ] In confirmatis omnia directo relinqui possunt, excepta hæreditate. Codicillis confirmatis hæres institui non potest: quamuis iisdem confirmatis restituendi iussio comprehendi vtiliter possit.
units.tr: Although an heir cannot be instituted directly: in confirmed codicils all things can be left directly, except an inheritance. An heir cannot be instituted by confirmed codicils, although an order to restore can usefully be included in those same confirmed codicils.

units.la: ] id est, per actionem, vt formula hypothecaria, & in tit. 19. formula communi diuidundo, familiæ erciscundæ, finium regundorum. Actio porro nihil aliud est quam formula. Cuiac. hic & Paci.
units.tr: (Gloss, not marked in the original): that is, by action, as in the hypothecary formula, and in title 19 the formula for common division, for partition of an inheritance, and for fixing boundaries. Moreover, an action is nothing other than a formula. Cuiacius here and Pacius.

units.la: Qui fideicommissarius ] De prætore fideicommissario adde d.l. 2. §. 32. ff. de orig. iuris, l. 78. §. 6. ff. de legat. 3. l. 4. in sin. ff. qui ad libert. Gothofred. hic.
units.tr: Trust-bequest praetor: on the trust-bequest praetor add d. l. 2. §. 32. ff. de orig. iuris; l. 78. §. 6. ff. de legat. 3.; l. 4. at the end, ff. qui ad libert. Gothofred here.

units.la: In prouinciis vero l. cum etiam C. de reb. cred. Hodie fideicommissa per actionem petuntur, & omnino sublatæ sunt à Iustiniano legatorum & fideicommissorum differentiæ.
units.tr: In the provinces: l. cum etiam C. de reb. cred. Today trust bequests are sought by action, and Justinian has altogether abolished the differences between legacies and trust bequests.

units.la: Pœnæ causa ] In eo fideicommissa olim etiam non differebant tit. 24. §. 17. sup. eod.
units.tr: For a penalty: in this respect trust bequests formerly did not differ either: title 24. §. 17 above, same title.

units.la: Incertæ personæ ] In eo quoque olim conueniebant fideicommissa & legata, tit. 24. §. 18. sup. eod.
units.tr: To an uncertain person: in this too trust bequests and legacies formerly agreed: title 24. §. 18 above, same title.

units.la: Trebelliano senatusconsulto ] vid. Inst. de fideicommiss. hæred. & ad S.C. Trebell.
units.tr: Trebellian senatus-consultum: see Inst. de fideicommiss. hered. and on the S.C. Trebellianum.

units.la: Vel deducta ] Legendum, vt. Hæc vero de Pegasiano & Trebelliano fusius explicantur in Instit. Iustiniani, neque desiderant interpretationem. Cuiac.
units.tr: Or with a deduction: it should be read as ut (that). These matters concerning the Pegasian and Trebellian are explained more fully in the Institutes of Justinian, and do not need interpretation. Cuiacius.

units.la: Igitur si de hæreditate incapaci restituenda promiserit, primum omnium hæreditas fisco vindicatur, nec si exhausta sit hæreditas, Falcidia retinetur, verum Falcidia fisco applicatur ex rescripto Diui Pij l. 3. C. ad l. Falcid. l. heres ff. de his quib. ut indign. Cuiac. hic & Paci.
units.tr: Therefore, if he has promised to restore an inheritance that is incapable of being restored, the inheritance is first of all claimed for the treasury, and even if the inheritance has been exhausted, the Falcidian deduction is not retained; rather the Falcidian share is applied to the treasury by the rescript of the deified Pius. l. 3. C. ad l. Falcid.; l. heres ff. de his quib. ut indign.; Cuiacius here and Pacius.

units.la: Libertas dari] vid. §. 2. Inst. de sing. reb. per fideicomm.
units.tr: Libertas dari] see §. 2, Inst. de singulis rebus per fideicommissum.

units.la: Tit. XXVI. De Legitimis heredibus.
units.tr: Title XXVI. On Legitimate Heirs.

units.la: INtestatorum ingenuorum hereditates pertinent primum ad suos heredes, id est, liberos qui in potestate sunt, cæterosque qui in liberorum loco sunt. Si sui heredes non sunt, ad consanguineos, id est, fratres & sorores ex eodem patre. Si nec hi sunt, ad reliquos adgnatos proximos, id est, cognatos virilis sexus, per mares descendentes, eiusdem familiæ: id enim cautum est lege duodecim Tabularum, ac si intestatus moritur, cui suus extabit heres, nec adgnatus proximus familiam habebit.
units.tr: The inheritances of those dying intestate who were freeborn pass first to their heirs of the body (sui heredes), that is, the children who are under power (in potestate), and the others who stand in the place of children. If there are no heirs of the body, they pass to the blood relations (consanguinei), that is, brothers and sisters from the same father. If there are none of these, they pass to the nearest remaining agnates, that is, male-line relatives descending through males, of the same family. For the law of the Twelve Tables provides this: if a man dies intestate, having an heir of his own, and no nearest agnate, he shall have the family.

units.la: Si defunctus sit filius ex altero filio mortuo, iam nepos vnus, vel etiam plures, ad omnes hereditas pertinet, non vt in capita diuidatur, sed vt in stirpes, id est, vt filius solus mediam partem habeat, & nepotes quotquot sunt alteram dimidiam. Æquum est enim nepotes patris sui loco succedere, & eam partem habere, quam pater eorum si viueret, habiturus esset.
units.tr: If the deceased is the son of a son who has already died, then one grandson, or even several, takes the whole inheritance, not divided by heads but by stirpes: that is, the son alone has half the share, and however many grandsons there are share the other half. For it is fair that grandchildren succeed in their father's place and have the share their father would have had if he were alive.

units.la: Quandiu suus heres speratur heres fieri posse, tandiu locus agnatis non est: velut si vxor defuncti prægnans sit, aut filius apud hostes sit.
units.tr: As long as an heir of the body may be hoped to become an heir, there is no place for agnates: for example, if the wife of the deceased is pregnant, or a son is among the enemy.

units.la: Agnatorum hereditates diuiduntur in capita, veluti si sit fratris filius, & alterius fratris duo plures ve liberi: quotquot sunt ab vtraque parte personæ, tot fiunt portiones, vt singuli singulas capiant.
units.tr: Inheritances of agnates are divided by heads, as when there is a son of one brother and two or more children of another brother. As many persons as there are on each side, so many portions are made, so that each takes a single portion.

units.la: Si plures eodem gradu sunt agnati, & quidam eorum hereditatem ad se pertinere voluerint, vel antequam adierint, decesserint, eorum pars accrescit his qui adierint. Quod si nemo eorum adierit, ad insequentem gradum ex lege hereditas non transmittitur: quoniam in legitimis hereditatibus successio non est.
units.tr: If several agnates are in the same degree, and some of them wish the inheritance to belong to them, or die before they have entered upon it, their share accrues to those who have entered upon it. But if none of them has entered upon it, the inheritance is not passed by law to the next degree, since there is no succession in legitimate inheritances.

units.la: Ad fœminas vltra consanguineorum gradum legitima hereditas non pertinet: itaque soror fratri sororive legitima heres fit.
units.tr: A legitimate inheritance does not pass to women beyond the degree of blood relations; thus a sister becomes the legitimate heir of her brother or sister.

units.la: Ad liberos matris intestatæ hereditas ex lege 12. Tabularum non pertinebat: quia fœminæ suos heredes non habent. Sed postea IMPP. Antonini & Commodi oratione in Senatu recitata, id actum est, vt sine in manum conuentione, marrum legitimæ hereditates ad filios pertinent, exclusis consanguineis, & reliquis agnatis.
units.tr: By the law of the Twelve Tables, the inheritance of a mother who died intestate did not pass to her children, because women have no heirs of the body. But afterwards, when the Emperors Antoninus and Commodus had a speech read in the Senate, it was provided that, without marriage with manus, the legitimate inheritances of mothers pass to their children, with blood relations and other agnates excluded.

units.la: Intestati filij hereditas ad matrem ex lege duodecim Tabularum non pertinet: sed srius liberorum habeat, ingenua trium, libertina quatuor, legitima heres fit ex Senatusconsulto Tertulliano: si tamen et filio neque suus heres sit, quiue inter suos heredes ad bonorum possessionem sessionem à Prætore vocatur: neque pater, ad quem lege hereditas, bonorumve possessio cum re pertinet, neque frater consanguineus. Quod si soror consanguinea sit, ad utraque pertinere iubetur hereditas.
units.tr: By the law of the Twelve Tables, the inheritance of a child who died intestate did not pass to the mother. But by the Tertullian senatusconsult she becomes a legitimate heir if she has three children (if freeborn) or four (if freedwoman); provided that the child has no heir of the body, and that she is not called by the praetor to possession of the goods among the heirs of the body; and provided that neither the father, to whom the inheritance or possession of goods belongs by law, nor a blood brother is there. But if there is a blood sister, the inheritance is ordered to pass to both.

units.la: Legitimis haredibus ] id est, de hereditate ab intestato 3. Inst. 1.
units.tr: Legitimis heredibus] that is, on the inheritance from intestacy, 3. Inst. 1.

units.la: Primum ad suos] §. 1. Inst. de haredit. ab intestato vid. Goth. ad l. XII. tabul. lib. 2.
units.tr: Primum ad suos] §. 1, Inst. de heredit. ab intestato; see Goth. ad l. XII. tabul. lib. 2.

units.la: Cui suus extabit haeres nec ] Hæc sunt perturbata. Legendum est, Ac si intestatus moritur, cui suus haeres, nec extabit adgnatus, &c. & hæc prima legis verba Paulus interpretatur in l. si quis posthumos §. pen. de lib. & post. reliqua in l. pronuntiatio de verb. signif. Apparet autem ex hac 12. tab. lege suorum nomen esse ex 12. tab. quod Callistratus tradit in l. liberorum de verb. signif. Hos enim omnes, inquit suorum appellatione lex 12. tab. comprehendit. Igitur in l. vlt. de bon. dam. In iure ciuili, id est, in 12. tab. possim similia exempla proferre quam plurima, in quibus ius ciuile pro 12. tab. accipitur. vid. Cuiac. & Pacium hic.
units.tr: Cui suus extabit haeres nec] These words are corrupt. It should read: Ac si intestatus moritur, cui suus haeres, nec extabit adgnatus, &c. Paulus interprets these first words of the law in l. si quis posthumos §. pen. de lib. & post.; the rest in l. pronuntiatio de verb. signif. It appears from this law of the Twelve Tables that the word suorum comes from the Twelve Tables, as Callistratus relates in l. liberorum de verb. signif. For the Twelve Tables, he says, include all these under the term suorum. Therefore in l. vlt. de bon. dam. In the civil law, that is, in the Twelve Tables, I could bring forward very many similar examples in which the civil law is taken to mean the Twelve Tables; see Cuiac. & Pacium hic.

units.la: Familiam habeto ] leg. 195. in sin. ff. de verb. signific.
units.tr: Familiam habeto] leg. 195, in sin. ff. de verb. signific.

units.la: Si defunctus ] Legendum, si defuncti sit filius, & ex altero filio iam mortuo nepos §. cum filius de hared. quae ab intest. defer. Sensus hic est. Nepotes ex filio iam mortuo avo in stirpes cum tum patruo succedere. Plane sunt hæ perpetuo in liberorum linea obseruandæ regulæ, Proximior vlteriorem non excludit, Hæreditates pro stirpibus diuiduntur, non pro virilibus portionibus. Cuiac. & Pac. h.
units.tr: Si defunctus] It should read: if the deceased is the son of a son who has already died, and grandchildren from a son already dead, see §. cum filius de hared. quae ab intest. defer. The sense is this: grandchildren from a son who has died before the grandfather succeed in stirpes along with their uncles. Clearly these are rules to be observed always in the line of descendants: the nearer does not exclude the more remote; inheritances are divided by stirpes, not by equal shares per head. Cuiac. & Pac. h.

units.la: Vt in stirpes ] §. vlt. in f. Inst. de hared. ab intest. vid. Goth. ad l. 12. tab. lib. 2.
units.tr: Ut in stirpes] §. vlt. in f. Inst. de hared. ab intest.; see Goth. ad l. 12. tab. lib. 2.

units.la: Speratur hæres ] l. 3. ff si pars hereditat. l. 30. §. 1. ff. de adquir. hared. l. 5. in sin. ff. unde legitimi.
units.tr: Speratur hæres ] l. 3. ff. si pars hereditatis; l. 30. §. 1. ff. de adquirenda hereditate; l. 5. in fine, ff. unde legitimi.

units.la: Tandiu locus ] Venter seu posthumus agnatos defuncti excludit l. 26. ff. de statu.
units.tr: Tandiu locus] The womb, or posthumous child, excludes the agnates of the deceased; l. 26. ff. de statu.

units.la: Agnatorum hereditates ] Ergo superiores duæ regulæ in agnatorum serie non obseruantur. nam etsi sit frater, & filius fratris iam mortui, frater solus succedit. §. hoc etiam §. si plures de legi. agnator. success. Ex nouella Iustiniani frater non præfertur atque vna fratrum filii succedunt. Vltra fratrum filios in capita fit diuisio, quod & inter ipsos fratrum filios nullis concurrentibus fratribus, obseruari Constantinus probat lib. 5. epitom. & verum est. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Agnatorum hereditates] Therefore the two earlier rules are not observed in the series of agnates; for even if there is a brother and the son of a brother who has already died, the brother alone succeeds; §. hoc etiam; §. si plures de legi. agnator. success. By a novel of Justinian, the brother is not preferred, and the sons of brothers succeed together. Beyond the sons of brothers, the division is by heads, which Constantine also shows is observed among the sons of brothers themselves when no brothers are present; lib. 5. epitom.; and this is true. Cuiac. h.

units.la: Diuiduntur in capita ] vid. Gothof. ad Nouel. 118. c. 3. in sin.
units.tr: Diuiduntur in capita] see Gothof. ad Nouel. 118. c. 3. in sin.

units.la: Duo pluresve ] d c. 3. adde §. 4. Inst. de legit. agnator. 2. Caius 8. c. 3.
units.tr: Duo pluresve] d. c. 3.; add §. 4, Inst. de legit. agnator. 2.; Caius 8. c. 3.

units.la: Si plures ] l. si ex pluribus de suis & legit. her.
units.tr: Si plures] l. si ex pluribus de suis & legit. her.

units.la: Adcrescit his ] §. vlt. Inst. de S. C. Orphitiano. vid. Gothofred. ad leg. 9. ff. de suis. Add. Paul. 4. sent. 8. §. vlt.
units.tr: Adcrescit his] §. vlt. Inst. de S. C. Orphitiano. See Gothofred. ad leg. 9. ff. de suis. Add Paul. 4. sent. 8. §. vlt.

units.la: Quod si nemo ] In suis, in legitimis non est successio. quia, vt Paul. ait li. 4. sentent. omnis legitima successio proximiori defertur. In honorariis est successio, vt ecce, non petente auunculo magno, succedit propior sobrinus. l.
units.tr: Quod si nemo] In heirs of the body there is no succession among legitimate heirs, because, as Paulus says in lib. 4 sentent., every legitimate succession is deferred to the nearer. In honorary succession there is succession: for example, if the great uncle does not seek it, the nearer cousin succeeds. l.

units.la: 2. C. de success. edict. At filio non adeunte, nepos non admittitur, nisi ex iure praetorio, ex parte vnde liberi. Ex constitut. Iustiniani in legitimis hodie est successio. §. placebat. de legit. agnat. success. nam & in legitimis tutoribus est successio. l. 3. §. pen. de leg. tut. (Cuiac. & Pacius h.)
units.tr: 2. C. de success. edict. But if the son does not enter, the grandson is not admitted, except by praetorian law, on the side from which the children come. By the constitution of Justinian, there is now succession among legitimate heirs; §. placebat, de legit. agnat. success. For there is also succession among legitimate guardians; l. 3. §. pen. de leg. tut. (Cuiac. & Pacius h.)

units.la: In legitimis ] Secus in hereditariis leg. 2. C. de successorio edicto.
units.tr: In legitimis] It is otherwise in hereditary succession; leg. 2. C. de successorio edicto.

units.la: Vltra consanguineorum gradum ] idque iure ciuili & l. Voconia institutum, Paul. 4. sent. 8. §. 3. de lege Voconia vid. Cuiac. ad tit. Inst. de l. Falcid. Gothof. hic.
units.tr: Vltra consanguineorum gradum] and this was established by civil law and the Voconian law; Paulus, 4 sent. 8. §. 3.; on the Voconian law see Cuiac. ad tit. Inst. de l. Falcid.; Gothof. hic.

units.la: Ex lege 12. tabularum ] vid. Goth. in not. ad ll. 12. tab. lib. 2.
units.tr: Ex lege 12. tabularum] see Goth. in not. ad ll. 12. tab. lib. 2.

units.la: Non pertinebat ] Instit. de S.C. Tertull. & in princ. de S. C. Orphit.
units.tr: Non pertinebat] Instit. de S.C. Tertull. and in princ. de S. C. Orphit.

units.la: Imperatorum , Antonini & Commodi ] l. sacratissimi ad S. C. Tertull. quam & S.C. secutum est, quod dicitur Orphitianum.
units.tr: Imperatorum, Antonini & Commodi] l. sacratissimi ad S. C. Tertull., which was also followed by the senatusconsult called Orphitian.

units.la: Vt sine in manum conuentione ] etiamsi vulgo quaesiti sint liberi. vid. tit. 9. sup. eod.
units.tr: Vt sine in manum conuentione] even if the children were born outside marriage; see tit. 9. sup. eod.

units.la: Ex lege 12. tab. ] Goth. ad ll. 12. tab.
units.tr: Ex lege 12. tab.] Goth. ad ll. 12. tab.

units.la: Non pertinet ] Instit. de S. C. Tertull. in princ.
units.tr: Does not apply Instit. de S. C. Tertull. in princ.

units.la: Ex S.C. Tertulliano ] Quod factum est Diui Pij temporibus.
units.tr: From the Senatus consultum Tertullianum This was done in the times of the divine Pius.

units.la: Sitamen j quando mater succedat filio.
units.tr: If however, when the mother succeeds her son.

units.la: Quiue inter suos ] vt puta emancipatus.
units.tr: Or among their own: for example, an emancipated son.

units.la: Neque pater ad quem lege hereditas ] Hæreditas aut bonorum poss. vnde legitimi, siin emancipatione manumissor exstiterit.
units.tr: Nor the father to whom the inheritance comes by law: an inheritance or possession of goods, whence the legitimate heirs, if the father was the manumittor in the emancipation.

units.la: Bonorum possessio ] vnde decem personæ, si in emancipatione manumissor non exstiterit. l.si ad patrem de suis & legit. her. §. sunt autem de bonor possess. Si ex testamento præteritus sit, non manumissori datur querela. l.1. §. final. si à parent. quis fuer. manum. manumissori bonorum possessio contra tab. vt manumissori, querela vt patri. l.si à milite §. final. de milit. testam. l. pater filium. l. filio §.1. de inofficioso testam. ex Iustiniani constitutione pater pro manumissore semper habetur, id est, contraxisse fiduciam semper videtur. Cuiac.h.
units.tr: Possession of goods: whence the ten persons, if the father was not the manumittor in the emancipation. l.si ad patrem de suis & legit. her. §. sunt autem de bonor possess. If a son has been passed over in a will, the manumittor is not given a complaint. l.1. §. final. si à parent. quis fuer. manum. The manumittor has possession of goods against the tablets, as manumittor; the complaint is as father. l.si à milite §. final. de milit. testam. l. pater filium. l. filio §.1. de inofficioso testam. By Justinian's constitution the father is always regarded as manumittor, that is, he is always held to have contracted the fiduciary obligation. Cuiac.h.

units.la: Ad utrasque ] Ad matrem pro dimidia, si filia decesserit, pro virili, si filius. l. 2. C. Theod. de secund. nupt. sed hæc vt sint à Iustiniano mutata, vid. in Instit.
units.tr: To both: to the mother, for half if the daughter has died, for a share per head if the son has died. l. 2. C. Theod. de secund. nupt. sed hæc vt sint à Iustiniano mutata, vid. in Instit.

units.la: Tit. XXVII. De Libertorum successionibus vel bonis.
units.tr: Title XXVII. On the successions to freedmen, or their goods.

units.la: Libertorum intestatorum hereditas primum ad suos heredes pertinet; deinde ad eos quorum libertifunt, velut patronum, patronam, liberosve patroni.
units.tr: The inheritance of freedmen who die intestate first belongs to their own heirs (sui heredes); then to those whose freedmen they were, such as the patron, the patroness, or the children of the patron.

units.la: Sifit patronus & alterius patroni filius, ad solum patronum hereditas pertinet.
units.tr: If the patron and the son of another patron are both living, the inheritance belongs to the patron alone.

units.la: Item patroni filius patroni nepotibus obstat.
units.tr: Likewise, the son of a patron stands in the way of the grandchildren of the patron.

units.la: Ad liberos patronorum hereditas defuncti pertinet, vt in capita, non in stirpes diuidatur.
units.tr: The inheritance of the deceased passes to the children of the patrons, and is divided per capita, not per stirpes.

units.la: Legitimæ hereditaris ius quod ex lege duodecim Tabularum descendit, capitis minutione amittitur.
units.tr: The right of legitimate inheritance, which descended from the law of the Twelve Tables, is lost by loss of civil status (capitis deminutio).

units.la: Ad suos hæredes ] Institut. de successf. libert. in princ.
units.tr: To their own heirs ] Institutes, On the successions of freedmen, at the beginning.

units.la: Patroni nepotibus obstat ] l. 23. §. 1. ff. de bon. libert. in princ.
units.tr: Stands in the way of the grandchildren of the patron ] Digest, law 23, §1, On the goods of freedmen, at the beginning.

units.la: Ad liberos patronorum ] l. si libertus praterito §. vlt. de bon. libertor.
units.tr: To the children of the patrons ] Law "si libertus praterito", final §, On the goods of freedmen.

units.la: Vt in capita ] vid. Goth. in notis ad l. 23. in f. ff. de bonis libertor.
units.tr: Per capita ] See Gothofredus in his notes on law 23, at the end, On the goods of freedmen.

units.la: Legitimæ hereditatis ] Hæc sententia de ingenuorum sententia accipienda est. l. capit. de suis & legit. hared. non libertorum d. l. si libertus praterito in princ. eademque de tutela legitima diximus tit. 2. nec vero quispiam ex inscriptione huius tituli argumentetur: nam ea sectiones non sunt Vlpiani, quinimo sunt, omnia meo iudicio legenda vno contextu. eis quidem certe nihil est inconcinnius, ait Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Of legitimate inheritance ] This statement is to be understood of the inheritance of freeborn persons (ingenui), see the law "capit." On heirs of their own and legitimate heirs; not of freedmen, see the said law "si libertus praterito" at the beginning; and we have said the same of legitimate guardianship under title 2. Nor should anyone argue from the inscription of this title, for those divisions are not Ulpian's; indeed, in my judgement they should all be read as one continuous text. Certainly nothing is more incongruous than they are, say Cujas and Pacius here.

units.la: Tit. XXVIII. De Possessionibus dandis.
units.tr: Tit. XXVIII. On Granting Possessions

units.la: BOnorum possessio datur, aut contra tabulas testamenti, aut aduersus tabulas intestati.
units.tr: Bonorum possessio is granted either against the tablets of a will, or against the tablets of intestacy.

units.la: Contra tabulas bonorum possessio datur liberis emancipatis, testamento præteritis, licet legitima ad eos non pertineat hereditas.
units.tr: Possession of goods against the tablets is granted to emancipated children who were passed over in the will, even though they are not entitled to the legitimate inheritance.

units.la: Bonorum possessio contra tabulas liberis tam naturalibus, quam adoptiuis datur. Sed naturalibus quidem emancipatis: non tamen & illis, qui in adoptiua familia sunt. Adoptiuis autem, his tantum qui in potestate manserunt.
units.tr: Possession of goods against the tablets is granted to natural children and adopted children alike. But to natural children only if they have been emancipated, and not to those who remain in the adoptive family. To adopted children it is granted only to those who remained under power.

units.la: Emancipatis liberis ex edicto datur bonorum possessio, si parati sunt cauere patribus suis qui in potestate manserunt, bona, quæ moriente patre habuerunt, se collaturos.
units.tr: By the edict, possession of goods is granted to emancipated children if they are ready to give security to their fathers, who remained under power, that they will bring into collation the goods the father had at his death.

units.la: Secundum tabulas bonorum possessio datur scriptis hæredibus, scilicet si eorum quibus contra tabulas competit, nemo sit, aut petere nolint.
units.tr: Possession of goods according to the tablets is granted to the instituted heirs, namely if there is no one to whom possession against the tablets belongs, or if such persons are unwilling to seek it.

units.la: Etiam si iure ciuili non valeat testamentum, forte quod familiæ mancipatio vel nuncupatio defuit, si signatum testamentum sit, non minus quam septem testium ciuium Romanorum signis, bonorum possessio datur.
units.tr: Even if the will is not valid under the civil law, perhaps because the mancipation or nuncupation to the family was lacking, possession of goods is nonetheless granted if the will was sealed with the seals of not less than seven Roman citizen witnesses.

units.la: Intestati datur bonorum possessio per septem gradus. Primo gradu liberis: Secundo legitimis heredibus : Tertio proximis cognatis: Quarto familiæ: Quinto patrono, patronæ, liberisve patroni, patronæve: Sexto viro, vxori: Septimo cognatis manumissoris, quibus per legem Furiam plus mille asses capere licet, si nemo sit ad quem bonorum possessio pertinere possit: aut si quidem, sed ius suum omiserit, populo bona deferuntur ex lege Iulia caducaria.
units.tr: Possession of goods on intestacy is granted through seven degrees. In the first degree, to the children; in the second, to the legitimate heirs; in the third, to the nearest cognates; in the fourth, to the family; in the fifth, to the patron, the patroness, or the children of the patron or patroness; in the sixth, to the husband or wife; in the seventh, to the cognates of the manumitter, who by the Furian law may take more than a thousand asses, if there is no one to whom possession can belong; or, if there is, but he has let his right lapse, the goods are assigned to the people under the Julian law on caducous property.

units.la: Liberis bonorum possessio datur, tam his qui in potestate vsque in mortis tempus suerunt, quam emancipatis, item adoptiuis, non tamen etiam in adoptionem datis.
units.tr: Possession of goods is granted to children, both to those who were under power up to the time of death and to the emancipated, likewise to adopted children, but not to those who were given in adoption.

units.la: Proximi cognati bonorum possessionem accipiunt, non solum per fœminini sexus personam cognati, sed etiam agnati capite deminuti. Nam licet legitimum ius agnationis capitis minutione amiserint, natura tamen cognati manent.
units.tr: The nearest cognates receive possession of goods, not only cognates through a person of the female sex, but also agnates who have suffered loss of status. For although they have lost the legitimate right of agnation through loss of status, they nevertheless remain cognates by nature.

units.la: Bonorum possessio datur parentibus & liberis intra annum, ex quo petere potuerunt: ceteris intra centum dies.
units.tr: Possession of goods is granted to parents and children within a year from the time when they could first seek it; to others within a hundred days.

units.la: Qui omnes intra id tempus si non petierint, ad bonorum possessionem sequens gradus admittitur: perinde ac si superiores non essent, idque per septem gradus fit.
units.tr: If all these do not seek it within that time, the next degree is admitted to possession of goods, just as if the earlier ones did not exist; and this proceeds through seven degrees.

units.la: Hi quibus ex successorio edicto bonorum possessio datur, heredes quidem non sunt, sed heredis loco constituuntur beneficio Prætoris.
units.tr: Those to whom possession of goods is granted by the edict on succession are not indeed heirs, but are placed in the position of heirs by the benefit of the Praetor.

units.la: Ideoque seu ipsi agant, seu cum his agatur, sictitiis actionibus opus est: in quibus heredes esse finguntur. Bonorum possessio aut cum re datur, aut sine re. Cum re, si is qui accepit cum effectu bona retineat: sine re, quum alius iure ciuili euincere hereditatem possit: veluti si suus heres intestato sit. Bonorum possessio sine re est, quum suus heres euincere hereditatem iure legitimo possit.
units.tr: Therefore, whether they sue themselves or are sued by others, fictitious actions are needed, in which they are feigned to be heirs. Possession of goods is granted either with the thing or without it. With the thing, if the one who receives it keeps the goods with effect; without the thing, when another can overturn the inheritance by the civil law, as when a sui heres dies intestate. Possession of goods is without the thing when a sui heres can overturn the inheritance by legitimate right.

units.la: De possessionibus ] 3. Inst. 10. 37. ff. 1.
units.tr: On possessions] Inst. 10. 37. ff. 1.

units.la: Contra tabulas ] §. 2. sup. eod.
units.tr: Against the tablets] §. 2. sup. eod.

units.la: Aduersus tabulas ] §. 5. inf. eod. id est, secundum vid. tit. 20. §. 14. sup. eod.
units.tr: Against the tablets] §. 5. inf. eod., id est, secundum vid. tit. 20. §. 14. sup. eod.

units.la: Intestati ] Legendum, aut intestati.
units.tr: Intestati] Read, aut intestati.

units.la: Contra tabulas ] §. 3. Inst. de bonor. poss. & 37. ff. 4. & 6. C. 12.
units.tr: Against the tablets] §. 3. Inst. de bonor. poss. & 37. ff. 4. & 6. C. 12.

units.la: Emancipatis ] imo & suis, siue sint naturales, siue legitimi, siue posthumi. §. 3. infr. eod. Sed non est necessaria iure ciuili. Cuiac. & Gothofred.
units.tr: Emancipatis] Indeed also to the sui, whether they are natural, legitimate, or posthumous. §. 3. infr. eod. But it is not necessary by the civil law. Cuiac. & Gothofred.

units.la: Tam naturalibus ] l. 1. ff. de bonor. poss. contra tabul.
units.tr: Even to natural children (Digest 37.4.1, on possession of goods against the tablets)

units.la: Non tamen & illis ] Eos qui in adoptiua familia sunt, Praetor non nouit, non vocat inter suos. Vnde consequens est, inter legitimos quoque eos non vocari. nam qui sui non sunt, proculdubio nec legitimi sunt. l. scripto. unde lib. l. de bonis §. 1. de Carboniano edicto. Cuiac. b.
units.tr: Non tamen & illis] The Praetor does not recognise those who are in an adoptive family, and does not call them among his own. Hence it follows that they are not called among the legitimate either; for those who are not sui are doubtless not legitimate either. l. scripto. unde lib. l. de bonis §. 1. de Carboniano edicto. Cuiac. b.

units.la: Si parati sunt cauere] l. 1. §. 9. ff. de collat.
units.tr: If they are ready to give security] l. 1. §. 9. ff. de collat.

units.la: Patribus ] Manifestum est, legi debere, fratribus, cauere autem debent, vel re ipsa conferre.
units.tr: Patribus] It is plain that it should be read fratribus; they must give security, or else bring the goods into collation in fact.

units.la: Secundum tabulas ] vid. tit. C. de bonor. poss. secundum tab. 6. C. 11. ff. si tabula testamenti extabunt. add. §. 3. vers. secunda. Inst. de bonor. possess. & 6. C. 12. de bonor. possess. secundum tab. Gothofred. hic.
units.tr: According to the tablets (see title C. on possession of goods according to the tablets; Digest 38.6, with the note "if the tablets of the will survive"; add §3, second clause, Institutes on possession of goods; and C. 12 on possession of goods according to the tablets; Godefroy here)

units.la: Scilicet si eorum quibus contra tabulas ] Nam prior est contra tabulas quam secundum tabulas. inde ex prima parte, vel ex primo edicto bonorum possessionem dari, id est, contra tabulas. I. ideoque l. scriptus de Carbon. edict. L. 2. de bon. liber. Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Namely if there is no one to whom possession against the tablets belongs] For the possession against the tablets comes before that according to the tablets. Hence possession is granted by the first part, or by the first edict, that is, against the tablets. I. ideoque l. scriptus de Carbon. edict. L. 2. de bon. liber. Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Etiam si iure civili ] Inde edictum translatitium Verris, si de hereditate ambigitur, & tabulae testamenti obsignatae non minus multis signis quam e lege oporteat, ad me proferentur: secundum tabulas testamenti potissimum hereditatem dabo. qua de re & in l. 23. diximus. ait Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: Even if by the civil law] Hence the translatitian edict of Verres: if there is doubt about an inheritance, and the tablets of the will, sealed with not fewer seals than the law requires, are brought before me, I will give the inheritance chiefly according to the tablets of the will. On this matter we have also spoken in the law 23. Thus Cuiac. here.

units.la: Non minus] tit. 23. §. 6 sup. eod. l. 2. C. de bonor. possess. secund. tab.
units.tr: Not fewer] tit. 23. §. 6 sup. eod. l. 2. C. de bonor. possess. secund. tab.

units.la: Septem gradus ] Omissa est bonorum possessio, unde decem personae: sed si pater manumissor sit, sane verum est, septem duntaxat gradus esse.
units.tr: Seven degrees] The possession of goods is omitted, whence there are ten persons; but if the father is the manumitter, it is certainly true that there are only seven degrees.

units.la: Secundo legitimis] inter quos & Patroni sint Patronorum que liberi.
units.tr: Secondly, to the legitimate] among whom are also the children of the patrons and of the patronesses.

units.la: Tertio
units.tr: Third

units.la: Tertio proximis cognatis ] Tertio decem personis, quas extraneo manumissori praeferebat. vid. §. 3. Inst. de bonor. poss. sed haec successio hic omittitur.
units.tr: Tertio proximis cognatis: Third, the nearest blood relations, who were preferred to an outside manumitter, ten persons in all. See §. 3, Institutes, on possession of goods. But this succession is omitted here.

units.la: Quarto familiae ] id est, agnatis Patroni, haec dicitur, Tum quasi ex familia. sic enim lege in Institutionibus Iustiniani. ait Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Quarto familiae: This refers to the agnates of the patron, the so-called "family" (tum quasi ex familia), for so you read in the Institutes of Justinian. Cujacius, on this passage.

units.la: Sine mo sit ] Hoc est, initium alterius sententiae.
units.tr: Sine mo sit: That is, the beginning of the other sentence.

units.la: Ex lege Iulia caducaria ] de hac in l. quidam §. quotiens de legat. 1. item in l. ergo §. eadem constitutio, de fideicomm. lib. in illo loco, quare & si caducis legionis, vel, ut alij codices habent, caducis legionibus, bona delata sint, idem erit probandum: nam caducariis legibus, legendum esse omni asseveratione confirmamus, id est, legibus Iuliis. quae enim delata dicuntur, legibus delata ut sint, necesse est. denique hoc significat, vacantibus bonis fisco vindicaris constitutionem cessare. ut in l. quod Diuo. de manum. testam. Haec vero notae Cad. leg. errori causam dedere. Cuiac. & Pac. h.
units.tr: Ex lege Iulia caducaria: On this, see the law "quidam" §. "quotiens", de legatis 1; likewise the law "ergo" §. "eadem constitutio", de fideicommissis, book ... In that passage: "wherefore, even if the goods have been delivered to the caducary legion, or, as other manuscripts read, the caducary legions, the same must be held; for we affirm with every assurance that 'caducariis legibus' should be read, that is, by the Julian laws. For those things are said to be delivered, it is necessary that they be delivered by the laws." Finally, this means that the constitution ceases when the goods are vacant and claimed by the fisc, as in the law "quod Divus", de manumissis testamento. But the note on the Codex of laws has given rise to this error. Cujacius and Pacius, on this passage.

units.la: Liberis bonorum ] vid. tit. ff. unde liberi.
units.tr: Liberis bonorum: See the title in the Digest, "unde liberi".

units.la: Ex successorio edicto ] successorium edictum eo dicitur, quod det successionem inter bonorum possessores: quanquam & eam quoque clausulam contineat, quae definit tempora petendae bonorum possessionis. Caeterum ex illa potissimum parte appellationem sumit, qua in locum eorum, qui intra tempora petitionis bonorum possess. non admiserunt, sequentes vocantur, qui & ob eam causam ex successorio edicto, ex successoria parte, ex beneficio successorij edicti, ex successorio capite, venire dicuntur. l. vlt. l. 1. § sed videndum. de succeff. edict. l. vlt. C. eod. l. 1. § pen. de iur. & fact. igno. Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Ex successorio edicto: The successory edict is so called because it grants succession among the possessors of goods; although it also contains that clause which fixes the time for claiming possession of goods. Moreover, it takes its name chiefly from that part by which those who follow are called in the place of those who did not admit the claim within the time allowed for seeking possession of goods. For this reason they are said to come "from the successory edict", "from the successory part", "by the benefit of the successory edict", "from the successory chapter". See the law "ultimo", the law 1 §. "sed videndum", de successoriis edictis; the law "ultimo" C. eod.; the law 1 §. "penultimo", de iuris et facti ignorantia. Cujacius and Pacius here.

units.la: Si suus hares intestato ] Hæc ab interpunctionibus mendosa sunt. nam sic distingui ea oportet: Si suus hæres intestato sit bonorum poss. sine re est, cum, &c. Cuiac. b.
units.tr: Si suus heres intestato: These words are faulty because of the punctuation. For they ought to be divided thus: "If a sui heres has died intestate, the possession of goods is without a claim, when, etc." Cujacius, on this passage.

units.la: Tit. XXIX. De Bonis libertorum.
units.tr: Title XXIX. Concerning the Goods of Freedmen.

units.la: Cuius Romani liberti hereditatem lex duodecim Tabularum patrono defert, si intestato sine suo herede libertus decesserit. Ideoque sive testamento facto decedat, licet suus heres ei non sit, seu intestato, & suus heres ei sit, quanuis non naturalis, sed vxor puta quæ in manu fuit, vel adoptivus filius, lex patrono nihil præstat. Sed ex edicto Prætoris si testamento facto libertus moriatur, aut vt nihil, aut minus quam partem dimidiam bonorum patrono relinquat contra tabulas testamenti, partis dimidiæ bonorum possessio illi datur, nisi libertus aliquem ex naturalibus liberis successorem sibi relinquat, sive intestato decedat, & vxorem forte in manum vel adoptiuum priuum filium relinquat, æque partis mediæ bonorum possessio contra suos heredes patrono datur.
units.tr: By the law of the Twelve Tables, the inheritance of a Roman freedman passes to his patron, if the freedman dies intestate and without a heir of his own body. Therefore, whether he dies after making a will, even though he has no heir of his own (suus heres), or dies intestate but has a heir of his own who is not a natural child, such as a wife who was in the hand of her husband (in manu), or an adoptive son, the law gives the patron nothing. But by the edict of the Praetor, if a freedman dies after making a will and leaves the patron either nothing or less than half of the goods, the patron may claim against the will the possession of half of the goods (bonorum possessio partis dimidiae). This is refused to him if the freedman leaves a successor among his natural children. Likewise, if he dies intestate and leaves a wife in the hand of her husband or a son adopted by him, the possession of half (bonorum possessio partis mediae) is given to the patron against the heirs of his own body.

units.la: In bonis libertę patrono nihil iuris ex edicto datur. Itaq; si intestata moriatur liberta, semper ad eum hæreditas pertinet.
units.tr: The patron has no right under the edict in the goods of a freedwoman. So if a freedwoman dies intestate, the inheritance always passes to him.

units.la: Licet liberi sint libertæ, quoniam non sunt sui heredes matri, obstat patrono lex Papia Popæa. Postea libertas quatuor liberorum iure tutela patronorum liberauit, & cum intulerit, iam posse eas sine auctoritate patronorum testari, prospexit vt pro numero liberorum libertæ superstitum virilis pars patrono debetur.
units.tr: Although the children of a freedwoman are not her heirs of their own body, the Lex Papia Poppaea stands in the way of the patron. Later, the right of four children freed freedwomen from the guardianship of their patrons, and when it had been established that they could now make a will without the patron's authority, it provided that, according to the number of children surviving the freedwoman, a male share is owed to the patron.

units.la: Liberi patroni virilis sexus, eadem iura in bonis libertorum parentum suorum habent, quæ & ipse patronus. Fœminæ vero, ex lege quidem xii. Tabularum, perinde ius habent, atque masculi patronorum liberi.
units.tr: The children of a male patron have the same rights in the goods of their freedman parents as the patron himself. Daughters, however, under the law of the Twelve Tables, have the same rights as the sons of patrons.

units.la: Contra tabulas autem testamenti liberti, aut ab intestato contra suos heredes non naturalis bonorum possessio eis non competit. Sed si iustrium liberorum habuerunt, etiam hæc iura ex lege Papia Popæa nanciscuntur.
units.tr: But against the will of a freedman, or against the heirs of his own body in intestacy, the non-natural possession of goods does not belong to them. But if they have three children, they obtain these rights also under the Lex Papia Poppaea.

units.la: Patronæ ex bonis libertorum illud ius tantum habent, quod lex xii. Tabularum introduxit. Sed postea lex Papia patronæ ingenuæ duobus liberis honoratæ, libertinæ tribus, id iuris dedit, quod patronus habet ex edicto.
units.tr: Patronesses have from the goods of freedmen only that right which the law of the Twelve Tables introduced. But afterwards the Lex Papia gave patronesses, if freeborn and honoured with two children, or freed-born with three, the same right that a patron has under the edict.

units.la: Item liberis ingenuæ trium libertorum iure honoratæ eadem lex id ius dedit, quod ipsi patrono tribuit.
units.tr: Likewise, the same law gave to the children of a freeborn woman honoured by the right of three freedmen the same right that it gave to the patron himself.

units.la: In Latino secus est §. vlt. de successs. liberti. l. i. C. Theod. de petit. hæred. Legendum; & aut nihil, §. i. de successs. liberti.
units.tr: In the Latin it is otherwise, §. last, de successionibus liberti. l. 1. C. Theod. de petitione hereditatis. It should be read: and either nothing, §. 1, de successionibus liberti.

units.la: Hæc est quinti gradus bonorum possessio: quæ & nullis extantibus suis hæredibus patrono dabitur; si bonorum possess. unde legitimi non admiserit: nam sibi ipsi succedi posse iam pridem receptum est. l. i. §. sed an. de successs. edict. Cuiac. & Pac. hic.
units.tr: This is the fifth degree of possession of goods: which is given to the patron when there are no heirs of his own, if the possession of goods from the legitimate source has not admitted him; for it has long been accepted that one may succeed to oneself. l. 1. §. sed an, de successionibus edicti. Cujacius and Pacius here.

units.la: Nam de liberto prætor edixit, non liberta: & de suis hæredibus, quales fœmina non habet.
units.tr: For the Praetor's edict speaks of a freedman, not a freedwoman, and of heirs of one's own body, of which a woman has none.

units.la: Ergo l. 12. tabular. non Prætoris edicto quæ sequuntur ita restituenda sunt. Nam licet liberi sint libertæ, quoniam non sunt sui hæredes matri, non obstant patrono. Lex Papia Poppæa, libertas; Ait, non obstant patrono. Hoc utique verum est antiquo iure: nam post Senatusconsultum Orphitianum liberi intestatæ libertæ patronos excludunt. l. 1. in princ. & §. si nemo ad Tertull. Ait Cuiac. & Pacius hic.
units.tr: Therefore the law of the Twelve Tables and not the Praetor's edict; the following are to be restored thus. For although the children of a freedwoman are not her heirs of their own body, they do not stand in the way of the patron. The Lex Papia Poppaea, freedwoman; it says they do not stand in the way of the patron. This is certainly true under the ancient law; for after the Senatusconsultum Orphitianum the children of an intestate freedwoman exclude the patrons. l. 1, in princ. and §. si nemo, ad Tertullianum. Cujacius and Pacius say here.

units.la: Eadem lex cauet, vt liberto testaro, vel intestato defuncto relicto vno, vel duobus liberis, patronus virilem, relictis tribus, vt nihil auferat, & vt ita demum quando pauciores sunt quam tres, viriles auferat, si libertus centenarius sit. §. postea de success. lib. Ex quibus apparet, quantum inter libertum & libertam intersit. quod & Valent, in Novel. de libertis probat: Cuia. hic.
units.tr: The same law provides that when a freedman dies by will or intestate, leaving one or two children, the patron takes a male share if three are left, and that he takes a male share only when there are fewer than three, if the freedman is a centenarian. §. afterwards, de successionibus liberti. From these it appears how much difference there is between freedman and freedwoman; which Valentinian also proves in the Novel on freedmen. Cujacius here.

units.la: Fœmina vero ] Iure antiquo, quo & hodie vtimur, inter liberos patroni nulla est differentia sexus: Prætorio iure plus tribuitur masculis quam fœminis. Cuiac.
units.tr: But a woman] By the ancient law, which we still use today, there is no difference of sex among the children of a patron; by the Praetorian law more is given to males than to females. Cujacius.

units.la: Non naturalis ] pro non naturales. Cuiac.
units.tr: Not natural] for not natural (persons). Cujacius.

units.la: Patrona ] est differentia inter patronum & patronam, non quidem ex 12. tab. sed ex lege Papia: nam licet nullis extantibus suis hæredibus, quo casu locus est legi 12. tab. idem patronæ ius, quod patrono sit: iure tamen prætorio non aliter patronæ datur bonorum possessio contra tab. vel ab intestato contra suos hæredes, non naturales, quam si ingenua duobus, libertina tribus liberis honorata sit. Cuiac. h.
units.tr: Patroness] There is a difference between patron and patroness, not indeed under the Twelve Tables but under the Lex Papia: for although, when there are no heirs of one's own (the case in which the law of the Twelve Tables applies), the patroness has the same right as the patron, yet under the Praetorian law the possession of goods is given to a patroness against the will or in intestacy against the non-natural heirs of her own body only if she is honoured by two children if freeborn, or three if freedborn. Cujacius here.

units.la: Patrono] Legendum patronæ.
units.tr: To the patron] Read: to the patroness.

units.la: Honorata ] Oneratæ. §. 3. Inst. de S. C. Tertul.
units.tr: Honoured] Burdened. §. 3, Inst. de Senatusconsulto Tertulliano.

units.la: FINIS
units.tr: END
